System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 System Administration Guide

Intended Audience This guide is intended for users who are involved in client and employee administration. Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot view them or make changes. To effectively use this guide, you must also have background knowledge of systems, payroll, benefits, and human resources.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 13 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security PrismHR uses role-based security to manage user accounts. The use of multi-factor authentication (MFA) further ensures security. Administrative users control system access across multiple dimensions to ensure that company, client, user, and employee information is secure and protected. Access controls include: • Limiting user access to the system with user roles and user types • Configuring user access based on IP address • Configuring user printer access • Setting up strong login security, including multi-factor authentication, account locks, and password expiration • Limiting user access to clients with Client Access Groups

Security Best Practices 14 Defining Client Access Groups 20 Defining User Roles 22 Defining Users 31 Multi-Factor Authentication Security 60 Changing Passwords 69

Security Best Practices System Security Features You can use PrismHR security features to mitigate risk, including multi-factor authentication (MFA), direct deposit change notifications, password expiration and complexity settings, Internet Protocol (IP) whitelisting, and several audit reports.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Enabling MFA offers an additional layer of security to verify a user’s identity and prevent unauthorized access to employee data. In addition to a username and password, MFA requires one more method of authentication to

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

verify the user’s identity before login access is granted on a particular device. The system sends a generated code to the user’s email account or mobile device through SMS text messaging to further verify the user’s identity. If enabled, the MFA process triggers when it does not recognize the browser or device attempting to login, or if a set number of days have passed since the last MFA attempt. In PrismHR, your organization can enable multi-factor authentication at the system, client, or user level. Enabling MFA at the system level affects all service provider, worksite manager, and worksite trusted advisor users. A separate option is also available for employees accessing Employee Portal (EP). To enable MFA at the system level, use the Authentication Services form (Back Office > System Parameters > Action Menu > Authentication Services) in PrismHR:

Service Providers MFA is enabled by default for all service provider users in PrismHR. For more information, please see Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication for Service Provider Users.

SMB Clients MFA can be set up for all your clients or on an individual client basis. MFA is enabled automatically for all worksite managers and trusted advisors. All new managers and advisors will have MFA enabled by default.

Direct Deposit Notification You can configure ClientSpace to notify employees when a change is made to their direct deposit information. These notifications can help worksite employees and service providers be more proactive in detecting and preventing fraud attempts.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 15 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Enforce Strong Passwords A strong password is the foundation of system security. Strong passwords consist of at least six characters and are a combination of numbers, letters, and symbols. PrismHR passwords can be case-sensitive—both uppercase and lowercase letters are recommended. Ensure your passwords for superusers and managers are sufficiently complex. You can encourage or even require your users to change passwords periodically. For help with passwords, use a password-generation resource such as strongpasswordgenerator.com and a password management solution such as lastpass.com. In PrismHR, you can require the use of punctuation with passwords and set password expiration limits using the Authentication Services form (Back Office > System Parameters > Action Menu > Authentication Services).

Be Suspicious Educate your users to be wary of emails with embedded links or attachments of any kind. While they may look legitimate, clicking a link or attachment can hand over access to your computer to hackers. Phishing efforts often include requests for account credentials from what appears to be a co-worker. Once a hacker has access to your computer, all your stored passwords may be available.

Restrict User Access In PrismHR, you can restrict individual user access to specific IP addresses or a range of addresses. This means that any device (computer, mobile phone, tablet) in your network must come from an approved IP address. By restricting user access, you limit the devices and networks with access to PrismHR, making it much more difficult for an outsider to gain entry to the system.

Audit Reports PrismHR has robust reporting features that can help tip you off to suspicious activity. PrismHR strongly recommends that you run the following reports: • Employee ACH Information and ACH Journal • Checking Accounts and ACH Originators • Client Banking Information • Login History Report • Sensitive Information Changes Report When you inspect your reports, look for an unusual number of changes, or for account numbers/transit numbers that are the same or very similar. Confirm that any changes are accurate. Fraudulent fund transfers are typically initiated and tested in small amounts just before a large sum is removed from the system. Additionally, PrismHR recommends a review of all ACH audit records, ideally right before the ACH files are transmitted. This will confirm that nothing was altered during the business day. Even one change that was not authorized can indicate a vulnerability.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Report Instructions PrismHR strongly recommends that you run these reports. To check that changes are legitimate, run the same report (Find All Changes to a File) with different parameters (below). Employee ACH Information and ACH Journal 1. Select System Administration > File > Audit Control Maintenance > File Audit Reports > Find Changes to a File Report. 2. In the Audited Filename field, enter one of the following: • To run the report for employee ACH information, enter EMPLOYEE.ACH. • To run the report on the ACH journals, enter ACH.JOURNAL. 3. Leave the Audited Record ID and Audited Fieldname fields blank. 4. For the dates: • If running the report first thing in the morning, enter the previous day in the first Update date range field, and then enter T in the second field to indicate today’s date. • If running the report in the evening, enter T in both fields to see all changes made today. 5. Leave Optional Company ID blank. 6. Click F2-Create Report. Carefully review any changes in numeric fields (account numbers, transit numbers, and so on). Check for: • Activity that occurs extremely late or extremely early in the day. This activity is suspicious. • Changes from direct deposit of funds to Green Dot Bank or American Express pre-paid cards. These modifications require extra scrutiny to ensure they are legitimate. Checking Accounts and ACH Originators 1. Select System > Report > Find Changes to a File. 2. In the Audited Filename field, enter one of the following: • To run the report for checking accounts, enter CHECKING.ACCOUNTS. • To run the report on the ACH origination accounts, enter ACH.ORIGINATORS. 3. Leave the Audited Record ID and Audited Fieldname fields blank. 4. For the dates: • If running the report first thing in the morning, enter the previous day in the first Update date range field, and then enter T in the second field to indicate today’s date. • If running the report in the evening, enter T in both fields to see all changes made today. 5. Leave Optional Company ID blank. 6. Click F2-Create Report. 7. Make sure the bank account numbers are correct. These bank account numbers are where transfers would go for refunds, payments to the originators, and so on.

Create Processes Ongoing vigilance is the best practice to minimize the vulnerability of your organization and your clients. To ensure the safety of system information, establish best practices for your company and work with a security expert to mitigate your overall security risk.

Defining Client Access Groups Client access groups define the clients, cost centers, and sub cost centers a user can access. Use the Client Access Groups form to manage user access to clients, cost centers, and sub cost centers. Access this form in the Back Office menu under System|Change. Assign a client access group to any service provider in the system. After entering initial setup information (name and ID), you can restrict clients in one of several ways. Permit and restrict user access to these entities using the panels on this form. Different panels display for different Assignment Method values. Use the Assignment Method panels and procedure that most closely matches your organization’s requirements. For example, if Grant Access to all Clients with exceptions is selected, Restricted Clients, Restricted Cost Centers, and Restricted Sub Cost Centers are visible.

Note: The system includes a feature for grouping clients into cost centers and sub cost centers. For example, you can have one cost center and sub cost center for clients in the Northeast and another for clients in the South. Use these groupings to control client access at a high level.

Defining User Roles Define the forms and fields in PrismHR that users with a specific role can access on the User Roles form. Provide either full access to a form (including editing form data) or read-only access. Your organization should have a well-planned strategy for applying role-based security.

Using the Actions Menu From the Actions menu: • Select the option to create, copy, or delete a user role. • Control document management access (upload, delete, move, rename, and other updates) for your Service Providers, Worksite Trusted Advisors, and Worksite Managers. To access these settings, select a role ID and click Document Security (See Maintaining Document Security on page 30). See Viewing the Audit Log on page 86 for information on the Audit function.

Note: The User Report and the User Roles Report (available from the Reports menu) display valuable information about how users and user roles are currently set up.

Viewing Role Information Enter the Role ID or click the field title and select the role from a list. The form populates with specific information on that role.

Filtering Form Types Filter the form access list by form Type by selecting an option from the Type Filter field. For example, select Payroll to view payroll-related forms.

Obsoleting a User Role Obsolete a user role that is no longer in use by enabling Obsolete. (Selecting Role ID displays the User Role Search list, where the Obsolete column indicates whether the user role is obsolete (Y) or not obsolete (N).) Note the following: • You cannot assign an obsoleted role to a user or obsolete a user role that is currently assigned to active users. If this occurs an error message displays, “This role must be removed from all active users before it can be obsoleted!” • Once a user role is obsolete, you cannot manually enter an obsoleted role for a user.

Searching for Forms Search for a particular form in the list by entering a query in the Search for Description field.

Understanding Role-Based Security Role-based security allows administrators to grant access to a system based on roles. These roles are typically associated with job functions.

Note: We strongly recommend that you use the principle of least privilege when assigning user roles. Your users need only the privileges necessary to do their jobs.

For example, you might have roles for Payroll Processors and Benefits Representatives. You could apply these roles to users to grant them access to the relevant forms.

You might also have a role for Benefits Administrators. This grants access to administrative forms that you do not necessarily want to give all Benefits Representatives. You can assign both the Benefits Representative and Benefits Administrator roles to users who should have access to forms for both roles.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

If a user is assigned more than one user role, and one allows access to a feature while another denies it, then the system does not allow the user to access the feature.

On the other hand, if the form is allowed in one role and removed from the other, then a user with both roles can access it.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 24 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

The administrator grants access to forms and removes them from user roles. Note: The Reports section in this guide describes the reports available that you can run to review user role details, worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor user setup, and data security access information.

Service Provider and Worksite Manager Roles There are two types of user roles: Service Provider and Worksite Manager. Assign the user role type in the User Type field when you create a new role. • Service providers are users who work for your organizations and should not have many restrictions on data entry or other processes. You can assign these roles to service provider user accounts. • Worksite managers are users who work for your clients and can be restricted by optional required fields or approval policies. You can assign these roles to worksite manager and worksite trusted advisor user accounts.

Note: Account Management roles (for service providers) and Human Resource Roles (for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors) determine what actions users can perform, and what assignments they can have. They are not related to the user roles that you set up.

Creating a New Role Create and configure new user roles with the Role Maintenance form. To access this form, open the Actions menu in User Roles and select New Role.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 25 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Note: You cannot use a different case structure of an existing Role when creating or copying a new user role. For example, you cannot create the user role glsp if the user role GLSP already exists. If you try to create or copy a new user role using an existing role but with a different case structure, an error message displays.

To create a new user role: 1. Enter a unique Role ID that briefly indicates its purpose (for example, PAYPROC). 2. Enter a role Description that clearly describes its purpose (for example, Payroll Processor). 3. Select a User Type: • Service Provider: PEO employee or other user at an organization. • Worksite Manager: Manager for a client, or trusted worksite advisors. 4. Click Save to create the new user role.

Note: By default, no forms are assigned to the role.

Copying a User Role Create a new user role based on an existing one with the Role Copy form. To access this form, open the Actions menu in User Rolesand select Copy Role.

Note: The new role will be identical to the role you copied, except for its Role ID and Description.

  1. Select the Role ID of the role you want to copy. The list includes all user types, both service providers and worksite managers. Be sure that you know the name of the role you want to copy.
  2. Enter a new Copy To Role ID. The role ID should indicate its purpose (for example, BENADM).
  3. Enter a Description that clearly describes its purpose ( for example, Benefits Administrator).
  4. Click Save.

Editing a User Role Edit new and existing user roles directly from the User Roles form. When you finish editing information on the form, click Save.

Adding and Removing Forms You can add and remove forms as needed: • Click Add to add form access and to select that form in User Role Maintenance. • Click Remove to remove form access from a role.

Changing User Access to a Form Configure user access to a form by selecting the text in the Access column until the correct setting displays. There are three access settings:

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 26 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

• Full: Users can view and edit information but cannot see fields that are denied in the field-level security settings. • Inquiry: Users can view information but cannot edit the form. • Deny: Users cannot see the form.

Note: If one role permits access to a feature and another role prohibits access, the system denies access in both instances. Avoid this by removing the denied form from that user role. If one role permits access and the other role does not include the feature, the user will have appropriate access.

Configuring Field-Level Access Select the Field option in the Security column to set field-level access to a form. This only applies to certain forms.

Maintaining User Roles User Role Maintenance lists the forms and features that are not currently associated with the role. You can add any of these forms to a user role by clicking Add in the User Roles form. Forms may not display in the list for the following reasons: • Added recently to PrismHR • Not added to the role • Removed from the role.

Note: Forms with the word details in the Description sometimes apply only to the first tabs of Employee Details (Name) and Client Details (Detail), not all tabs in the forms. Each tab has its own security setting. For example, Employee Work (EMPLOYEE.PER*MAINT.WORK) is the Work tab in Employee Details.

  1. Use Type Filter to limit to forms of a specific type.
  2. To select forms: • Choose Select All to add all forms visible in the list. Deselect the option to deselect all forms. • Check Select next to each form to select or deselect it.
  3. Click Accept. All selected forms are added to the user role.
  4. Click Save in the User Roles form.

Updating User Role Descriptions You can update user role descriptions by selecting the Role Description option on the Actions menu. In the Role Description form, enter or select a user from the Role ID field and the current description displays. Enter a New Description and click Save. For example:

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 27 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Note the following: • You must enable the HRPY.WORK*UPDATE.ROLE.DESC process ID to display the Role Description option on the Actions menu. • Updates to role descriptions are noted in the audit log.

Configuring Field Security Your organization can set field-level security for some forms, as indicated in the Security column of the User Roles form. Some fields are required by the system and cannot be customized. • Field indicates that field-level security is available. • Field Set indicates that security is established for the form.

Setting Field Security

To access field security for a form: 1. Click Field or Field Set in the Security column on User Roles. The Field Security Maintenance form opens.

Note: If no fields display, field-level security is not set up.

  1. Locate the permission you want to configure, and set Permissions by clicking the link until one of the following displays: • Enable: Users can edit the field • Disable: Users cannot edit the field. • Hidden: Users will not see the field (available for certain fields).
  2. Select Y (required) or N (not required) in the Required column. Only enabled fields can be set to required.
  3. When you are finished, click Save.
  4. Click Save in the User Roles form. A service provider can hide fields that are required by Worksite Managers or Worksite Trusted Advisors. In these cases, a message displays to warn you that hiding a required field could prevent the user from saving the form.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 28 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Adding Fields for Security

To require security for a field: 1. Click Add on the Field Security Maintenance form. This opens the Field Security Selection form, which lists fields without security. 2. Click Select next to the field that requires security. 3. Click Accept. The Field Security Maintenance form displays again. 4. Locate the permission you want to configure, and set Permissions by clicking the link until one of the following displays: • Enable: Users can edit the field • Disable: Users cannot edit the field. • Hidden: Users will not see the field (available for certain fields). 5. Select Y (required) or N (not required) in the Required column. Only enabled fields can be set to required. 6. When you are finished, click Save. 7. Click Save in the User Roles form.

Note: If a user has two roles with different field security settings, the system honors the settings for the first role assigned to the account. The administrator must take this into consideration when designing and assigning roles.

Adding Bulk Form Access Grant form access to multiple user roles simultaneously with the Bulk Role Update form.

To add form access to user roles in bulk:

  1. Open the User Roles form by clicking (Back Office) and locating the form name under System|Change.
  2. Open the Actions menu and select Bulk Role Update. The Bulk Role Update form displays.
  3. Click Form to view a list of all available forms and select a form name, or enter the desired form name (for example, BILLING.CODES*MAINT).
  4. A list of user roles displays.
  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.
  6. Select Accept, then click Save in the User Roles form.

The system checks to see whether the user role is associated with any user accounts: • If not, click Yes to confirm that you want to delete the user role. • If one or more accounts are assigned to the user role, the system displays a message: “This role must be removed from all users before it can be deleted!” You can see what users have what roles with the User Report.

Defining Users You can define user access to clients and system features on the Users form. Also, you can copy or delete existing user accounts, view a user’s login history, and set other information on this form. Note: Service providers whose user role provides access to the Users form can also access this form by selecting the User Record option on the Actions menu in the Employee Details form. PrismHR users are one of the following types: • Service Provider: PEO employee or other user at your organization. • Worksite Manager: Manager for a client. • Worksite Employee: Employee for a client. • Worksite Trusted Advisor: User who works for one or more clients, and is not necessarily an employee. • I-9 Approver: User that secures who can approve I-9 Section 2. • Pay Card Account Approver: User that secures who can enter Pay Card account numbers. • Employee Manager (Leave Request only): User who has access to direct employees listed in the Reports To field on the employee record. • PTO Administrator: User who has access to the full list of Planned Time Off Requests. • Worksite Manager Proxy: User who can proxy into the system as a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor by selecting the Worksite Manager Proxy option on the Actions menu. (See Defining the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy Role for Service Providers on page 53.) • Employee Portal Proxy: Provides user with read-only access to employees’ Employee Portal records by selecting Employee Portal Proxy in the Account Management Roles panel (service providers only). (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.) • Enrollment Proxy: User who can act as an employee and execute the employee’s enrollment selections (Benefits Enrollment only). • Onboarding Proxy: Provides user with read-only access to employees’ full onboarding workflows by selecting Onboarding Proxy in the Account Management Roles panel (service providers only) or in the Human Resource Roles panel (worksite managers/worksite trusted advisors only). (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.) • Benefits Approver: User who can approve benefits-related actions for clients assigned in Data Security (Benefits Enrollment only). • Client Manager: User who can receive notifications (make this assignment in the Notifications Recipients form). • Direct Deposit Approver: User who can approve direct deposit updates stored in the employee details record. Note: You can only assign this role to service providers.

Validating the Payroll Process During the payroll process, PrismHR performs validations in the Users form. A system administrator can suppress these for payroll processors to prevent any of these validations or warning messages.

Validation and Process Details Step Lock Out - Calculation This validation occurs when a system administrator has executed a system-wide lockout from the payroll calculation process. System administrators might do this when they must apply an emergency patch that affects the payroll calculation process. A system administrator can then suppress this validation and have one user test the updated process before allowing any other payroll processors to proceed. Service Type “HRN” - If a client’s service type is HRN (HR Services Only), the system does not Calculation allow users to calculate a payroll for the client. Payroll Processing This validation compares the value of the Payroll Processing Through Through Date - Date set on the Lockout Payroll Processing Control Date form to the Calculation/Finalization pay date being processed. If the payroll processing date is earlier than the pay date, the system prevents the process from continuing. 7 Days Future - This validation does not allow the calculation to proceed if the pay date Calculation is more than seven days in the future. ACH Days Warning - This is a warning that the system displays if the pay date is not far Calculation/Finalization enough into the future to meet the ACH processing deadline.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 40 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Validation and Process Details Step Lock Out - Finalization This validation occurs when a system administrator has executed a system-wide lockout from the payroll finalization process. System administrators might do this when they must apply an emergency patch that affects the payroll finalization process. A system administrator can then suppress this validation and have one user test the updated process before allowing any other payroll processors to proceed. Do Not Service - This validation does not allow the finalization process to proceed if the Finalization client is marked as Do Not Service. Payroll Calculation Timing This is a warning that the system displays if the payroll calculation was not completed on the same day as the finalization. Re-Start Warning - This is a warning that the system displays if it detects that the user is Finalization restarting the payroll finalization process. Post Time Cutoffs - This validation fails if the time at which the payroll finalization process Finalization starts is beyond any of the process cutoff times defined. Terminated Client - This validation checks the client status before termination. Finalization Validate Pay Date (LE/LT This validation is based on the value of the Validate Pay Date Code Today) value in System Parameters. SUTA State Lockdown This validation is based on the SUTA state lockdown rules defined in the system. Payroll Finalization If this is selected, then the user can see the Finalize All button in Warning SuperBatch.

Assigning User Roles Maintain the user roles that apply to this user with the User Roles panel. Each role determines what forms and fields the user can access. • Click + to add a new role and then click Role ID to select the User Role. • Click x to remove a role for that row.

Note: If a user is assigned more than one user role, and one allows access to a feature while another denies it, then the system does not allow the user to access the feature. This is to ensure the security of your organization’s information and that of your clients. If instead one role allows access and another role has simply removed it, the users can access it.

If a user has two roles with different field security settings, the system honors the settings for the first role assigned to the account. The administrator must take this into consideration when designing and assigning roles. You can also select the Human Resource Roles for this user.

Multi-Factor Authentication Security Note: As of September 2019, Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is now automatically enabled for Service Provider users.

A major challenge of system security is keeping user credentials secure. User names, passwords, and personal information such as date of birth are no longer considered secure. This is especially true for people who have ever used a public computer in a library, or accessed a secure website over a public Wi-Fi network. Community computers and public Wi-Fi are vulnerable to screen scraping or decrypting technologies which put credentials at risk. Because many people use the same credentials across websites, phishing schemes and malicious redirects also play a part in security breaches. If a cyber-criminal has access to one set of your credentials, that criminal may have access to all of them. MFA security for service providers, worksite managers, worksite trusted advisors, and customer users helps keep credentials secure. MFA provides an additional level of user authentication outside of the web browser. When MFA is enabled in PrismHR and a user tries to log in, the system generates an email or text message with a unique validation key. This key, or passcode, is valid for a single use and expires after a set time period. The email or text message authenticates the legitimate user. It also notifies the rightful account owner that an unauthorized user has stolen their credentials. To begin using MFA, you must first set up a message template in PrismHR. Message templates send the emails or text messages that contain the text and unique passcode.

Note: For MFA to be effective, all users must have a valid email address or mobile device number associated with their user account.

MFA requires that after a certain number of days accessing the system from a device, each user is prompted to request an authorization code. The system sends the code to the email address or mobile device number associated with the user account, after which the user enters it and can access the system.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 60 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Authentication is necessary for each device that accesses the system. For example, if a user logs in with multiple devices, they must authenticate separately on each device.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 61 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Configuring MFA Email Templates and Services You must set up an email template before implementing MFA. This template contains the text and passcode (the <> substitution variable) that users receive by email when they attempt log in.

Note: Multi-factor authentication requires a message template. You can associate the message template with the MFA passcode email service.

1. Open Message Templates (found in                under System|Change).
2. Enter a Message ID (for example, MFA).
3. Enter a Description (for example, MFA Template).
4. Select the Content Type: TEXT or HTML.
5. Enter the Subject line for emails that use this template.
6. Enter the Body of the message. Be sure to include the <<KEY>> substitution variable in the message. The
   user enters this when they log in with multi-factor authentication.

7. Click Save in the Message Templates form.

Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication Your organization can enable multi-factor authentication security at the system, client, or user level. After the number of days is specified in Authentication Services, affected users are prompted to request an authorization. This authentication applies to each device used to access PrismHR (computer, tablet, and so on).

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 63 Chapter 1 User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

Enabling System-Level MFA Enabling MFA at the system level affects all service provider, worksite manager, and worksite trusted advisor users, and the period applies to all levels of authentication.

To enable MFA for the entire system:

  1. Open System Parameters (found in under System|Change).

  2. Select Authentication Services from the Actions menu .

  3. Set the sMFA Device Expiration period.

  4. Set the sMFA Device Expiration for Employee Portal period.

  5. Set the sMFA Security Code Access method to Email (default) and/or SMS (text sent to mobile device). This determines where security codes are sent during the Account Access Confirmation process. • SMS is enabled - It’s enabled for all employees, service providers, managers, and trusted advisors. It cannot be enabled for individual users or clients. • SMS destination - For service providers, managers, and trusted advisors: authorization codes are sent as a text message to the phone number saved in the Mobile Phone field on the Users form. For employees: The phone number saved in Cell Phone on the Employee Details form (HR menu > Employee Details > Address tab) is used for text messages and authorization codes.

  6. Optional: Select IP Whitelist Skips sMFA. This feature applies only to PrismHRand not to EP.

  7. Click Save in Authentication Services.

  8. Click Save in System Parameters.

    After enabling MFA, whenever a service provider, worksite manager, or worksite trusted advisor logs into PrismHR, the Account Access Confirmation dialog displays:

Enabling Client-Level MFA Enabling MFA at the client level can affect all service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors associated with the client.

To enable client-level MFA: 1. Select the client to enable MFA. 2. Open Client Details (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 3. Select Security from the Actions menu. 4. Set security options (under Access) as needed:

Option Description sMFA Device Expiration Use the global setting, a different interval period from the global setting, or disable MFA for this client. When enabled, all users associated with this client who access the system will need to re-authenticate their access after the specified time interval, if any, for each device they use. The system prompts them to request an authentication code, which it sends to the user’s specified email address. The user can then enter the authentication code to regain system access.

User Account Access with MFA Once a user triggers the MFA login process, the system sends an authorization code to the email address associated with the user’s account.

Note: To use MFA, your organization must ensure that all users who might be affected have an email address on their accounts.

Reauthorizing Standard MFA Login Service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors are prompted to request an authorization code after a specified number of days accessing the system from a device.

The user follows this process: 1. A message notifies the user that they will receive a security code by email (the email address is masked for security) The user must click Submit. 2. The system sends the message with the authorization code and displays a form that allows the user to enter the security code. 3. The user receives the email with the authorization code and enters it in the form. 4. The user clicks Submit and is logged in to the system.

Resetting Forgotten Passwords For MFA Login (Trusted Advisors) This process applies to worksite trusted advisors who use MFA when resetting a forgotten password. 1. Click Forgot your password? in the login form. 2. Enter your Username and click Continue. The system sends two messages: a link to a form, and the authorization code itself. 3. Click the link in the email to access the User Registration & Password Reset form.

4.   Enter [the] Security Code received in the second email. Manually type in the code to avoid copy and
     paste mistakes.
5. Enter the New Password and Confirm New Password.
6. Click Continue.
     If there are any issues with the password, the system displays a message to try again.
7. Once the password is successfully reset, the system returns to the login screen where you can log in with
   the new password.

Changing Passwords Change a user password on the Change Password form.

To change your password or that of another user: 1. Verify the Username is correct and you are on the correct user’s page. 2. Change your own password by entering your Current Password. Note: If you are resetting an employee’s password, you don’t need to enter their current password. 3. Enter a New Password. The system validates the password. If validation fails, PrismHR provides information on creating a valid password. 4. Re-enter the password in the Confirm New Password field. The next time the user logs on, use the new password. Note: The read-only Requires New Password field, which is enabled by default and cannot be disabled for security purposes, prompts employees to create a new password the next time they log into the system. 5. Click Save. The next time the user logs on, use the new password. Note: If you are resetting an employee’s password, this resets the lockout period, if any, in cases where the password is being changed because the employee was locked out of EP after too many failed login attempts.

Chapter 2 System Parameters System parameters control the behavior of PrismHR, and should be maintained carefully after installation. There are two forms for configuring global settings: • System Parameters: Features many settings for controlling payroll, printers, MFA, global codes, security, and other aspects of the system. • Global Configuration: Provides settings for many high-level system preferences, including enabling benefits enrollment, SBEA features, and user home pages.

Maintaining System Parameters Maintain system-wide settings for PrismHR with the System Parameters form.

Note: Some features are not available to all users.

• Setting General System Parameters (page 72): Sets parameters such as mail codes and company IDs • Setting Up Global Codes (page 112): Defines deduction, pay, and bill codes • Setting Global Accounting Parameters (page 113): Sets parameters such as accounting interface and export paths • Customizing My Support Team Dashboard Contacts (page 115): Customizes the contacts that display on your My Support Team Dashboard

Using Custom Feature Codes Your organization can specify custom feature codes in PrismHR at the system level to customize its behavior for all clients. These are some of the most common feature codes available for you to use; do not implement other custom feature codes unless instructed to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

Custom Feature Code Type Category Short Description 2019STATUSES Controls when access to 2019 W-4 filing statuses is removed/displayed since users might delay converting to the new form and need to continue accessing these older records. If you activate the 2019STATUSES custom feature code, the following options display in the Federal Tax Filing field on the HR|Change|Employee Tax form: • Single or Married, but withhold at higher Single rate • Married If you remove this custom feature code, these options no longer display. However, any employees with one of these settings already configured remains in this status. A/RMASTDBA Global Accounting Updates A/R Master using the Client DBA, not Legal Name. A/RMASTUPD Global Accounting Updates A/R Master on save of matching Client Master. ACADATABUILD Global ACA Enables improved performance for building ACA data. Custom Feature Code Type Category Short Description ACHHARDENFORCE Global ACH When a payroll batch is dated such that ACH cannot be processed, the system stops the posting process rather than displaying a warning and converting ACH payments to checks. ACH causes POST to halt, if batch date fails ACH tests. ACHNAMEPARSE Global ACH Uses space delimiter between last name and first name. Use this feature code if your bank does not accept child support files that include commas. In the ACH journal for child support, when the last name is shorter than seven characters, the first name will be appended with a space separating it from the last name. (The default behavior is to separate the names with a comma.) The name displays in the ABBREV.NAME field in the ACH journal and comprises exactly ten characters. If the last name includes seven or more characters, there is never a separator. The names are concatenated with neither a space nor a comma. ACHPROCESSLOCK Global ACH During ACH build, checks for pending batches and provides options for dealing with them.

Customizing My Support Team Dashboard Contacts The Customizable My Support Team Fields are used to administer the Employee Portal for your users. After enabling the DASH_SUPPORT_TEAM_ADD custom feature code (See Using Custom Feature Codes on page 87), the Customizable My Support Team Fields panel displays on the System Parameters form.

You can add a description for each custom field, which determines how these fields display on the Company Account form. For example, you can add shift categories as a description for each custom field. After saving these field descriptions, go to the Company Account form by selecting the Account tab from the Client|Change|Client Details menu. The customized fields display in the Customize My Support Team Dashboard panel, where you can select a contact for each field. (See the PrismHR Client Administration Guide.)

Clearing Backup Account Assignments Use the Clear All Backup Account Assignments form to clear all backup account assignments regardless of which clients are listed in the import file. Important! This process cannot be reverted. Note: This form is only available for service providers.

To clear all backup account assignments: 1. Click Back Office and select System Parameters under System|Change. 2. Click Process. A message displays, “This will clear all Backup Account Assignments for ALL Clients. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue. 3. The clearing process runs. A message displays indicating that all backup account assignments for all clients have been cleared. Click OK.

Note: The backup account assignments no longer display when you select Backup Assignments on the Account tab in the Client Details form. Use the Data Import Tool to import new backup account assignments.

Establishing SSO Services Use this form to establish the single sign-on service names and URLs that the system uses to negotiate with other web-based software products. For complete details about setting up SSO services, please review the Single Sign-On Guide.

To set up single sign-on services for this system: 1. Click Back Office and select System Parameters under System|Change. 2. Click the Actions menu and select SSO Services. 3. In a new row, enter a unique Service ID. 4. Enter a service Description. 5. Select the service Type, which is typically External for a vendor and Internal for services hosted on your organization’s servers. • Internal: This opens the target service in an inline frame (iframe), which displays within PrismHR. • External: This opens the target service in a separate window or tab (depending on your browser settings). 6. In the Service Destination field, select whether single sign-on with this service will be Inbound (to PrismHR) or Outbound (from PrismHR). 7. Enter the Service URL, which is the web location of the “destination” product. 8. Click Save.

Selecting Default Menus with ESS Menu Builder Select default menus for Employee Portal (EP) with ESS Menu Builder. These menus are used for clients that haven’t defined their own menus.

Adding Menu Headers and Menu Items Menu headers are the top-level menus seen by EP users.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 127 Chapter 2 System Parameters

To do this Perform these steps Add a new header 1. Click New Menu Header. The Add a New Menu Structure window displays.

                                2. Enter a menu header label in the Text field. This displays in EP on the menu
                                   tile.
                                3. In the Tool-Tip Text field, enter the text that appears when hovering the
                                   mouse over the menu header.
                                4. Enter the main page web URL for a menu in the Link field.
                                5. Display a menu icon by entering the Image URL, which is the file path for the
                                   image. For example, img/flatimages/svg/tiles/myself.svg. See ESS Menu Tile
                                   Images on page 129 for a list of available images and the associated file path.
                                6. Click Save. You return to the ESS Menu Builder form, which displays the new
                                   header.
                                7. Repeat steps 1 through 6 to create a new menu, or click Save.

Edit header text 1. Click the edit icon in the header box. The Edit Menu Header window opens. The fields are the same as Add a New Menu Structure. 2. Edit the items as needed. 3. Click Save.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 128 Chapter 2 System Parameters

To do this Perform these steps Add menu items Drag items from the Available Menu Items list to the rectangle below the appropriate header. 1. Click the name of a menu header to expand it. 2. Click and hold an available menu item you want to add. 3. Drag the item to the rectangle under the menu header and wait until the cursor changes to a + sign. 4. Release the mouse button. The menu item now appears in the menu structure. 5. Rearrange sub-menu items by dragging and dropping them within the list. 6. Delete sub-menu items by clicking the trash can icon. 7. Click Save.

Maintaining Tax-related Information Maintain tax-related information using the Miscellaneous Global Parameters panel.

Field Description Use Employer SUI Rate as Company Bills SUI to clients using an employer’s SUI rate for the applicable work SUI Bill Rate state.

Vertex Tax Geocode Override Override standard GeoCode values that are sent to the Vertex tax Option calculation engine for processing. This is a global setting, and there are also client and employee settings. Options are: • Use Worksite GeoCode as listed: Uses the worksite location GeoCode and performs no overrides. • Override Work GeoCode with Resident GeoCode: Overrides the standard GeoCode values that are sent to the Vertex tax calculation engine for processing. Uses the employee’s resident GeoCode, which is defined in the Employee Details Address tab (either GeoCode or Override GeoCode). This is typically selected when employees work from home. • Override Work GeoCode with Home Location GeoCode:Uses the employee’s “home” location assignment to supply a GeoCode for the location-based portion of taxes. This is not routinely used. • Override T/S GeoCode with Resident GeoCode: Uses the employee’s resident GeoCode from the Employee Details Address tab in place of the GeoCode on the time sheet.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 135 Chapter 2 System Parameters

Field Description Default Federal Tax Rate for Suppl Default tax rate used for special payroll batches. The default is 22% when Pay using Supplemental Pay and the system uses 22% as the tax rate. If you want to use a different rate, enter it here. Open Enrollment / New Hire Codes for organizations that use OnHRP. Users are prevented from Authorization Code changing Web Sections and Web Categories after running the ACE Process to enable employee enrollments. This authorization code is required to make changes. Do Not Repeat Data on W-2 PDFs This setting will be auto-applied to 2025 and beyond, so that data will Beginning In not repeat on subsequent employee W-2 pages unless that information did not fit on the previous page of the form. Block SSN Auto W2 Updates • If unchecked, any update to an employee SSN will update all existing W-2 Forms in the system. This means prior period W-2 Forms (if any) also get updated with the new SSN. • If checked, any update to an existing employee SSN will NOT update the existing W-2 Forms (if any) in the system. W-2 Forms built after the SSN update will display the new SSN. This applies to • SBEA W-2 Forms • Standard W-2C Forms • SBEA W-2C Forms Example: • If this field is unchecked, and if you updated an employee SSN using the Update Employee W-2 Forms in 2022, it would update the SSN on W-2 Forms for the employee for 2022 and also on the W-2 Forms for the employee existing in the system for prior years also if any. • If this field is checked, and if you updated an employee SSN using the Update Employee W-2 Forms in 2022, it would update the SSN on W-2 Forms for the employee for 2022 but NOT on the W- 2 Forms for the employee existing in the system for prior years if any.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 136 Chapter 2 System Parameters

Field Description PTM Identifier Number The PTM Identifier Number is the assigned Processor Entity Identifier Number used to identify employers and clients in PrismHR.

                                         Note: The purpose is to collect the data from PrismHR processors to
                                         import the tax liabilities into PTM’s (Assure Payroll Tax Management)
                                         transaction tables. This requires an identifier number to ensure the
                                         data stays segregated.

                                         •   This field is optional and supports alpha numeric characters.
                                         •   The PTM Identifier Number field must be set at the system level on
                                             the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, in order for the PTM
                                             Identifier Number field to be available on the Employer Details form.
                                         •   If no PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the
                                             Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then no PTM Identifier
                                             Number will display on the files.
                                         •   If an employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form
                                             exists for an employer and the same or a different PTM Identifier
                                             Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global
                                             Parameters form, then the employer PTM Identifier Number will
                                             override the system level PTM Identifier Number. Then:
                                             •   All E and C records associated with that employer will report the
                                                 employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form.
                                             •   The employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details
                                                 form will appear on all such records like the Daily Tax Export
                                                 (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the
                                                 Quarterly Tax Export reports.
                                             •   This record is not a static position number in the txt file, but will
                                                 be the last record shown. It will be the last column in the CSV
                                                 output.
                                         •   If an employer PTM Identifier Number does not exist on the
                                             Employer Details form, but a system level PTM Identifier Number
                                             exists on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the
                                             system level PTM Identifier Number on the Miscellaneous Global
                                             Parameters form will appear on all such records like the Daily Tax
                                             Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and
                                             the Quarterly Tax Export reports.

Setting Up Content for Notifications Use the Notification Templates form to set up content for the notifications you want to send to employees or groups during enrollments or onboarding. Note: This form is used only in Benefits Enrollment and in Onboarding. See the following topics: • Setting Up Notification Templates (page 143) • Setting Up Notification Templates (page 141)

Setting Up Notification Templates The Notification Templates form is used to create templates for the notifications that are sent to employees or groups during onboarding. Each template specifies the content that is included in the notification, such as the subject and message body, as well as the criteria for sending the notification and the communication method used to send the notification. When defining notification content, substitution variables can be used to replace generic information with specific information from PrismHR. Once the template has been created, the Notification Recipients form can be used to define the recipients who receive the notification. In addition, the notifications can be added to a workflow using the Workflow Library.

Note: Notification templates that have been attached to a workflow or a notification recipient record cannot be deleted.

To set up a notification template: 1. Click Back Office.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 141 Chapter 2 System Parameters

  1. From System|Change, select Notification Templates. The Notification Templates form displays.

  2. In the Notification Templates panel, complete the following fields:

    Field Action Template Id To modify an existing template, enter a template ID or click Template Id to display a list of existing templates. To create a new template, click Create a New Template. An available template ID is entered in the Template Id field. Name Enter a name for the template. This name identifies the template and displays in the list of available templates when assigning notification recipients. Description Enter a description of the template. Language Default For future development. Does not currently impact the functionality of PrismHR. Subject Enter a subject for notifications sent using the template.

                           Note: Do not use square brackets ([ or ]) in this field as doing so will prevent
                       recipients from receiving notifications sent using this template.

    Message Body Enter the body text for the notifications sent using the template. SMS Body For future development. Does not currently impact the functionality of PrismHR.

  3. In the Notification Triggers panel, complete the following fields:

    Field Action Trigger Type Select a notification trigger type. • Time Based: Notifications are sent a specific number of days before or after the workflow’s due date. If the notification engine is set up to check in the morning, the notifications are sent in the morning. If the notification engine is set up to check every other day, the notifications are sent every other day. Notification engine settings are defined using the Notification Control Panel. • Event Based: Notifications are sent when a specific event occurs, such as when an onboarding workflow is completed. The notification engine runs in the background and periodically checks to see whether there are notifications to send and sends event-based notifications when they turn up during the check. Trigger Condition If Time Based is selected in the Trigger Type drop-down, the following options are available:

                           •    Workflow is launched

 Number of Days           Enter the number of days before or after the workflow's due date at which to

                          drop-down.

Web Service User Security Users of the PrismHR API are strongly encouraged to make full use of the web service user security settings described in this document.

Basic Security Settings On the Web Service User form, you can configure a number of security settings to restrict the capabilities of API users: • Access to API versions • Access to specific lists of clients • Access to lists of IP addresses • Access to API endpoints (this can be restricted further to a specific time range)

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 157 Chapter 2 System Parameters

Version, Client, and IP Security Use the Minimum API Version field to prevent your user from accessing older versions of the API.

Note: prismhr-api corresponds to version 2.0+

Use the Company Access grid to control the client access of API users. You can deny access to all clients except those in the list, or grant access to all clients except those in the list.

Use the Allowed IPs grid to control the IP addresses from which this user can make API calls. You can also enter an IP range if necessary.

Note: The option to Disable IP Restrictions is intended for development purposes only. Do not enable this setting in production.

Access Control Options for Allowed Methods Many Allowed Methods support their own specific security settings, providing you with additional ways to fine- tune the data access of your web service users. The three main types are: • PII Unmasking • Option-level access control • Field-level access control PII Unmasking Example: EmployeeService.getEmployee#NOMASKSSN|NOMASKDOB

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 158 Chapter 2 System Parameters

By default, the API always returns certain sensitive data fields as asterisks. For example, an ssn value would return as “--***“. You can apply different NOMASK options to reveal the data in these fields. The different NOMASK options correspond to different categories of PII. In the example above, Social Security Numbers and dates of birth would be returned in full. See the API documentation website for details about unmasking PII. Option-level access control Example: EmployeeService.getEmployee#PERSON|CLIENT|COMPENSATION These settings enable you to control the possible categories of data that can be retrieved with an Allowed Method. For example, you might want to restrict a web service user so they can only pull employee personal details (PERSON), while denying access to the employee’s pay details (COMPENSATION). These settings can only be applied to specific Allowed Methods. A complete list is located on the API documentation website. The article lists them in reverse chronological order of release. Field-level access control Example: EmployeeService.updateEmployeeFields#DENY|birthDate|reportsTo Similar to option-level access control, these settings grant or deny the ability to modify specific data fields. For a complete list of valid fields, see the API documentation website.

Best Practices PrismHR encourages you to observe all the web service user best practices described in the [link to WSU Best Practices] article. In short, we encourage you to: 1. Review all web service users periodically and remove or inactivate any users you no longer need. 2. Avoid entering or saving the web service user password in the Contact Information field. 3. Set up Pending Approval Emails for permission updates. See Setting up Approval Emails for Pending Updates to Web Service Users on page 164. 4. Make sure your passwords meet your company’s secure password policies. Notify vendors and partners before password changes. 5. Use all available web service user security features, including IP restrictions, endpoint restrictions, and option-level security. 6. Create a unique web service user for each integration so you can customize the security settings.

Option-Level Access Control Allowed Methods Reference: For a complete list of allowed methods for web service users, see the System Administration User Guide.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 159 Chapter 2 System Parameters

Background Some PrismHR API endpoints, like EmployeeService.getEmployee, return extensive information about entities in the system. For example, getEmployee can return employee record data including addresses, pay setup, benefits setup, and bank accounts. The request parameters of these endpoints usually include an attribute called option (or something else) where you can specify the category of data you want to return. The implementation notes of these endpoints provide a complete list of supported options. For security reasons, you may not want your web service user to have access to all this data. For example, you might want to restrict access to the Client option supported by getEmployee, because you need the employee’s address and tax setup but you do not need client-specific information about the employee, such as their department or default location.

Syntax To apply option-level access control to a Web Service User’s allowed methods, append a number sign # to the service and operation name, followed by the first option. If there are multiple options, separate them using the pipe sign |. The general syntax is: ApiService.operation#Option1[|Option2[|Option3[|…]]] Example

Notes About prismhr-api In prismhr-api, the new version of the API, the specific behavior of these option-level access settings will depend on the nature of the endpoint. In the case of getEmployee, the web service user can only access the employee’s name and ID unless they include a value in the option request parameter, such as DirectDeposit or Pay. By default, the web service user has access to all options. By applying option-level security settings, you can restrict the user’s access to a specific list of options. On the other hand, by default SystemService.getEvents will not return garnishment-related events unless you apply the option-level security setting for garnishments (see below).

PII Unmasking Like option-level security, umasking of personally identifiable information (PII) is applied at the endpoint level. As a result, both features use the same basic syntax. See the API documentation website for more information about PII unmasking.

WARNING: The Disable Method Restrictions web service user flag will override all endpoint- and option- level restrictions defined in the Allowed Methods table. However, any PII unmasking options in the table

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 160 Chapter 2 System Parameters

will still be applied.

To ensure that your vendors can access only the types of data you want them to access, we do not recommend enabling this setting.

BenefitService.getEmployeePremium You can use these settings to control the types of benefit billing rates returned by this method. l BenefitService.getEmployeePremium (no options) — grants full access to this method, without restriction. l BenefitService.getEmployeePremium#None — grants access to only the base method without any further options. Only returns the billing rates. l BenefitService.getEmployeePremium#PremiumRates — grants access to the base method and the PremiumRates option. Can return billing and premium rates. l BenefitService.getEmployeePremium#ContributionRates — grants access to the base method and ContributionRates option. Can return billing rates and contribution rates. l BenefitService.getEmployeePremium#PremiumRates|ContributionRates — grants full access to this method, without restriction. Can return billing, premium, and contribution rates.

BenefitService.getGroupBenefitRates l BenefitService.getGroupBenefitRates#BILLING — the web service user can only use the Billing option l BenefitService.getGroupBenefitRates#PREMIUM — the web service user can only use the Premium option l BenefitService.getGroupBenefitRates — both options are available

ClientMasterService.flagClientsForEverify ClientMasterService.flagClientsForEverify#None prevents the web service user from calling this endpoint with the UNFLAG option. The UNFLAG option disables E-verify for the client.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 161 Chapter 2 System Parameters

CodeFilesService.getUserDefinedFields/setUserDefinedFields Append one or more user-defined fieldTypes to restrict the web service user’s access to those field types. A complete list is available in the implementation notes for these endpoints. If no field types are appended, the web service user has access to all fields. Example CodeFilesService.getUserDefinedFields#ClientDetails|Departments — the user is only allowed to retrieve user-defined fields associated with Client Details and Departments.

DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails These options allow the web service user to pass only certain values in the garnishmentType request parameter. l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#C — child support l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#SP — spousal support l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#I — IRS tax levy l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#B — bankruptcy order l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#S — state tax levy l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#FTB — franchise tax board l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#O — creditor wage garnishment l DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#SL — student loan You can also combine these options. Example DeductionService.getGarnishmentDetails#S|FTB|SL — allows the web service user to query state tax levy, franchise tax board, and student loan garnishments for a particular employee.

EmployeeService.getEmployee/getEmployeeBySsn/getEmployeeSSNList When called without any options in the request body, these endpoints return only the employee ID, first name, middle name, and last name. You must pass specific option values to retrieve employee data from that category. The complete options are listed in the implementation notes for these endpionts. l To return employee personal information, append #PERSON in the Allowed Methods grid. l To return employee contact information, append #CONTACTINFORMATION in the Allowed Methods Grid. l To restrict a web service user from using any of these options, append #NONE in the Allowed Methods grid: EmployeeService.getEmployeeBySsn#NONE l By default, web service users can access all request options. To limit them to only a subset of options, append those options in the Allowed Methods grid. See the example below. Example

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 162 Chapter 2 System Parameters

EmployeeService.getEmployee#PERSON|CLIENT|COMPENSATION — grants access to only the Person, Client, and Compensation options. EmployeeService.getEmployee and getEmployeeSSNList also support the #NOMASKFOURSSN option. This unmasks only the last four digits of Social Security Numbers in the endpoint response.

Note: If you apply both NOMASKSSN and NOMASKFOURSSN, only the last four digits will be unmasked.

EmployeeService.getHistory If you append one or more history type codes, the endpoint only allows the web service user to return data for those history types. Review the type Swagger documentation for a complete list of history type codes. For example, EmployeeService.getHistory#S|J only permits the web service user to return data about status history and job history.

Note: The endpoint will return an error if you include any non-permitted type codes in your request.

PayrollService.getEmployee401KContributionsByDate PayrollService.getEmployee401KContributionsByDate#None — prevents the web service user from using the CENSUS option. We recommend using this setup if you do not want to expose the sensitive information returned by this option.

PayrollService - Payroll Voucher Endpoints This section applies to: • getPayrollVouchers • getPayrollVouchersForBatch • getPayrollVouchersForEmployee • getPayrollVoucherById To exclude the directDeposit response object, append #NODIRECTDEPOSIT to any of these endpoints. For example: PayrollService.getPayrollVouchers#NODIRECTDEPOSIT.

l PrismSecurityService.getUserList#M — return only Worksite Manager users l PrismSecurityService.getUserList#A|M — return Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors, but not Service Providers l PrismSecurityService.getUserList#I|M|A — return all user types

SystemService.getEvents/getNewEvents Append #GARNISHMENT to these endpoints if you want to receive garnishment events. Use this form when the PEO (and not the client) provides an HSA match. The system prorates annual amounts if someone is enrolled mid-year. To do this, you must add the custom feature code of HSAPEOMATCH to the custom feature codes list. See Selecting Data on page 171 4. In Match Amt, enter the match amount paid by the PEO for the specified plan and year. 5. If necessary, add another Plan, Plan Type, and Match Amt.

Selecting Data Many of the forms used in W-2 processing provide linked data fields. Each linked field provides a table where you can enter data to use. You can either enter the data manually or you can click the link to display a list from which you can make a selection. Your access privileges determine the items that are shown in the list. This topic uses Employer ID as an example, although there are many other linked fields from which you can select other types of data. Each data item that you select is shown in a separate row in a table. You can insert and delete rows in the following ways: • To insert a row at the end of the table, click + next to the Employer ID link. • To insert a row at the beginning of the table > next to the selected Employer ID. • To delete a row, select it and click x.

To manually select an employer: • Select a blank row and enter the Employer ID. The system provides the Employer Name.

To select an employer using a linked field: 1. Select a blank row and then click the Employer ID link. 2. In the list of results, select an employer using the following navigational techniques. Since some lists can be quite long, the system provides various navigation options for you to find the information you want. The options are shown at the bottom of each page in the list. The available options may differ slightly depending on the data that you select.

Configuring System-Level Settings for Coronavirus-Related Paid Leave Note: Known Issue with Billing - Workarounds are now available for this issue. See the article Compliance with COVID-19-Related Legislation on the CRC for more information.

The Families First Coronavirus Response Act establishes coverage rules for employees who must take time off due to the COVID-19 outbreak. Use this form to configure system-level settings for paid leave defined by this act. For detailed, step-by-step instructions on setting up COVID-19 features, please see the article Setting Up Coronavirus-Related Paid Leave on the Customer Resource Center.

Note: Please ensure that you set up all necessary COVID-19 pay codes and bill codes before you edit this form.

To set up pay codes for emergency paid leave: 1. Select the bill codes you want to assign for system-level COVID-19 leave tracking. 2. Select one or more pay codes to associate with emergency FMLA, self care-related paid sick leave, and dependent care-related paid sick leave. See the table below for descriptions of each field. 3. Set the wage and tax cap logic, as appropriate. 4. When you finish, click Save.

Assigning Pay Codes for Emergency Paid Leave

Pay and Billing Event Settings

Field Description Emergency Tax Credit Select the billing event you set up to track COVID-19 paid leave credits. Rebate Billing Event Emergency Medicare Select a billing event to track employer-side Medicare tax credit rebates for COVID- Credit Rebate Billing 19 leave. Event

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 174 Chapter 2 System Parameters

Field Description Emergency Paid Sick Select or enter a pay code to use for COVID-19-related sick leave payments when Leave (Self-Care) Pay the employee takes time off to care for themselves. Code Emergency Paid Sick Select one or more pay codes to use for COVID-19-related sick leave payments Leave (Dependent-Care) when the employee takes time off to care for a dependent. Pay Code Emergency FMLA Pay Select one or more pay codes to use for COVID-19-related FMLA payments. For Code example, you can enter one pay code with a Factor of 1.00 and another with a Factor of 0.67.

Cap and Credit Settings You can configure credit cap settings according to your needs. Refer to the following table for descriptions of the fields and their settings. The federal legislation defines the creditable wage limits as follows: Aggregate • FMLA: $10,000 • Sick (Dependent-Care): $2000 OR $5110 minus credits from Sick (Self-Care), whichever is less • Sick (Self-Care): $5110 minus credits from Sick (Dependent-Care) • If an employee works 8 hours or fewer per day, there is a $200/day cap Daily • FMLA: $200 per time sheet line item • Sick (Dependent-Care): $200 per time sheet line item • Sick (Self-Care): $511 per time sheet line item

Note: We strongly recommend setting wage cap and tax credit cap logic to the same value. Using different settings can cause serious irregularities.

Field Description Default Wage Cap Logic The federal legislation specifies the legal extent to which employers must compensate workers for coronavirus-related leave. Employers can pay employees more, but they only receive credit up to the defined limits. Select whether to use the daily caps or overall (aggregate) caps specified in the legislation. This setting reduces employee pay to the appropriate limits, if it exceeds those limits. While we strongly recommend against using this setting in general, you can select No Limits if you don’t want employee pay reduced in this way.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 175 Chapter 2 System Parameters

Field Description Default Tax Credit Cap Logic Select whether to enforce the federally defined tax credit caps. You can limit based on either the aggregate or daily cap. This should use the same setting as Default Wage Cap Logic. Default Suppress Client The client rebate is reflected as a separate bill pending entry in an invoice line Rebate item. The line item shows total credits accumulated this pay period, along with the rebate associated with this invoice. If the entire rebate is not owed at once, the system tracks rebates that are owed and that can be taken, based on the limit structure. If you don’t want the system to automate the rebate process, select this option. Otherwise, select an option for Default Client Tax Credit Rebate Cap Logic, below. Default Client Tax Credit If you choose not to suppress the client tax credit rebate, you can select an Rebate Cap Logic option for applying caps to this rebate. You can either apply No Limits (the system bills the client and subtracts all credit accrued ) or you can cap at the client’s Form 941 liability, where the rebate for this pay period is calculated based on whether there is 941 liability from prior payrolls against which it can rebate. In other words, the amount available to rebate for a payroll = QTD 941 Liability minus QTD system-generated rebates. For example, if you have $1,000 in creditable wages and Medicare tax for a payroll (no 941 liability) and, quarter-to-date, you have $5,000 in un-rebated 941 liability, you can rebate the full $1,000 for the payroll because there is enough liability to rebate against. Note that if the rebate for a payroll is higher than the 941 limit, the system creates a client bill pending entry with a date of 10/14/2114. This is an intentional programming decision to prevent the entry from being pulled into the next payroll. For more information about this setting, see the Known Issues section at the top of this document.

Using the COVID-19 Leave Estimate Report This report retrieves employee hours and payment information to help you set up emergency paid leave that complies with the Families First Coronavirus Response Act.

To run this report: 1. If you want to filter by Employee Type or Pay Method, select the appropriate option(s). 2. If you want to filter by employee, select the appropriate Employee(s). 3. Click Run. The report generates.

Analyzing the Report For each employee, the report returns: • General employee information (employee number, name, type, pay method, and hire date). • Hours Worked (total and two-week average). Does not include sick time hours. • Standard Hours (2 weeks). Uses the Standard Hours value on Employee Details > Pay, adjusted based on the employee’s pay method. For example, the value for employees on a monthly pay cycle is:

•    Sick Leave Hours (Suggested, Actual, Taken, and Remaining). Suggested hours default to 80 for full-
     time employees. For part-time employees, the value is their two-week average unless the employee was
     hired within the last 6 months. In that case, the value is just the employee's Standard Hours on
     Employee Details > Pay. You can override the Actual Sick Leave Hours value using a new field on
     Employee Details > Other, called COVID-19 Paid Sick Max Hours.
•    Rates of Pay and 2/3 these values, in compliance with the legislation. The Standard value pulls from
     Employee Details. The Average (Last Pay Period) value is calculated using data from the last pay period.
     The system divides wages by hours, adjusted according to any FLSA settings on the employee's pay
     codes. If no FLSA settings exist, the system simply divides all gross payments to the employee by the
     number of hours.
