Creating Client Categories Group and sort companies with Client Category Codes.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 185 Chapter 3 System Code Files

To create a new client category code: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select Client Categories under System|Change. 3. Enter a Category Code that represents a client category (for example, RET or CON). 4. Enter a Category Description (for example, Retail or Construction). 5. Click Save.

Creating FLSA Exemption Categories You can group and sort FLSA exemption category codes using the FLSA Exemption Category form.

To create a new FLSA exemption category code: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select FLSA Exemption Category under System|Change. 3. Enter an FLSA Exemption Category Code that represents that represents an FLSA exemption category. For example, ADMIN or Q1. 4. Enter an FLSA Exemption Category Description. 5. Click Save. Note the following: • You must enter both an FLSA Exemption Category and an FLSA Exemption Category Description to save the new category code. • To delete an existing category code, enter or select the FLSA Exemption Category Code and click Delete. A warning displays, “Are you sure you wish to delete? This will remove the override from any employee who has this Exemption Category.” Click Yes to continue. • To clear information displaying in the form, click Clear.

Creating or deleting a Client Status Use this form to create or delete a client status.

To create or delete a client status: 1. Click Back Office. Under System|Change, click Client Statuses. 2. Status Code - Enter an alphabet from one of the following options or click the Status Code link and select an existing status code from the Select Client Status dialog box. To create a new status code, enter the appropriate option. • P=Pending • I= Inactive

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 186 Chapter 3 System Code Files

•    C=Client Cancelling (Pre-Termination)
•    T=Terminated
•    A=Active
  1. Status - The status description auto-populates for existing status codes or enter the appropriate one from above while creating a new status code.
  2. Status Class - The status class auto-populates for existing status codes or select the appropriate one from the following drop-down while creating a new status code: • Pending - This is the initial status when setting up a client. The client can still be deleted. You cannot process payroll for such a client. • Active - Client cannot be deleted if there is payroll history. You can process payroll for such a client. • Inactive - Client cannot be deleted. You cannot process payroll for such a client. Once a client is set to Inactive, then the client is removed from superbatch. • Terminated - If the client status class is Terminated, enter the number of days to process manual batches in the Term Allow Manual Days field. This field only appears if the status code is set to T. A terminated client cannot be activated. • Client Cancelling (Pre-Termination) - Same as Inactive.
  3. Click Save to save the changes.
  4. Click Delete to delete an existing status code.
  5. Click Cancel to clear the form at any time.

Establishing Reason Codes for Client Terminations You can establish a reason code when terminating a client using the Client Term Reasons form.

To establish a reason code when terminating a client: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select Client Term Reasons under System|Change. 3. Enter or select a Reason Code for terminating a client. If you are creating a new code, enter something brief but meaningful. 4. Enter a Reason Description for terminating a client. This is the full description. 5. Select a Valid Status Uses option for terminated clients, inactivated clients, or both. 6. Enter the Obsolete Date when this code is no longer used. 7. Click Save.

Configuring Global New Hire and Dependent Fields Specify whether fields are optional or required for standard and onboarded new hires and employee dependents on the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form. The new hire fields display on the New Hire form. The dependents fields display on the Employee Dependents form.

Note: These fields apply only to clients that do not have custom override settings applied. For instance, fields that are not flagged as required on the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form but have been flagged as required on the New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides form (located in the Client menu under Client|Action| New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides) override the global settings for the specified clients.

To indicate global required field settings for the New Hire and Employee Dependents forms: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) under System|Change. 3. For each of the New Hires fields, indicate whether it is mandatory: • Required for Standard New Hire: Indicates whether the field is required when clients enter new hire information without electronic onboarding. • Required for Onboarded New Hire: Indicates whether the field is required when clients have their new hires onboard electronically. 4. For each of the Dependents fields, indicate whether it is mandatory: • Required for Dependent: Indicates whether the field is required for data entry when clients complete the Employee Dependents form. 5. Click Save.

Note: Clicking Cancel while editing this form reverts the form to the state it was initially in when you first accessed the form (if you have performed no Save actions) OR reverts the form to the state it was in after the most recent Save action (so that only unsaved changes are removed).

Setting New Hire Questions You can create new hire employee questions using the New Hire Questions form. These questions can be assigned to a specific work location state with the New Hire Wizard.

Note: You can submit a maximum of 30 questions. For more information about assigning new hire questions, see the System Administration Guide.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 188 Chapter 3 System Code Files

To do this Perform these steps Creating a New Hire Question 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select New Hire Questions from the System|Change menu. 3. Click New Question. The Question ID field populates with NEW, and the system generates an ID when you save the new question. 4. Enter the Question Text to display in the New Hire Wizard. 5. Select the Field Type to define the format for the answer to the question. • If you select Dropdown, the system prompts you to enter the values for the drop-down. • If you select Radiobutton, the system prompts you to enter the default value (No = unselected, Yes = selected) as well as the description of the radio button. Only one option can be set to Yes. 6. Select Mandatory if users must answer the question. 7. Click Save. Editing a New Hire Question 1. Enter the Question ID. 2. Change the Question Text and Field Type, if needed. 3. Click Save. Assigning New Hire Questions The PrismHR administrator assigns questions to specific states using the State Rules form. The system then presents the question to new employees on the Additional State Questions page of the New Hire Wizard during the new hire process.

Setting Global Approval Policies There are many places in PrismHR where actions require approvals before they are finalized. Examples of this include new hires, pay rate changes, and client payroll approvals. Approval policies are defined at the global or client level. to learn about creating client-level approval policies. Each approval policy specifies who must approve an action before it is finalized. There are different approval levels. Client worksite personnel can approve actions (for example, a pay rate change entered for an employee by a departmental manager), and a service provider’s internal staff can approve actions. Approval policies might also require approval from both worksite and service provider users.

Note: Click View All Policies to view the policies defined for your organization, and select one to edit.

At the global level, policies for each approval type can be defined by service type. For example, you can define that all payroll approvals for PEO clients must be approved by any client worksite user who has the Payroll Authorizer role assigned to their user account.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 189 Chapter 3 System Code Files

Note: When service providers enter HR-related changes, those changes go through without requiring approvals. Only payroll-related processes made by service providers are subject to approval policies.

To set global approval policies: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select Global Approval Policies under System|Change. 3. Fill in the fields as required.

                                Change, and Leave of Absence. You can use the Payroll Approval (Multistep)
                                option to set up a multi-step payroll approval process. (See the PrismHR
                                Approvals Guide.)
                                Note: The ACH Maximum option is only available for service providers.

Creating S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments Use the S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments form to calculate and create tax adjustments to Federal Income Taxable wages ONLY (no state or local income tax) for S-Corp owner employees for the amount of company paid benefit plans (up until the date the utility ran). The process selects the records in the Employee Benefits Register for each employee that fits the criteria and totals the company contributions to any or all benefit plans for the selected insurance class. Once the process has completed the calculation and accumulation of fringe pay amounts, a report is generated that details the fringe benefit amounts for each employee. Fringe benefits are often considered extra benefits outside of a company’s standard health insurance offerings. The employer is the provider of the fringe benefit, even if a third party provides the actual benefit. For example, an employee may receive legal services through an attorney that is paid by the employer, but the employer is still the provider of the fringe benefit. Before using this process, ensure that a Fringe Pay Code was set up. The

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 213 Chapter 3 System Code Files

total amount paid by the client for the applicable benefits will be assigned to this pay code and appear on each adjustment voucher. The pay code must be a non-cash fringe benefit type, otherwise, taxes will be deducted if the wrong pay code is selected.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form click Back Office > Employer|Action > S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments.

Using Substitution Variables Substitution variables are tags that you can use as placeholder text when building message template content. When generating the message, the system replaces the variable with data pulled from the system. Substitution variables are similar to mail merge fields in word processing programs. They give content a more personal impact and make it easier to customize and reuse content for multiple employees, clients, workflows, and enrollment periods. Substitution variables behave differently depending on where you use them: • Specifying Substitution Variables for Messages • Working with Substitution Variables for Onboarding • Working with Substitution Variables for Benefits Enrollment

Specifying Substitution Variables for Messages Substitution variables for messages behave differently based on the message type they are used for and only work in specific message types. For example, you might set up a form for a workflow that includes text using the substitution variable for the employee’s name: Welcome, <<EMPLOYEE.NAME>>! When the employee views the form, the substitution variable is replaced by the employee’s name and displays as: Welcome, Jane M. Smith! Users can include the following substitution variables in both notifications and custom forms. These variables are case-sensitive and you must type them exactly as shown in the Substitution Variable column.

Working with Substitution Variables for Onboarding Substitution variables used in Onboarding are tags you can use as placeholder text when building content in custom forms and notifications. For example, you might set up a form for a workflow that includes text using the substitution variable for the employee’s name: Welcome, <>! When the employee views the form, the substitution variable is replaced by the employee’s name and displays as: Welcome, Jane M. Smith! Managing Messages Manage messages with the Messages form, which displays messages sent through the system. For example:

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 229 Chapter 4 Sending and Receiving Messages

To Do this Read a message Click Date Received, From, or Subject. The Message Review form displays. A check mark displays in the Read column for each message read. Messages display on this panel as follows: • Unread messages display in bold text at the top of the list • Messages display in chronological date order, with the newest messages displaying first. Note: Pagination controls display for clients who have more than 26 messages. Change an item in the panel Click Refresh to update the display. Importing Network ZIP Codes You can Import zip codes to benefit plans that have a network assigned with the Network ZIP Codes import template.

Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 234 Chapter 5 Maintaining Information With System Code Files and Utilities

To upload and import ZIP codes, do the following: 1. Click Back Office, then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. 2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Network ZIP Codes import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it. The sample header file contains a single column header labeled “ZIP”.) The layout requirements are: Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data. Category Description ZIP (required): The ZIP code(s) you are importing. Required? Indicates if the field is required.

  1. Before you import, you must complete the following required fields. Use this option To define this Plan ID Benefit plan ID for zip code import. Network ID Network ID for zip code import.

Updating ZIP Codes Importing ZIP codes adds them to the benefit plan record, but it does not update the ZIP code records at the system-level. You must enter All ZIP codes at the system-level to attach them to a benefit plan. System-level zip code records always display City & State information in the table. If this information is not displayed, then the zip code record does not exist at the system-level. When zip code records are correctly entered at the system-level, you can attach them to the benefit plan. The import form can save the imported record, but when you select the Network ID to view the benefit plan’s networks in the Benefit Network Locations form, the system displays the following error message for each ZIP code that cannot be validated: Warning - Key [ZIP code] is not valid for ZIP codes PrismHR recommends that you review all imported ZIP codes and update ZIP code records in the Zip Codes form before you import. For more information, refer to “ZIP Codes” in the System Administration Guide.

and assign each of their clients to their associated office. Sub-cost centers are not linked to a specific cost center, allowing your organization more flexibility in using this feature.

Field Description Cost Center ID Enter an ID or click this field to search for existing cost centers. l For new cost centers, enter text that is brief but descriptive, such as NE for Northeast. l When searching for an existing cost center, in the Search Cost Centers dialog, select a cost center from the list or enter the Cost Center ID or Cost Center Name in the Refine Search section, then click Refine. Configuring an Invoice Logo Override for Sub-Cost Centers You can use the Report Print Options form to add an override to the Print Service Report Logo Filepath when configuring a sub-cost center, which helps manage branding for all clients within the same cost center. Note the following: • This feature is only available for service providers. • When Sub-Cost Center is enabled on the Cost Centers form and you add a Print Service Report Logo Filepath override for this sub-cost center, the system produces invoices using this logo for clients with the assigned sub-cost center. • Configuring an Invoice Logo in this form overrides any configuration at the system level, unless there is an override in place that was configured at the client level in the Print Service Report Logo Filepath field on the Report Print Options form, which is accessible by selecting Report Print Options on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.

Select Report Print Options on the Actions menu. The Report Print Options form displays. 5. Specify the complete path to the location on the mvQuery print server for report logo images in the Print Service Report Logo Filepath field. For example, C:.gif. 6. Click Accept. Note: If you selected a cost center that is not a sub-cost center (Sub-Cost Center is not enabled on the Cost Centers form) or you did not select any sub-cost center an error message displays, “Print Service Report Logo Filepath override is only available for Sub-Cost Center.” Click OK to continue.

Globally Recalculating Workers Compensation on Vouchers Use this form to recalculate workers’ compensation accrual (liability) amount in payroll vouchers, for a specific date range. You can also use this form to update both vouchers and the employee workers compensation register.

Security • Service Provider Only. • Does not use Client Access Group security.

Note: This utility will use the rates in effect on the voucher pay date. But, any workers’ compensation parameters taken from company records, state processing rules, or worker’s compensation policies will use current values.

Worker’s compensation will be recalculated using current values of the following parameters:

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 242 Chapter 5 Maintaining Information With System Code Files and Utilities

File Name Field Description WC.RATES Gross Rate WC.POLICIES Suppress G/L Accrual Suppress TRIA Premium Rate Template WC.MODS Use Override Rates Override Rate STATE.CODES W/C Wage Basis W/C Wages Sheltered Week Ends on Day Rate/Hundred LOCATION.CODES Wc Policy Work Comp State JOB.CODES Job Master Classification JOB.CODE.MASTER Work Comp Class EARNING CODES Factor Worker Comp Taxable Pay Class Rate Class Comp State CLIENT MASTER W/C Policy Work Location Based W/c Calc Service Type

To access the form, click System. Under System|Action, click Recalculate Workers Compensation on Vouchers (Global).

To globally recalculate workers’ compensation on vouchers: 1. Enter a Start Date, which is the date from which you want to recalculate, by globally applying the changed rates, or other changed workers’ compensation parameters. 2. Enter an End Date, which is the date up to which you want to recalculate, by globally applying the changed rates, or other changed workers’ compensation parameters. 3. Click Update W/C Values. A job progress window displays. Select Yes to continue. (Since this is a global utility, the processing time depends on the date range selected.) 4. Click Close. A message box appears, telling you the number of voucher records updated and number of voucher errors if any. 5. Click OK to close the message box. The job progress window also closes now.

  1. Click Update Report. The Workers Compensation Recalculation Report opens, showing the amount of Accrual Change made for each affected employee.
  2. Click the XLS link on the Workers Compensation Recalculation Report to download the report.
  3. Click Error Report. The Workers Compensation Recalculation Error Report opens, showing the list of prior payroll vouchers not updated, and the reason thereof.
  4. Click the XLS link on the Workers Compensation Recalculation Error Report to download the report.
  5. Click Clear to clear the form.

Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers Use this form to update any existing vouchers that need to be included in the Flat Amount by Hours Worked Global PTO accrual calculations when enabling Global PTO functionality mid-year for a client. This process will not calculate accruals or create PTO registers. You should use this process when you enable Global PTO mid-year and need to account for accruals in the past. So, when you enable Global PTO mid-year, this process allows the look-back calculation method the ability to pick up the vouchers in the past to accurately represent the YTD accrued balances for Global PTO.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, click the Payroll menu. Under Action, click Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers.

To recalculate Global PTO vouchers in PrismHR: 1. Complete the following field:

Field Name Description Start PAY Date Enter the starting date of the pay date range from when you want recalculate to Global PTO for payroll vouchers.

  1. Click Preview. A job progress window opens and shows the total number of records to be updated. Click Close. You will see a preview consisting of the following columns: • VOUCHER : Payroll number • EMPLOYEE ID : The employee id • EMPLOYEE NAME : The employee name • ORIG PTO PLANS : The original Global PTO Plans assigned to the employee • NEW PTO PLANS : The new/changed Global PTO Plans assigned to the employee • ORIG PTO TYPES : The original Global PTO Plan types assigned to the employee • NEW PTO TYPES : The new/updated Global PTO Plan types assigned to the employee • MESSAGE : Any message provided
  2. Click the Download hyperlink to download the above information in a .CSV format.

  1. Click Update to update the Global PTO information on the required payroll vouchers. You will receive a warning message stating You are going to apply these changes to these vouchers. Once completed, you will be returned to the main screen • Click No to go back without making any changes.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 250 Chapter 8 Configuring Document Upload for High-Availability Web Servers

Chapter 8 Configuring Document Upload for High- Availability Web Servers This procedure applies only to on-premise organizations. Database administrators who need to support multiple web servers for a high-avaibility (HA) configuration can create a DOC.CONFIG record in GLOBAL.PARAMS for each service user. 1. In the central database location, copy the main DOC.CONFIG record. 2. Append .username to the new record (for example, DOC.CONFIG.userbob). The username is the one used to connect from the web server to the database server 3. Make any necessary edits to the configuration record (for example, the WEB.IP configuration). When the specified user connects, the system uses the configuration information from their record. If the user has no custom configuration record, the system uses the default DOC.CONFIG record’s information.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 268 Chapter 9 Reports

Field Name Description Check Options Controls what is printed on checks. You can suppress values, include values that should print, add page breaks, and so on. These options will be added in addition to any options that exists at the client level. • Always Display Gross Wages: When selected on any check format modified (in the list for the other check stub enhancement portion), displays GROSS WAGES and NET WAGES displayed on the check stub. • GROSS WAGES display in addition to TOTAL NET PAY. This calculation replaces the prior logic to optionally display Gross Earnings and provides a modified calculation. • GROSS WAGES includes the total of all pay codes on the current payroll voucher that have a pay class of Earnings, Reported Tips, Non-Cash Fringe Benefits. When this option is selected, ignores the option to include expense reimbursements in gross pay. • When GROSS WAGES are displayed, the NET WAGES option displays under the Net Pay Distribution section of the check stub. NET WAGES includes only Cash Pay codes with a pay class of Earnings. Any deductions and taxes are subtracted from this value and display as the NET WAGES. • Exclude Non-Cash Fringe from Gross Wages: When selected, excludes Fringe Benefits from being recorded in Gross Pay on Pay Stubs. Note: You need to select this option along with the Always Display Gross Wages option. If you try to select the Exclude Non-Cash Fringe from Gross Wages option when the Always Display Gross Wages option is not selected, an error message displays, “Always Display Gross Wages selection is required to Exclude Non-Cash Fringe from Gross Wages.” • Once you have selected both the options on the Print Service Global Check Parameters form, then: • Gross Wages are calculated as the total of all pay codes on the check stub that have a Pay Class of Earnings or Reported Tips, regardless of the flag setting, AND • Net Wages are calculated as Gross Wages (as described above less Pay Class of Reported Tips) less Deductions and Taxes regardless of the flag setting. (Note: You can work with PrismHR, if you need to add more storage.) In addition, you can view the storage being used by a client. For example:

Note: This dashboard is only available for service providers. The Document Storage Dashboard displays the following information: • Your total document storage size • Storage size by document category • Document storage size by company To filter which clients you want to view, enter the company name or a term used in multiple company names in the Filter field. The Companies panel re-displays the company or companies that match the name you entered.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 329 Chapter 12 Importing Favorites

Chapter 12 Importing Favorites You can use the Favorites Template Import form to pre-populate user favorites by importing the forms identified in the Template Process IDs panel, with the flexibility to add or remove those favorites templates in the future. There are two sections in this form: Favorites Template and Import User Favorites. For example:

Note the following: • This feature is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Favorites Template Import form.

System Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 330 Chapter 12 Importing Favorites

• Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Favorites Template Import form displays the form in read-only format. • Users whose role is set to DENY for any forms listed in the Process field will not display in their favorites list after the import finishes. • This form does not use Client Access Group security. • This form does not produce an Audit log.

To create and import a favorites template: 1. Click Back Office. 2. On the System|Change menu, select Favorites Template Import to access the favorites import utility. The Favorites Template Import form displays. 3. Expand the Favorites Template panel. 4. Enter a new Template ID, or enter or select an existing template. Do the following: a. For a new template ID, enter the Template Description (must be one word and only contain alpha- characters). b. For an existing template ID, the Template Description and Template Process IDs display. Note: You can update the Template Description, but not the Template ID. 5. Enter or select the process IDs for the forms to associate with the template in the Process field. (You must select at least one process ID.) If you select the process IDs from the Select User Process list, click Done to add them. The Name displays. Note: The Select User Process list displays the available Process IDs and their Process Description. (The system only displays process IDs that can be added to a user role in the User Role Maintenance list in the User Roles form.) 6. Click Save. A message displays, “Saving an existing Favorites Template will not update Users Favorites. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue. 7. To use the sample import file template, select Download Sample Header File and download the template. 8. Select Upload File in the Import User Favorites panel to upload a new or existing template. 9. Select Add Files, select the template, then select Start Upload. Click Close. The uploaded template name displays. 10. Click Import. After the import finishes, the system adds the identified forms to the user’s existing favorites list. 11. Click View Transaction Report to download the import details. (This report lists whether the update was successful for each User ID and the Template ID.) Note: If both the User ID and the Template ID in a row are invalid, the report lists the error on a separate line in the report. Note: To delete an existing favorites template, simply enter or select the template and click Delete in the Favorites Template panel. A message displays, “This will delete the Favorites Template. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 ACA User Guide

Intended Audience This guide is intended for users involved in ACA-related reporting to the IRS. This includes filing data using Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C, among others. ACA feature setup involves making significant changes to both global and client-level information. To complete the procedures in this guide, you must have permission to access and modify these settings. This guide assumes that you have already set up all the initial defaults, files, and preferences required for system administration, as well as basic client information. ACA compliance features are closely tied to the PrismHR benefits administration feature set. If you need a review of concepts related to system and client benefit plan setup in PrismHR, see the Benefits Administration User Guide. It is also helpful to have general knowledge of tax accounting and the ACA itself. This document explains some of the basics of the ACA as it pertains to using the software for reporting, but it is not a replacement for official guidelines provided by the IRS.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 1 Background

Chapter 1 Background This guide describes the setup and administration of system features related to the Affordable Care Act.

About the Affordable Care Act The Affordable Care Act (ACA) is a comprehensive health care reform law enacted in March 2010. The law was enacted to make affordable health insurance available to more people. It provides consumers with subsidies in the form of premium tax credits. These tax credits lower costs for households with incomes between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level. The Affordable Care Act also expanded the Medicaid program to cover all adults with incomes below 138% of the federal poverty level. However, not all states have expanded their Medicaid programs. The Affordable Care Act requires employers to offer health insurance to their full-time employees if they have at least fifty full-time equivalents . According to the act, employers must complete Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Form 1095-C for any employees who qualify as full time and send this form to them. Once per reporting year, employers must also send one Form 1094-C and all employee Forms 1095-C to the IRS. Employers must submit the information to the IRS by the end of February if filing by paper, or by the end of March if filing electronically. To review the official IRS documentation, see the online Instructions for Forms 1094-C and 1095-C.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 13 Chapter 1 Background

About Year-End Processing: IRS Forms ACA-related year-end processing involves working with IRS Forms 1094-C and 1095-C.

Background Form 1095-C indicates, for each month of the reporting year: • Coverage offered to an employee • Lowest-cost premium available • Safe harbor coding • Plan enrollment for self-insured plans Form 1094-C contains employer information (“client” information in PrismHR). This includes: • Contact information • Number of employees • Percentage of employees offered appropriate coverage • Transitional relief or methods used • Other employers part of the same large employer group

Supported Outputs Note: Because the Form 1095-C PDF uses employer information from Form 1094-C, you must fill in this information in the client 1094-C record before you can print any 1095-Cs.

The system builds ACA data and ACA reports on a client-by-client basis. If you configure your settings correctly, you can also account for employees who worked for multiple clients within the same group. In this case, you must identify the appropriate employees and then manually adjust their coding – for one or more clients. At this time we do not support Forms 1095-B and 1094-B.

The system produces the following ACA transmission outputs: • Printable Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C PDFs, for each client • Billing Document Specialists (BDS) and CIC Plus (CIC) download files to submit to third-party processing companies • Employee Portal (EP) PDF downloads – PrismHR only • ACA Information Return (AIR) file

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 1 Background

The ACA Information Return File After you finish building your ACA data, you can create the ACA Information Return (AIR) file, which enables you to e-File your ACA information to the IRS. This file includes: • A checksum in the SHA256 format. • A Prior Year indicator. This tells the IRS if you are filing for a reporting year prior to the most recent one. It is set to No unless you run it for a year two or more years before the year in which you build the AIR file. For example, if you run the report in 2021 for 2020, it will be No. If you run it for 2019, it will be Yes.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 15 Chapter 1 Background

How the System Builds ACA Data The system builds ACA data using specific rules outlined here.

Determining Employee Eligibility The system checks for the lowest-cost single plan for which an employee qualifies.

Note: The cost is based on the size of the employee contribution. Therefore, set this information up carefully.

  1. First, it checks the benefit rules. Employees can qualify for benefit rules based on their status, type, and seniority: • Status indicates whether the employee is active, on leave, or terminated. • Type indicates whether the employee is full-time, part-time, or some other designation. • Seniority is based on either the employee hire date or seniority date, depending on your settings.
  2. If the employee does not qualify under any of those benefit rules, and is included in Offered Employees Maintenance (see Setting Up ACA Offered Employees), the system then checks the ACA Benefits Eligibility Rules (see Setting Up ACA Benefits Eligibility Rules).
  3. If employees do not qualify based on either of those sets of rules, the system checks the optional grid. It reviews the grid line-by-line until it reaches a plan for which the employee qualifies. We recommend using the optional grid only if you do not maintain benefit plans and benefit rules in the system and you have no other option.

Determining Offer Codes and Employee Shares Form 1095-C provides spaces for a monthly breakdown of employee healthcare coverage offers and contributions. The system uses specialized logic to determine which offer code (line 14) and contribution amount (line 15) to populate in these spaces. For the purposes of the data build process, an offer of coverage – as defined by the ACA rules – has been made if an employee is eligible for at least one qualifying benefit plan.

Note: Ensure that you have already set up the appropriate system-level billing rates for the relevant benefit plans.

For more information about offer code and safe harbor code calculation logic, see the reference flowchart under Additional Information about Building ACA Forms.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 1 Background

The system reviews data in the following locations:

Category Associated Form/Data Reviewed Employee details HR > Change > Employee Details Employee benefit group, status, type, hire date, status date, and ZIP code.

                    Note: ZIP code data is used for any location that has regional plans. Please note any
                    employee ZIP code changes during the year, as this information is used in ACA data
                    builds.

Client-level Client > Change > Benefit Rules and Work Centers > Compliance > ACA Processing > benefit eligibility Benefit Eligibility Rules (ACA) rules Each benefit eligibility rule must define specific employee statuses, types, and wait periods that qualify under the ACA. The system also notices any employee-level overrides for ACA- related features. For more details about client benefit eligibility rules, please see Setting Up ACA Benefits Eligibility Rules. Client-level System > Change > Group Benefit Plans contribution rules For plans where the employee is eligible, the system reviews the associated employee- only plan type to obtain the lowest employee contribution amount. Client benefits Client > Change > Benefit Plan Setup setup The system looks for client-level benefit plan data during this process. For best results, ensure that: • The appropriate start and stop dates are set up for each plan. • Employee statuses are associated correctly on each plan. • The Coverage Ends On field is correct – this field impacts safe harbor coding. System-level System > Change > Group Benefit Plans/Group Benefit Plan Types group benefit The process checks the system-level setup of each plan for which the employee is eligible. plan setup It determines whether it is a medical plan, is self-insured, meets the ACA minimum value and minimum coverage requirements, and is offered to employees, spouses, and/or dependents (see image below for the associated settings). Plans can also be conditionally offered to spouses (defined by 1J and 1K coding). You can configure this in the Special Options panel of the Group Benefit Plans form.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 17 Chapter 1 Background

Offer Code Selection Logic Note: For detailed descriptions of each code, please see the IRS instructions for Form 1095-C. You can also review the status code logic flowchart under Additional Information about Building ACA Forms.

To populate offer codes, the system determines the appropriate “Code Table 1” code for each eligible plan, for each month. It populates the code in this priority order (where 1A is highest priority): 1A > 1E > 1K > 1C > 1D > 1J > 1F > 1H

The other two offer codes follow specific rules:

Offer Code Rule 1H (no Populates: coverage • When an employee is inactive for an entire month. offered) • In the month of termination if coverage would not have continued through the end of that month (as determined by the Coverage Ends On field in client-level benefit setup). 1G Populates only when all 12 months of data are complete for any employee who was: • Not full-time during any part of the year. • Enrolled in self-insured coverage at any time during the year.

Employee Share Calculation Logic For each month, the system compares the cost of the employee-only plan type of all eligible plans for the employee. It then selects the lowest value and populates it in the ACA register. An employee share only populates on Form 1095-C when line 14 contains one of the following offer codes: 1B, 1C, 1D, 1E, 1J, or 1K.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 Background

Determining Safe Harbor Codes Safe harbor codes populate on line 16 of Form 1095-C (“Section 4980H Safe Harbor Codes and Other Relief for ALE Members”). The safe harbor code logic is complex and based on many factors. First, the system checks the applicability of IRS non-safe harbor codes in the following order: 2A > 2C > 2D > 2B. Then, it follows the order 2F > 2G > 2H, based on the safe harbor method enabled in the system- or client-level ACA parameters. For details, see Configuring Global ACA Parameters and Configuring Client ACA Parameters.

Important Notes About Safe Harbor Determination The safe harbor column clears at year-end for any employees who have offer code 1G. If you have set client-level plans to terminate at the end of the month (rather than when the employee is terminated) normal safe harbor coding applies in the month of termination. If the plan terminates upon employee termination, code 2B populates.

System Limitations The IRS states that if the Minimum Essential Coverage Indicator is No for any month, then codes 2F, 2G, or 2H should not be used for those months. To avoid any situation where the value is set incorrectly to No, we did not create any logic for this use case.

If you want the Minimum Essential Coverage Indicator to be “No” for any months: 1. Use the Export 1095 Registers tool. See also Exporting 1095 Registers on page 85. 2. Limit the results to only the months in question with safe harbor codes 2F, 2G, or 2H. 3. When you generate the file, delete those safe harbor codes from the file. Leave the entries blank. 4. Import the file back into the system.

The Indexed 9.5% According to the IRS, the 9.5% standard for affordability testing is actually an indexed percentage and follows the plan year. The system allows your organization to enter the appropriate indexed percentages at the system- and client-level. The percentage you enter follows the plan year. For example, the system uses the 2019 amount until the benefit plan year start date, and the 2020 amount for the remainder of the year.

Form W-2 Wages Safe Harbor Logic (Code 2F)

To evaluate this safe harbor code, the system: 1. Calculates employee Form W-2 wages for the entire calendar year. 2. Divides the wages by the months the employee was employed during the calendar year. 3. Multiplies the resulting value by the indexed percentage (see the section above). 4. Compares this value to the employee share of any month during which the employee was offered coverage.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 19 Chapter 1 Background

Federal Poverty Level Safe Harbor Logic (Code 2G) Like the 9.5% indexed percentage, the system value for the federal poverty level also follows the plan year. This means that it would use the 2019 value until the benefit plan year start date, and would use the 2020 amount for the remainder of the year. The IRS provides flexibility on the federal poverty value you can use for a given year. Federal poverty levels are released at the end of every January and must be adopted within six months (mid-July). For this reason, your organization can indicate the appropriate federal poverty level for each plan year on a client-by-client basis, using the client-level ACA Parameters. If you do not enter anything at the client level, the system-level values apply.

When applying the safe harbor, the system: 1. Multiplies the applicable federal poverty level by the indexed percentage indicated. 2. Divides this value by 12. 3. Compares it to the employee share for the month.

Rate-of-Pay Safe Harbor Logic (Code 2H) Per federal regulations, the system rate-of-pay logic also follows the plan years. • For employees who are not salaried, the system uses either the hourly rates at the start of the plan year OR the rate during the month tested (whichever is less). That rate is multiplied by 130. • For salaried employees, the system uses the monthly salary at the start of the plan year. If the employee salary is reduced during the year, the system does not apply the safe harbor for the entire plan year. When applying the safe harbor, the applicable rate of pay is multiplied by the indexed percentage indicated and compared to the employee share for the month, as it does for codes 2F and 2G.

Chapter 2 A General Outline of ACA Processing This chapter provides a step-by-step general description of how to set your system up for ACA processing, from configuring system parameters to transmitting your data. If you need concrete procedures for completing these tasks, please skip to the next chapters. However, if you need a more general overview of the major steps in the process, review this chapter.

Step 1: Ensure Proper Benefit Setup Note: If you need to refresh your knowledge of benefits administration concepts, you can review the Benefits Administration User Guide.

Before setting up ACA features in PrismHR, review and adjust your global and client benefit plan settings. Proper configuration will provide a smoother experience with our ACA reporting features. For detailed procedures, see Setting Up ACA Benefits Eligibility Rules.

System-Level Group Benefit Plan Setup Set up the following benefit parameters on the Group Benefit Plans form (from the Back Office menu under System|Change):

Parameter Action Insurance Ensure medical plans are set to Medical. Exclude non-medical plans flagged as Medical from ACA Class reporting (select Do NOT Include in ACA Reporting). Plan Types This panel requires one employee-only plan type. Bill Rates You must set these up for an employee-only plan type.

Review and set the seven ACA parameters in the Special Options panel: Table 1: ACA Parameters Parameter Settings Does NOT Meet ACA Minimum Essential Coverage Select or deselect.

Parameter Settings Does NOT Meet ACA Minimum Value Requirements Select or deselect. Do NOT Include In ACA Reporting Select or deselect. Self-Insured Plan Select or deselect. For ACA Reporting, Plan Covers Employee? Select or deselect. For ACA Reporting, Plan Covers Spouse? Yes, No, or Conditional For ACA Reporting, Plan Covers Other Dependents? Select or deselect.

Client-Level Benefit Plan Setup You might need to adjust client-level benefit plans and benefit rules.

When you adjust client benefit plans: Set the following parameters on the Client > Change > Benefit Plan Setup form: • The appropriate Status, Start Date, and Stop Date for each medical plan. • The Coverage Ends On field in Group Benefits Setup.

When you adjust client benefit rules: Set the following parameters on the Client > Change > Benefit Rules form: • The Contribution Rules for each plan, for each effective date. • The Eligibility Rules for each plan for each effective date: employee status, type, and service rules. • For any plan with networks, set an eligibility rule for a plan without entering a network ID.

Other Settings Remember to adjust these miscellaneous settings as necessary: • If a benefit plan contains multiple employee-only plan types, use one of the workarounds to ensure that the correct codes are reported. See Configuring Group Benefit Plan Settings for the ACA. • If employees are eligible for multiple networks within a single plan, you might need to configure a “dummy plan” for the client without networks. • Otherwise, configure all plans appropriately. These configurations include but are not limited to: • Cafeteria plan rules • Networks • Risk factors • Employee overrides

Step 4: Start Building Data in Background After setting up the appropriate parameters, you can initiate ACA data builds. This procedure is documented under Activating the ACA Data Build.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 2 A General Outline of ACA Processing

At the start of the next month after you enable the ACA data build feature code, the system automatically builds ACA data for any previous months in the reporting year. Users cannot see or access the ACA data, but the register build process uses it to generate the reporting files and forms. If your organization made any system changes that, you think, unintentionally impacted your ACA data, then you need to rebuild it. The system will not rebuild those months as a background process. For assistance with these issues, contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

Step 5: Process ACA Data When you are ready to begin year-end reporting, use these and related procedures to review your ACA data, finalize it, and prepare it for transmission to the IRS and employees.

Step # Description Notes Related Procedures 1 Rebuild ACA If you made adjustments to setup, benefit plans, employees, or Rebuilding Data, if anything else in any way that could impact the 1095-C registers, you ACA Data required need to rebuild the ACA data. 2 Build ACA The system populates 1095-C registers using ACA data, so you must Building ACA 1095-C build that data first. The register build process automatically populates 1095 Registers the Employee Form 1095-C Registers. It also clears prior data from the Registers registers. After this initial build, you can rebuild the 1095-C registers as many times as needed. Importing 1095-C Data You can also import ACA data for an employee’s Form 1095-C: • Go to Work Centers > ACA Processing > ACA Processes > Import/Export > 1095C Data Import. • Any month imported for any employee will overwrite that month’s data only. • Existing covered individuals will be overwritten only if there is an exact name match. Step 7: Handle Mid-Year Client Considerations Review the following common issues and apply the suggested workarounds if they arise. If you need additional help, do not hesitate to contact support. For more troubleshooting-related topics, please see Common Questions about Forms 1094-C and 1095-C and, more generally, the section on Additional Information about Building ACA Forms.

Issue 1: Employee is not in the system but requires a 1095-C Issue: You cannot create a 1095-C register record for former employees that are not in the system, either manually, by register build, or by import. Solution: Create a terminated take-on employee record. Access the Terminated Take-On Employee Entry form (located in the HR menu under HR|Action. Complete this form.

Issue 2: No Offer Codes or Employee Share Issue: For the months prior to the client start date with your service provider, there are no offer codes or employee share data. This is because there is no benefit plan or eligibility data. Solution: Before the ACA data build, set up one or more benefit plans for the client with the appropriate bill rates, eligibility rules, and so on, to reflect the offerings in those previous months.

Issue 3: 2C Safe Harbor Coding/Enrollment Data Not Working Correctly Issue: For months prior to the client start date with your service provider, there will be no employee enrollment data. As a result, the 2C safe harbor code will not populate appropriately for those months. For self-insured plans, covered individuals’ coverage will also not be reflected accurately. Solution: 1. Build the ACA 1095-C registers.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 25 Chapter 2 A General Outline of ACA Processing

  1. After building the registers, use the Export 1095-C Register Data feature to export the months prior to the client start date.
  2. Adjust any safe harbor code to 2C (other than 2A or anywhere 1G applies) for months each employee was enrolled in coverage.
  3. Adjust covered individual entries as well.
  4. Import the file.

Issue 4: 2F Safe Harbor Coding/W-2 Wages Safe Harbor not Generating Issue: For the entire year (including after the client start date with your service provider), 2F might not generate in situations it otherwise should if the W-2 wage data does not reflect the total W-2 wages for the year. Blank entries would generate in its place. Solution: 1. Build the 1095-C registers. 2. After building the registers, use the Export 1095-C Register Data feature to export all months. 3. Review for blank safe harbor code entries. 4. For employees where blank entries exist, determine the full-year W-2 data and whether it would satisfy the 2F safe harbor. 5. Adjust the file and import it.

When you select this option, the system includes only employees who lived in New Jersey at some point during the prior year, in accordance with state reporting requirements.

For detailed procedures, see the chapter: Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS.

Important Notes Please note that: • PrismHR creates these files for the specified client. • You must be registered with the IRS to submit files. • The Additional Clients selection list is not for submitting multiple clients at once. Import the register data into your live environment. 3. Verify that the information is correct in the live environment. 4. Set the plan types back to employee-only in your test environment.

Create a new Group Benefit Plan, and assign it one employee-only plan type, entering all of the amounts for the lowest cost employee-only plan type that you offer. 2. Assign it to the client. 3. The Rate of Pay Safe Harbor looks at monthly pay for salaried employees. It excludes any salaried employee whose rate of pay dropped from the Safe Harbor consideration during the calendar year. • For salaried employees, it uses the rate of pay as of the first of the plan year. • For hourly employees, it uses either the rate of pay at the start of the year or the rate of pay as of the first of each month (whichever is less). 5. Setting LNAP Overrides These parameters relate to IRS code 2D: “Employee in a section 4980H(b) Limited Non-Assessment Period”. By default, PrismHR will assign the 2D series 2 code for the maximum possible LNAP, even if coverage is offered during that period. These settings provide more coding flexibility on Forms 1095-C for employees who are still within their first 90 days of employment. Table 4: 2D Override Fields Field Name Action Limit “2D” Status to 3 Months Limits the 2D offer code to the first 90 days of employment. After 90 days, you must select a different offer code, even if the employee has a mid- month hire date. Continue “2D” if Employee’s Status Changes to Full- When an employee’s status changes to full-time, Time During LNAP PrismHR will continue using “2D” for up to 3 calendar months, or 4 months if the period includes a partial month. You cannot use this setting to include more “2D” months than defined in the initial measurement period. End “2D” Period on Offer of Coverage Prevents the system from defaulting to a “2D” code when the employee’s series 1 code reflects an offer of coverage (for example, 1A).

Setting Federal Poverty Data The Federal Poverty Amount and % of Poverty Level fields are assigned based on plan years, not calendar years. For example: if the plan year runs from June 1, 2019, through May 31, 2020, the system uses the amounts entered for Plan Year 2019. If the plan year starts on January 1, then the plan year matches the calendar year.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 32 Chapter 3 System-Level Setup

This feature provides flexibility in case the IRS makes changes to the percentage before the start of the next year.

To configure federal poverty data: Enter the federal poverty amounts for each year. You need to do this for each upcoming year before the end of January of that year. For example, you need to enter the amounts for 2026 before the end of January 2026. 1. Create a new row in the table. 2. Select the reporting Year. 3. Enter the Federal Poverty Amount for a household of one. 4. Enter the % of Poverty Level the system uses to calculate affordability. Do not include the percent sign: for example, 9.5% = 9.50. For example: the Federal Poverty Amount for 2015 was $12,000 and the percentage was 9.5%. To determine the affordability of benefits in this year, PrismHR divides 12,000 by 12 to get a monthly amount, and then multiplies the result by 0.095. The final result is $95. If a benefit plan costs an employee more than $95 per month, then it is not considered affordable for ACA reporting.

Setting Up Look-back Periods Use the Periods panel to set up measurement, administration, and stability periods for new and ongoing employees at the global level. You can override these settings at the client level.

About Look-back Periods The ACA specifies three periods for determining employee eligibility: Measurement, Administration, and Stability. • Measurement Period: This look-back period determines whether new variable hour/seasonal employees are full-time (working 130 hours or more within the period). For Ongoing Employees, who have worked one full standard measurement period, this determines the average number of hours they work (130 or more = full-time). • Administration Period: This is the period between the Measurement Period and implementation of benefits. 90 days maximum. • Stability Period: This is the coverage “lock-in” period for employees identified by the system as full-time (based on the results from the Measurement Period). Must be 6-12 months long. In this panel, you can configure these periods for both new and existing employees.

Procedure

To configure look-back and eligibility periods on the system level: 1. Specify the number of Months or Days in the Measurement Period. For Ongoing Employees, specify the period Start Month/Day. 2. Specify the number of Months or Days in the Administration Period, and indicate whether the period Starts First of the Month.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 33 Chapter 3 System-Level Setup

  1. Specify the number of Months or Days in the Stability Period.
  2. Indicate the Break-In Service Term. This field specifies maximum number of weeks (default is 13) where the employee is not employed but remains eligible for healthcare if they are rehired. After this period, the system counts the employee as “starting new” instead of as ongoing. For example, you might enter 26 weeks for an educational institution.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 34 Chapter 4 Client-Level Setup

Chapter 4 Client-Level Setup You must establish some ACA settings at the client level. Some settings are optional.

How the System Determines Employee Eligibility The system checks for the lowest-cost single plan for which an employee qualifies. The lowest cost is based on the size of the employee contribution, so it is important to set up this information correctly. 1. First, the system checks the benefits rules. Employees qualify for these based on their status, type, and seniority: • Status indicates whether the employee is active, on leave, or terminated. • Type indicates whether the employee is full-time, part-time, and so on. • Seniority is based on either the hire date or seniority date, depending on your settings. 2. If the employee does not qualify for any of those and is included in Offered Employees Maintenance, the system then checks the ACA benefit rules. 3. If employees do not qualify based on either of those sets of rules, the system uses the optional grid. It checks the grid line-by-line until it reaches a plan for which the employee qualifies. Your organization should use the optional grid only if you are not maintaining benefits and benefit rules in the system and you have no other option for getting the information out of the system.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 35 Chapter 4 Client-Level Setup

These are typically variable-hour employees that are considered full-time for ACA reporting purposes. You must specify the employment status and type for each of the relevant medical plans. You do not need to accommodate employee statuses and types that satisfy standard client-level benefit rules.

Note: The system determines benefits eligibility based on employee status and type, based on the rules your organization entered into the system, how you assign employees, and other factors. This form defines eligibility for both benefits enrollment and under the ACA. If an employee does not qualify for the benefit plan offered by the client – for example, by not working enough hours – then they are eligible for coverage under the ACA. For more details, see How the System Determines Employee Eligibility.

Configuring Client ACA Parameters Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

You can use the client-level ACA parameters to override system-level ACA parameters (see Configuring Global ACA Parameters on page 31). You can also specify other client-specific information on this form.

Basic Parameters Review the information below for details about some of these override settings.

Safe Harbor Compensation Basis Types The system provides three basis type options to determine employee compensation and, by extension, the affordability of offered ACA coverage:

Basis Type Description Federal Poverty Level Affordability is based on annual household income, factored by household size; you can set annual federal poverty level overrides in the table below. Rate of Pay Affordability is based on a multiple of the lowest pay rate for the employee. Form W-2 Wages Affordability is based on a multiple of the employee’s Form W-2 wages for the calendar year.

About the Rate of Pay Safe Harbor The Rate of Pay safe harbor looks at the monthly pay of salaried employees. It also excludes any salaried employee whose rate of pay dropped, during the calendar year, from the safe harbor consideration. Rate of pay is determined differently for salaried and hourly employees: • For salaried employees, the system uses the rate of pay on the first day of the plan year.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 37 Chapter 4 Client-Level Setup

•    For hourly employees, the safe harbor uses the lesser of: either the rate of pay at the start of the year or
     the rate of pay as of the first of each month.

As documented on the form and in the official ACA guidance, each of these basis types is also associated with its own ACA series 2 offer code: • 2G – The coverage offered is affordable based on the Federal Poverty Level safe harbor • 2H – The coverage is affordable based on the Rate of Pay safe harbor • 2F – The coverage is affordable based on employee Form W-2 Wages

Federal Poverty Level Overrides If you set the client basis type to Federal Poverty Level/2G, you can also specify override values for this metric. The Federal Poverty Amount and Percent of Federal Poverty Amount fields are assigned based on plan years, not calendar years. For example, if the plan year runs from June 1, 2019 through May 31, 2020, the system users the amounts entered for Plan Year 2019. If the plan year starts on January 1, then the plan year matches the calendar year. Use the table on this form to specify yearly poverty level overrides, as needed: • First, select the appropriate calendar Year. • Enter the Federal Poverty Amount for a household of one. • Finally, enter the % of Poverty Level used to calculate affordability.

Procedure

Select a Safe Harbor Compensation Basis Type (see above for details). 3. Select the Benefit Plan Year Start Month and Day if the plans are not on a calendar year cycle and you need to override the system-level date settings. 4. Specify whether Cafe Plans Are For Medical Only – this only applies to clients who have cafeteria plans. This determines whether the system takes into account the client cafeteria plan contribution when calculating the cost of insurance for applicable employees and benefit plans. 5. If necessary, specify any annual overrides related to the Federal Poverty Level (see the sections above for details). 6. Click Save.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 41 Chapter 5 Activating the ACA Data Build

Chapter 5 Activating the ACA Data Build After your organization enables the ACADATABUILD custom feature code, the system builds employee 1095-C registers once a month over the course of the year. This improves the performance of the final register build.

Note: After setting the feature code, the first user who logs in will initiate the first build process. You should either log out and lock back in to start the build, or have another user log in.

If you have not set the custom feature code yet, you can set it up and initialize it during an off-peak time, like the evening or a weekend. This is because the initial run of the process takes a long time and impacts performance. After the initial run, the process will run in the background when users log in, updating information. If at any point you need to adjust your information and rebuild it, you must do that manually.

Procedure To enable this feature: 1. Open the Back Office menu and select System Parameters under System|Change. 2. In the Custom Feature Codes table, create a new row and enter ACADATABUILD. 3. Click Save.

Chapter 7 Editing Form 1094-C Information Use this Edit 1094 Form form in PrismHR to generate or edit Form 1094-C for clients. ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 55 Chapter 9 Importing Form 1095-C Data

ACA 1095-C Data Import Specifications Employee Form 1095-C data must meet the following specifications before it is imported into the system.

File Format The file should be in ASCII text file (.txt) with tab delimiters. For example, you can use an Excel spreadsheet to enter all of the data as specified below, then save it as a tab-delimited .txt file.

Record Types The 1095 Data import file contains two record types: • Employee Offer and Coverage (2) – Transaction record to submit employee offer and coverage data included in Part II of the form. • Covered Individuals (3) – Transaction record to submit data on covered individuals included in Part III of the form.

Field Type in the Import File • Alphanumeric – any printable character • Amount – any digit from 0 through 9 and an embedded decimal, for example, 123.98 • Numeric – any digit from 0 through 9 • Date – date field in either MM-DD-YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY format

Covered Name Formatting Covered (dependent) names cannot include any special characters, such as commas, periods, apostrophes, or quotations marks. It should be in a format such as: FirstName LastName FirstName MiddleInitial LastName FirstName MiddleName LastName Suffix For example: Jason Argonis Jason A Argonis Jason Aristos Argonis Jr Notice that there are no periods after abbreviations, nor commas before the suffix.

File Order The records in the file can be submitted in any order.

File Name We recommend that you use a unique name for each file, for example, CL100_1095C.txt.

Chapter 10 Setting Up ACA Offered Employees Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

Use the ACA Offered Employees form, also known as the ACA Offered Employees Register, to specify part-time employees who need to be reported as full-time employees for ACA purposes.

Overview Once you have determined the eligibility of employees under a certain client based on the client-level benefits eligibility rules, you can specify stability periods for those employees. The system uses stability periods to determine whether to generate Form 1095-C for that employee. In the given calendar year, if an employee has at least one month of stability, they will receive a Form 1095-C. The system will populate the appropriate 1095-C offer code for the month (or months) within the stability period. In short, based on the information entered on this form, any full-time employees who have a stability period of at least one month in the current calendar year will receive a Form 1095-C.

Procedure To configure the offered employees register for ACA reporting purposes: 1. Open the Work Centers menu.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 63 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C After setting up and building your data over the course of the year, you can use PrismHR to build ACA reporting forms for clients and employees. This chapter contains four primary sections: • Background information: About 1095 and 1094 Registers • Running pre-build Reports: Before You Begin • Building the registers: Build Procedures • Additional information including common questions, avoiding penalties, resetting data, and safe harbor code calculation diagrams: Additional Information about Building ACA Forms

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 64 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

About 1095 and 1094 Registers The system stores ACA-related data in the employee 1095-C registers and the client 1094-C registers. Forms 1094-C and 1095-C rely on the data accumulated in these registers over the course of the reporting year. If you want to generate the IRS forms, you must first build these registers. The system does not create them automatically.

About 1094-C Registers Note: See here for a copy of Form 1094-C.

The system will pre-populate most data while building these client registers. We highly recommend checking to ensure the accuracy of this data. Remember that this register includes some auto-populated data and some fields that require manual entry.

About 1095-C Registers Note: See here for a copy of Form 1095-C.

Employee 1095-C registers contain data for lines 14 through 16 of Form 1095-C, for each employee. They also include Part 3/covered individual information, when applicable. You can build employee 1095-C registers in one of three ways, or using a combination of all three: • Register builds • Data import • Manual data entry

The Data Build Process The register build feature clears all prior register data. The import and manual entry processes overwrite the specific data, respective to the row being adjusted (or write it, if no entries exist). • The data build process is controlled by the ACADATABUILD custom feature code. • The next time a user logs into the system after this code is enabled, data begins building for the year-to- date for any large employers. • When a user logs in after January 1, the data build completes for the prior year (the reporting year). The system builds data in the background over the course of the year for clients indicated as ACA large employers, . The system routinely checks if the data is up to date for all prior months in the calendar year. If not, it compiles the data for any missing months.

Manually Re-triggering Data Builds

Note: If you need to re-trigger for 1000 or more employees, please contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team for assistance.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 65 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Users can manually re-trigger the data build at any time. Once re-triggered, the system no longer builds the ACA data for the months that were built with the background process prior. For example, if you manually re-trigger the process in December after using the background process to build the data for January through November, the system will not automatically build the data in the background for January–November, (unless you contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team for assistance). The background process will continue to automatically build the ACA data for future months. When the data for the final calendar month finishes building, the system uses the aggregated information to make any final adjustments to the data. This is because certain codes, like 1G, cannot be assigned unless data is known for the full year (in the case of code 1G, the system needs to “know” whether the employee was ever not full-time at any point during the year, but was enrolled in self-insured coverage).

Notes on Building 1095-C Registers

Note: The register build process relies almost entirely on ACA data. This means the system must build the data before the register build can work properly. If you have a partial year of data, the system only builds a partial register.

If you previously built your registers based on an incomplete year of data, you can rebuild the registers again once the complete ACA data is recorded. You do not have to perform a rebuild in this case. If you alter your ACA or benefit plan setup and want to trigger different register build results, you must first rebuild the data.

Form Generation The system only creates Forms 1095-C for: • Employees outside of their 2D limited non-assessment periods, who had an employee type of “full-time” during any part of the year. • Employees on the ACA Offered Employees Register (See Setting Up ACA Offered Employees on page 60) who were eligible for coverage at some point during the year, based on the standard client-level benefit rules as well as ACA benefit eligibility rules. • Employees enrolled in self-insured coverage at any point in the year. The system does not create Forms 1095-C for: • Employees flagged as a sub-S-corp principal • Business owners • 1099 contractors The system does not automatically determine if an employee flagged as part-time should be measured as full- time. You must use the ACA eligibility reports and add any part-time employees who should be counted as full- time to Offered Employees Maintenance.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 66 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Before You Begin We recommend running the reports in this section before you proceed to the data build procedures.

Report setup: • You can ensure that certain pay codes do not display on ACA reports: See also Excluding Pay Codes from ACA Reports on page 67. • You can override the employment type of certain employees, for ACA reporting purposes: See also Setting Up ACA Type Overrides on page 68. • You can determine the leave status codes to include on the Eligibility Report: See also Including Leave Status Codes on the Eligibility Report on page 68.

Reports you can run: • You can use the Employee Classification Analysis Report to review employee types. Use this information to correct system data before you run the Large Employer Test Report to determine which companies are affected by the Affordable Care Act. See Running the Employee Classification Analysis Report on page 69. • The Large Employer Test Report indicates clients who qualify as ACA “large employers”. For details about setting up and using this report. • You can use the Eligibility Report to review employee eligibility for ACA coverage under your current system setup. For details about setting up and using this report, see Running the Monthly ACA Eligibility Report on page 70 and Running the ACA Eligibility Report.

Excluding Pay Codes from ACA Reports You can exclude specific pay codes from the output of several reports, including the Large Employer Test Report, Eligibility Report, and Eligibility Report (Legacy).

To exclude pay codes from these reports: 1. Open the Back Office menu. 2. Under System|Change, select Pay Codes. 3. Enter the ID of the Pay Code you need to change. 4. Select the Exclude From ACA Hours Calculation option. 5. Click Save.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 67 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Setting Up ACA Type Overrides Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

Use this form to define full-time employees as part-time for certain periods, if this is required for ACA reporting.

To set up employee type overrides for ACA reporting: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Setup and Client Setup, select ACA Type Overrides. 4. Select an Employee. 5. Enter the Start Date and End Date of the period in which the system will treat the employee as part-time, for ACA reporting purposes. 6. Click Save.

Including Leave Status Codes on the Eligibility Report Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

The system uses the information entered on this form to determine whether an employee has worked enough hours during the reporting period to be identified as full-time. If you identify an employee as on leave, the report calculation will include the days they were on leave.

Background To be considered a full-time employee, an employee must work an average of 130 hours for each month included in the date range for which the report is run. If the report is run from January 1 to March 31, that would mean an employee needs to work at least 390 hours during the reporting period: (9 months x 130 hours)/1 month = 1170 hours (where one month = 24 hours x 31 days = 744 hours) If, during that same time period, an employee was on valid leave (as indicated by one of the Leave Status codes on the ACA Reports Parameters), then the number of required hours will be adjusted by a factor based on the total days in the report and the total number of days the employee was on valid leave. For example: • Employee is on valid leave for 25 days • The number of days in the report is 273 days • Factor = (273 - 25) / 273 = .9084 • The number of hours for this employee to be full time = .9084 x 1170 hours = 1062.828 hours.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 68 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Procedure

To set up leave status codes: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Setup and Reporting Setup, select Leave Status Codes Overrides for ACA Coverage Report. 4. Enter or select each Leave Status Code you want to include in the eligibility report. 5. Click Save.
