The Eligibility Reports indicate employee eligibility for health care coverage under the ACA. Eligibility is based on employee hours worked over a certain measurement period. You can establish this period at the global level and override it at the client level, if necessary. For more information about these setup parameters, see the topics on global and client-level period setup: • Configuring Global ACA Parameters

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 71 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

• Configuring Client ACA Parameters You can run the Eligibility Report for either current employees or new hires. The period information comes from the Period Setup section of the Client ACA Parameters. If that information is not defined, the Period Setup values come from the system-level ACA parameters. The following example of the global Periods panel includes sections for new employees and ongoing employees. These correspond to the two types of ACA eligibility report you can run.

Before You Begin You can specify certain leave status codes to include on the report, even if the report would not normally include those employees: use the Leave Status Codes Overrides for ACA Coverage Report form to do this. See Including Leave Status Codes on the Eligibility Report for details.

About the Start and End Date Fields When setting up this report, you must enter a Start Date and End Date. The system uses this date range to select any employees who had a measurement period during this time. These dates can be up to one (non- calendar) year apart. The report logic is different based on whether you run the report for new hires or for ongoing employees.

New Hire Report The new hire report selects employees using the report start and end dates, in conjunction with the New Hire Measurement Period in the global or client ACA settings. For example, if you run the report for new hires with a start date of 9/15/2026 and an end date of 10/15/2026, and the New Hire Measurement Period is 9 months, then for all clients on the report the system will include employees who were hired between 12/16 of the previous year and 1/16/2026 (notice that this range is 9 months before the entered dates). Note the following: • This measurement start date is specific to this report. Each employee has a different measurement start based on their effective hire date.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 72 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

• To select vouchers, the system uses the date that comes 31 days after the End Date. • There is nothing in the client or global Period settings that affects the validity of the start and end dates you enter for this report.

Ongoing Employee Report For the ongoing report, the system uses the year passed in the report start and end date fields. The month and day must be within the range from the Start Month/Day specified for the ongoing period. For example, if you enter 1/1/2026 and the start for the period is January 1, then the measurement start date for the report will be 1/1/2026. If the Ongoing Measurement Period is 6 Months, then the measurement end date will be 6/1/2026. • Like the new hire report, this report selects vouchers based on the date that comes 31 days after the specified End Date. • The Start Date must be before, or the same as, the Measurement End Date. • The End Date must be the same as, or after, the Measurement End Date. • If these dates are not correct, the report will not be generated for the client.

Interpreting the Eligibility Report Output Use this section to better understand the output of the eligibility report.

“Number of Weeks” and Week End Dates • Weeks run from Sunday through Saturday, except the first and last weeks in the measurement period. • The first week starts on the measurement period start date, and ends on the following Saturday. • The last week starts on Sunday and ends on the last day in the measurement period. • The number of weeks in the report is based on the measurement periods, as well as the Start Date and End Date from the report setup parameters. • The Number of Weeks count is the number of days in the measurement period divided by seven. It is not the total number of weeks for all employees on the report.

Employee-level “Number of Weeks” and Hours • Report hours accumulate for each employee, in each week in the measurement period. • When assigning hours to a particular week, the system uses the charge date on the employee time sheet to select that week. • If the hours do not have an associated charge date, then the system uses the Pay Period End date for the voucher. • If there are no hours for a certain week within the employee measurement period, the report still uses that week when it calculates the average.

Calculating Hours • If the pay code Calculation Method is Standard and the Pay Reason is Hourly, then the report counts the number of Hours Paid. Otherwise, it counts the Hours Worked. • If a pay code is set to be excluded from ACA hours calculation, the report does not include those hours in the report. • You can also import external hours into the system. The report will include these hours.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 74 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Review the following table for descriptions of other values in the report:

Column Description Employee The total of all hours for every week in the employee measurement period. Total Hours Average Total employee hours divided by the number of weeks in the employee measurement period. Hours Valid Leave If an employee was on valid leave during the reporting period, the report totals the number of Days leave days. The number of days in the report is weighted against the number of days of valid leave. This factor is used to adjust the full-time employment (FTE) requirements for the employee. FTE Flag If the employee worked an average of 30 hours per week, this flag is set to Y, otherwise it is set to N. If valid leave days affected this calculation, an asterisk also displays (Y or N), and the report includes a footnote with an explanation. Health The report checks for all medical benefits plans. If the employee is actively enrolled in a medical Coverage benefit plan with a coverage start date before the end of the measurement period, this is set to Y, otherwise it is N. If an employee is actively enrolled in any medical benefit plan, then Waived is set to N. Waived If an employee: • is not actively enrolled in any other medical benefit plan, and • has waived coverage in any other medical benefit plan with a coverage start date before the end of the measurement period this column displays a Y.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 75 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Column Description Break in A break in service is a period when the employee is not active. The Break in Service Term is Service usually 13 weeks unless otherwise specified in the client-level ACA Period setup. Valid leave days are counted as active and are not treated as a break in service. The report uses the last hire date for all employees when determining a break in service: • If the last hire and original hire dates are the same, then there was no break in service. • If the dates are not the same, but the difference is fewer than 4 weeks, the system counts those weeks as zero. • If the system determines that the total employment time – before being terminated or going on invalid leave – is greater than the difference between 4 weeks and the number of Break in Service Term weeks, then the system counts those weeks as zero. • If total employment time – before being terminated or going on invalid leave – is less than the difference between 4 weeks and the Break in Service Term weeks, then the employee starts new on the last hire date. • If the difference between the last hire date and original hire date is greater than the Break in Service Term, the employee starts new on the last hire date. • If the employee goes back and forth between employed and not employed, and never exceeds the maximum break in service time, the system uses their original hire date. If a break in service with the allowed weeks occurs during an employee measurement period, a double asterisk displays in front of the employee status class (for example, **A) and the report includes an explanatory footnote.

More Information About the Dates on the Eligibility Report

On both reports • The Effective Hire Date is the last employee hire date, based on the hire date in the employee record and the break in service logic. • If Period setup requires that the administration period start on the first of the month, the measurement end date is extended to the last day of the month when it is calculated. • Both reports select employee vouchers by employee ID, then by client, and finally by the period end date on the voucher. • To select vouchers, both reports use the date 31 days after your entered End Date. The system processes the hours in the voucher based on the charge date or — if a charge date is not used — based on the voucher period end date. These settings ensure that the system processes all charge dates. • Both reports use the charge data associated with the hours from the voucher (or the voucher period if there is no charge date associated with the hours) to determine the week within the measurement period. The reports then accumulate the hours in that week.

About the Large Employer Test Report The Large Employer Test Report identifies clients that employ 50 or more employees. It displays the status of each employee, as of the End Date of the report. The system derives the hours for this report from two sources: • Processed payroll information from the system. • External ACA-related employee hours that have been updated using the External ACA Hours utility.

Note: Before running the Large Employer Test Report, PrismHR recommends that you analyze the average hours worked and if the current employee type is appropriate. For example, if an employee averages 80 hours per month then they should not be flagged as full-time. If they are, it can have a negative impact on the Large Employer Test Report.

Review the following topics for more guidance: • Large Employer Test Report Considerations (page 78) • Omitting Employees from the Large Employer Test Report (page 79) • Establishing ACA Large Employer Status (page 81)

Large Employer Test Report Considerations

Employment Classifications

The system considers the following information when creating the Large Employer Test Report: • If an employee is classified as full-time active on the first and last day of a month, the report displays 120 hours for that month. • If an employee is not full-time, the report displays their actual hours , but the amount displayed will not exceed 120 hours per month. The report uses hours paid for any Standard pay codes with Pay Reason set to Hours. For pay codes that do not meet these criteria, the report uses hours worked, if any exist. • If the employee works at least 120 hours each month for the months specified, the report counts the employee as 1.

Seasonal Employees • Employees with Seasonal status will not be included if they worked 120 or fewer consecutive days. • Employees will be included on the report if they were not considered seasonal-only during the reporting period. In other words, if they were Active and Full- or Part-Time Non-Seasonal at any point in the report period, they will be included in the report, regardless of the number of days this was true. The Seasonal flag will also be enabled on their employee record so that, if there is any question about their status, the Seasonal flag will make them stand out in the report.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 78 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

     Consider this example: Joe starts the year as a seasonal employee. Sixty days later, Joe becomes a full-
     time employee. In this scenario, Joe’s entire employment period will be included in the report and the
     Seasonal flag will be set to Y.

Control Groups When clients are part of a Control Group, as indicated in Client Details or Company Master configuration, they will be listed under that Control Group Client in the Large Employer Test Report.

Important Notes and Considerations Employment Classifications

The system considers the following information when creating the Large Employer Test Report: • If an employee is classified as full-time active on the first and last day of a month, the report displays 120 hours for that month. • If an employee is not full-time, the report displays their actual hours , but the amount displayed will not exceed 120 hours per month. The report uses hours paid for any Standard pay codes with Pay Reason set to Hours. For pay codes that do not meet these criteria, the report uses hours worked, if any exist. • If the employee works at least 120 hours each month for the months specified, the report counts the employee as 1. Seasonal Employees • Employees with Seasonal status will not be included if they worked 120 or fewer consecutive days. • The report does include employees who were not considered seasonal-only during the reporting period. In other words, if they were Active and Full- or Part-Time, Non-Seasonal at any point in the report period, the report will include them. The system will also activate the Seasonal flag on their employee record so that, if there is any question about their status, the Seasonal flag will make them stand out in the report. Consider this example: Joe starts the year as a seasonal employee. Sixty days later, Joe becomes a full-time employee. After this change, a service provider runs the Large Employer Test Report for the year and includes Joe’s client or employer. In this scenario, Joe’s entire employment period will be included in the report, and his Seasonal column entry will display as Y on the report (and on his employee record in the system).

Running the ACA 9.5% Rule Test Report Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

This report displays the Total Annualized Pay and Form W-2 Box 1 calculations for currently elected employee health plans. The results of this report can help employers decide which type of wages they will use to determine plan affordability. The ACA advises employees to not pay more than 9.5% of their household income to an employer in exchange for a single portion of the lowest cost health care plan available to that employee. If employers need to use alternative methods for calculating this value, ACA regulations specify three safe harbor options they can use instead of the annual household income: • Form W-2, Box 1 wages • Total Annualized Pay • Federal Poverty Level (FPL)

Note: During the annualizing process, the system bases employee rate of pay on the last day of the report period.

Procedure

To run this report: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing.

  5. To exclude employees who do not have coverage, select the Exclude Employees Without Coverage? option.
  6. Click Generate Report.

Building ACA 1095 Registers Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

Use this form to build Form 1095-C data registers for ACA reporting. To avoid building incomplete data, PrismHR generally recommends running the register build after the end of the reporting year. Whenever your organization runs the build process, the system will overwrite any existing ACA 1095 register records. It will also update the counts in the client 1094-C register for the selected reporting year, because those counts are derived from the employee 1095-C registers.

Note: Before building registers, we also recommend running the ACA Data Status Report to verify that the ACA data is complete. See also Running the ACA Data Status Report on page 84.

To build ACA 1095-C registers: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Processes, select Build ACA 1095 Registers. 4. Select the reporting Year for which you need to build registers. 5. Enter or select a Client ID if you want to build registers for only that client, or leave the field blank to process all applicable clients. 6. Click Create 1095 Data. The system will send you an email notification when the process completes.

Running the Export This feature exports Form 1095-C register data as a text (TXT) file that you can then view, edit, and import back into the system. The export file includes the records for employee offer and coverage data (type 2), covered individuals (type 3), and the employee’s employer and home worksite location. The Employer and Home worksite are provided for reference only. You will want to delete these fields before moving forward with the edit and import.

Note: Please note that the report includes only employees and months with Form 1095-C register data. For example, if you run the report at the end of October 2026, it will not include any information for November or December of that year.

To export 1095-C registers: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Processes and Import/Export select 1095 Register Export. 4. Select the appropriate Report Year. 5. Enter a Client ID if necessary. If you do not specify a client, the export runs for all clients. 6. You can apply Export Filters to limit the data returned by the export file. By default, the report includes all register data and all codes. Specify the months and codes you want to include in the report:

  1. In the Include Employees with Share Not Less Than field, enter the maximum number of shares needed to exclude an employee from the report. Leave this field blank to include all share amounts.

Editing the File You can open the file with a text editor or a spreadsheet program such as Microsoft™ Excel®. Make sure to save it as a text file so you can import any changes back into the system. There are some important things to note about making edits:

Decimal Places in Employee Share

Note: If a column in a text file is not formatted correctly, decimals can be lost during the import process.

The import process requires 2 decimal places for any Employee Share value. If the decimal places are missing, the import function inserts them. For example, if the export runs and an employee share is 100.00, but the spreadsheet program changes this to read 100 and saves the value without the decimal places, the system will import it as 1.00. Therefore, you must ensure that values in the text file include the two decimal places.

To prevent decimal place errors for any Type 2 entry (employees): • Before you save and import, make sure the seventh column (G, in Excel) only contains numbers with two decimal places. • For any Type 3 entry (covered individual), do not format the data as a number with two decimal places: this data represents a birth date. • You can sort the spreadsheet so Type 2 entries are at the top and Type 3 entries are at the bottom, and then select all the cells in that column that apply to Type 2 entries.

Considerations for Covered Individuals When importing the file, covered individuals are identified by Social Security number first, and then by date of birth if no Social Security number is present. • If you find that a covered individual’s name is incorrect, you can edit it in this file. • If the Social Security number or date of birth is incorrect or missing, do not try to edit these values in the export file. Instead of updating this record with an import (which would create a new covered individual

record), you must use the Edit Employee 1095 form to change this information directly (See also Editing

Additional Information about Building ACA Forms This section contains any other documentation relevant to the ACA data build process, including helpful notes and an FAQ.

ACA Penalty Avoidance Recommendations Before submitting Forms 1094-C and 1095-C to the IRS and your employees, PrismHR strongly recommends you review the contents of these forms for common errors resulting in penalties. The IRS leverages three types of penalties for (real, or perceived) employer mandate violations. These penalties are: • Failure to file/furnish: up to $270 (or more in the case of intentional disregard) per Form 1095-C with incorrect data or if the form is submitted late to the IRS/employees • 4980H(a): $2,320 per every full-time employee for any month the 95% minimum essential coverage (MEC) standard is not met, if a single employee receives a premium tax credit • 4980H(b): $3,480 per individual employee who was not offered MEC The most common errors that result in penalty assessment notices are usually self-evident reporting errors on Forms 1094-C and 1095-C. Two specific examples include: • Form 1094-C submissions with the MEC Indicator for one or more months set to No • Form 1095-C submissions with blank Box 16 Safe Harbor code entries

WARNING: In order to provide the most accurate reporting results possible, PrismHR uses configuration and data-driven logic when it sets the MEC Indicator and Safe Harbor codes. This leaves open the possibility that the system might set the MEC Indicator to No and leave Box 16 for Safe Harbor codes blank. Therefore, we highly recommend reviewing MEC indicators and safe harbor codes before submission.

Recommended Review Processes PrismHR recommends using the following processes to avoid potential issues when submitting Forms 1094-C and 1095-C to the IRS.

MEC Indicator Use the Part 3 of the Edit 1094 Form screen (See also Editing Form 1094-C Information on page 46) to adjust the MEC Indicator for all ALE clients. The values for any month and client can be edited. If a value for any month is incorrectly set to “No”, set it to “Yes.”

Safe Harbor Codes Use the Form 1095-C Register Export utility (See also Exporting 1095 Registers on page 85) to review system- generated safe harbor codes on this form.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 93 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

The default download configuration produces all Form 1095-C data for all clients and employees in our import format. You can scan the output to identify any missing safe harbor codes.

To add or edit any codes in the export file: 1. Edit the export file. 2. Save the file on your local machine. 3. Import the updated file back into the system (See Importing Form 1095-C Data on page 55). You can also adjust Form 1095-C data per employee directly (See also Editing Form 1095-C Information on page 53).

ACA 1094 Count Report In PrismHR, use the ACA 1094 Count Report (found in the Reports menu under HR > Report) to review MEC Indicator values per employee for any month of the year.

MEC must be offered to at least 95% of ALE Member’s full-time employees and their dependents. The report tests if employees are included in the count by using the total full-time count for any month as the denominator, and the total MEC count for any month as the numerator. On this report, review any employee with 1 for full-time count (FT) and 0 for MEC, as this indicates they should have been offered MEC, but were not. This is any employee out of a 2D limited non-assessment period that either: • was a full-time employee for the month, or • was identified as being ACA Full Time for that month on the ACA Offered Employees register.

More Notes About Offer Code Calculation The system calculates the offer codes based on information entered in the various forms that pertain to the ACA.

A few notes about this calculation logic: • The system replaces 1E with 1A when the employee share is less than the federal poverty line. • If an employee has the 1G offer code in a month, the employee’s share and safe harbor codes (Lines 15 and 16) are empty. • Code 1J indicates that the employee was offered a medical plan that covers the employee and conditionally covers a spouse. • Code 1K indicates that the employee was offered a medical plan that covers the employee and other dependents and conditionally covers a spouse. • Codes 1I and 2I were valid for reporting year 2015. They are not valid codes for any year after that. • Codes 1L through 1S were introduced in 2020. They correspond to individual coverage health reimbursement accounts (HRAs) offered to employees, non-employees, spouses, and dependents. Some codes also determine whether the employee’s worksite ZIP code or their residential ZIP code displays on line 17, which was also introduced on the 2020 version of the form.

Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Notes on Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C Note the following about the way the system handles the information and builds the registers for these forms.

Employee Data in the Form 1094-C Register Build The Full-Time Employee Count includes any employee who was active on the first of a month that the system determined to be ACA full time for the month. It determines this at the time of the register build or the import.

Employees in the Form 1095-C Register Build Employees’ employment status determines whether they are included in the Form 1095-C register build.

Full-Time Employees If an employee is flagged as full-time, the system considers them eligible on the first of the month that is three months after the hire date. If, under company eligibility rules, the employee was not offered benefits on or before that date, Line 16 is blank for those months.

Variable-Hour Employees If an employee qualifies for coverage under the client’s benefits eligibility rules, the system populates the correct code on the Form 1095-C. This is based on the entries in Offered Employees Maintenance form. See Setting Up ACA Offered Employees on page 60.

COBRA Enrollees The register build handles employees who were offered or enrolled in COBRA during the current year. Employees who were covered by COBRA but were not employed at any point during the year are correctly excluded from the register.

W-2 Wages for Affordability Testing Calculations The system factors the number of months that an employee was offered coverage into the Safe Harbor proration.

When the system uses the employees’ W-2 wages for affordability testing, it adjusts the amounts used in the calculation by performing these steps: 1. Get the year-to-date W-2 wages. 2. Get the number of months in the year when coverage was offered for any day in the month. 3. Get the number of months in the year when the employee was active on any day in the month. 4. Divide the number of months coverage was offered by the number of months employed. 5. Multiply the result by the W-2 wages. 6. Multiply that result by 9.5 percent (0.095). 7. If the lowest-cost contribution is less than or equal to the final result, then the plan is affordable.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 99 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Common Questions about Forms 1094-C and 1095-C These are some frequently asked questions about the IRS forms for Affordable Care Act (ACA) reporting.

What goes in Line 14 (Offer Code) and Line 15 (Employee Share)? The register build only looks at company-level eligibility and contribution rules when it determines what populates each employee’s line 14 and line 15. The system then scans through the contribution rules for the employee-only plan types for these benefit plans. Generally, the benefit plan with the lowest employee cost is used as the employee share, and this determines the value for the line 14. Preference is given to a 1A benefit plan, as well as 1I relief.

Note: If terminated employees receive offer codes, your organization probably did not set your eligibility rules to exclude terminated employees. If you receive 1H when you should not, your organization probably did not set a company-level rule entry for any medical plan.

Known Issue The system assumes one type of employee-only benefit plan per offering. If you have more than one, register build results may vary. This includes usage of networks where the employee is eligible for more than one network.

Workaround 1. Set up a “dummy” benefit plan by copying a benefit plan with multiple employee-only plan types (or multiple networks). 2. Assign a single employee-only plan type (the plan type with the lowest cost available to the employee) to this benefit plan. 3. Assign this benefit plan to the company. Make sure to enter a start date that matches when the benefit should be considered for register build purposes. 4. Assign the appropriate eligibility and contribution rules to this benefit plan. If the above steps do not work, terminate the benefit plan that is causing the issue at the company level, making sure to backdate the termination date to a day before January 1 of the current reporting year.

An employee register was note built. What happened? There are circumstances where the system might not build a register for an employee when your organization believes that employee should have one. Form 1095-Cs are only necessary for those employees entitled to an offer of coverage during any part of the reporting year. This includes the following: • Employees who have the full-time Employee Type, who were hired on or before September 1, and who are therefore out of their limited non-assessment period before the end of the year. • Employees listed in the company’s Offered Employees Maintenance form. Your organization must use this register to alert the system of any variable-hour employee (employees who have the part-time Employee

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 100 Chapter 11 Building Form 1094-C and Form 1095-C

Type), who measured full-time in a previous measurement period. You must enter these employees in the
company’s Offered Employees Maintenance and include the start and end dates of their subsequent stability
period. The system treats these employees as full-time and entitled to an offer of coverage for the duration
of this stability period.

Note: Check your system-level setup to see if your employee type codes are appropriately flagged as full- or part-time.

Why are there blank entries in Line 16? Once an employee is entitled to an offer of coverage (see the previous question for more information), there are three possible scenarios for Line 16 (Safe Harbor Code): • The value 2C, if the employee was enrolled in any medical coverage for the entire month • Depending on which safe harbor you select, the values 2F, 2G, or 2H, if the employee share meets that safe harbor standard • A blank value, if the system determines that the safe harbor was not satisfied by comparison to the employee share For the W-2 wages safe harbor, federal regulations provide a very specific method of proration for any employee not offered coverage for the entirety of the year. For the rate-of-pay safe harbor, federal regulations provide numerous options based on changes in rate-of-pay, whether an employee is salaried or paid hourly, and whether the plan offerings are calendar year.

Known Issues • When using the rate-of-pay safe harbor with a non-calendar year plan entry, entering rate-of-pay changes may result in the incorrect rate being used to calculate the safe harbor. The PrismHR Customer Support Team recommends that you review the results for any employee with a rate-of-pay change during the appropriate plan years when using this safe harbor. • In some instances, you may get a blank safe harbor entry in the employee’s month of termination. The PrismHR Customer Support Team recommends that you review the register build results for any employee terminated during that year.

Why is a 2D Code in Line 16? The value 2D may appear on the 1095-C for any full-time employee hired between October 2 of the previous year and September 1 of the current reporting year. The standard limited non-assessment period for full-time employees is three months, plus any first partial month after hire. 2D is the code associated with the limited non-assessment period. The system prioritizes 2D over anything other than 2C. Therefore, a 2D code would be appropriate, and take precedence over anything other than 2C, for the following: • Three consecutive months, starting with the month of hire, for any employee hired on the first of the month; and • Four consecutive months, starting with the month of hire, for any employee not hired on the first of the month.

Chapter 12 Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS The PrismHR system can electronically transmit client ACA returns to the IRS. This process is called E-filing.

Note: If you want to electronically transmit your Forms 1094-C and 1095-C, you must register in the ACA Information Returns (AIR). You can register with the IRS at this link.

These procedures are required for each 1094-C client account that you need to submit:

Step Description Reference 1 After registering with the IRS, enter your TCC in the system. See Setting Up ACA Transmitter Control Information on page 102. 2 Create and send the test files. See Creating the Test Submission on page 104. 3 Once the IRS approves the test submission for the client, See Creating the ACA Transmission File create and submit the transmission files. on page 112. 4 Submit the files to the IRS using their AIR UI Channel. See also AIR Transmission: Uploading the ACA Files on page 116 5 After submitting the files, you will receive a receipt ID from See Entering the IRS Receipt ID on page the IRS that you need to track. 118.

In some circumstances, you might need to correct or replace information: • Corrections: If you need to make adjustments to a client or employee after the IRS accepted the transmission, you can send a correction. See Submitting a Correction on page 120. • Replacements: If the IRS rejected a transmission or submission, you must send a replacement. See Submitting a Replacement on page 123. If you encounter problems, see ACA Transmittal Tips & Tricks on page 125 for suggestions.

Setting Up ACA Transmitter Control Information Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 102 Chapter 12 Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS

Under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) insurance companies, self-insured companies, and large businesses that provide health insurance to their employees must submit information returns to the IRS reporting on the health insurance coverage of each individual. You are required to file electronically if you plan to submit 250 or more returns. You must have a Transmitter Control Code (TCC) to electronically file AIR Forms 1094/1095-B and 1094/1095-C. You can obtain this code during the registration process. Use the ACA Download Master Code form to add your master code to PrismHR.

To download the master code for the Affordable Care Act: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Setup and Global Setup, select ACA Download Master Code. 4. Complete these fields as required:

Reviewing Transmission File History On the Form 1094-C edit form, you can view a list of past transmission files for a specific employee or client, for both the Federal and California downloads.

Reviewing the ACA Transmission File XML Output Open the XML output file in a text editor, like Notepad, and search for the words “Issue”, “Omit”, and “Null”. • If you find “Issue” then there is a data discrepancy on the client side. • If you find “Omit” or “Null” then you need to contact PrismHR Customer Support for assistance.

Checking that the File Size is less than 100 MB The IRS requires that files be smaller than 100 MB. The size of a file is dictated by the number of characters in it, so file size varies based on many different factors. There is no hard and fast rule about the number of records that will cause a file to exceed 100 MB. Internal testing shows that it involves many thousands of employees. You must check the size of the output file to ensure that it is the correct size. If the file is larger than 100 MB, use data from an employee report to complete the From Employee and To Employee fields. See

Using the From Employee and To Employee Fields Use the From Employee and To Employee fields in the ACA Transmission Form only if the output files you created for this client were larger than 100 MB. With these fields, you can specify a range of employee IDs to include in the file. Using some simple math, you can calculate the approximate number of employees you can include on the file based on the size of the original output file, and then use the report output below to adjust your range appropriately.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 114 Chapter 12 Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS

To use the From Employee and To Employee fields:

Step 1: Run the Employee Report, Sorted by ID 1. Select the Employee Name report and set the Primary Sort to Employee ID. 2. Click Run.

Step 2: Use this Information In the Submission Process 1. In the Employee From and Employee To fields, enter the range of employees that will reduce the size of the output file to meet the IRS requirements. For example, if you generated a file for all of the client’s employees and the output file was 150 MB, you can estimate that if you include the first half of the employees from the report in first file and the second half of the employees in the second file, then each of the two output files will be less than 100 MB. 2. Proceed with the remaining steps in the process, then check the size of the output file. If any file exceeds the limit, begin the procedure again and use a more limited range of employees.

AIR Transmission: Uploading the ACA Files Use these instructions as general guidelines for submitting final client information to the IRS. If you submit this file to the state of New Jersey or to Washington, D.C., you must select the NJ State Submission option before you create the file. When you select this option, the system appends a record to the transmission file for every employee who resided in New Jersey or D.C. at some point during the year.

Note: These instructions are not meant to replace the instructions provided by the IRS or your state reporting body. Refer to Section 4 of the Affordable Care Act (ACA) Information Returns (AIR) Submission Composition and Reference Guide, or any documentation provided by your state government.

To submit your ACA transmission files: 1. Log in to the AIR UI Channel (Testing or Production) using the credentials for the Contact or Responsible Official on the AIR TCC Application. 2. Select the organization and click Submit Selected Organization. 3. If prompted, select AATS and click Submit Selected Version. The Affordable Care Act Information Returns page displays. 4. Click Upload ACA Forms. The ACA Transmission File Upload page displays. Use it to upload the Manifest and Form files that you generated for the client. Make sure that these files have the same time stamp and have same names (aside from the prefix), or the IRS will not accept the transmission. 5. Click the Browse button next to the Manifest File field. 6. Find and select the manifest file for the upload. This is the file that begins with the Manifest_ prefix. 7. Click the Browse button next to the Form File field. 8. Select the form file for the upload. It has the same name as the manifest file, only without the prefix. 9. Verify that the information in the ACA Transmission File Upload page is correct.

ACA Transmittal Tips & Tricks Use this information if you need help during the IRS electronic transmission process.

Important: Register Rebuilds Require PrismHR Support If you already submitted an original file and you find that you need to rebuild the 1095-C registers, you must contact PrismHR support! Do not do this without assistance from a representative of the PrismHR Customer Support Team. Rebuilding the 1095-C registers on your own could cause you to lose critical transmission ID data and the IRS will reject your new transmission in that case.

Contacting Support If you need to contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team, please provide this information in your ticket: 1. Take a screenshot of the errors. 2. Click Download and save the error file. 3. Open a support ticket and include the screenshot. 4. When a support representative contacts you, send a secure e-mail containing the files you submitted to the IRS and the detailed download of errors.

Additional Clients Based on client setup, you might need to select additional clients so that you can file your forms correctly with the IRS. Our system creates Form 1094-C and Forms 1095-C at the client level. If you select additional clients, they will all be reported under the Form 1094-C filing of the active client. This includes all employee Forms 1095- C.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 125 Chapter 12 Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS

One possible real-world example is a staffing organization that needs to separate a single company into multiple client accounts.

Keep Transmission IDs and Receipt IDs Make sure you keep a record of each transmission ID and its corresponding receipt ID, when you receive it from the IRS. The system populates the transmission ID on “Edit 1094 Form” (See also Editing Form 1094-C Information on page 46), but you must enter the receipt ID when the IRS sends it to you.

Note: The receipt ID is separate from the submission ID. Make sure you use the receipt ID.

Transmission versus Submission A transmission is an entire file that you transmit to the IRS. The transmission also contains the submission, which is the Form 1094-C record with or without associated Form 1095-C records. At this time, PrismHR supports only one submission per transmission. That means that there will be only one Form 1094-C on each XML file that you create in the system. It is possible that the IRS will reject either the transmission or the submission. • If they reject the transmission, that means that there is something inherently wrong with the file overall. • If they reject the submission, there are some specific issues with the file. When you submit a replacement, you will indicate whether you are replacing a transmission or submission based on the rejection statement from the IRS.

Error in Transmission File Upload If you receive an immediate error upon submission (as shown below), you need to submit another transmission using the same type, whether it was an original, correction, or replacement.

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 126 Chapter 12 Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS

Transmission/Submission Accepted with Errors If a transmission or submission is accepted with errors, you should submit a correction. The IRS will identify the specific items that are in error. For example, they might specify an item in the Form 1094-C or certain Forms 1095-C. Once you make the corrections, submit them: see Submitting a Correction on page 120. If you cannot resolve the problem, submit a ticket to the PrismHR Customer Support Team: to see the information you need to provide so that they can quickly assist you.

Correcting a Correction Consider the following special case: 1. The IRS accepted a transmission, with errors. 2. You submit the correction and the IRS accepts it. 3. Later, you determine that you actually need to make another correction to that record. In this case, when you submit the correction, you need to use the receipt ID for the correction (not receipt ID of the original transmission).

ACA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 127 Chapter 12 Transmitting ACA Data to the IRS

The IRS Rejected My Transmission or Submission If the IRS rejects your original transmission or submission (as in the case below), then you must send another one using the Replacement Submission Type. • Do not use replacement for rejected corrections. See Submitting a Replacement on page 123. • If you are having trouble understanding the issues, see Contacting Support above.

What do the error codes mean? See Appendix A of the AIR Submission Composition and Reference Guide for a list of error codes and descriptions.

Other Common Issues Here are some common issues that can cause the IRS to reject a transmission, or accept it with errors: • Any non-standard punctuation, as well as starting or trailing spaces • A covered individual is listed, but not marked as “covered” for any month • The value in an All 12 months field is different from a setting in any an individual month or months • Invalid Social Security or Employer Identification numbers • Invalid Receipt ID • Incomplete data, such as the information for only the first six months of a year • Sending the same file after it got “through the door” and was rejected (you must send a new one). • Creating the wrong type of file (original, replacement, or correction). If you submit an original and it should be a replacement, the IRS rejects it. • Manually editing a file: the manifest has a checksum and a file size count. If someone manually edits the form file and does not manually edit these, it will not work. • Trying to submit a test file for a client after your TCC code has moved to the IRS Production system. • Attaching the wrong files to send to the IRS, such as the Form file from one ZIP and the Manifest file from another.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 4 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction The SBEA User Guide explains the functions and features related to setting up, processing, and reporting information for compliance with the Small Business Efficiency Act. The guide is divided into two major sections: • System-level Setup – The tasks and steps involved in enabling the SBEA feature set, defining certified PEO employers, and creating and assigning client federal entities. • Other Setup Procedures – Important SBEA-related procedures that do not fit neatly into the system-level setup process. • Reports – Other helpful SBEA-related reports.

SBEA Overview Introduction to Certified PEOs and the Small Business Efficiency Act The IRS provides a voluntary program through which PEOs can apply for certification, under the Tax Increase Prevention Act of 2014. This act includes within it the Small Business Efficiency Act, or SBEA. A certified PEO under this system is called a CPEO. Registering as a CPEO provides additional institutional legitimacy to PEOs by requiring them to: • Maintain a bond with the IRS for the year • Submit annual, independent CPA audits to the IRS • Submit independently certified, quarterly assertions to the IRS demonstrating payment of employment taxes • Pay an annual fee to remain certified The act also provides benefits for both CPEOs and their clients: • Guarantees that PEO clients still qualify for any applicable federal tax credits • Removes any federal payroll tax liability from the PEO’s clients • Guarantees that clients are not double-taxed if they join or leave a CPEO mid-year • Provides the CPEO with a federal tax credit for the SUTA taxes they pay

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 Introduction

SBEA Reporting Requirements Every year, CPEOs must submit two additional forms to the IRS. These forms detail PEO tax liabilities, broken out client by client: • Form 940 Schedule R: specifies federal unemployment tax (FUTA) • Form 941 Schedule R: specifies federal income tax, OASDI (Social Security) tax, and Medicare taxes For more information about these forms, consult this page on the IRS website.

Setting Up SBEA Compliance in PrismHR Before setting up SBEA functionality, make sure you understand the following important concepts and features.

Client Federal Entities The SBEA requires CPEOs to break out federal taxes client by client during IRS reporting. PrismHR provides a number of features to help you comply with these reporting requirements. After completing the setup process, this functionality will be implemented in your system: • Federal taxes are broken out by client. • The gross-to-net calculation on an employee’s payroll voucher uses a new register for limit testing: the Client Federal Entity Tax Register. Originally, the system used employer tax registers during this calculation. In the PrismHR system, a client federal entity (CFE) represents a client of your organization that is included in SBEA reporting. Each client federal entity corresponds to a specific client FEIN used in this reporting. During SBEA setup, the system creates a new CFE ID for each of these clients. During the year, federal taxes accrue on the appropriate Client Federal Entity Tax Registers. Since SBEA-related reports pull data from these registers, you can break out federal taxes client-by-client for IRS reporting.

Overview of SBEA Setup in PrismHR SBEA feature setup is a multi-step process, but PrismHR provides several automated utilities to simplify this process. Refer to the following table and diagram for a high-level overview of the process.

Federal Entity Tax Registers

Using SBEA Features After you run the voucher update utility and rebuild client federal entity tax registers, the system will be ready to process tax information according to SBEA guidelines. During payroll initialization, the system posts the CFE ID and an SBEA wage code to each payroll voucher. It then copies that voucher’s federal tax data to the appropriate client federal entity tax register. Later, when you run SBEA-related reports, PrismHR uses the different CFE IDs to break out this tax data properly.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 Introduction

Important Notice About Enabling SBEA Features Make sure you and your organization understand the implications of enabling the SBEA feature set in the system.

Note: Only perform SBEA setup and client-level Form W-2 processing if your organization has a total understanding of all components of the SBEA features.

• Before enabling the SBEA feature set, and especially before any register rebuild, PrismHR strongly advises that you test everything in a demo environment. • Perform the setup on a “quiet system” (during off-peak use hours). • Setting up SBEA features will transfer accrued federal tax liability from the employer level to “client entity” level. Be extremely cautious if you need to make such a change mid-year. • If you do make a change mid-year, note that your organization must rebuild the client entity registers. Consult PrismHR before making such a change. • Note that inserting any retroactive employer-certified start dates or client entity-certified contract start dates does not adjust payroll data for the year prior to the current date. Your organization must rebuild the register in that instance; be sure that this is what you should to do. • SBEA setup makes no changes to your current billing structure. PrismHR strongly recommends that you use client-level billing in conjunction with your SBEA setup. • If your organization intends to break out Forms W-2 by client entity: • Note that the system separates the forms by entity by employer, displaying the client entity name and FEIN. • If you will use a third-party download or e-File, note that you might need to adjust the files to group together client records across employers or to add some employer indicator to each client entity group.

Form W-2 for SBEA Note: If your organization decides to create Form W-2 files using the setup for certified PEOs, you must contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team and request that your system be enabled for SBEA W-2s.

The Form W-2 features in the system can support SBEA-certified PEOs, breaking out the information by employer and then by client federal entity. They also support internal clients and clients not in a certified relationship, breaking the information out by employer only.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 8 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

Chapter 2 System-Level Setup To use the SBEA features in the system, you must first configure a range of settings. Please note that many of these setup procedures are best performed on days where there is no active payroll, because they impact the behavior of payroll processing.

Enabling the SBEA Feature Set To begin setting up SBEA features in PrismHR, you must enable SBEA functionality on the global level. After enabling these settings, the system adds new fields to the Employer Details form. Use these fields to designate an employer as certified and set up basic SBEA reporting information.

To enable the SBEA features in PrismHR: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Under System|Change, select Global Configuration. 3. Select the Enable SBEA Feature Set option. This turns on the features that support SBEA compliance. 4. Click Save.

Flagging Employers as Certified PEOs After you enable SBEA features, you can designate employers as certified PEOs and specify a range of dates for collecting SBEA-related tax information. After you indicate that an employer is SBEA-certified, you must

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

complete the setup process to run any payrolls that include a client or employee assigned to this employer — either as primary or alternate.

To designate an employer as a CPEO: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Under Employer|Change, select the Employer Details form. 3. Enter the Employer ID. Employer information populates the form. 4. Select Certified PEO. This indicates that the employer is certified as a PEO by the IRS. 5. Enter the Certified Start Date. This is the date the certification went into effect. SBEA tracking begins with payrolls where the pay date is on or after this date. 6. If the certification expires, you can also enter the Certified End Date. 7. Click Save.

Limit Testing on Employer Register After you enable the SBEA feature set, the system automatically performs limit testing using data from the client federal entity tax registers. However, if an employee works for multiple clients under the same employer, the limit testing does not take this into account. Use the Limit Testing on Employer Register field to adjust this behavior so that the system checks the employer register, rather than the client federal entity register, during this testing. Consider the following example: • John Doe works for both Client A and Client B, both under Employer 1. • John’s federal tax cutoff is $7000. • John earns $5000 at Client A and $5000 at Client B. The portion of John’s taxed income will depend on which register the system checks. This depends on how you have set up the system: Employer is Not Marked as a CPEO If Certified PEO is not selected, the system calculates taxes for all $5000 of John’s Client A wages and only $2000 of John’s Client B wages, or $7000 total. This is the correct tax limit. Employer is a CPEO, Limit Testing on Employer Register is Disabled If Certified PEO is selected and Limit Testing on Employer Register is not selected, John pays taxes on all $5000 from both clients. The system does not consider Client B’s wages along with Client A’s wages because they are stored in different client federal entity tax registers. Therefore, the system does not take into account that John has reached his tax limit. Employer is a CPEO and Limit Testing on Employer Register is Enabled If Certified PEO and Limit Testing on Employer Register are both selected, the system calculates taxes for all $5000 of John’s Client A wages and $2000 of John’s Client B wages, or $7000 total, the same as if Certified PEO were not selected.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

Creating Client Federal Entities Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

During first-time SBEA implementation, you can use the SBEA Auto Create Client Federal Entities form to create and assign client federal entity tax registers. This process assigns the “Certified PEO” flag on Employer Details. After this, the system creates and assigns client federal entity IDs to clients. These fields are identical to what is defined under the client ID: name, address, city, state, ZIP code, and FEIN. The client federal entity ID is the same as the client ID.

To create client federal entities: 1. Click Work Centers, then go to Tax > SBEA Processing > Setup > SBEA Auto Create Client Federal Entities. 2. Select an Employer ID (the employer must be a Certified PEO). 3. Enter a Certified Relationship Start Date, which is the date the contract was signed. This controls the SBEA wage code. Wage code A will be on any voucher after this start date. If the date is left blank, Wage code C is used. 4. Click Run. A report displays with the processing steps, number of records created, and the date and time the process ran.

Updating Vouchers with SBEA Information The SBEA Voucher Update Utility takes the federal taxes that were previously tracked and accrued at the employer level and associates them with client federal entities. It adjusts previously processed payroll vouchers by flagging them with the client federal entity ID that the employees worked for. It also marks each voucher with the appropriate SBEA wage code.

Note: Run the SBEA Voucher Update Utility during off hours. Do not rebuild tax registers while processing payroll. This process can take a while. Federal taxes must be associated with the client federal entity to ensure correct client tax Schedule R reporting for SBEA purposes.

Your organization needs to use this utility if: • You did not complete SBEA setup before your certification start date. The most common example is to accommodate a retroactive certification. • You are making adjustments mid-year or backdating start dates.

SBEA Wage Codes Note: If you are not a CPEO, you do not need to worry about SBEA Wage Codes.

The voucher update utility adds two pieces of information to each voucher: client federal entity ID and SBEA wage code. You created and assigned CFE IDs in the previous step. The system determines which wage code to post. There are three options: • A - The client is in a certified relationship with the employer.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

 •   B - The client opts to use the 95% rule for a particular worksite exclusion.
 •   C - The client is not in a certified relationship with the employer.

Checking Voucher Information You can confirm that the utility posted the CFE ID and SBEA wage code to each voucher on the Payroll Voucher form.

To check the SBEA information on a specific payroll voucher: 1. Open the Payroll Voucher form, found under Payroll|View. 2. Enter or select a Voucher Number. The form populates with information. 3. Check the values in the Client Fed. Entity and SBEA Wage Code fields. 4. Repeat for any other vouchers you want to check.

Using the SBEA Voucher Update Utility Use the SBEA Voucher update utility to retroactively add or update the client federal entity ID on the payroll vouchers. You need to run this utility for several different reasons. For example, • When a PEO becomes a certified PEO mid-year and needs to retroactively stamp vouchers. • When the entity ID has been edited on the client details or the client’s worksite location record. This utility provides the capability to restamp the payroll vouchers by client. If the system detects that the client federal entity ID was updated on any vouchers, it displays the following warning message: To ensure accurate tax calculations for subsequent payrolls, you must rebuild your client federal entity tax register under Tax > SBEA Processing > Setup > SBEA Rebuild Client Federal Entity Tax Register.

To use the SBEA Voucher Update Utility: 1. On the Work Center panel, click Tax > SBEA Processing > Setup > SBEA Voucher Update Utility.

About Client Federal Entity Tax Registers Client federal entity tax registers track tax information for a specific federal entity, for SBEA reporting purposes. MasterTax Files Customers who enabled the SBEA feature set can also use the MasterTax PTS and RTS files to report their tax data in accordance with the act. When properly configured, the system will create F codes on the MasterTax reporting files, identifying the federal tax data based on the associated client federal entity.

PTS File The PTS file breaks out federal tax data by client. If the client is associated with multiple CPEO employers, the client will be associated with multiple F codes on the reporting files. This helps to link voucher data based on the common pay agent (the employer).

Important MasterTax Interface Settings • Provide SBEA Payroll Breakout: If this field is enabled, the PTS file will break out the federal tax basis and liability amounts by client federal entity. • Include Certified Relationship Setups: If this field is enabled, the PTS file output will include the 210 (company setup) records that link the client federal entity to the employer. The system creates the 210 record specifically for employers. On the 210 record for each employer, position 45 indicates the EIN Type. When this value is P (as shown below) it indicates that the employer is a common pay parent. • The 9-digit number after the P is the employer FEIN.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

•    Likewise, on the 210 record for the client federal entity (F code), position 45 will be a C, which denotes
     the client as a common pay child. The next 9 digits are the EIN for the associated employer.

Note: In order for the system to associate the 210 records with the F codes, you must enable Send Company Tax Record in PTS File on the MasterTax Interface Parameters. Activating this setting can cause issues in MasterTax if the FEIN and Unemployment ID numbers in PrismHR do not match the FEIN and unemployment IDs in Mastertax. If this describes your situation, PrismHR recommends using the SBEA Relationship file instead of performing company setup on your daily PTS file (see below).

Note: PrismHR is working with MasterTax to support the 940 R; MasterTax does not support the 943 R.

To support the RTS file, you must set your MasterTax RTS version to 36 or higher. see Setting MasterTax Interface Parameters on page 15 for more information.

About the File Effective January 2020, SBEA employers can enable the Build W-2 Records? parameter to break out Form W-2 reporting records on the RTS download. The Build FUTA Exempt records? field can only be used with MasterTax versions 37 and above.

CPEO e-Filing Note: To file your 940/941 Schedule R correctly, MasterTax now requires Federal Withholding and Unemployment tax data at the client level.

To file as a CPEO in MasterTax, you must contact MasterTax Support to verify that you have a MasterTax PEO license. If you do not, you will need to convert your MasterTax license to a MasterTax PEO license. MasterTax will make every attempt to ensure your invoice does not increase as a result of switching to this new license type. Please have the following information ready when you contact MasterTax Support: • Number of Employer/PEO companies • Number of total employees • Number of clients. MasterTax will provide you with the new monthly fee (if it is not the same as your existing monthly fee) and the additional client setup fee associated with adding new clients to MasterTax. The PTS import file creates the requisite client structure within MasterTax. The import assigns new client payroll codes (which begin with the letter F) to existing clients that were previously set up within MasterTax, and creates new companies for clients that have not been set up. A client company record would typically already be set up in MasterTax for any client in a client reporting state. The file will also create the Common Pay Agent link to link the Employer to the Client for Federal tax codes so that when MasterTax creates the 941 Schedule R for the Employer, it will have the appropriate client information. Before importing this file into MasterTax, we strongly recommend reviewing your current configuration within MasterTax by navigating to Company View, selecting a Company, and clicking the FEIN link under the Company tab

Note the following implications of the import: • All new client payroll codes on the file with the same FEIN will link together under a single company record within MasterTax; • This company record will have a Common Pay Agent link to 1 employer; • If a client company with the same FEIN already exists in MasterTax, any new client payroll code(s) with that FEIN will link under this existing client company record; • If a client company with the same FEIN does not already exist in MasterTax, any new client payroll code(s) with that FEIN will create and link under a new client company record.

Important Note About Creating New Clients If your organization has enabled the SBEA feature set, the system automatically creates a client federal entity when users create a new client record, and automatically associates the entity with the new client. If the new client shares an FEIN with an existing client, you must edit the new client record and set it to the same client federal entity ID as the existing client.

Note: The system does not populate the Starting Date in the SBEA Certified Relationship Periods table. Users must manually enter the date on which the client entered into the certified relationship with the employer in the Client Federal Entities form.

Manually Adding Client Federal Entity IDs For each client that is serviced by a certified PEO, your organization must add the federal entity ID to the client record. Please note that you can only enter this information if the employer assigned to the client is marked as a certified PEO in the employer record.

Note: If your organization has just enabled the SBEA feature set, there is a utility to assign client federal entity IDs to all clients. In a system with SBEA features enabled, when a user creates a new client and assigns it to a certified PEO employer, the system automatically creates a client federal entity record and assigns it to the new client.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 26 Chapter 3 Other Setup Procedures

To add a federal entity ID to the client: 1. Open Client|Change > Client Details. 2. Enter the Federal Entity ID in the Contract panel of the Detail tab. 3. Click Save.

Exclude Internal Employees from SBEA Reporting Your organization can exclude clients from SBEA reporting. For example, a PEO can exclude its own internal (or “corporate”) employees. Employees of excluded clients will not appear in any client federal entity register. Note that, on the MasterTax files, employee data for internal clients displays as employer data and also displays on line 13 of Form 941 Schedule R.

To specify the clients to exclude: 1. Open System Parameters from the Back Office menu under System|Change. 2. Open the Actions menu and then select Miscellaneous Parameters. The Miscellaneous Global Parameters form opens. 3. Enter the Internal Client ID for each client used for internal employees. 4. Click Accept. 5. Click Save at the bottom of the main System Parameters form.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 27 Chapter 3 Other Setup Procedures

Tax Limit Basis for Client Billing If your organization uses the SBEA feature set, you must set the PEO tax limit basis to be for the Client, rather than the Employer. This setting impacts client billing. You must also ensure that all clients with a certified PEO employer do not have their tax limit basis override set to Employer.

Setting Up the Tax Limit Basis To set the system-level tax basis: 1. Open System Parameters from the Back Office menu . 2. Select the Actions menu and then select Tax Year Limits. 3. In the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form, set the PEO Tax Basis for the appropriate reporting year to Client. 4. Click Accept. 5. Click Save in System Parameters.

Removing the Client Override To remove the client-level tax limit basis override: 1. Open Client|Change|Client Details. 2. Ensure that you have selected the appropriate client . If not, click the client name that displays above the form and then choose the appropriate client. 3. Select the Other tab. 4. Set Tax Limit Basis to –Select–. 5. Click Save. 6. Repeat steps 2 through 5 for each client you need to edit.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 28 Chapter 3 Other Setup Procedures

SBEA Settings in Worksite Locations There are circumstances where you need to set SBEA information at the worksite level: • A single client might have worksite locations with different Federal Employer Identification Numbers (FEINs) than other worksites. In this case, on the Worksite Locations form, you would assign the client federal entity that has the FEIN associated with that worksite. • Clients can enter into a certified relationship but have one or more worksite locations that do not pass the “85% test”. In this case, you can use the SBEA Ineligibility Periods panel to enter the dates the locations were ineligible. This information is important for your quarterly reporting for Schedule R (Form 941 and Form 940).

To set SBEA information at the worksite level: 1. Open Client|Change > Worksite Locations. 2. Enter the Location Code. 3. Expand the Other Parameters panel. 4. Enter the Federal Entity ID only if the location is a different federal entity than the client. 5. In the SBEA Ineligibility Periods panel, enter the Starting Date and Ending Date of the ineligibility periods when the location did not pass the 85% test for certification under the SBEA. 6. Click Save.

Form W-2 Processing for SBEA There are some special considerations to keep in mind when processing Forms W-2 in an organization that includes one or more SBEA-certified employers. The SBEA is unclear as to how certified PEOs must produce their Forms W-2. PrismHR offers certified PEOs the option to break out Forms W-2 by employer and then by client federal entity, and to report under the client federal entity. Currently, you must contact PrismHR and request that we enable this feature. If your organization is considering this option, contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 29 Chapter 3 Other Setup Procedures

Build W-2s From Client Federal Tax Registers Note: Important! The Form W-2/SBEA breakout feature was designed for a very specific use case that originates from vagueness in IRS reporting guidelines for CPEOs. Only enable this feature if you encounter this use case and need to account for it. If you want to leverage this feature, PrismHR highly recommends performing appropriate testing first, to ensure that it will have no adverse effect on your data in the context of reporting or E-filing. If you need more information, please contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

If your organization is a Certified PEO (CPEO), you can declare the entity under which Forms W-2 and Forms 1099 are processed in PrismHR. Your organization can select the Name, Address, and EIN for the client, employer, or both. These changes reflect on Form W-2 PDF generation, BDS/CIC downloads, printed Forms W-2, and printed Forms 1099.

Note: This functionality only works if SBEA features are enabled.

To build W-2s from client federal tax registers: 1. Open System|Change > Global Configuration from the Back Office menu. 2. Select Build W2s From Client Federal Tax Registers. 3. Click Save.

SBEA User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 30 Chapter 3 Other Setup Procedures

SBEA W2/1099 Name Control Use the Employer Details form to declare the entity under which Forms W-2 and Forms 1099 are processed.

To set up W2/1099 name control: 1. Open Employer|Change > Employer Details from the Back Office menu . 2. In the SBEA W2/1099 Name Control panel: • Enter the appropriate Year. • Select the Name, Address, and EIN you want. These values will display on Forms W-2 and Forms 1099. 3. Click Save.

Viewing the Job Control Status Report When a process is complete, you may have the option to access a Job Control Status report. This report shows the Job Number, the date and time when it started and stopped, and the job status. It also shows the date and time that each step in the process was executed. To open the Job Control Status report, click Report in the message that informs you that processing is complete. You have the following options: • Navigate through multiple pages using arrows to move forward, back, to the beginning, or to the end. • Go directly to a page by typing the page number in the Page box. • Enter search text in the Search box. Click Search Next to find the next occurrence. • In the Actions menu, select Print, Convert to PDF, or Print/PDF Pages. • Click XLS to export the report to Excel format and save it in your Downloads folder.

Form W-2 Reconciliation Report If your organization reports on SBEA-certified employers and files Forms W-2 at the employer level, you might see some unexpected results. This is because, under the SBEA, tax accruals and limits are respected at the client federal entity level. If you create Forms W-2 at the employer level and an employee worked for two clients under the same employer, their data will be combined on a single Form W-2. The W-2 Reconciliation Report enables you to find employees who have Medicare or Social Security taxes greater than expected, based on their taxable amounts.

To run the Form W-2 Reconciliation Report: 1. Open the Work Centers menu and select W-2 Processing under Work Centers|Tax. 2. Under W-2 Reporting, select W-2 Reconciliation Report. 3. Enter the Employer ID. 4. Enter the Tax Year. 5. Click Run. The report generates.

The report displays any employees whose withholdings exceed the limits. Your organization can then determine how best to reconcile the data on those forms.

Running Tax Register Reconciliation Reports Evaluate employee tax registers and identify potential discrepancies between payroll vouchers and tax summaries with the Tax Register Reconciliation Report.

To run a tax register reconciliation report: 1. Click Reports. 2. Under Payroll|Reports, select Tax Register Reconciliation Report. 3. Fill out these fields as required.

 Field                              Description
 Employer ID / Client ID            Enter employer and client IDs to select a set of employees associated with
                                    these entities.
 Year                               Enter the tax year
 From Employee ID / To              Specify a range of employees (by ID) to include in the report.
 Employee ID
  1. Click Run. The report only displays employees with discrepancies between their rebuilt payroll vouchers and employee tax summaries.

Intended Audience This guide is intended for users who need to import data into PrismHR, including file formats and details on specific imports.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool The Data Import Tool lets you upload data and import it into the system. The Data Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back Office menu. For example, the following form displays after you access the Data Import Tool and select the Department Codes import template option:

Note the following: • The list of Import Template options display in alphabetical order. • You can also access the Data Import Tool by selecting its link on the Benefit Imports & Reporting landing page. (You must have either Full or Inquiry access set in your user role for the Data Import Tool (HRPY.WORK*DATABASE.IMPORT.ENTRY). Otherwise, this link does not display.) Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you select the import template that you want on the Data Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields. In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing, whose link resides on the Data Import Tool form, to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type. Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file: • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.”

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

• If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

Using the Sample Header File Before starting the import process, you can first download a sample header file by clicking that link on the Data Import Tool form after selecting an import template option or from a local form that displays the Import icon ( ), such as the Departments form. For example:

Note: The header file is in .csv format. You can save the file in .csv or .txt format. After you click the Download Sample Header File link, the system downloads or prompts for download a sample header file that displays columns and headers that match each column and description for the import template option. Also, the file displays a title that matches the selected option. Note: The sample header file is only available to users who have access to the selected import template option.
