Uploading/Importing a Database File To upload and import a database file in .txt format and import its data, do the following: 1. From the Import Template drop-down menu in the Data Import Tool form, select the template type. 2. At the bottom of the form, click Find File. The Upload a File dialog displays. 3. Click Choose File and browse to the .txt file you want to upload. 4. Click Open. 5. Click Submit.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

If the file uploads successfully, a confirmation message displays. If your file does not upload successfully, an
error message displays. Click Close, then click Clear to try again or to upload a different file.
  1. Click Close to return to the Data Import Tool form, where the file name and the imported content display.
  2. Review the content, and then click Import to complete the process. A confirmation dialog displays to confirm that the file content was successfully imported. If the import process encounters duplicates, a dialog displays stating the data already exists. Click OK. The Import Duplicates form displays. To process the duplicate data, you can either click Skip or Replace with New. If you want to apply the action to all data, select the Apply to all option.

Troubleshooting If errors occur during the import process, do the following: 1. Click OK. 2. Click the Messages tab and review the error messages.

  1. Click Import to proceed. If the import is successful, a confirmation dialog displays.
  2. Click OK to proceed and view the report or click Close to restart the process.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 15 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

Viewing the Report To view the report on the data you uploaded and imported, do the following: Click Report.

The data displays in a report format, which includes the Import Status results. The report (see example below) displays all imported records and includes any records that were skipped.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

When you finish reviewing the report, close the report window and click Clear to upload another file.

Importing ACA Offered Employees You can use this import template to import part-time employees who need to be reported as full-time employees for ACA purposes for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. Note: This import template is only available to service providers.

To upload and import ACA offered employees, do the following: 1. Select Client. 2. From the Client|Change menu, select ACA Offered Employees. The ACA Offered Employees form displays.

  1. On the ACA Offered Employees form, click Import to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Deny.) The ACA Offered Employees import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the ACA Offered Employees form.

    You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) The layout requirements are:

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 17 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data. Category Description • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • Employee ID (required): The ID of the employee who works for the client. • Stability Start Date (required): The Start Date is based on the predefined stability periods for the relevant employee type. • Stability End Date (required): Populates automatically after you select a Start Date. • Type (required): Date that applies to employee holiday time. • ACA Offer Of Coverage (required): Indicates an offer of coverage for eligible employees.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

Note the following when using the ACA Offered Employees import template: • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the ACA Offered Employees form cannot import data using the ACA Offered Employees import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form. • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the ACA Offered Employees form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the ACA Offered Employees form. • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the ACA Offered Employees form can view the ACA Offered Employees import template for Miscellaneous Invoice, but cannot import data. • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data. • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company. • A warning displays if you import an employee who is not a part-time employee, but you can still import that employee. • You can import duplicate part-time employees if they do not have the same dates. For example, if employee ZXY uses the date 1/1/2023, you cannot import that employee using the date 1/1/2023, but you can import employee ZXY using the date 5/1/2023.

Importing Backup Account Assignments You can use the Backup Account Assignment import template to import backup account assignments to reduce the amount of manual work required. Note: This import template is only available to service providers.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

Importing Benefit Adjustments You can import multiple benefit adjustments for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required. Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import benefit adjustments, do the following:

  1. Click (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.
  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Benefit Adjustments import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) The layout requirements are:

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

Field Description Category Description • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employee whose benefit billing record will receive an adjustment. • Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the Benefit Plan that requires an adjustment. • Plan Period (required): The benefit plan period in the format YYYYMM. For example, 202310 for October 2023. • Bill Amount (required): The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of an adjustment. • Employee Contribution: The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount. • Cycles (required): The number of future payroll cycles to apply an adjustment. • Start Date (required): The Start Date of the period when the deduction related to an adjustment goes into effect. • Insurance Cost: The premium cost associated with an adjustment. • Adjustment Amount: The B/R adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of an adjustment. • Retro Enroll: Whether an adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Valid values are Yes or No. • Comments: Descriptive comments about an adjustment.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

Note: Cycles Billed is not a required field anymore for importing Benefit Adjustments. It will automatically be set to 0 when importing Benefit Adjustments.

Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) The layout requirements are:

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 25 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

Field Description Category Description • Bill Date (required): Date on which billing occurs; the system recognizes different formats as long as they are in the order month, day, and year (if no year is specified, the system uses the current year). • Bill Event Code (required): Billing event code. • Bill Rate (required): Billing rates for each billing unit. • Bill Unit (required): Number of billing units. • Client ID (required): ID of the client for this billing line item. • Employee ID (required): ID of the employee associated with the line item, if applicable (must be in the client in the row). (Optional when using Location.) • Location (required): Location code associated with the line item, if applicable. (Optional when using Employee ID.) • Division: Division code associated with the line item, if applicable. • Comment (max 40 characters): Comment for the line item, if appropriate. (Note: If there are more than 40 characters in a comment, an error displays.) • Department: Department code associated with the line item, if applicable. • Shift: Shift code associated with the line item, if applicable. • Project: Project code associated with the line item, if applicable. • Cost: Cost amount can be positive to charge against the line item, or negative to lower the total amount. • Pay Group: Pay group associated with the line item, if applicable (requires a Location for calculating taxes). Note that you cannot have both an employee ID and a pay group in the same file; the system will reject it if you do. • Payroll Type: Indicates the type of payroll, which can be Regularly Scheduled (R), Manual (M), or Special (S). • Repeat Thru Date: Indicates when the recurring event starts and stops. (Use the MM/DD/YYYY date format.) • Repeat Cycle (required if Repeat Thru Date is used): Indicates billing frequency, which can be one of the following:

                                     •   W = Weekly
                                     •   B = Biweekly

Importing Certified Pay Rates for Projects You can import certified pay rates (that is, position code, position title, base rate, fringe rate, and prevailing wage rate) for projects to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To upload and import certified pay rates for projects:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) You can enable one of the following fields during imports: • Keep existing data: Retains existing data during the import and only adds or replaces new certified pay rates included in the file for the project. • Replace existing data: Replaces existing data with data included in the file but does not remove data that is not included in the file (that is, leaves existing data, adds new data, and updates duplicates). For example, a duplicate would be a client ID, project code, and position code that is already listed on the Certified Pay Rates panel on the Projects form. • Remove existing data (default): Removes existing data in the Certified Pay Rates panel on the Projects form that is not included in the file for that client. The layout requirements are:

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Field Description • Based On Item: Additional based-on types to the commission rule at the client level, such as Percent of Bill Code, Profits to Admin, Workers Compensation Profit, Benefit Commission Type, and Benefit Commission Percentage. • Based On Plan: Indicates the ID of the commission plan that exists at the system level. (Cannot be used in conjunction with Amount, Flat or Percent, Based On, and Based on Item.) • Target Amount: Indicates the commission’s target amount, which is used in conjunction with the Percent of Target Amount Based On option. (You can enter up to two decimals in this field. The system truncates values with more than two decimals.) The Target Amount field value is an overall dollar figure the system multiplies by the Amount Percent value to calculate the salesperson’s commission payout amount. For example, a Target Amount set to 100,000 for a 30% of Target Amount Commission setup would pay out $30,000 as the Commission amount for the defined commission period. Required? Importing Client Details Special Delivery Instructions You can import special delivery instructions for clients to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 37 Chapter 1 Using the Data Import Tool

To upload and import client details special delivery instructions, do the following:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.
  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Client Details (Special Delivery). When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) You can enable one of the following fields during imports: • Replace existing data: Replaces existing data with data included in the file but does not remove data that is not included in the file. For example: • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes. • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system keeps the location 2 delivery method data. • Remove existing data (default): Removes existing data that is not included in the file for that client. For example: • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes. • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system removes the location 2 delivery method data. • Keep existing data: Prioritizes keeping existing data and adds new data included in the file. (That is, if data exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.) For example: • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system keeps the existing data, not the data included in the file. • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the location 2 delivery method data remains the same in the system. The layout requirements are:

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Field Description Category Description • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • All Locations: Indicates if special delivery method applies to all locations. • Location Code: Indicates location code for this special delivery. • Company Override Method: Indicates special delivery methods defined in your system. • Days In Transit: Indicates special delivery method’s number of days in transit. • Bill Event Codes: Indicates ID of billing event that the system uses to track this special delivery method. If there is no charge for the special delivery method, leave this field blank. • Special Bill Amt: Indicates override for the standard billing amount for this client. • Create Spec Sheet: Indicates that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. (Do not use this option if a special sheet is not necessary.) • Method Active: Indicates status of this special delivery method. • Method Until: Indicates date when the special delivery method should stop being used for the client. • Special Message: A special message that prints on the special delivery sheet. • Name: Indicates name that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • Address: Indicates address that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • Address 2: Indicates second address line that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • City, State, Zip Code: Indicates city, state, and zip code that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • Delivery Sheet Format: Indicates special delivery sheet format used to ensure that the address on the printed special delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

When this option is checked, the validation logic evaluates any previously identified dependent record not included in the current import file to determine if that dependent record has current coverage or prior coverage history. Additionally, an informational message stating, “Required fields may vary based on client setup for New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides” displays. • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have current coverage or prior coverage history: The record is skipped and the following error message displays: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID [Dependent ID Number] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with it.” A variation of this same message displays when multiple dependent records with current coverage or prior coverage history must be skipped for the same employee: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID’s [Dependent ID Numbers separated by a comma] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with them.” • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have no current coverage or prior coverage history associated with it: The record is deleted. This validation works similar to the validation logic used when you attempt to manually delete a dependent with coverage history from the system. In that instance, a message displays indicating that you cannot delete the record but you can mark it Inactive.

Chapter 2 Performing Employee Fields Import The Employee Fields Import utility imports and updates employee information using a tab-delimited text file or a CSV file into the various tabs and fields of the Employee Details record. There are two sections to this form: Generate Import Spreadsheet and Import Employee Data. Important! This form enforces Client Access Group (CAG) Security. To access this form:

  2. On the Operations|Action menu, select Employee Fields Import to access the fields import utility. The Employee Fields Import form appears. This form includes these features: • Generate Import Spreadsheet: Create an import spreadsheet for later use by saving existing settings and then downloading the spreadsheet. This aids in performing subsequent field updates for your employees. (Understanding Employee Fields Import Workflow.) • Import Employee Data: Import a tab-delimited text or CSV file with updated field information for employees. (Importing Employee Data.)

Translation Tables Use translation tables to convert codes found in the data file to standard action codes that PrismHR software uses. External action codes are located in an external data file, and standard action codes correspond to external action codes. Options include: • Action Translations: Enter action codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard action codes in the next column. • Client Translations: Enter company IDs found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard company IDs in the next column. • Plan Translations: Enter benefit plan codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard benefit plan codes in the next column. • Plan Type Translations: Enter plan type (coverage levels) found in the external data file in this column Enter the corresponding standard plan types in the next column. • Network Translations: Enter network codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard network IDs in the next column. 1. In the Translation Tables dialog box, click Actions. The Benefit Import Actions Translation Table form opens. 2. To indicate the action the system should take for each line of data, enter the External Action Codes found in the data file and the corresponding Standard Action Codes from the following table.

Code Name Description ADD Creates a new benefit enrollment. WAIVE Waives coverage for an existing enrollment. CHANGE Changes the plan type/coverage of an existing enrollment. TERM Terminates an existing enrollment. DEPEN+ Adds a covered dependent to an existing enrollment. You can also use this to add covered dependents to a new enrollment, as long as the new enrollment occurs in the file before the line that adds the dependent. BENEF+ Adds a beneficiary to an existing enrollment. You can also use this to add a beneficiary to a new enrollment, as long as the new enrollment occurs in the file before the line that adds the beneficiary. DEPEN- Removes a covered dependent from an existing enrollment.

TERMHSA Terminates an existing health savings account (HSA) enrollment. CHANGEFSA Changes the plan type/coverage in an existing flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. CHANGEHSA Changes the plan type/coverage in an existing health savings account (HSA) enrollment.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 123 Chapter 8 Importing EEO-1 Data

Chapter 8 Importing EEO-1 Data Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Use the Import EEO-1 Data form to correct any errors that were identified by the Export EEO-1 Data feature. The form also provides some import preferences you can customize.

Note: Use either .txt. or .csv files with this feature. The format of the input file must match the format generated by the EEO-1 data export feature.

File Requirements Note: This form accepts input files that follow the format of the EEO-1 export file. The import will ignore any data in columns to the right of the System column, as these are informational only.

You can import employees who do not already have records in the system. There is a setting on this form that determines whether to include them in the report. See the procedure below for more information. If you want to import data for employees that are not already in the system, you must assign each of these employees a unique ID on the import file. For example, you can use their SSN, a unique number, or some form of their name. This ID will act as their employee ID on the report.

Requirements for the EEO-1 import file: • It can be a .txt file with tab delimiters OR a .csv file. • Employee names must not contain any special characters, such as commas, periods, apostrophes, or quotation marks. • Employee names must be formatted: FirstName MiddleName LastName Suffix. • Give the import file a unique name. • If you are importing employees that are not in the system, give them a unique Employee ID. See the note above.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 124 Chapter 8 Importing EEO-1 Data

Procedure To import EEO-1 data into PrismHR: 1. Open the Work Centers menu and select Work Centers|Compliance > EEO Processing. 2. Under the EEO-1 Report Processing category, select Import EEO-1 Data. 3. The EEO-1 Report As Of Date populates automatically from the EEO-1 configuration. Change this value if necessary. 4. Use the Replace Behavior option to specify how the import process works: • Modify and Replace Existing Data – if data exists in the system for employees listed in the file, PrismHR overwrites that data with the data from the import file. • Clear All Data and Replace – PrismHR deletes all EEO-1 register data for all employees (even employees not listed in the import file) and creates new EEO-1 registers using only data from the import file. 5. Select whether to Import Employees That Are Not in Prism. Otherwise, PrismHR will ignore data for any employees not already in the EEO-1 registers. For details, review the Import File Requirements section, above. 6. In the Import File panel, specify the number of Header Lines to Skip. For example, enter 1 if the import file has header data or labels in the first row. 7. Click Choose File. A new form displays where you can upload the import file. 8. Upload the file and click submit. 9. Click Import Data to run the import. The Job Control form displays the imported employees. 10. After the process completes, select Error Report to review any errors.

Chapter 9 Using the New Employee Import Dashboard (Batch Management) This form is the starting page for the New Employee Import feature. Batch management lets you view past import statistics, download reports or the original import file, and verify what was imported and perform troubleshooting (if required). You launch the New Employee Import wizard from this form. When you initially access this dashboard, it automatically filters imports in progress by your login ID.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the import dashboard:

  1. Click .
  2. From Operations|Action, click New Employee Import to access batch management. Options include: • Imports in Progress: Provides information on multiple import files that have started the import process. • New Import: Click to launch the New Employee Import wizard and access the New Employee Import Setup form. • Past Imports: Provides details on an import, such as the person who initiated the import. Also allows downloads of the original import file. • Import Format Management: Manages code translations and accesses Import Field mappings. See Import Format Management.

Viewing Imports in Progress You can view existing imports that are in progress but not completed. This allows you to continue working on an import from where you last left off. The system supports multiple file imports in progress at a time. The Imports in Progress table includes these columns:

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 126 Chapter 9 Using the New Employee Import Dashboard (Batch Management)

Option Description Filter By User Filters the imports in progress by the specific user that performed the import. You can also select All to display all users. Default setting is the user ID that was used for logging in to the system. If the logged in user does not have any in progress batches, then all batches are displayed. Name Name of the import file. Click the link to open the form that corresponds to where you are in the import process. For example, if you are still fixing import data, the system opens the Review and Fix Data form. Status Current step in the import work flow. Steps are: 1. File Upload 2. Data Mapping 3. Review & Fix Data Status workflow changes operate as follows: • First time through the import, you click Next. The status for the import is updated to reflect the screen that the Next button directs you to. For example, if you go to Data Mapping, this results in a saved step of 2-Data Mapping. • If you return to a previous screen but do not make any changes, your currently saved step will not change. • If you return to the Setup screen and upload a new file or change the field mapping selection and then click Next, the step count resets. • If you return to Data Mapping and change the Code Set selection and then click Next, the system warns you that changes to the translation code set reverts all previously fixed errors. Clicking Yes dismisses the dialog, resets the import using the newly selected code set, and directs you to the Review screen. Clicking No dismisses the dialog and keeps you on Data Mapping. The step is set to 3 - Review and Fix Data. • The Close button has no impact on the status step for the import. Clicking Close on any screen returns you to Batch Management. Last Modified Date Date an import file was last modified. Last Modified User User that modified the import file. Actions Click the trash can icon to delete an import in progress. (Note: This action cannot be reversed.)

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 145 Chapter 13 Importing Employee Tax Basis from Successor

Chapter 13 Importing Employee Tax Basis from Successor Use this process to transfer the employee tax basis to PrismHR for a client that has come on midyear to ensure accurate voucher calculations. This could occur for employees that work for a client reporting SUI state (such as Michigan). It could also occur for certified PEOs that import federal taxes from a successor. If an employee has already reached their tax limit for SUI before being moved to a PEO that uses PrismHR software, then a mechanism is required to import earlier tax data for the employee, or they will start accruing tax again.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To import the tax transfer basis: 1. Format an Excel spreadsheet using this format.

                         Column                Information

                          Col A               Client ID

                          Col B               Employee ID

                          Col C               Employer ID

                          Col D               Tax Year

                          Col E               Reason

                          Col F               Billing Only? (Use only Y, N or S)
                                              Y=Yes, N=No and S=Suppressed for the billing

                          Col G               Tax Code

                          Col H               Tax Basis

                           Col I              Tax Amount

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 146 Chapter 13 Importing Employee Tax Basis from Successor

  1. Save the Excel file as tab-delimited, pipe-delimited, or .csv.

  2. Record the file name and where it was saved.

  3. Click Back Office .

  4. From Operations|Import Processing, click Import Transfer Tax Basis from Successor.

  5. Click Upload File.

  6. Set these optional fields if required: l Delimiter- Separates the data fields in the import .txt file. Let the system determine the delimiter (default, Auto) or set the delimiter to the separator type in the import tile (Comma, Tab, Pipe). l Qualifier- Used in conjunction with delimiters in fields. Qualifiers are placed around each field to indicate that it’s the same field. The most common qualifier is a double quote. Additional options are Auto (default), None, and Single Quote. l First Lines to Skip - Instructs the system to ignore a specific number of lines (column headers) in an import file. The default is 0, and up to 10 lines can be skipped.

  7. Click Upload File. A file upload dialog box displays.

  8. Click Choose File and navigate to the file you created.

  9. Highlight the file name and click Open, then click submit. The system displays a message about whether the file uploaded successfully and how long the upload took.

  10. Click Close. The file contents display as a preview.

  11. Click Import to write values to the appropriate tax registers.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 151 Chapter 14 Using the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool

  1. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.
  2. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.
  3. Click Start Upload to upload the file.
  4. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.
  5. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process. While processing the uploaded file, the following validation occurs: • If any mandatory field is missing from the file, the system displays an error message, “ is a required field.” • If the system does not associate the Employee ID with the From Client field, it displays an error message, “Employee not located in client .” • If the values in the Pay Group, To Retire Plan, To Position, and To Location fields are not valid for the To Client record, then the system displays an error message, “Record . is not on file in <field’s filename>.” • In the Termination Reason field, the system identifies a valid value only if the REASON.CODES contain “Termination.” If you provide any other value, the system displays an error message, “ is not a valid Term Reason Code.”
  6. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR. After the import finishes, the following occurs: • If Transfer YTD Check Stubs is enabled, the program transfers the YTD check stubs. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is enabled, the program terminates the employee on the original client using the corresponding Termination Date and Termination Reason from the upload file. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is disabled, the program does not terminate the employee on the original client. • If Terminate Benefit Coverage Today is enabled, the program terminates the employee’s benefit coverage. • If the uploaded file contains a mix of employees who are successfully validated and employees that fail the validations, those employees that are successfully validated are transferred appropriately and the employees that fail validation are documented in the error log and are not transferred or terminated.
  7. Click Report to view the transaction report. This report contains the following information: • Successfully transferred employees display “Success” in the Import Status column. • Employees that failed validation and could not be transferred display “Skipped” in the Import Status column. The “Comments” column for the failed transfer employees displays the error message for whichever failed validation event prevented the transfer.

Save the Excel file as a comma-separated values (CSV) file or plain text file. 3. Record the file name and where it was saved.

Chapter 16 Managing Batches for Check Import Process Use the Check History Import form for batch management for the check import process. All processes required for check imports can be only accessed from this form using a wizard which takes you step by step through the check import process.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import. Important! If you have employees listed in several clients and employers, you might need to complete a successor wage import before processing a check history import. Note the following instances when you should perform this action: • An employee is listed in the same employer for multiple companies as an active employee: Since this makes a difference for taxes, it affects how the limits are honored. The employee is listed within the same employer, so the system pushes the taxes that were previously processed at the first company to the taxes on this import, so they are over the limit and not including any charges. • An employee is listed in two different employers: The voucher honors the limit for each, so the system does not display any of the taxes over the limit but instead collects those taxes as well. Note: This is typically correct, but if a client only collects the taxes under one employer and the employee is listed in two employers and you do not want to account for taxes under both employers, you can use successor wages to account for those wages. With successor wages in place, the system will not collect taxes under both employers.

Total Net Pay The total check amount contained in the batch. Reports (CSV) You can click the drop-down beside the Download Reports link to display the following links to reports for the corresponding completed Batch ID: • Original Import File - Click this link to download the check import file used for this batch in a .CSV format. If this batch is only for manual check entry where a check import file is not used, this link will remain inactive. • Checks not Imported - This link will only be active if there are checks that have not been imported. The number of checks not imported is displayed here. Click this link to download the Checks not Imported Report in .CSV format. • Voucher Summary Report - Click this link to download the Voucher Summary Report for this batch in a .CSV format. • Total Taxes Report - Click this link to download the Total Taxes Report for this batch in a .CSV format. • Voucher Details Report - Click this link to download the Voucher Details Report for this batch in a .CSV format.

Import Setup This is the first screen of the check import wizard. Use this form to set up a batch for the check import process or update an existing check import batch. • The Import Setup option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. • You can only access this screen from the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen. • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function. • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To create or edit a check import batch, complete the following: 1. Under the Import Batch Setup section, you can either create a new check import batch or Copy Existing Import batch which would copy all the Code Mapping as well as the FICA & FUTA conditions of that batch on to this screen. a. To copy from an existing check import batch, click Copy Existing Import. Select the Batch ID you want to copy from in the Select Import Batch dialog box. Click OK to close the dialog box. b. Batch ID - This field is read only: i. This field will by default show NEW if you come to this screen by clicking New Import on the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen. When you proceed to the State & Code Setup screen in this case, a new Batch ID will be generated.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 164 Chapter 16 Managing Batches for Check Import Process

     ii. To edit an existing check import batch in progress, click the Batch ID link on the Managing Batches
         for Check Import Process screen. The Batch ID will show here. You cannot edit the Batch ID. When
         you proceed to the State & Code Setup screen in this case, the Batch ID will remain the same.
     iii. You can click Previous on the State & Code Setup screen to come back to this screen to edit an
          existing check import batch. The Batch ID will show here. You cannot edit the Batch ID. After editing
          the check import batch when you proceed to the State & Code Setup screen, the Batch ID will
          remain the same.
c. Batch Name - The name for this batch:
     i.   If you are creating a new check import batch, then enter the name for this batch here.
     ii. If you are editing an existing check import batch, then edit the name of the check import batch here.
d. Client ID - The client ID for whom checks will be imported in this batch:
     i.   If you are creating a new check import batch, then enter the Client ID here, or click the Client ID link
          and select the Client from the Select Client dialog box.
     ii. If you are editing an existing check import batch, then edit the Client ID here, or click the Client ID
         link and select the correct Client from the Select Client dialog box.
     iii. If you enter or select more than one Client ID a warning displays, "Clients with different taxation
          rules should have their own check history import batch." Click OK to continue.
  1. Under the FICA & FUTA section, complete the following fields:
    1. If Medicare tax amounts are zero, select one of the following:
      1. Include Medicare taxable amounts on vouchers - This is the default option where Employer paid Medicare taxable amounts are included on all vouchers in this check import batch.
      2. Do not include - Select this option if you do not want to include Employer paid Medicare taxable amounts included on all vouchers in this check import batch.
    2. If OASDI tax amounts are zero, select one of the following:
      1. Include OASDI taxable amounts on the vouchers - This is the default option where Employer paid OASDI taxable amounts are included on all vouchers in this check import batch.
      2. Do not include - Select this option if you do not want to include Employer paid OASDI taxable amounts included on all vouchers in this check import batch.
    3. Employer FUTA (Tax Code 00-17), select one the of the following:
      1. Include - By default, calculation of employer FUTA tax is included on all vouchers in this batch.
      2. Suppress - Select this option if you want to suppress the calculation of the employer FUTA tax on all vouchers in this batch.
  2. Under the Upload File section complete the following if you want to upload the checks from a file. Skip this section if you only want to enter check history manually.
    1. Click Upload File to upload a check import batch file in a .txt or .csv format. A dialog box opens.
    2. Click Choose File to select the check import batch file from your system in a .txt or .csv format.

Note: When importing a .csv file, you do not need to remove the headers.

Click Next to save all changes made to this screen and go to the State & Code Setup screen. • If no file has been uploaded, then the State & Code Setup screen appears. • If you have already uploaded a file to import from, then a job progress window opens. The system starts to load the State Tax Rules from the default for the states included in the import file and the imported code setup from the imported spreadsheet. • Click Close once the process is complete to go to the State & Code Setup screen.

Warning - Uploading a replacement Check History Import file You may need to upload a replacement check history import file if you have imported a wrong check history import file or the check history import file is badly formatted and so on. If you try to upload a new check history import file when a check history import file has already been uploaded using the import utility, and to prevent unexpected data loss, you will receive the following pop-up message: Checks have already been imported from a file. If you proceed, the previous imported checks will be cleared and you will lose any corrections you have made. Manually entered checks will be retained. Do you want to clear the existing imported checks and start over? • Click Yes to upload a new check history import file. The file upload pop-up appears. • Existing checks uploaded earlier using the import utility are not cleared until you select the replacement check history import file and click Next. • Checks that were entered manually will be retained.

File Audit From this Import Batch Setup screen, you can click the Actions menu and select the Audit option to show the Audit Log Display. You can view the logs for all the changes made for this Batch ID.

Check Import Batch Status Report This report displays the summary information for all check import batches.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on the Check History Import Batch Status Report form.

To access the form, on the Back Office menu, under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import Batch Status Report. You can also access this menu from the Check History Import form. On the Back Office menu, under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import. Click Batch Status Report in the Tools section on the top right.

To generate a summary of all check import batches: 1. Select a Batch Type:

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 172 Chapter 16 Managing Batches for Check Import Process

     •    All
     •    Completed
     •    In Progress
2. Click Generate Report. The Check Import Batch Status Report opens in a new window.
3. Click the XLS link to download the report.

Note the following: • If you select All in the Batch Types field, the report displays all check history import batches under any status (including In Progress and Completed), sorted by Batch ID. For check history import batches created in PrismHR the following batch statuses are available: • 1 - Import Setup • 2 - State & Code Setup • 3 - Enter Check History • 4 - Review & Fix Data • 5 - Calculate Taxes • 6 - Import Complete • If you select Completed under Batch Type, the report displays all completed check history import batches from PrismHR, sorted by Batch ID. • If you select In Progress under Batch Type, the report displays all check history import batches from PrismHR that are in progress, sorted by Batch ID.

Report Output This report contains the following columns:

Column Name Column Description Batch ID This is the check history import batch number. Batch Name This is the name of the check history import batch. Created In The application where this check history import batch is created. Batch Status The status of this check history import batch. Client ID The client ID (or multiple IDs) for whom the check history import batch is created. Note: The space limitations in this column truncate multiple IDs. Download this report to ensure you can view all IDs included in this column. Status Date The date on which this check history import batch was last processed. Processed By User ID The user ID of the person who last processed this check history import batch.

State & Code Setup This is the second screen of the check import wizard. Use this form to set up the State Tax Rules for the selected check import batch and Code Translation Tables for Earnings, Deductions and Taxes for the check import batch selected in the Import Setup screen. Note the following: • The State & Code Setup option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. • You can only access this screen when you click Next on the Import Setup screen. • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function. • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

This form has the following two sections: • State Tax Rules • Code Mapping

Setting Up State Tax Rules You will need to have state tax rules setup for each state that appears in your imported data either using the check import utility or manual check entry. You can set up the state tax rules for each state from the State Tax Processing Rules link under Tools section in the Check History Import form. If the rules are not set correctly for any of the states that appear in your imported data, you will see errors/discrepacies later in the workflow.

To set up the State Tax Rules for the selected check import batch: 1. If you are importing checks from an import file, then the system will automatically load the default State Tax Rules for all the states contained in the imported spreadsheet. This will ensure that you can set up all the required state tax codes correctly to prevent future errors. The following fields appear in an inline grid along with the values imported for each field: • State - all the states codes contained in the original import file are listed here.

•    State Income Tax Shelter Flag
•    SUTA Shelter Flag

•    Employee SDI Shelter Flag
•    Employee SDI Taxable Limit
•    Employer SDI Taxable Limit
•    Employer SDI Tax Rate (%)
•    Misc Employer State Taxes

You can click a state link above to open the State Tax Rules form for the state in a modal. • The Rule Type section will not be visible. • The Rule Type will be set to Batch as you are accessing this form while processing this check import batch. • The Batch ID will be pre-populated which you cannot change. • The corresponding Batch Name will be displayed. • The Batch Status will display State & Code Setup which is the screen from where you are accessing the State Tax Rules form. • You can edit all the fields on this State Tax Rules form including the State Code. You cannot save this form unless a State Code is selected. • Click Save to save the changes and you will return to the State Tax Rules Section. The changed values will reflect on the inline grid. • Click Delete to delete the state tax rules for the selected state. • Click Cancel to close the form. All changes will be lost. • Click Close to close the form. Changes are saved and reflect in the inline grid.

  3. Click Copy State to Default to copy the state tax rules for this batch to the default state tax rules.

Setting Up Code Mapping For each code that appears in the import spreadsheet, choose the corresponding code in your PrismHR system. Make sure to choose codes with the same tax- settings, or the totals will not match.

If you are importing from a file, then the system will load the codes for Earnings, Deductions and Taxes from the imported spreadsheet. If the imported codes are already contained in your PrismHR code translation tables, they will also reflect in the appropriate table. If not then you will need to manually provide the PrismHR code so

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 175 Chapter 16 Managing Batches for Check Import Process

that the system can calculate the Earnings, Deductions, and Taxes appropriately. As you already get to see the number of foreign codes that you need to translate (if any), the chances of getting errors is reduced and you can complete the process faster.

Earnings

To map the Imported Pay Codes, complete the following: a. Enter the corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Imported Pay Code OR b. Click the Map to Prism Pay Code link and search from the Select Pay Code dialog box. c. Check the Pay Code Description to confirm that you have selected the correct Prism Pay Code for the corresponding Imported Pay Code. d. In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Imported Pay Code from the Select Pay Code dialog box.

Deductions

To map the Imported Deduction Codes, complete the following: a. Enter the corresponding Prism Deduction Code for the Imported Deduction Code OR b. Click the Map to Prism Deduction Code link and search from the Select Deduction Code dialog box. c. Check the Deduction Code Description and the Deduction Type to confirm that you have selected the correct Prism Deduction Code for the corresponding Imported Deduction Code. d. In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Deduction Code for the Imported Deduction Code from the Select Deduction Code dialog box.

Taxes

To map the Imported Tax Codes, complete the following: a. Enter the corresponding Prism Tax Code for the Imported Deduction Code OR b. Click the Map to Prism Deduction Code link and search from the Select Deduction Code dialog box. You can use the Paid By filter to narrow down your search for the correct Prism Tax Code. c. Check the Tax Code Description to confirm that it is the correct Prism Tax Code for the corresponding Imported Tax Code. d. In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Tax Code for the Imported Tax Code from the Select Tax Deduction Code dialog box. e. You have the option to select if the Prism Tax Code selected is Sheltered or not from the drop-down under the Sheltered? column.

Enter Check History This is the third screen of the check import wizard. Use this screen to manually enter a check. Skip this step if you do not need to enter checks manually. If you previously manually entered checks for this check import batch, they display on this screen in an inline grid. Review & Fix Data This is the fourth screen of the check import wizard. Use this screen to review the check history and make corrections. Both imported or manually created checks are listed on this screen. • The Review & Fix Data option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. • You can access this screen from the Enter Check History screen or from the Calculate Taxes screen. • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function. • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

This screen has the following sections: 1. The first section gives a summary count of this check import batch. It shows the following: • The total number of checks in this import batch. • The total number of errors that need to be fixed before you can complete this check import batch. As you fix the number of errors, this count will reduce unless the fix has not generated further errors. • The total number of warnings that need to be fixed before you can complete this check import batch. As you fix the number of warnings, this count will reduce unless the fix has not generated further warnings. • As you fix the errors/warnings, it shows the number of errors/warnings fixed for this check import batch. • The total number of checks in this check import batch that will not be imported. 2. The second section gives the totals for this check import batch for the following parameters: • Total Hours • Total Gross Pay

• The Calculate Taxes option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. • You can only access this screen from the Review & Fix Data screen. • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function. • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites. • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

You must run the Calculate Taxable Earnings & Create Vouchers process.”

To calculate taxable earnings and create payroll vouchers, complete the following: 1. Click Calculate Taxable Earnings & Create Vouchers. A job progress window appears showing the processing. The system first calculates taxable earnings and then creates payroll vouchers. a. If payroll vouchers have already been created for this check import batch a pop-up message displays, Payroll vouchers have already been created for this batch. Do you want to delete them and create new payroll vouchers? i. Click OK if you want to delete the existing payroll vouchers of this check import batch and create new ones. ii. Click Cancel if you do not want to delete the existing payroll vouchers of this check import batch. b. If the system finds any errors on either process, it will show up on the job progress window. i. Click Close to close the job progress window. A pop-up message confirms that The Create Payroll Vouchers process completed with errors. Click OK to proceed. ii. Click Error Report to view the Error Report for Create Payroll Vouchers Process for this check import batch on screen. Click the XLS link to download this error report to your system to review and make the necessary adjustments.

Note: The Error Report button only displays if errors are found while running these processes.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 192 Chapter 17 Importing Tax Register Adjustments

Chapter 17 Importing Tax Register Adjustments Tax registers contain a running total of amounts deducted from employee paychecks or contributed by their employer. You can process tax adjustments when required such as when an employee has an incorrectly assigned withholding tax. Proceed carefully with the tax adjustment process. When you process a tax register adjustment, you are changing the only record of taxes withheld for employees in the system.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

This procedure describes how to import an Employee or Payroll Tax Adjustment into PrismHR. Information is also provided to view the appropriate voucher once the tax adjustment import has occurred. The steps involved are: • Creating a Spreadsheet • Importing the Tax Adjustment • Verifying Imported Tax Information Important! The import process does not currently support billing, so you must leave the Suppress Billing column blank in the import file or use “Y” in that column.

Creating a Spreadsheet To create this spreadsheet: 1. Create an Excel Spreadsheet with this tax import information. Remove any commas or headers in your data to avoid tax adjustment import problems.

 Column                        Information
 Col A                         Company ID
 Col B                         Employee ID
 Col C                         Adjustment Date (MM/DD/YYYY)
 Col D                         Employer ID

Importing Tax Adjustments To import tax adjustment information: 1. Select Tax Adjustment Import from the Payroll|Change menu. The Tax Adjustment Import form displays. 2. Set these optional fields to match the contents of your import file: • Delimiter: Separates the data fields in the import .txt file. Let the system determine the delimiter (default, Auto) or set the delimiter to the separator type in the import tile (Comma, Tab, Pipe). • Qualifier: Used in conjunction with delimiters in fields. Qualifiers are placed around each field to indicate that it’s the same field. The most common qualifier is a double quote. Additional options are Auto (default), None, and Single Quote. • First Lines to Skip: Instructs the system to ignore a specific number of lines (column headers) in an import file. The default is zero (0), and up to 10 lines can be skipped. 3. Click Upload File. A file upload dialog box displays. 4. Click Choose File and navigate to the file you created. 5. Highlight the file name and click Open, then click submit. The system displays whether the file uploaded successfully and how long the upload took. 6. Click Close. Chapter 18 Importing the Data File If a client is set to use a time sheet import on the Client Details Time Sheet tab, use Time Sheet Import to import the data file.

To import the data file, do the following:

  1. In the Time Sheet Entry form, click Time Sheet Import . The Time Sheet Import form opens.
  2. Select the Payroll Number. The Pay Groups information displays.
  3. If there is more than one time sheet import definition for the client, select the one you want to use from the Import Definition ID drop-down.
  4. Enable the Use Import for Hours Worked and Employee Default Hours for Hours Paid field to populate the employee’s default hours (not standard hours) on the timesheet. Note: This field only displays if you enable the TS-LOAD.HRS.WORKED (Global) or TS-LOAD.HRS.WORKED-C (Client) custom feature code on the System Parameters form.
  5. Click Start Import. The Upload File window opens.
  6. Click Choose File. Navigate to the location of the file, select it, and then click Open.
  7. Click Submit. When the file upload completes, a confirmation message appears.
  8. Click Close. You return to the Time Sheet Import form.
  9. If there were any errors, they display in the Error Report. For example, if an employee has hours allocated to a charge date that occurs prior to the employee’s hire date, a warning message displays.
  10. Click Review to look at the imported data. If there is more than one page, use the Previous Page and Next Page buttons to navigate the imported time sheet data.
  11. If the data is accurate, click Post Data to Time Sheets. The system processes the data and creates the time sheets.
  12. Click OK in the confirmation message.
  13. If there were any errors, they display in the Error Report, which you can print.
  14. Click Edit Time Sheets. You return to the Time Sheet Entry form, where you can proceed to the next step of the process.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 198 Chapter 19 Uploading Multiple Documents

Chapter 19 Uploading Multiple Documents Using .ZIP file format, you can upload multiple documents to the Document Repository. Documents can include logos and other images, PDF files, spreadsheets, and other types of files.

Creating the .ZIP File For bulk uploads, construct .ZIP files exactly as follows. Any variation causes the upload to fail. • Use PKZIP or the Compressed (zipped) folder option in Windows Explorer to create a .ZIP file that contains the documents for bulk upload. • Do not use any implementation-specific features or the file does not extract correctly. • Encryption, passwords, or other security measures are not supported, and cause the upload to fail. • Arrange the folders and files in the .zip file following the directory structure, with three sub-folders (client, employee, public) contained in the root folder. Files placed in the root directory (that is, outside the sub-folders shown) and files placed in any other sub-folders are not supported and cause the upload to fail. Directory names must be in lowercase.

Sub-folder Description client Files in this folder are restricted by Client ID after upload in the Document Repository. • The folder name and all sub-folder names must be in lowercase (client). • The client folder must contain one sub-folder per client, with the folder name set to match the Client ID (including any leading zeroes). For example, if the Client ID is 1908, the sub-folder for that client must be named 1908. • The client documents should be placed inside the client sub-folder. No additional sub-folders are permitted.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 199 Chapter 19 Uploading Multiple Documents

Sub-folder Description employee Files in this folder are restricted by Client ID and Employee ID after upload in the Document Repository. • The folder name and all sub-folder names must be in lowercase, for example (employee). • The employee folder must contain one sub-folder per client, with the folder name set to match the Client ID (including any leading zeroes). For example, if the Client ID is 1908, the sub-folder for that client must be named 1908. • Each client sub-folder must contain one sub-folder per Employee ID, with the folder name set to match the Employee ID. For example, if the Employee ID is 22386, the employee sub-folder must be named 22386. • The files should be placed inside the employee sub-folder. No additional sub-folders are permitted. public Files in this folder are imported with no security restrictions, and are viewable by everyone after upload in the Document Repository. • The folder name must be in lowercase (public). • All files must be placed within the public sub-folder. No additional sub- folders are permitted.

Uploading the .ZIP File To upload the .ZIP file: 1. Click (Back Office).

  1. From System|Change, select Document Repository.
  2. Click Bulk Upload (Zip). The Upload window opens.
  3. Click Choose File and select the .ZIP file to upload.
  4. Click Submit. After the upload completes, the system automatically extracts the documents, stores them in the Document Repository, and generates a metadata.csv file. You can review for errors and edit as needed, with the following restrictions: • Do not change the value in the first column (uuid).. The system uses this value to locate the files in the document repository. Do not remove the first row containing the column headings. • The columns userClassification, label, description, and version are strings and are always treated as a single value. • Classification labels must match the classifications in the Document Repository. • To avoid processing errors, do not use quotation marks inside any of the column values.

Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 200 Chapter 19 Uploading Multiple Documents

•    In the userTags column, specify multiple tags by separating them with a comma.
  1. Import the metadata.csv file back into PrismHR using the Metadata Import Entry Form to complete the upload process.

Importing the metadata.csv File To import the metadata.csv file into PrismHR, use the Metadata Import Entry form, located in the Back office menu under System > Action. The metadata.csv file is generated when you upload multiple files to the Document Repository using the bulk upload. This is the final step in uploading multiple files to the Document Repository. You must complete it for the files the files to display correctly.

To import the metadata.csv file into PrismHR: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Action, select Metadata Import Entry. 3. Click Start Import. The Upload window opens. 4. Click Choose File, and select the file to upload. 5. Click Submit. The imported data displays. If the file contains invalid information, the system displays an error. • To view the data, click Done with Errors • To scroll through the report, click Next Page and Previous Page. • To discard the data, click Cancel. 6. Click Post Data to complete the import.

This affects employees who were terminated and re-hired. They need to be paid but have not yet been re- hired in the system. Import Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 212 Chapter 24 Managing Batches for Check Import Process

Chapter 24 Managing Batches for Check Import Process Use the Check History Import form for batch management for the check import process. All processes required for check imports can be only accessed from this form using a wizard which takes you step by step through the check import process.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import. Important! If you have employees listed in several clients and employers, you might need to complete a successor wage import before processing a check history import. Note the following instances when you should perform this action: • An employee is listed in the same employer for multiple companies as an active employee: Since this makes a difference for taxes, it affects how the limits are honored. The employee is listed within the same employer, so the system pushes the taxes that were previously processed at the first company to the taxes on this import, so they are over the limit and not including any charges. • An employee is listed in two different employers: The voucher honors the limit for each, so the system does not display any of the taxes over the limit but instead collects those taxes as well. Note: This is typically correct, but if a client only collects the taxes under one employer and the employee is listed in two employers and you do not want to account for taxes under both employers, you can use successor wages to account for those wages. With successor wages in place, the system will not collect taxes under both employers.

          completing a successful check import. The template contains two header rows.
          •    COLUMN HEADER
          •    REQUIRED/OPTIONAL

If you use our template, you do not need to delete these headers noted above when saving your file for imports. Our system will automatically detect the headers to ensure data integrity.
