New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 4 New Employee Import User Guide

Intended Audience This guide is intended for users who are involved in client and employee administration. Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot view them or make changes. To effectively use this guide, you must also have background knowledge of systems, payroll, benefits, and human resources.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview The New Employee (New Hire) Import feature provides a bulk import process that loads new employee data from a third party source into PrismHR. You are guided through the import process with an Import Wizard that leads you through the steps required to bring in your data.

Employee Import Workflow The new hire workflow operates like this: 1. The Service Provider (SP) receives new hire data from one of their clients. 2. The SP creates an import batch for a specific client. Data translation and file settings required for the import are assigned to the batch. 3. The SP uploads an import file (CSV or tab-delimited) with column headers. The only format you can import without column headers is one that matches the HRP-Expanded-TXT field mapping. 4. The SP confirms that data is mapped correctly between their data and PrismHR data. This data is mainly used for user-defined import templates. 5. Employee data is staged in a temporary work directory. 6. The SP is directed to the Review & Fix Data (Screen 3) form where they can make changes on the fly, which eliminates the need to adjust and re-import the file. 7. Employee data is converted and brought into the system.

New Employee Import Screens The forms used for New Employee Import include: • New Employee Import Dashboard - The entry point for the New Employee Import wizard. You can view import batches in progress as well as past imports that were completed successfully. Data Translations translate third-party codes into PrismHR codes set up in the system. Import Field Mapping creates custom templates for commonly imported file types.

Note: You do not need to use Data Translations unless the codes contained in the import file do not match the current codes set up for the client. The STD set is selected by default, but it does not contain any custom translations unless it is added by you (the SP).

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

• Import Setup - On Screen 1, you create the batch import name, apply the import field mapping, and upload the file you are importing. You can then see whether there are errors associated with the imported file. The application will let you know if the selected field mapping does not match the uploaded file, and if a field mapping exists that does match, the system will alert you. • Data Mapping - Screen 2 displays results of the import field mapping selected from imported data. It helps validate that the correct information was uploaded and the right settings were applied in Screen 1 of the Import Wizard. If required, select a Translation Code Set to translate any codes in the imported file to codes set up in the system. • Review & Fix Data - Screen 3 displays imported and translated employee data that you can edit directly in each cell of the data mapping table. Only the columns that contain errors are displayed. You can add new codes for: Department, Division, Position, Project, Shift Code, Work Group, and Worksite Location. • Import Complete - Screen 4 shows a summary of the employees loaded into the system and assigned either Employee IDs or prehire records that are created for OB.

Import Wizard Steps Indicator The Import Wizard Steps indicator helps you understand where you are in the import process. You can view how many more steps are required and also displays where you are when returning to a saved step. There are four steps in the wizard that appear across the top of the New Import dashboard. The active step in the import process is highlighted and the text is bold. For example, Data Mapping is the active step.

You can return to the previous step from Data Mapping and Review & Fix Data steps by clicking Previous. For example, you may need to go back to a previous step in the import process to change a parameter or to correct issues in the original import file by uploading a revised file. For convenience, the name of the import you are working with is shown on each screen of the process (Screens 2, 3, and 4).

When returning to the Import Setup step, the Import Name is read-only. You can change the Field Mapping selection or upload a new file. When you click Upload File you are notified that this action cannot be undone and are prompted for confirmation. Uploading a new file wipes all data associated with the import and restarts the import process.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

Using the New Employee Import Dashboard (Batch Management) This form is the starting page for the New Employee Import feature. Batch management lets you view past import statistics, download reports or the original import file, and verify what was imported and perform troubleshooting (if required). You launch the New Employee Import wizard from this form. When you initially access this dashboard, it automatically filters imports in progress by your login ID.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the import dashboard:

  1. Click .
  2. From Operations|Action, click New Employee Import to access batch management. Options include: • Imports in Progress: Provides information on multiple import files that have started the import process. • New Import: Click to launch the New Employee Import wizard and access the Setting Up the New Employee Import (page 17) form. • Past Imports: Provides details on an import, such as the person who initiated the import. Also allows downloads of the original import file. • Import Format Management: Manages code translations and accesses Import Field mappings. See Managing Code Translations and Import Field Mappings

Viewing Imports in Progress You can view existing imports that are in progress but not completed. This allows you to continue working on an import from where you last left off. The system supports multiple file imports in progress at a time. The Imports in Progress table includes these columns:

Option Description Filter By User Filters the imports in progress by the specific user that performed the import. You can also select All to display all users. Default setting is the user ID that was used for logging in to the system. If the logged in user does not have any in progress batches, then all batches are displayed. Name Name of the import file. Click the link to open the form that corresponds to where you are in the import process. For example, if you are still fixing import data, the system opens the Review and Fix Data form.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 8 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

Option Description Status Current step in the import work flow. Steps are: 1. File Upload 2. Data Mapping 3. Review & Fix Data Status workflow changes operate as follows: • First time through the import, you click Next. The status for the import is updated to reflect the screen that the Next button directs you to. For example, if you go to Data Mapping, this results in a saved step of 2-Data Mapping. • If you return to a previous screen but do not make any changes, your currently saved step will not change. • If you return to the Setup screen and upload a new file or change the field mapping selection and then click Next, the step count resets. • If you return to Data Mapping and change the Code Set selection and then click Next, the system warns you that changes to the translation code set reverts all previously fixed errors. Clicking Yes dismisses the dialog, resets the import using the newly selected code set, and directs you to the Review screen. Clicking No dismisses the dialog and keeps you on Data Mapping. The step is set to 3 - Review and Fix Data. • The Close button has no impact on the status step for the import. Clicking Close on any screen returns you to Batch Management. Last Modified Date Date an import file was last modified. Last Modified User User that modified the import file. Actions Click the trash can icon to delete an import in progress. (Note: This action cannot be reversed.)

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

Viewing Past Imports Past imports provides a status on import files that have successfully completed the import process. Fields include:

Field Description Date From / To Specifies the date range for past imports. Select a start and end date from the calendar selector. This range defaults to the last 30 days, including the current date. If the date range is invalid, the system displays an error message. Name Name of the report. Click the link to download the report. Date Completed The date when the import was successfully completed. Processed by User Name of the user that submitted the import. Number of Employees Number of employees successfully imported and converted. This value does not include employees that were manually or automatically removed from the import. Note: If an employee is hired into a worksite location that has an override work geocode setting in place, that setting will flow through to the Tax Geocode Override Option field on the employee record. Employees Not Included Employees that were excluded from the import because of file errors or because they are still in onboarding. Original Import File Click the link to download the original import file.

Note: You must have permission to access specific clients in past imports, or you will not be able to import data into these client import files.

Managing Code Translations and Import Field Mappings You can use the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form to manage code translations and Import Field mappings.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Code Translation Tables Code set selections are made with Code Translation Tables. You can create, modify, or clone translation code sets; you can also make code sets obsolete. Code translation sets convert existing code values in the file to the codes that are created for the client within PrismHR.

Note: You do not have to enter translated codes if they exactly match the codes within PrismHR.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

To create a new code set: 1. From the New Employee Import form, select Code Translation Tables to open the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form. 2. Select a Table. These are the code translation tables used by this process: • Client Master • Division • Department • Employee Status Codes • Employee Term Reasons • Employee Type Codes • Employer Master • Ethnic Codes • Position Codes • Location Codes • Project Codes • Shift • Pay Group • Citizenship Status • I9 Identification Document • I9 Eligibility Document • 2nd Form I-9 ID Document • 3rd Form I-9 ID Document 3. Enter a title for the new code set. 4. Enter an imported code and a PrismHR code. 5. Click Save for each table you add codes to (before switching to a different table). If you try to close the window without saving, the system warns you about unsaved changes.

Note: You do not need to set up any code translations for a client as the values can be edited on Screen 3. You would need a code translation set created only for values on the file that cannot be selected from existing records in PrismHR.

To manage existing code sets: 1. Select Code Translation Tables to open the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form. 2. Select a Table.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

  1. Click the Code Set link to open the Select Translation Table Code Set list and select a code set. Available code sets display in the form (the STD code set is always available). You can narrow the search by entering a keyword or filter by code set status (that is, All, Active, Obsolete). Reset the search field and filters if needed to start a new search. Note that code sets can specify translation values across all available tables.
  2. Optional: Add an Imported Code and PrismHR code to the list.
  3. After a code set and table are selected, the system displays Imported Codes on the left and equivalent PrismHR Codes on the right. You have these options: • Save: You can save a new code set, or save changes made to an existing code set. • Clone: Save changes to an existing code set and create a new code set. Name the new code set in the Code Set field. If a code already exists with that name, the system warns you with an error message. • Make Obsolete: Click to make the existing code set obsolete. You cannot perform this action on the STD code set. Imports in progress are able to use an obsolete code set if this code set was selected before it was made obsolete. If a code set is marked Obsolete, you cannot choose this value on the Apply Translation Code Set field on the Data Mapping screen. • Reactivate: This icon displays when you load an obsolete code set and you want to reactivate the code set. • Close: If changes are unsaved when you click Close, the system asks if you still want to close the window. Click Yes to delete unsaved changes and return to Batch Management, or click No to stay on the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form.

Creating and Editing Import Mappings Use the Import Field Mapping form to create or edit import mappings and map codes from your spreadsheet to PrismHR codes.

To access this form: From the Batch Management form, click Import Field Mapping (under Import Format Management). Or, from the Back Office menu, navigate to Operations|Action and click Import Field Mapping.

Autodetect From File File auto-detection provides a way to upload a sample file in the desired format (.csv or .txt) so the system can automatically detect how the file is set up.

Note: PrismHR recommends uploading a file and letting the auto-detect function assist with mapping.

When you upload the file, the system attempts to match up the incoming field names with PrismHR fields or pre-defined alternative field descriptions. This auto detection occurs during file upload and the system displays a process window that details the upload progress. Parameter values in File Settings are automatically selected based on the contents of the uploaded file. You can adjust these parameters and apply changes. The system flags these errors: • Duplicate column headers: You must change the duplicate header name and save changes. • No column headers: You must update column headers with names.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

Once the file is uploaded and interpreted by the system, Column Mapping is updated to reflect how incoming field names match up with PrismHR fields. You can edit Imported Column Header and Prism Field to refine the field mapping.

File Settings Auto-detect parameters become active after a file is upload and includes these options: • Number of header lines to skip: This value controls how many rows in an uploaded spreadsheet are skipped before parsing it for values. Values range from 1-10, with a default of 1. • Delimiter: Available options are comma (default) and tab-delimited.

Import Field Mapping Section The Import Field Mapping section configures your settings to import field mappings into the system.

To set up the import field mapping: 1. Select a Type. Currently, the only available option is Employee; this field will be expanded to other types of imports in the future. 2. Select a Field Mapping ID (required) from the Select Field Mapping look-up table. Field mappings have been created that align with import spreadsheets: • Prism-Standard • Prism-Expanded (default) • HRP-Expanded These are based on the Expanded and Standard HRP import formats. They vary slightly from the originals in that they do not include blank or discontinued columns. The standard field mappings include PAY.GROUP, AUTO.PAY, and I9.FROM.OB in addition to the fields found in the HRP version of the import.

Note: Only spreadsheets that match the HRP-Expanded-TXT file can be imported without headers.

  1. Enter a known field mapping ID or description in the Search Box. You can also filter results by status (All, Active, Obsolete).

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 13 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

  1. Select an item from the results that display. The Import Field Mapping form displays with populated fields. For example:

    Field/Control/Button Description Show Only Errors and Warnings Filters the status column so only errors and warnings are displayed. Filter by Required Filters the fields by their Required status. Options are: All, Yes, No, Conditional. Conditional fields are optional entries, such as Gender or Personal Email. Filter by Category Filters the field mappings by Category. Options are: All, Personal, Employment, Contact, Work Authorization, Pay, Tax, Benefits, Custom, I-9, Pay Allocations, HR. Status A green check mark indicates that a field match was found with the system. A red exclamation point indicates that the field was not recognized. A gold triangle means the autodetect function was not able to match the field with 100% accuracy and you need to check these fields to ensure they map to the correct PrismHR field. Imported Column Headers The headers (field names) in the import spreadsheet that are being mapped to the equivalent PrismHR fields. Prism Field You can enter PrismHR field codes manually, or click Prism Field

Working with New Employee Import Data Mapping New Employee Import: Data Mapping is step 2 of the Import Wizard. This form displays the results of the import definition that you selected from imported data. It helps validate that the correct information was uploaded and the right settings were applied in Step 1 of the Import Wizard. This form has three panels: • Import Wizard Steps Indicator - Data Mapping is step 2 in the Import Wizard and the steps indicator highlights Step 2 Data Mapping to indicate where you are in the process. • Field Mapping - Determines the columns that appear in an import file and in what order. • Code Translations - Indicates the code set used for this import.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

Understanding Field Mappings Field mappings determine what columns appear in your import file and in what order. If you are using a file downloaded from a third party, you might need to create a new field mapping to ensure that data is imported correctly. Note: All columns in this form are read-only, displayed for validation only. If the information looks incorrect, you may need to start over and select a different field mapping. Mapping columns include: • Column Letter - Corresponds to the column letter in the import file. • Imported Column Header - Title of the header specified in the import file. • Prism Field - Prism field code. For example, FIRST.NAME for First Name. • Prism Field Description - Friendly text description of the PrismHR field. For example, the code CLIENT.ID translates to Company ID. • Required - Indicates whether a field is required (Yes) or not (No). Global and Client field overrides are not displayed. • Sample Data - Displays a sample of what a field mapping generates for a specific code. For example, FIRST.NAME will display an employee name, such as John.

• Next - Opens the Enhanced Employee Import dialog and displays a list of import errors. Click Close to display Screen 3, Review and Fix Data (New Employee Import: Review). Click Report to view, download, or print a report of the import errors. • Previous - Returns to Step 1 in the Import Wizard. This lets you change a parameter or fix issues in the original import file by uploading a revised import file.

Reviewing New Employee Import The New Employee Import: Review form displays imported employee data that you can edit directly in each cell of the data mapping table. Only the columns that contain errors are displayed. This is Screen 3 of the New Employee Import Wizard and is not accessible through Search. The Import Overview dashboard displays: • Employees - Total number of employees in the import file • Companies - Total number of companies represented • Errors - Total of all errors (not rows with errors)

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 19 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

• Warnings - Total of all warnings (not rows with warnings) • Fixed - Total of all warnings and errors fixed by the user • Not Importing - The total of all employees either in the onboard process or selectively excluded from the import These totals are filters for the import file. As edits are made to the file, totals can change, such as the number of fixed items.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Reviewing and Fixing Data Imported data is translated into PrismHR codes. The data includes all columns that contain errors or warnings, which are highlighted in pink. These columns appear for all rows, even if those rows are free of errors. The columns that appear, regardless of spreadsheet order: • Status indicator (icons) - Hover over an icon for an employee to view a summary of errors or warnings. • First Name • Last Name • Company ID • Employee ID These columns do not horizontally scroll.

Understanding Import Corrections Erroneous data appears in the Import Corrections table, which is an editable inline grid. A red icon appears in rows containing erroneous data. For example, a zip code is highlighted because it does not contain 5 digits.

Editing Data You can correct data by entering it directly in the cell. If there is a code associated with the cell, a selector can be opened to select from a list of codes either by clicking on the look-up icon (magnifying glass) to the right of the data or by pressing Control+Enter in the highlighted cell. You can edit the text in all other fields, even those that do not contain errors. Use these keyboard shortcuts to navigate through the table: • Tab - Move right • Shift+Tab - Move left

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

• Up/Down Arrows - Move vertically.

Note: When you correct data and exit the field cell, the system automatically sends the entire Employee record back through the import engine to confirm if there are any additional errors.

Dates: You can either use the calendar date picker or enter the date manually. Quick date functions such as t for today’s date, or t-1 for yesterday’s date are supported. A horizontal scroll bar appears if the total width of all columns exceeds the overall table width. You can scroll by clicking the scroll arrows, or hold the Shift key while scrolling the mouse wheel. Note that the first four columns are frozen and do not scroll horizontally. Click the look-up icon (magnifying glass) to open the look-table associated with that field. The magnifying glass icon turns blue when you hover over it.

Hover over an error or warning icon to see this message:

Note the following: • If a row contains both a warning and an error, the error icon displays first. Once the error is cleared, the warning icon appears. Data with a warning flag can be edited. It is also possible to submit an import file with warnings. • A table cell with look-up icon indicates that a selector for that code type can be opened to make different selections. You can click on the icon or press Control+Enter to open the selector. Available selectors include: • Benefit Group • Cross Company EID • Department Code • Division

• If inline help is displayed, you can still edit values in the table. • If the new value is correct, the pink background color is removed. • If you enter a non-existent code, the system tells you it does not exist. • If you remove a required code, the system tells you this code is required. • Filter counts displayed in the Import Overview Dashboard are updated when changes are made to the table. • You can assign selected employers to a particular worksite location for clients. If this occurs, you can only select that particular employer. If you are not assigning employers on the worksite location form, then the primary and alternate employers are shown on the lookup. • If an attribute value is an error for more than one employee, and the error is fixed either by entering it manually or selecting the value from a lookup table, the system asks whether you want to fix the other instances of this value. Similarly, if a value is cleared from a cell, and it appears in other cells, the system asks whether those other values should also be removed. If you correct errors by creating a new code, all cells with the same attribute are automatically corrected as well.

Note: All changes are automatically saved and a Changes Saved indicator displays.

Filtering Data One way to filter data is selecting options from the Show drop-down. You can show All employees, only errors or warnings, only employees in onboarding, or only employees not being imported. The number of employees filtered for an option appears in parentheses.

Sort Order Take note of the following for sorting information in the Import Corrections table:

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 22 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

•    The default sort order is first by employee last name, and second by employee first name. Sub-sorting
     within groups of identical fields is also employee last name with a secondary sort on employee first
     name.
•    Sorting is case-insensitive.
•    Status: First action is rows with errors, warnings, fixed, and then rows with no import errors (clear).
     Second action is the reverse of the first action.
•    Employee Fields: First action is an alphanumeric sort of 0-9, A-Z. The second action is a reverse
     alphanumeric sort of Z-A 9-0.
•    Date: First action is reverse chronological order, and the second action is the reverse of the first action.

Revalidation of Data When you click Submit on the Review screen, the system re-runs the import validation to determine whether any edits outside of the import workflow affect the data within the import. The Final Evaluation of Import Data screen opens with a system message saying it is evaluating the import data to ensure no associated data changes were made outside of the import. If no errors are found, the system proceeds with conversion. If errors are found, the system displays a message saying changes to client setup or codes were detected and that you need to review the data and fix any errors.

Adding New Codes You can add new codes for a client by clicking look-ups that are directly linked to the PrismHR form for that category.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To add a code (using Position as an example): 1. From Import Corrections on the Review form, click into a table cell with an error and press Control+Enter to launch the Select Position selector.

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

  1. Click Create New Position to access the Select Position form for creating position codes. When new codes are created and saved, the system returns to the Review form. The table cell that triggered the code selector is updated with the new code.

Code Categories Code categories you can add with a Create New… link include: • Department Code - See Maintaining Departments. • Division - See Maintaining Divisions. • Position Code - See Defining Positions. • Project - See Maintaining Projects. • Shift Code - See Setting Company Shift Parameters. • Work Group - See Defining Work Groups. • Worksite Location - See Maintaining Worksite Locations.

Code Validation When you select a file to import, the system displays an error message if there are newly added codes that cause errors. You can then correct them and specify whether to include these new codes in the import. Codes can be added in the following ways:

New Employee Import User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 24 Chapter 1 New Employee Import Overview

• If a code was added from within the workflow import and it matches the imported or translated code, the system checks all rows for other instances of the same code. For all matching codes in the import, it clears the error highlighting on the table cell, updates the row icon and import dashboard to reflect the changes, and displays a message similar to this: 6 error(s) fixed with the addition of Position Code [BAR] • If a code was added from within the workflow import, it may differ from the imported or translated code because you changed the imported code while fixing an error. For example, you may have incorrectly entered BAT on the spreadsheet instead of BAR. In this case, the system checks all rows for other instances and if it finds any, it prompts you to specify whether to update all instances or only the highlighted cell. Based on your response, it clears the error highlighting on the relevant table cells, updates the row icon and import dashboard to reflect the changes, and displays a message similar to this: 6 error(s) fixed with the addition of Position Code [BAR] • If one or more codes are added outside of the workflow, you can correct them on the Review form. • If new errors are introduced, error counts on the table filter and dashboard are updated.

Understanding Company Import Information This panel displays Company ID, Company Name, and Import Options. This is data extracted from the import file and is read-only. The Import Options drop-down includes: • Auto-enroll employees in PTO and group benefits (default) • Do not auto-enroll

Note: PTO auto-enroll rules need to be set up and group benefit plans must be set to auto-enroll.

Employees are automatically added to the next payroll batch if one is available. Employees that are still in onboarding are not added to a payroll batch until they have completed onboarding.

Using Employee Exclusion Report Use this report to download a spreadsheet or report that includes all employees not imported to more easily review and address the issues that prevented importing and then upload them in a new import. The report lists excluded employees that were not imported (because either you or the application excluded the user), and creates a CSV file that includes all the columns for each employee. Data is not translated and edits made on the Review form are not included. An asterisk precedes each cell that contains an error and each row provides an additional column at the end that includes each error message. Tables on the Batch Management and Setup screens contain an Employees Not Included column and each row under the header includes a link to the file.

To exclude an employee: 1. From the Review & Fix Data form, click on the employee name, and in the pop-up, disable the Import Employee toggle. This is helpful when specific employee data cannot be addressed right away and is holding

up an import.
  1. Uncheck the Import Employee box.

Note: If an employee is excluded, this appears as a filtering option in the Show drop-down. Employees in onboarding are automatically excluded from the import.

If an employee is excluded, the status icon changes to a Ban icon and the row’s background color changes

to light gray. After the import is submitted and converted, the system retains a record of excluded employees that you can download as a report. You can flip an employee’s status back to included, which returns any errors or warnings associated with that employee before they were excluded.

Download an Employees Excluded Report

To download this report: 1. From the Past Imports table on the New Employee Import dashboard, click a report link under the Employees Not Included column. The system downloads the file to your local drive. 2. Open the file for further analysis.

Confirming New Employee Import Use this form to confirm information for imports that have completed successfully (Step 4 in Employee Import Wizard). This form is not available using Search. You can also generate a report for the import and for the original import file so you can audit issues that arise post-import. Click Done once all information is checked and the import is finished; you are returned to the Batch Management screen.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

The table that appears upon import completion displays: • Name - Name of the import file. Click the import file link to view a spreadsheet of imported employee data. Each successfully imported employee includes: • Client Name [ID] • Employer Name [ID] • Employee ID • Last Name • First Name • Job Title • Location • Department • Division • Project • Work Group • Shift • Original Hire Date • Pay Rate • Date Completed - Date the import was successfully submitted. • Processed by User - The person who submitted the import. • Number of Employees Imported - Number of employees successfully imported and converted. Does not include employees manually or automatically removed from the import. • Employees Not Imported - Text link displaying the number of employees manually or automatically removed from the import file. You can export this data as a report that helps review and fix issues that prevented importation and can later upload these employees in a new import file. • Original Import File - Name of the .txt or .csv file that was originally imported into Prism. Chapter 1 Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process The forms that you need to set up time off are available together in the Time Off Setup Workflow process, where you begin by selecting Time Off Setup Workflow on the Client|Change menu. When you access this menu option, the Time Off Setup Workflow form displays. For example:

Important! This process only applies to setting up new time off plans, not editing existing plans. (You can only edit existing plans in the legacy PTO Work Center. Click in the header area of the Time Off Setup Workflow form to access the legacy PTO Work Center. See Using the PTO Work Center on page 27.) Note the following: • The Time Off Setup Workflow feature is only available for service providers. • You can also access the Time Off Setup Workflow form either by entering the form name in the Search menu or by selecting Time Off Setup Workflow in the Plan Setup column, which you can access on the Work Centers Quick Access panel after selecting PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment.

Getting Started You can use the Time Off Setup Workflow form to continue setting up in-progress time off plans or create new time off plans. (See Setting Up Time Off Plans (page 3).) Note: To set up a new time off plan, click New Setup, which displays the Add Time Off Setup Batch form, where you can name the batch.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 1 Chapter 1 Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process

Understanding the Process Steps The Time Off Setup Workflow process provides access to the following: • Step 1, Time Off Type: Begin the time off setup process using the Time Off Type form, which you can access from the Time Off Setup Workflow form (see Setting Up Time Off Plans). In this step, you will set the type for the time off plan. (See Setting Time Off Plan Type.) • Step 2, Set Up Plans: Create or update the employee time off accrual schedule, plan, pay, and portal configuration. (See Setting Up Employee Time Off on page 7.) • Step 3, Time Off Confirmation: Review the saved information from steps 1 and 2 and make updates. (See Confirming Time Off Plan Settings on page 20.) • Finalizing the information: After confirming that the information is correct click Finish Setup, which commits the saved time off plans to the system. Important! Clicking Finish Setup finalizes the time off plan information that you made in this workflow. If you need to make more updates, you must now make them in the legacy PTO Work Center. A message displays, “After finishing the setup all future updates will take place outside of this workflow. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue the process. The Creating Time Off Setups progress window displays. Click Close to return to the Time Off Setup Workflow form. Note the following: • If any errors display, close the progress window to return to the workflow and adjust the plan. • The time off plans you create display in the appropriate forms: PTO Classes, PTO Register Types, PTO Benefit Plans, and PTO Absence Codes. Note: If you do not have access to a form in the Time Off Setup Workflow, it does not display in the list.

Terminology Updates To help familiarize yourself with the new Time Off Setup Workflow terminology, note the following terms now in use when compared to the legacy PTO Work Center terminology:

Legacy PTO Work Center Term Time Off Setup Workflow Process Term PTO Class Time Off Type PTO Register Type Accrual Schedule PTO Benefit Plan Time Off Plan PTO Absence Codes Time Off Pay

Note: For a detailed comparison of terminology changes, see Understanding Time Off Setup Workflow Process Terminology.

Setting the Time Off Type You can use the Time Off Type form to set the type for a time off plan by either selecting a standard time off type in the list that displays (the type description displays in highlighted text with the type name displaying underneath) or creating a new type.

To set the type for a time off plan: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select Time Off Setup Workflow. The Time Off Setup Workflow form opens. 3. Select the time off plan in the Batch ID column where you need to set the type. The Time Off Type form displays. 4. Select the Time Off Type from the options that display (the type description displays in highlighted text with the type name displaying underneath) or select Add Type to add a new type. For example, you can create a new “Personal Holiday” time off type in the Add Time Off Type form that displays. (Both fields in the Add Time Off Type form are required.) Note the following: • You can only select one time off type. • You cannot duplicate existing time off types. Therefore, if you enter an existing Time Off Type Code the current description displays. If you update the current description, the system processes the updated description after you process the entire workflow. 5. Do one of the following:

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process

a. Click        to advance to the Set Up Plans form, which is step 2 in the Time Off Setup Workflow process
   (see Setting Up Employee Time Off). (The         button is disabled if you did not select a time off type.)
   The system enables the Time Off Type step on the left side by displaying the step number in green,
   confirming that this step is complete.

b. Click              to save the time off type and return to the Time Off Setup Workflow form.

Note: You can edit existing time off types by clicking the pencil icon ( ), which opens the Add Time Off Type form where you can update the Type Description.

Setting Up Employee Time Off You can use the Set Up Plans form to create or update the employee time off accrual schedule, plan, pay, and portal configuration. Note: The Set Up Plans form displays as part of step 2 in the Time Off Setup Workflow process, which is accessible when you select a time off type in the Time Off Type form and click (see Setting Up Time Off Plans). (This form cannot be accessed in the search menu and cannot be added to a user role. See Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process.) There are four panels in the Set Up Plans form:

You can do the following in these panels: • Setting Accrual Schedule: Use the Accrual Schedule panel to set when employees accrue time off. • Setting Up Employee Accrual Time Off Plan: Use the Plans panel to set up the plan that determines how much time off employees will accrue. • Setting Pay Information: Use the Pay panel to set the pay information for the time off type, which includes setting the Pay Code and Accrual Schedule. • Setting Portal Configuration: Use the Portal Configuration (Optional) panel to indicate whether an employee can submit a time off request in Employee Portal (EP). (All settings in this panel are optional.) Note the following when working in the Set Up Plans form:

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process

• You cannot access the Set Up Plans form in the search menu and or add this form to a user role. • Clicking in the Time Off Type form incorporates the time off type’s description in the header that displays at the top of the Set Up Plans form (that is, Set Up Plans). For example, if you select the “PTO Accrual” type, the header displays as “Set Up PTO Accrual Plans.” • You can move through the panels without selecting any settings. However, you must complete all the required fields in the panels before moving on to step 3, the Confirmation form. (The button is disabled until you complete this step.)

   Accrual Frequency         Select the accrual calculation that triggers during payroll processing.
                             (Required.)
                             •    Pay Period Accrual: Accruals calculate for employees with regular
                                  vouchers in the payroll. Calculations are from the last accrued
                                  through date through the end of the selected on option.
                             •    Anniversary Month: Accruals calculate when the on option crosses
                                  an employee’s anniversary day, and the last accrued through date is
                                  before that day.
                             •    Anniversary Year: Employees receive a lump-sum accrual for a paid
                                  time off benefit at the beginning of their anniversary year for
                                  benefits accrued through the end of the current year. The system
                                  triggers this accrual frequency when the on option crosses over the
                                  employee’s anniversary day.
                             •    End of Month: The system triggers this accrual frequency when the
                                  pay period crosses into another month or ends on the last day of a
                                  month. Accruals calculate through the end of the month, or the
                                  employee’s anniversary day for the month, depending on the on
                                  option.
                             •    End of Quarter: The system triggers this accrual frequency when the
                                  pay period crosses into a new quarter. Quarters are based on either
                                  the year-end or employee’s anniversary date, depending on the on
                                  option.
                                 Note: A warning message displays when you select End of Quarter,
                                 "Warning: Flat amount is the only Plan Accrual Method supported by
                                 End of Quarter Accrual Frequency. The Year End Basis must also be
                                 Fiscal Year ending on 6/30." Click OK to continue.
                             •    End of Year: Employees receive a lump-sum accrual for a paid time
                                  off benefit at the end of the fiscal year. When the end of the fiscal
                                  year corresponds to the end of the calendar year, the accrual
                                  triggers when the pay period crosses into the new year or the
                                  period end date is the same as the end of the calendar year.
                                  Otherwise, the accrual triggers when the period end date crosses
                                  the year end date in the current year.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process

   Field                    Description
                            •   First of Year: Employees receive a lump-sum accrual at the
                                beginning of the fiscal year. The First of Year trigger works exactly
                                the same as the End of Year trigger, except that the accrual level is
                                based on the employee’s seniority level as of January 1st of the next
                                year (instead of December 31st of the current year).
                            •   First of Following Month: The system triggers this accrual frequency
                                when the pay period includes the first day of a month. Accruals
                                calculate for the previous month.
                            •   First of Current Month: The system triggers this accrual frequency
                                when the pay period includes the first day of a month. Accruals
                                calculate for the current month.
                            •   First of Quarter: The system triggers this accrual frequency when

                                Quarter accrual frequency and the Pay Date on option. For
                                example, if the first pay date in Q4 occurs on 10/7/2024, time off
                                accrual occurs during that payroll. (Quarters are typically calendar

Understanding Time Off Setup Workflow Process Terminology The forms that you need to set up time off are available together in the Time Off Setup Workflow process, where you begin by selecting Time Off Setup Workflow on the Client|Change menu. When you access this menu option, the Time Off Setup Workflow form displays. Note: This feature is only available for service providers. Important! This process only applies to setting up new time off plans, not editing existing plans. (You can only edit existing plans in the legacy PTO Work Center. Click in the header area of the Time Off Setup Workflow form to access the legacy PTO Work Center. See Using the PTO Work Center on page 27.)

Accessing Time Off Setup Workflow Form To ensure whether you have access to the Time Off Setup Workflow form, update your setting on the User Roles form. For example:

Terminology Updates To help familiarize yourself with the new Time Off Setup Workflow terminology, note the following terms now in use when compared to the legacy PTO Work Center terminology:

Chapter 2 Using the PTO Work Center The forms that you need to perform a PTO process, change, or setup are available together in the legacy PTO Work Center, which is accessible from the Work Centers Quick Access panel. (Note: You can still access the individual PTO forms from their respective menus on the menu bar.) Important! This original PTO Workflow process has been replaced by the enhanced Time Off Setup Workflow process (see Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Process), which provides user-friendly forms to process employee time off plans for your clients. However, you must use the PTO Work Center to edit existing PTO processes. Note: The Time Off Setup Workflow feature is only available for service providers. The following centers display in the PTO Work Center:

Note: This feature is only available for service providers. However, if you apply the service provider dashboard (HRPY.WORK_DASH or HRPY.WORK_ENHANCED.DASH) to a worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor role in the Global Configuration form, when you log in to one of the PTO work centers as a WSM/WTA that has that center’s process ID added to their user role the menu displays on the dashboard in the Quick Access panel. The PTO Work Center provides access to the following:

• Leave Request Management: Provides access to the forms where you can process approved, backdated leave requests for salaried employees by creating a manual check adjustment, and review and make changes to employees’ time off (PTO) requests. (See Accessing Leave Request Management Forms on page 28.) • PTO Adjustments and Maintenance: Provides access to the forms where you can enter and maintain employee absences and the PTO registers. (See Accessing PTO Adjustments and Maintenance Forms on page 29.) • PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment: Provides step-by-step access to the plan setup forms, and access to the PTO enrollment forms. (See Accessing PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment Forms on page 30.) • PTO Reporting: Provides access to all the PTO reports. (See Accessing PTO Reporting Forms on page 32.) Note: If you do not have access to a form in the PTO Work Center, it does not display in the list. The PTO Accrual Recalculation form is helpful in case the initial setup was incorrect or you need to make a bulk adjustment. However, you must first update the PTO benefit plan/register for a PTO recalculation to appear. For example:

Note: This feature is only available for service providers. Important! At this time, a note displays stating that using the accrual recalculation tool might adversely impact employees who have forced PTO accrual on manual or special batches is a preparatory warning. The system functionality to force PTO accruals on manual or special payrolls will be included in a future release.

To recalculate PTO accruals: 1. Enter or select the PTO Class. 2. Select the Register Type. 3. Enter or select the Benefit Plan. 4. Select Preview. The system processes the PTO registers for that client, register type, and PTO benefit plan for the current plan year. (The date range automatically adjusts for each employee based on the year-end date in their register.) For example:

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 33 Chapter 2 Using the PTO Work Center

  1. Enter a Comment on Adjustment that will display on the PTO adjustment.
  2. Click Process Recalculation. A window opens that displays the processing steps.
  3. Click Close. A message displays, “Update Completed.” Click OK to continue.
  4. Click Download Report to view the PTO accrual recalculation details on-screen. (You can save the file by clicking XLS.) The report displays on-screen. (You can also select Download Report to save this report.) Note the following: • Each employee has one written absence journal where the system writes the actual PTO register once with the adjustment amount. • You can update accruals in the current plan year, but cannot close out the plan year or reset the YTD hours taken. • This process does not include carryover hours. • The adjustment effective date is based on the recalculation date. • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the PTO Accrual Recalculation form cannot access this form.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 34 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans Absence benefit plans are unique to each client and can differ from the simple to the extremely complex. Once you set up the absence benefit accrual files in PrismHR, the system automatically accrues paid time off (PTO) benefits for each employee according to the parameters you establish. Although it is important to understand how to establish these files, the real key to setting up the files correctly is understanding exactly how the client’s absence benefit plan works. Use these instructions to learn how to: • Establish the absence benefit plan, including carryover rules and accrual rates • Determine how and when accrual calculations should occur • Set up codes to identify PTO classes, register types, and absences

Tracking Absences PrismHR tracks paid absences automatically during regular payroll processing. Users can manually enter unpaid absences and review them at any time on a number of different absence reports.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 35 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

  1. The system refers to the pay code record for each pay code entered on an employee time sheet.
  2. If there is an Absence Benefit Code associated with the pay code, the system refers to the PTO Absence Code.
  3. If the Paid Absence Code indicates that the PTO Register needs updating, the system applies the hours from the time sheet to the employee’s register.
  4. If the number of absence hours is more than the total number of hours available, the payroll processor is alerted. The system gives them a warning, but lets the payroll processor continue.
  5. Absences that are unpaid and other adjustments to the PTO register are entered manually through the PTO Adjustment Entry. Unpaid absences do not affect the PTO register totals, but may be referenced through various reports and inquiries.

Defining PTO Classes Restrict the number of register types that can be assigned to an employee to avoid employee PTO register duplication with the PTO Classes form. You need to create only one of each paid time off class (such as vacation or illness).

To set a PTO class: 1. Select the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select PTO Classes. The PTO Classes form opens. 3. Complete the required information in these fields.

Note the following: • The system will transfer the prior year accrued hours from the accrual register to the balance register for employees enrolled in a Linked Accrual PTO Register when the plan year is triggered. • If you set up a transfer to another PTO class code more than once an error message displays, “Transfer to is already in use.” (You cannot have two PTO classes transferred to the same PTO class because this is a 1:1 relationship.) • If you enable Linked Accrual but do not select the Transfer To PTO class an error message displays when you click Save, “Transfer To PTO Class is required.” • The system tracks changes made to PTO Classes in the audit log.

Creating PTO Registers Use the PTO Register Types form to create or update a PTO register. PTO registers track the usable hours of PTO that employees accrue over the course of the year. The events the trigger PTO accrual, and the strict definition of “year,” are defined on this form.

Note: The PTO Register Type indicates when employees accrue paid time off. The PTO Benefit Plan indicates how much paid time off employees accrue.

To create a PTO register: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select PTO Register Types. The PTO Register Types form opens. 3. Complete the following:

Using Customized Accrual Subroutines If the client uses an accrual method that differs from methods previously described, use a customized accrual subroutine.

Note: Contact a systems professional to design a subroutine using the parameters described here.

To design a subroutine: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select PTO Register Types. 3. In Trigger Method, select Custom Basic Routine. The Custom Basic Subroutines panel displays.

  1. In Trigger Subroutine, enter a custom trigger method subroutine to determine whether hours should accrue for each employee. The format is:

            SUBROUTINE
        SUBR.NAME(ABSENCE.REGISTER.REC,EMPLOYEE.SSN,ACCRUAL.TRIGGERED)

    The variable ACCRUAL.TRIGGERED should return either a 0 (zero) or 1 (one). If the value returned is 1, the system calculates an accrual.

  2. In Calculation Subroutine, enter a customized subroutine to replace the standard daily accrual calculation. The subroutine must have the following parameter list:

            SUBROUTINE
        SUBR.NAME(COMPANY.NO,EMP.SSN,REG.TYPE,ABSENCE.REGISTER.REC,
        BENEFIT.PLAN.REC,VOUCHER.REC,HOURS.ACCRUED)

    The hours accrued should be returned in the variable HOURS.ACCRUED. The calling program does not accept the return of a negative number. If the system returns a negative number, it is set to zero instead. Do not return a number with an embedded decimal point because it will be truncated.

Learning About PTO Benefit Plans A PTO benefit plan, or absence benefit plan, determines how much paid time off an employee can accrue. The employee PTO register is the place where the system keeps track of how much has been accrued and taken by the employee. The PTO Benefit Plan establishes limits on the amount of paid time off that may be earned. This is the number of hours that can be carried over from one plan period to the next, or the number of hours the employee can earn. Clients often have more than one PTO benefit plan, for example: • Vacation

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 43 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

•      Sick
•      Personal
•      Other plan types that represent time accrued and taken according to the client’s policy

You can also have more than one type of benefit plan, such as multiple vacation plans. The Benefit Plan is assigned to an employee at enrollment.

Note: The PTO Register Type indicates when employees accrue paid time off. The PTO Benefit Plan indicates how much paid time off employees accrue.

Defining PTO Benefit Plans To define PTO benefit plans that determine employee paid time off accruals, use the PTO Benefit Plans form.

Note: The PTO Register is where the system tracks how much paid time off the employees have accrued and taken. For more information, see Creating PTO Registers (page 37).

Each PTO Benefit Plan establishes limits on the amount of paid time off that employees can earn and how many hours they can carry over from one plan period to the next. Clients often have more than one PTO benefit plan. For example: • Vacation • Sick • Personal • Other plan types taken according to client policy that can represent time accrued

Note: To copy a PTO plan from another client, use the Copy from another plan option, and then edit the PTO plan information as required.

Employee PTO Plan Enrollment PTO Benefit Plan Start Date When enrolling employees in the Employee PTO Register, the Benefit Start Date must be entered carefully. The Flat Amount by Hours Worked calculation method will adjust automatically. If a past date is entered, on the first calculated payroll, hours will accrue retroactively for all payrolls since that date in the current register year. This will occur regardless of the Calculated Through Date entered during the enrollment. In the following example, if payroll is processed and dated 6/30/2019, the employee will accrue sick time on all vouchers dated 4/8/19 to 6/30/19.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 59 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

When enrolling employees in the plan retroactively, no adjustment is needed. On the first calculated payroll, PrismHR will calculate the total hours worked from the benefit start date of the current year to the payroll date and accrue in full. This calculation will occur with each payroll. Since this plan will automatically adjust, PTO Register adjustments are not possible when using this method. Any adjustment made will be reversed on the next payroll, as the system will constantly calculate back to the benefit start date of the current year and accrue all hours. If YTD Calculated hours are entered during the enrollment, no hours will accrue until the system calculates that the employee has exceeded the accrual that was entered based on hours paid.

Understanding Unlimited PTO Benefit Plans The Employee PTO Registers and Employee PTO Register Inquiry forms contain fields that do not apply. They also do not include the Hours Calculated/Carry-over Details panel because that information does not apply to unlimited PTO plans. After the first payroll of the new year, the date fields in the registers might not update because there are no accruals. They update only after the employee uses PTO hours in a posted payroll. Note the following: • The Employee PTO Register Adjustment form does not allow users to make adjustments to unlimited PTO plans. • During payroll initialization, there are no warnings about PTO balances for employees enrolled in an unlimited PTO plan. • Payroll vouchers for employees with unlimited PTO plans show the hours used but not any calculated (accrued) hours. • The Employee PTO Detail Report shows no information for carryover, accrued, or available time.

Defining Unlimited PTO Plans Define Unlimited as the Calculation Basis for PTO benefit plans with the Pay Codes for Hourly Accrual, Pay Period Accrual Thresholds, and Flat Amount per Hours Worked panels. Any accrual information entered in those panels is ignored when Calculation Basis is Unlimited. Any fields related to carryover and accruals in the PTO Benefit Plan panel are disabled because plans that offered unlimited PTO do not accrue hours.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 60 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

To define an unlimited PTO plan: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select PTO Benefit Plans. The PTO Benefit Plans form opens. 3. In Calculation Basis, select Unlimited.

  1. Fill in fields as required for the unlimited PTO plan (see Defining PTO Benefit Plans (page 44)). The system does not calculate hourly accruals for employees enrolled in unlimited PTO plans, so completing fields in the Pay Codes for Hourly Accrual, Pay Period Accrual Thresholds, and Flat Amount per Hours Worked panels is not required.

Defining First Year Prorated Amounts You can use the First Year Prorated Amounts panel in the PTO Benefit Plans form to change the number of hours employees will receive in their first year of employment, which helps handle numerous PTO changes. For example, if a client allows five hours of PTO to accrue per pay period, they might only allow three hours to accrue per pay period for the employee’s first year, if they were hired from July to December.

To define first year prorated amounts: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select PTO Benefit Plans. The PTO Benefit Plans form opens.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 61 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

  1. In Calculation Basis, select Flat Amount. The First Year Prorated Amounts panel displays. For example:

  2. Select the Month and enter the Flat Accrual Amount and Max Per Year amount as required for the Flat Amount PTO plan (see Defining PTO Benefit Plans (page 44)). Note the following: • The system uses the employee’s hire date to determine which month accrual to use. • If the employee is a rehire, the system uses the last hire date to calculate their prorated amount. • The prorated information is only used for flat accrual plans. • To save the information, you must enter both a Month and a Flat Accrual Amount. Otherwise, an error message displays, “In row 1, Both a Month and Flat Accrual Amount must be selected.” • You can only add numeric values for the Flat Accrual Amount. Otherwise, an error message displays, “A valid number is required.” • Once an employee reaches their Max Per Year PTO hours they no longer accrue any more PTO hours for that year.

  3. Click Save.

Linking PTO Accrual Plans . You can use the Linked Accrual Plans feature to accrue employee PTO hours for transfer once the plan year ends. This feature consists of two PTO plans that you must set up so employees can accrue time for a plan year in one register that they cannot use until the plan year ends. After the plan year ends, the accrued hours move to a new register where employees can use their PTO hours. (Employees can have several different linked accrual plans, one for sick time, one for vacation time, and so on.) Note the following:

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 62 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

• Employees must be enrolled in two PTO registers (one for accrual and one for balance) to use this feature. If there is no Balance PTO register associated with the linked class for the employee, then the system does not move anything will from the Accrual register to the Balance register. (The hours remain in the Accrual register.) • If the Balance PTO Register has a yearly maximum set, the system moves prior year balances from the Accrual register to the Balance register up to the maximum amount. (The remaining amount in the accrual register is lost.) • When the system transfers accrued hours from the Accrual register to the Balance register, it places the hours in the Balance register in the YTD Calculated column. • Accrual plans accrue for the pay period and then transfer to the Balance plan.

Using Linked Accrual Plans Feature To use the Linked Accrual Plans feature, you must set up two PTO plans in the PTO Benefit Plans form: • Accrual plan: Accrues employee PTO time during the year. At the end of the plan year, the system transfers the hours in the accrual plan to the linked balance plan. (The Accrual plan resets to zero.) Employees can now use the accrued hours in the Balance plan. • Balance plan: Contains the transferred PTO accrual time. The following diagram demonstrates the setup for Linked Accrual Plans:

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 63 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

Note the following: • The employee’s accrual balance for the current year is the year-to-date PTO hours accrued from the previous year. • Employees carry over some hours in some cases, but most plans expire the hours at the end of the plan year. • Most of these plans are set up as anniversary plans, not by the plan year.

Setting Up the Linked Accrual Plans Feature

Set up the following: 1. PTO Class: Use the PTO Classes form to define which PTO classes will be used in conjunction with each other, consisting of a PTO class for the accrual and a PTO class for the balance. (See the Client Administration Guide for details on defining PTO classes.) For example: a. Create a PTO Class Code for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL. Note: Do not enable Linked Accrual. b. Create a PTO Class Code for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR. c. Enable Linked Accrual. d. In the Transfer To field, select VACBAL. Note: These PTO classes are now linked and cannot be linked to other classes. 2. PTO Register: Enable the Prior Year Accrual trigger method on the PTO Register Types form to trigger the balance register to move the accrued PTO hours from the accrual plan to the balance plan. (See the Client Administration Guide for details on working with PTO registers.) For example: a. Create a PTO Type Code register for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL. • PTO Class: VACBAL. • Year End Basis: Set Anniversary or Fiscal, but should match the Accrual register. • Trigger Method: Prior Year Accrual. • Trigger Date: Do not use. • Print on Check, Pay Stub Name, Paid Absence, Absence Code: Set these fields for the Balance register. b. Create a PTO Type Code register for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR. • PTO Class: VACACCR. • Year End Basis: Set Anniversary or Fiscal, but should match the Balance register. • Trigger Method: Select any trigger method. • Trigger Date: Select any trigger date.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 64 Chapter 3 Setting Up PTO Plans

     •   Absence Code: Set this field for the accrual register. (It is not currently used, but it should be
         populated.)
     •   Print on Check, Pay Stub Name, Inactive Register, and Paid Absence: Do not use.
  1. PTO Benefit Plan: Enroll employees in an Accrual plan and a Balance plan on the PTO Benefit Plans form. The Accrual plan determines the PTO time accrued. The system does not use the Balance plan to determine the accruals, but employees must be enrolled in both plans for the transfer to work correctly.
    1. Create a PTO Benefit Plan for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL. (You must select a calculation basis, but the system does not use it to calculate accruals.)

Understanding the Transfer Process When the system transfers accrued PTO hours, the employee register displays the accrued amount in the calculated column in the Balance register and displays an annotation, “Accrual Transfer MM/DD/YY,” in the details. The system then zeroes out the year-to-date accrual amounts in the employee Accrual register and displays an annotation, “XX number of hours moved to linked plan.”

Specifying PTO Auto-enroll Rules Specify plans that automatically enroll new employees with the PTO Auto Enroll Rules form. Companies with existing rules display information similar to this:

Note the following: • If there are PTO Auto Enroll Rules available for the active client and you delete all existing rules, the form refreshes and the Save and Delete buttons no longer display. • When an approval is approved for an applicable change, the system re-evaluates PTO auto-enroll rules and executes enrollments in the PTO Auto Enroll Rules form for current or past-dated Status/Type and Position changes. If the change date matches the system date or a prior date the following occurs: • If an employee meets the criteria for a rule and the rule is set to archive in the prior PTO Register, the system archives existing PTO Registers that share the same class as the PTO Register assigned to the affected rule. Chapter 4 Setting Up Global PTO Plans You can use PrismHR to set up PTO plans on the system level and automatically assign those plans to employees based on work location.

Background As described in the PTO User Guide, the PrismHR PTO features originally applied only to clients. This presented difficulties for organizations that needed to track paid time off for employees who regularly change location — such as those in the staffing industry. In response to this challenge, PrismHR introduced support for Global PTO plans that can track the accrual of employee paid time based on the employee’s worksite location. These new features enable you to set up discrete Global PTO plans and assign those to a state or even a specific GeoCode range. This setup structure provides significant flexibility in defining how and when employee paid time off accrues.

Activating Global PTO Features Note: Refresh your browser to see the changes from this feature code.

If you want to enable the new global PTO features, you must first apply the associated feature code.

To activate global PTO features: 1. Click Back Office and select System|Change > System Parameters. 2. In the upper right corner of the form, in the Custom Feature Codes table, create a new row. 3. Enter GLOBAL.PTO in this new row (be sure to include the period between GLOBAL and PTO). 4. Click Save. 5. Refresh your browser and then log in again, if necessary. The Global PTO forms and fields are now accessible.

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 76 Chapter 4 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

About the Features With these features enabled: • You can establish system-level PTO codes and plans, and then assign those at the state and local levels using new fields on the State Rules form. • Next time you run a payroll, PrismHR will detect any employees who work within the specified state and GeoCode ranges. The system will automatically perform the PTO accrual calculations associated with the specific PTO plans assigned to those locations. Those calculated accruals will be stored in a separate database record created for this purpose. • To fine-tune the global PTO auto-enrollment and hour accrual, you can use client-level opt-in settings and employee-level opt-out settings (described below). • If you want to review PTO accruals to ensure that they are set up accurately, you can use a new view option on the Employee PTO Register Inquiry form. • New in June 2022: For staffing customers, we now support global PTO plans for federal contractors. The FG state code provides a grid for Global PTO plans but not GeoCodes, as they are not necessary. If an employee PLACEMENT record indicates that they are a federal contractor, the auto-enrollment and accrual logic will assign them a PTO plan associated with FG. • New in June 2022: The PTO “auto-enroll and accrue” logic also takes effect whenever you perform a global PTO data import using the PTO Register Import form. • New in June 2022: A new payroll report is available. This report displays a list of employees who were auto-enrolled in global PTO plans within the current payroll batch. You can run this report during payroll processing or separately. See Reviewing Global PTO Auto-Enrollments for a Payroll Batch (page 83). • New in June 2022: Several options are now available for printing Global PTO register data on employee checks. Instead of a binary yes/no option, you can select Always, Never (default), or If Used/Accrued Only for any global PTO register. • New in March 2024: Leave requests made in the Employee Portal that the system pulls into timesheets using the red dot can be accepted there. • New in September 2024: Previously, all Global PTO functionality for the following forms were hidden unless the custom feature code GLOBAL.PTO was enabled. All Global PTO functionality are now available on the following forms without using the custom feature code GLOBAL.PTO. • System / Change / Global PTO Benefit Plans • System / Change / Global PTO Register Types • PTO Reporting / Reporting / Global PTO Auto Enrollment Report

PTO User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 77 Chapter 4 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

     •   System / Change / State Rules (Global PTO Plans)
     •   Client / Change / Client Other (Enable Global PTO)
     •   PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment / Plan Setup / PTO Absence Codes (Global PTO Checkbox)

Note: The custom feature code is still required to calculate Global PTO accruals. This requirement will be removed in an upcoming release.

Creating Global PTO Register Types Use the Global PTO Register Types form to set up PTO register types for plans that are not client-specific. PTO registers track the usable hours of PTO that employees accrue over the course of the year. The events the trigger PTO accrual, and the strict definition of “year”, are defined on this form. After setting up these rules, you can assign these codes using a specialized Register Types table on the PTO Absence Codes form. See Reviewing Accrual Histories.

To set up a global PTO register type: 1. Go to Back Office > System|Change > Global PTO Register Types. 2. Enter or select a Global PTO Type Code. 3. Enter a Description of the global PTO register type. 4. Select the Year End Basis – the means by which the system measures the end of a year (Anniversary or Fiscal). If you selected Fiscal, specify a Fiscal End Month and Day. 5. In the Trigger Method field, select Pay Period Accrual. 6. Set the other optional parameters, as needed. You can find descriptions of these fields in the online help for either the Global PTO Register Types form or the client-level PTO Register Types form. Both forms use the same logic for these fields. Deduction Logic PrismHR uses the following process to select PTO registers for time off deductions. Note that a local PTO plan is any plan assigned to a GeoCode range on the State Rules form. The specific GeoCode is determined by the worksite location associated with the PTO hour payout.

The basic PTO deduction logic takes this form: 1. Deduct from the local PTO plan that matches the worksite location GeoCode on State Rules (if one exists). Repeat until hours run out in the register. If this occurs, move on to the next step. 2. Continue deducting from any other local PTO plans that match the GeoCode and are associated with the employee. If none meet these criteria, proceed to the next step. 3. Look for state-level global PTO registers (no GeoCode range) assigned on the State Rules form. Deduct from any qualifying state PTO plans in order. If PTO hours are still required after all these deductions, the system generates a payroll failure or warning depending on the following settings: • Max Usage Limit Per Plan Year (Global PTO Benefit Plans form) • Stop Init If Exceed Limit (Global PTO Benefit Plans form)
