Chapter 6 Maintaining Employee Time Off Information Your organization can manually enroll employees in Time Off plans, enter absences, and adjust Time Off registers.

Manually Enrolling Employees in Time Off Register Use the Time Off Register Enrollment form to manually enroll employees in the Time Off register and set the starting hours. This is found in the HR menu under HR|Action. Note: You can create a new enrollment even if an employee has an archived register. Once you save the enrollment, PrismHR creates the register for the employee based on the accrual schedule and Time Off plan.

Note: To make changes to the employee’s Time Off register values, see Adjusting Accrued or Carryover Hours for Employees on page 107

To manually enroll employees in a Time Off register: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. Enter the Accrual Schedule used to track time off for this plan.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 102 Chapter 6 Maintaining Employee Time Off Information

  1. Enter the Time Off Plan in which to enroll the employee.

Note: PrismHR uses the Benefit Start Date to calculate the number of months the employee has worked for the client. The system uses this in conjunction with the rules defined for a Time Off plan to determine the number of hours the employee can earn during a given accrual period. The default is the employee’s last hire date, but you can change this.

  1. Enter the Benefit Start Date. The system uses this date to calculate the number of months that the employee has worked for the client. The default is the employee’s last hire date, but you can edit it as needed. See About Benefit Start Dates on page 103.
  2. Enter the Carryover Hours, which is the number of hours carried over from a previous accrual year. Typically, you would only enter this value when setting up the register for the first time.
  3. Enter the YTD Hours Calculated (+), which is the starting balance of Time Off hours accrued in the current year. Note: If you enroll an employee in a Time Off plan with an initial YTD Hours Calculated (+) (accrual amount) that is greater than the Max Per Year in the Time Off plan, a warning message displays in the Time Off Register Enrollment form when you enter the Calculated Thru Date, “Warning: no additional hours will be accrued because the initial amount is greater than the maximum accrual of hours set up in the Time Off plan.” To continue, click OK.
  4. Enter the YTD Hours Taken (-), which is the number of Time Off hours already used in the current year.
  5. Based on the entries, the YTD Hours Available (=) displays.
  6. Enter the Year End Date for the current year. The default comes from the plan’s setup.
  7. Enter the Calculated Thru Date, the date through which Time Off hours have been accrued. See Understanding the Calculated Thru Date Field on page 103 for more information on entering the correct date.
  8. Enter the Carryover Expires On date when the available carryover hours expire, if applicable.

About Benefit Start Dates The Benefit Start Date field dictates the calculation that the system uses. • You can only adjust the Benefit Start Date for employees enrolled in fiscal year registers. You cannot change it for anniversary-based registers. • When the eligibility for Time Off benefits is based on seniority level (the number of months worked), the system uses its calculation based on this date to determine the employee’s seniority level. • If the client’s Time Off register uses Anniversary Year End as the accrual schedule’s accrual calculation method, the system uses the date to calculate the Time Off register year-end date.

Understanding the Calculated Thru Date Field If the employee has accumulated Time Off hours prior to the initialization of this Time Off Register, you must enter the number of Time Off hours, any carryover hours available, and the date through which the hours were accrued.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 103 Chapter 6 Maintaining Employee Time Off Information

WARNING: If you do not enter the correct date in the Calculated Thru Date field, PrismHR may accrue excess hours for this employee.

It is critical that you enter the correct “accrued through” date in the Calculated Thru Date field. The system accrues any Time Off hours from this date forward, according to the terms of the absence Time Off plan and accrual schedule. To determine the date correctly, it is important to understand the client’s Time Off plan; that is, does it accrue increments of Time Off hours throughout the year, or perhaps deposit the whole amount at one time? For example, an employee has three vacation days available to her at the time you take on a particular client. The employee is not scheduled to accrue any more until January 1 of the following year. You must ensure the date you enter in the Calculated Thru Date field is December 31. The next time the register is triggered, whether the it is the next pay period, end of month, or another time, PrismHR will calculate the number of days between December 31 and the trigger date. During payroll processing, PrismHR automatically updates the employee’s Time Off register with any due accruals.

If you are going to update Time Off hours more frequently, such as when increments of time are deposited each payroll period, ensure you understand exactly what “accrued through” date the client used when they submitted the employee’s Time Off hours to you. Was it through the last day of the payroll period or through the pay date? You must determine the “accrued through” date with the client to ensure the employee’s Time Off register accrues correctly.

Processing Time Off Auto Register Enrollment The Time Off automatic enrollment process tests every employee against the eligibility rules (set up for the client in Time Off Auto Enroll Rules, found in the Client menu) and enrolls employees into absence benefits if they meet the eligibility criteria. Use the Time Off Auto Register Enrollment form as a quick way to build up a list of employees in a plan and assign them their first Accrued Thru Date. You would typically use this feature when you need to enroll existing employees in a new Time Off plan.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 104 Chapter 6 Maintaining Employee Time Off Information

To build up a list of employees in a plan and assign them: 1. If appropriate, enter the Benefit Start Date to override the default. The system uses this date to calculate the number of months that the employee has worked for the client. If you do not enter a date in the field, the system automatically calculates the date on which it would have begun for each employee. Note: The Benefit Start Date field will not override on registers where the Time Off Auto-Enroll Rule has either Seniority Date or Hire Date selected on the Use Seniority Date or Hire/Rehire Date? field. 2. In the Accrued Thru Date field, you should enter the date through which time off benefits would have previously been accrued. • When you enter a date, the system calculates each employee’s Time Off benefits from that date forward. • If you leave the date field blank, the system calculates each employee’s benefits from their date of hire through to today’s date. This is an extremely rare situation. Be sure that this is what you need to do, as it can impact payroll. Read How PrismHR Uses the Accrued Thru Date for Time Off BenefitsHow PrismHR Uses the Accrued Thru Date for Time Off BenefitsHow PrismHR Uses the Accrued Thru Date for Time Off Benefits to learn more. 3. Click Run. The system enrolls eligible employees in the plan, then displays a count of the employees who were enrolled. It also displays a list of any employees who were not enrolled and why.

  1. When you finish reviewing the information, click Close to exit the form or Cancel to clear the form and use it to run another enrollment process.

How PrismHR Uses the Accrued Thru Date for Time Off Benefits When it is time for payroll to send out paychecks, the system calculates Time Off benefits from the day after the last date through which the employee accrued benefits (the “accrued through” date) up through the period end date. For example, employees in the ABC Company are paid semi-monthly and were last paid on May 15. When they are paid on June 1, the system knows the accrued through date is May 15, so it calculates the Time Off benefits from May 16 through June 1.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 105 Chapter 6 Maintaining Employee Time Off Information

If your organization added ABC Company to PrismHR on May 20, you would want to automatically enroll the ABC employees in Time Off benefits. The system has never calculated payroll for these employees before, but its calculations require an “accrued through” date. You define the accrued through date as May 15, so the calculations result in a normal accrual cycle on June 1. Therefore, you use the Time Off Auto Register Enrollment form to not only automatically enroll the employees, you also define an Accrued Thru Date date for the system. When payroll processes the paychecks, the system determines the employees’ Time Off benefits from the day after the date you entered.

Entering Employee Absences Use the Employee Absence Entry form to enter employee absences from work. This is time off that will affect the employee’s Time Off register. This is found in the HR menu under HR|Change. You can: • Enter a paid absence: Sometimes salaried employees’ absences are not paid out on a time sheet, but they need to be subtracted from the Time Off register. When you use an absence code associated with a Time Off register, the system applies the hours as well as any comments you enter. • Enter an unpaid absence: Track absences for record-keeping purposes. There are reports that list unpaid absences. • Adjust “hours taken”: Adjust the total number of hours taken on the employee’s Time Off register. (To adjust the number of hours accrued or carried over, see Adjusting Accrued or Carryover Hours for Employees on the next page.)

Note: Absence Codes must exist before you can use the Employee Absence form.

To enter employee absences: 1. Enter the Employee ID by either typing the name or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records, or by clicking the field label to open the search window. 2. Select the Absence Code for this absence. 3. Enter the Date Absent, which is the day the employee was absent or the start date of the absence period if the absence spans multiple days. 4. Enter the total number of Hours Absent. 5. Enter a Comment for this absence, if applicable. For example, you can use this reference a specific voucher or event. 6. Click Save. The system generates the Journal ID when you save the absence entry.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 106 Chapter 6 Maintaining Employee Time Off Information

Adjusting Accrued or Carryover Hours for Employees You can use the Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form to adjust an employee’s number of accrued hours or carryover hours from a previous year. You can also adjust the accrued through date. This is found in the HR menu under HR|Change. Note the following when using the Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form: • Absence Codes must exist before you can use the Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form. • When you archive a register, you cannot adjust it. Therefore, to prevent you from making an adjustment to an archived register, these accrual schedules do not display as an option in the Accrual Schedule field.

Note: The system automatically assigns the Journal ID.

In addition, you can access the Time Off Register Adjustment Import form by clicking the Import icon ( ) that displays in this form. See Importing Time Off Adjustment Information on page 108 for more information.

To adjust an employee’s number of hours, do the following: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. Select the Time Off Accrual Schedule for this adjustment. 3. Enter the Effective Date, which is the day of the adjustment or the start date of the adjustment period if the adjustment spans multiple days. 4. Enter the Calculated Hours to add to the employee’s Time Off register. 5. Enter the Carry-Over Hours to add to the employee’s Time Off register. 6. Enter the Calculated Thru Date, which is the date through which you want to update the employee’s accrued through for the accrual schedule. Further accruals occur for payrolls with a pay date after this date. If you want to adjust only the date, enter zeroes in the hours fields. 7. Enter a Comment about the adjustment, if applicable. For example, you can use this reference a specific voucher or event. 8. Click Save.

Importing Time Off Adjustment Information You can use the Time Off Register Adjustment Import process to import time off adjustment information and to generate an error report and a transaction report. The time off adjustment information is imported using a comma-delimited, tab-delimited, or pipe-delimited text file that is created in Excel. Note: You can access the related report, Employee Time Off Detail Report. This report provides information about employees’ time off.

(Note: Only required if Adjustment Type ‘T’ is selected.) • Column 7 - Effective Date (MM/DD/YYYY). • Column 8 - Adjustment Hours. • Column 9 - Accrued Through (Optional). • Column 10 - Comment/Annotation (Optional). (Note: If you do not provide a comment, the default comment ‘Imported Adjustment’ displays in the Annotation column in the Employee Time Off Register form.) 2. Save the Excel file as a comma-separated values (CSV) file or plain text file. 3. Record the file name and where it was saved.

Obtaining Time Off Carryover Loss for Employees You can use the Employee Carryover Loss form to produce a report that displays time off carryover lost for each employee from the previous year. For example, if employees can carryover up to 40 hours of time off and an employee has 60 hours available at the end of the year, the report would display 20 hours of lost time off carryover. Note: The report that the Employee Carryover Loss form produces does not apply to global time off.

To obtain time off carryover lost for each employee: 1. On the Reports menu, select Employee Loss Carryover under Payroll|Reports. 2. Select the Accrual Schedule. 3. Select the Time Off Plan. 4. Enter or select the As Of Date. 5. Click Run. The Time Off Carryover Loss Report displays. For example:

The report columns are: • Employee ID: Employee ID. • Employee Name: Employee name. • Accrual Schedule: The Time Off accrual schedule. • Time Off Plan: The Time Off plan. • Carryover Lost: Amount of employee’s time off carryover lost since As Of Date.

Viewing the Job Control Status Report When a process is complete, you may have the option to access a Job Control Status report. This report shows the Job Number, the date and time when it started and stopped, and the job status. It also shows the date and time that each step in the process was executed. To open the Job Control Status report, click Report in the message that informs you that processing is complete. You have the following options: • Navigate through multiple pages using arrows to move forward, back, to the beginning, or to the end. • Go directly to a page by typing the page number in the Page box. • Enter search text in the Search box. Click Search Next to find the next occurrence. • In the Actions menu, select Print, Convert to PDF, or Print/PDF Pages. • Click XLS to export the report to Excel format and save it in your Downloads folder.

Performing an Employee Time Off Register Inquiry The Employee Time Off Register form displays paid time off for an employee, including the details of time accrued and taken. This form is found in the HR menu under HR|Change. You can also delete or archive a Time Off register for an employee using this form. The Time Off plan determines how much time off an employee will accrue, and the Time Off accrual schedule determines when the employee accrues time off. The employee’s Time Off register is where the system keeps track of the time off. It is a record of “credit” and “debit” transactions, and shows a running balance. Each time time off accrues, it is posted (credited) to the employee’s register; each absence is subtracted (debited) from the register. For example:

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 121 Chapter 7 Employee PTO Requests in EP

The drop-down lists only the plans in which the employee is currently enrolled. Note: If an employee is auto-enrolled in a Time Off plan, “Employee Auto Enrolled” displays. 3. Enter the Time Off Plan. Existing information for this employee displays in the form. • The rest of the top panel summarizes the Time Off plan information. • The Paid Hours Absent Details panel displays each absence taken. • The Hours Accrued/Carry-over Details panel displays each accrual earned by the employee. Note: If you change the Time Off Plan during the plan year ending pay period, you may need to make adjustments. 4. The Benefit Start Date displays the date that was selected when the employee was enrolled. The system uses this date to calculate the employee’s time off for this plan. Note: If you need to change this date, you can only change it for employees enrolled in time off with an Anniversary Year year-end basis plan in the following instances: • When there are no payroll-generated accruals (calculated hours). • When there are manually-entered accruals (calculated hours) or any other manual adjustments in the Employee PTO Register Adjustment form, the PTO Register Adjustment Import form, or the Employee

(See Entering Employee Absences on page 106.) • Make Employee Time Off Adjustments: Opens the Employee PTO Register Adjustment form to adjust the employee’s number of accrued hours or carryover hours from a previous year. You can also adjust the accrued through date. (See Adjusting Accrued or Carryover Hours for Employees on page 107.) • Manage Planned Time Off Requests: Opens the Planned Time Off Requests form, where you can review and make changes to employees’ time off requests. (See Working with Planned Time Off Requests on page 130.) Note the following about these shortcuts: • Only the forms you can access will display as shortcut links. For example, if you do not have access to the Employee Absence form, the Add an Employee Absence shortcut will not display. If you have no access or are denied access to both forms, the header and shortcuts do not display. • When you select a shortcut, the system automatically populates the selected employee in the form that opens. • After you make changes or adjustments in a form and click Save, when you close that form the adjustments immediately display in the Employee Time Off Register if the form is open to the same plan and register for those adjustments.
  2. If you want to terminate a Time Off register for an employee click Archive, which keeps an historical record of that register so you can refer to this information when seeking answers about what was done in the past. Note: You must select an Employee and Accrual Schedule to enable the Archive button. When you click Archive a warning displays stating that any pending Time Off request that have not been approved need to be manually removed using the Planned Time Off Requests form. Confirm this warning by clicking OK. Note: Archiving a Time Off register deletes the register’s Audit Log, so it is no longer available.

The report columns that display are based on the criteria specified in the form: • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first. • Employee: Employee ID. • Accrual Schedule: The paid time off type. • Start Date: The date the paid time off starts. • Accrued Thru: The date through which the paid time off is accrued. • Year End Date: The paid time off year end date. • Plan Description: The paid time off plan description. • Carryover: The amount of time carried over from a previous year. • Accrued: The amount of time accrued during this plan time frame. • Used: The amount of time used during this plan time frame. • Available: The amount of time carryover added to accrued minus the used time. • Date Taken: The date the paid time off was used. • Day Taken: The day the paid time off was used. • Reason: The reason given to use the paid time off. • Hours Used: The amount of time used for that date.

•    Location: The employee's location description.
•    Accrual Level: The accrual level entered.
•    Dept: The employee's department description.
•    Buyback Amount: The dollar amount the remaining paid time off is worth.
•    Hourly Rate: The employee's hourly rate.
•    Pay Group: The employee's pay group description.
•    YTD Accrued: The total time off hours the employee has accrued from the start of the plan year through
     the report date.
•    Payroll Equivalent: The dollar value of the employee's YTD accrued time off hours, calculated as accrued
     hours multiplied by the employee's hourly pay rate.

Chapter 8 Managers and Time Off in PrismHR When an employee submits a Time Off request, the manager/supervisor will receive in-product and e-mail notifications. The manager must log in to PrismHR (not Employee Portal (EP)) to manage their employees’ time off requests. Worksite managers and trusted advisors can view, approve, and cancel employee Time Off requests. Make sure everything is set up so that worksite users can manage employee Time Off requests. For more information, see Managers and Approvals.

Working with Planned Time Off Requests You can review and make changes to employees’ time off (PTO) requests in the Planned Time Off Requests form. The form is found in the HR menu under HR|Action. Important! The system circumvents leave approval security configurations and workflows for users with access to this form, which can result in unexpected behavior. Please note the following security used by this form: • Users with the PTO Administrator H/R Role and access to Manage Planned Time Off Requests can update leave for all employees in the client regardless of their Data Security access or the assigned PTO Approver. • Users without the PTO Administrator H/R Role and with access to Manage Planned Time Off Requests can update leave only for employees where the user has access via Data Security, regardless of the assigned PTO Approver.

Viewing Planned Time Off Requests The requests in the list are for employees at the active client who submitted them through Employee Portal (EP).

To view the planned time off requests for the client, do the following: 1. Go to the Planned Time Off Requests form. When the form opens, the following message displays, “Please wait while we get the leave requests.” (Note: This form defaults to the Display Pending and Display Approved options, so the system will display those entries.) 2. Use the filters at the top of the form to specify which requests to display. 3. If there is more than one page of results, the total number of pages displays above the results, and the Next Page and Previous Page buttons display at the bottom of the page. Long comments or multiple vouchers display additional lines on the form.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 130 Chapter 8 Managers and Time Off in PrismHR

Note: Each page displays up to 20 leave requests.

Making Changes to an Employee’s Time Off To make changes to an employee’s time off, you can: • Set an Approved request to Cancelled. • Set an Approved request to Paid. If you select Paid, then it is removed from this list and from any payrolls. • A yellow indicator displays next to the start date if it is before the period end date of the last completed scheduled payroll batch for the employee’s pay group. The system considers it to be a “back dated” request.

Time Off User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 131 Chapter 8 Managers and Time Off in PrismHR

The different statuses affect the system as follows:

Status Description Pending The Time Off request has not yet been approved, cancelled, or paid by the employee’s manager. Note: The request does not display on the timesheet in this status. Approved The Time Off request is approved and scheduled to be paid. Note the following: • If a manager cancels a Time Off request on this form and then the request is approved later on this form, the leave request indicator in the Summary Time Sheet Entry form is restored and the employee’s EP Time Off landing page displays the approved request. • The system does not record the user who approves a Time Off request as the leave approver in the Planned Time Off Requests form. Instead, the system displays the approver from the approval policy.

Cancelled The Time Off request is cancelled. This cancels an employee’s approved Time Off in the EP that occurs in the future. Note the following: • Canceling approved Time Off that occurs in the future stops the Time Off from being applied to the timesheet when it is created. • Canceling approved and applied Time Off on the current timesheet does not remove the indicator and the hours should be manually adjusted in the timesheet.

Paid The Time Off request was previously paid and the employee’s Time Off register was updated. Only service providers can select this option. Note: This status removes the leave request indicator from the timesheet and removes the request from the employee’s EP or Employee Portal (EP) Time Off landing page. It also hides the request from the Planned Time Off Requests form unless you choose to Display Paid.

Note: By default, worksite manager and trusted advisor users can only access employees who report to them, as indicated in the Employee Details Work tab. Users can be set to see all employees at the client that they are allowed to access by giving them the PTO Administrator account management role in the Users form. Note that if you want a user to be able to view requests but not approve them, the user role must have Inquiry permission for Planned Time Off Requests.

To view a planned time off request’s changes, click the Audit Log icon . The Audit Log Display opens, where you can click a log to display its changes.

Approvals Guide © 2026 PrismHR 3 Chapter 1 Approval Policy Setup

Chapter 1 Approval Policy Setup There are many places in PrismHR where actions require approvals before they are finalized. You need to set up approval policies as follows: • Ensure each approval policy specifies who must approve an action before it is finalized • Override global approval policies at the client level, and maintain policies for various approval types • Create custom HR approval roles for an Account Management (Service Providers) role or an HR Role (Worksite Managers/Trusted Advisors) • Establish the client’s payroll processing options

Setting Global Approval Policies There are many places in PrismHR where actions require approvals before they are finalized. Examples of this include new hires, pay rate changes, and client payroll approvals. Approval policies are defined at the global or client level. to learn about creating client-level approval policies. Each approval policy specifies who must approve an action before it is finalized. There are different approval levels. Client worksite personnel can approve actions (for example, a pay rate change entered for an employee by a departmental manager), and a service provider’s internal staff can approve actions. Approval policies might also require approval from both worksite and service provider users.

Note: Click View All Policies to view the policies defined for your organization, and select one to edit.

At the global level, policies for each approval type can be defined by service type. For example, you can define that all payroll approvals for PEO clients must be approved by any client worksite user who has the Payroll Authorizer role assigned to their user account.

Note: When service providers enter HR-related changes, those changes go through without requiring approvals. Only payroll-related processes made by service providers are subject to approval policies.

To set global approval policies: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select Global Approval Policies under System|Change. 3. Fill in the fields as required.

Setting Approval Policies Even if you have global approval policies, you can set approval policies at the client level. Using the Approval Policies form, you can maintain policies for several approval types. See also Global Approval Policies.

Note: You can click View All Policies in this form to view the policies defined for your organization and select one to edit.

Available Approval Types The following approval types are available: • Direct Deposit Change Approval Policy: This approval type uses the Direct Deposit Change option to require approval at the client or global level to store direct deposit information in the employee details record. For example:

Important! There must be a client-level or global-level approval policy in place to use this feature. (Without
an approval policy, the system immediately records any changes and applies them to the employee record.)
In addition, the approval policy only applies when an employee changes, adds, or removes the Transit
Number or Account Number in the direct deposit information.
When an approval policy is defined for a client using the Direct Deposit Change option and an employee,
worksite manager, or worksite trusted advisor submits a new or updated direct deposit or deletes a direct
deposit, the system sets the update to Pending status and an approval is required. (After approval, the direct
deposit follows the regular prenote process, if one is in place.) However, if a service provider makes an

Approvals Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Approval Policy Setup

update, the change does not go through an approval process and is immediately applied to the employee
record.
Note: The approval is submitted either from an employee making an update in Employee Portal or from a
worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor making an update in Employee Portal or in the Prism Core
application.
When an approval is pending and a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor tries to make a change,
the following occurs on the Deposit tab in the Employee Details form:
•    "Approval Pending" displays next to the Direct Deposit Information panel header.
•    If they select Save or Save & Close a message displays, "A prior direct deposit change is waiting for
     approval. Your updates will discard the previous changes. Do you wish to continue?" Click Yes to discard
     the previous update.

• Late Payroll Posting Approval Policy: This approval type stops payrolls from being posted on or after the Late Payroll Posting date and time during the finalization process, which prevents the payroll from finalizing until it is approved by a user in accordance with the applicable Approval Policy configuration. Note: To stop a payroll from finalizing, the client must have ACH billing configured on the Billing tab on the Client Details form by selecting one of the following statuses in the ACH Status field, Active, ACH by Division, or ACH by Location. In addition, the approval observes the positive or negative value in the Adjust to ACH Bill Day field, which adjusts the processing of the ACH if it is different from the employee pay date. • ACH Maximum Approval Policy: This approval type uses the ACH Maximum option, which you can configure using the Approval Policies form for a service provider. can view existing ACH Maximum Approval policies in read-only format and cannot make updates to the
policy setup.

Approvals Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Approval Policy Setup

• Client worksite personnel can approve actions (for example, a pay rate change entered for an employee by a departmental manager). • The internal staff of the service provider can approve actions. • Approval policies can also require approval from both worksite and service provider users.

Setting Up Approval Policies To set approval policies at the client level: 1. Go to the Approval Policies form on the HR|Change menu. 2. Select the Approval Type, which is the type of action that requires approval. 3. For each step, set one of the following: • Enter the PrismHR User ID, if the step requires that a specific user approve the action. • Specify the HR Role for worksite approvers. • Specify the A/M Role, which is the service provider account management role. When you include an A/M Role, you should select the A/M Filter from the drop-down as your organization’s security policy requires: • All Users with designated A/M role: Any user with the account management role can see the approvals. • Only A/M Assigned to Client: Only service provider users assigned to the client can see the approvals; the system checks the account assignment in the Client Details Account tab for the specified A/M Role and displays the approval for only that user.

Note: PrismHR automatically assigns a number to each approval step you select. The approvals are processed in that order.

where you can add the custom A/M Role or HR Role to the appropriate Approval Type. Once you create a

Setting Up Payroll Approval Your organization can set up the system so that the client can see the invoice and approve the payroll before it is complete. You can set approvals for both the initialization and finalization steps of the process.

Setting Up a Client for Payroll Calculation Approvals You do not need to define an approval policy to set the client to approve their payrolls.

To set up a client for payroll calculation approvals, do the following: 1. Go to the Client Details form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 2. Select the Control tab. 3. Select the Worksite Payroll Approval option to send an approval email after a payroll is calculated (initialized).

Setting Up an Approval Policy for Payroll Posting

To set up an approval policy for payroll posting, do the following: 1. You can set up approval policies for all clients or for the specific client. • To set up a system-level policy, go to the Global Approval Policies form. ( Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) • To set up a policy for the client, go to the Approval Policies form (found in the HR menu under HR|Change). Ensure that the correct client is selected. 2. If you are setting up a system-level policy, specify the Service Type. If you are setting up a client-level policy, continue to the next step. 3. From the Approval Type drop-down, select Payroll Finalization. 4. Define each of the users who need to approve the payroll when it is posted. (For example, you might specify the HR Role of Payroll Approver.) 5. Click Save.

Setting Up a User as a Payroll Approver

To make a user the client’s payroll approver, do the following: 1. Go to the Users form. (Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) 2. Enter the User ID of the user who will approve payrolls. If you are creating a new user account, enter the other information as needed. See the online help for the form or refer to the System Administration Guide for detailed instructions. 3. In Human Resources Roles, select Payroll Approver.

Defining Custom Message Templates for Approvals You can set up message templates to send for each kind of payroll approval for your organization to use instead of the system default. This allows you to customize the message.

To create a message template, do the following: 1. Go to the Message Templates form. (Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) 2. Enter the Subject line for emails that use this template. 6. Enter the Body of the message. You can incorporate HTML in the body of the message if you select the HTML format. 7. Click Save.

To use the template for approvals or finalization notices, do the following: 1. Go to the System Parameters form. (Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) 2. Open the Actions menu and then select Email Services. 3. Click + to add a new row.

You can change or reorder the columns as needed and the system displays messages to alert you to the impact that your edits will have. Use one of the following procedures to change or reorder the columns and get the results you want: • Changing Columns (page 14) • Reordering Columns (page 15) • Changing to a Different Type of Pay (page 15)

Changing Columns You can change the column from one pay code to another with the same earning type (such as cash). 1. In the Time Sheet tab of Client Details, edit one of the Pay Codes to change it to one for the same type of pay (for example, REG1 to REG2). 2. In the message “This action will replace pay code [REG1] with pay code [REG2] for all current summary time sheet records. These changes will occur when this form is saved. Do you wish to continue?” click the Yes button to reassign the values to the new pay code (for example, REG2).

Note: If you click No, the system does not change the pay code.

Reordering Columns If you want to rearrange the columns and, ultimately, keep the current hours assigned to the same pay codes they were before you changed the columns, follow these steps. 1. In the message “This action will replace pay code [REG3] with pay code [REG4] for all current summary time sheet records. These changes will occur when this form is saved. Do you still wish to do this [Yes], or move the values associated with the [REG3] to this new position [No]?”: • Click Yes to leave any values assigned to the new pay code (REG4). • Click No to assign any values back to the original pay code (REG3).

Changing to a Different Type of Pay If you need to change a pay code from one type of pay to another, you can only do so if there are no values entered in an active payroll. Examples are when you change to a pay code with a different calculation method or pay reason. • If there are no values, you can simply change the pay code. • When there are values in an active payroll, the system displays a message informing you that you need to use Payroll Control to delete and recreate the payroll. If that is what you need to do: 1. Open Payroll Control (found in the Payroll menu under Payroll|Change). 2. Enter the Payroll Number of the active payroll. 3. Click Delete. 4. In the confirmation message, click Yes. 5. Click Yes in the message to create a replacement payroll for the one you just deleted. 6. Return to the Client Details Time Sheet tab and change the pay code. 7. Users can proceed to enter data in the time sheet for the new pay code.

Note: If there are only a few values in the time sheet, you can simply delete them from the time sheet rather than deleting the entire payroll and creating a new one.

Chapter 2 Using the Approval Process When events take place that could potentially require an approval, such as a new hire or a payroll, PrismHR determines if there is a policy in place for the particular approval type. • If there is no policy definition, then the system immediately updates the database with the new hire or other information. • If there is an approval policy, then the system generates an approval event. If the first step for the approval is assigned to a particular user, then an e-mail is sent to that user. In addition, when the user logs in, the dashboard alerts the user of any pending approvals. Approvals Pending is found in the Client menu under Client|Action.

Working with Pending Approvals The Approvals Pending form lists any pending approvals that are assigned or available to you. • An approval that is assigned to a particular user can only be acted upon by that user. • Approvals are available to a user if one of the user’s roles matches the role applicable to the current approval step. Note: Click the Refresh button to remain on the same form or report while refreshing the window to display new entries. Note the following when working with pending approvals: • Existing employees and newly-entered new hires who have a preferred name display that name on the Approvals Pending form and associated approval forms. In this situation, the system uses the employee’s assigned preferred name instead of their legal first name. • If the employee does not have a preferred name, the system uses their first name, last name. • I-9 Section 2 and Pay Card approvals, or any approval associated with a pre-hire, display the employee’s legal first and last name even if a preferred name is available. • For Late Payroll Posting Approval Policies (see Setting Approval Policies and Setting Global Approval Policies for information about this policy): • When a Late Payroll Posting pending approval is approved: • The associated payroll batch status updates from POSTPEND > INITCOMP. • The Approval status is Approved.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction Background Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a 2019-2021 pandemic caused by the virus SARS-CoV-2. In March of 2020, the United States government began passing legislation to help mitigate the economic effects of the viral outbreak. From March onward, PrismHR began introducing features to help service providers comply with these new legislative requirements.

Note: The information in this section is included to help place the new COVID-19 features in their proper context. This section is not an exhaustive summary of these federal acts and their provisions.

Families First Coronavirus Response Act (FFCRA) The first legislative initiative took effect on April 1, 2020 and applies to employers with fewer than 500 employees, with some exceptions. It establishes special expansions to family medical leave and paid sick leave for employees affected by the COVID-19 outbreak. These payments can all be rebated, up to certain limits, by the federal government. The PrismHR COVID-19 features include logic that helps determine how these rebate credits accrue.

PrismHR Features Using the new, system-level COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters form, you can designate special pay codes and billing events to track COVID-related employee sick and medical leave. When you run a payroll batch that includes these pay codes, the system calculates the accrued (and remaining) rebate credits for each type of leave. It creates Client Bill Pending items associated with each type of rebate credit and, if any credits remain after the client rebate is applied, the system stores these credits in a carry-forward bill pending entry. The underlying logic can be adjusted at the system level. You can also view and adjust these bill pending entries in the system, if needed. Please note the following characteristics of the new Families First feature set: • Creditable wages paid under the sick leave and FMLA pay codes accrue under the following tax deduction codes: 00-80 (FMLA) and 00-81 (Sick time, self-care and dependent-care). The system uses these codes to track tax credits associated with these wages. • Medicare taxes associated with these creditable wages accrue under tax deduction code 00-82. Employers are entitled to a credit on all employer-side medicare taxes associated with these creditable wages.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 1 Chapter 1 Introduction

•    The system uses payroll warnings and hard stops to enforce wage cap limits, credit cap limits, and auto-
     rebate logic based on your configuration.

CARES Act The CARES (Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security) Act was also passed by the United States government in response to the 2019-2020 coronavirus pandemic. It provides financial support to both individuals and businesses affected by the pandemic. This support includes payments to taxpayers, expanded unemployment benefits, and payroll tax credits for businesses (see the section below). Businesses can claim tax credit on 50% of employee wages paid between March 13 and December 31, 2020. There is a cap of $5,000 credit per employee (equivalent to $10,000 in wages paid between these dates). Additional legislation at the beginning of 2021 updated these values to 70% of employee wages and $7000 credit per employee. This currently applies between 1/1/2021 and 7/1/2021. Both acts also establish rebates associated with healthcare-related payments. The system records rebate credits under tax deduction code 00-83 for this piece of legislation.

Paycheck Protection Program The CARES Act also implemented the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), which provides 100% federally guaranteed loans, backed by the Small Business Administration, to small businesses with financial need. It provides an incentive for small businesses to retain their employees during coronavirus-influenced economic turbulence. Businesses can use the PPP to cover payroll and employee benefit costs (up to $100,000 in payroll expenses per employee), as well as mortgage interest payments, rents, and utility costs, to a certain extent. From this loan program, small businesses can claim 2.5 times their 2019 monthly average payroll costs OR 10 million dollars (whichever is less). Seasonal employers calculate their average monthly costs using one of two lookback periods: • February 15, 2019 – June 30, 2019 • March 1, 2019 – June 30, 2019

PPP Loan Forgiveness To qualify for full PPP loan forgiveness, businesses must demonstrate that their full-time equivalency count did not decrease when compared to a provided lookback period. They must also indicate their use of loan funds for payroll and other costs.

August 8 Executive Order On August 8, President Trump authorized “Memorandum on Deferring Payroll Tax Obligations in Light of the Ongoing COVID-19 Disaster,” which instructs the Treasury to provide guidance on employee deferral of Social Security taxes between September 1 and December 31, 2020. PrismHR implemented basic functionality to support this deferral. You can use Paycheck Protection Program Reports in PrismHR to determine your clients’ loan forgiveness details. One report breaks down your PPP-related payroll costs. Another displays a breakdown of your monthly full-time equivalents.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 2 Chapter 1 Introduction

2021: Extensions to the CARES Act and the FFCRA In late 2020 and early 2021, Presidents Trump and Biden authorized legislation extending the benefits of the CARES Act and the FFCRA, respectively. The first round of legislation emerged from the Bipartisan-Bicameral Omnibus COVID Relief Deal and extended the expiration of CARES Act credits until March 31, 2021. The second round, passed in March 2021 as the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, extended the expiration of FFCRA credits and expanded their original caps. It also implemented some extensions to the CARES Act’s Employee Retention Credit and introduced new benefits for affected workers, such as fully-subsidized COBRA coverage for employees who lost their insurance during the pandemic.

Response and Interpretation PrismHR’s development approach was based around the following assumed requirements: • Reset COVID-19 wage, credit, and hour caps, such that on April 1 2021, any employee who previously used qualified sick leave would once again be able to claim the full amount of hours/wages allotted by the act. • Add support for a new employer Social Security tax credit. • Orient credit calculation toward charge dates. In other words, the prior legislation’s rules and limits would apply to sick leave taken on March 31, regardless of pay date. For example, if an employee took sick leave that was charged for March 31, but that employee was not paid until April 10th, they should accumulate sick leave credits under the old legislation because the charge date falls before April 1.

Important Setup Procedures

Currently, its default value is 03/31/21. Handling Split payrolls based on These new features assume that the legislative changeover will payrolls whether charge dates fall emphasize charge dates, rather than pay dates, for credit within the before or after April 1, and calculation purposes. Recall that the new SS Credit Start Date field refers to pay dates, not charge dates. (The Medicare Credit changeover strategically adjust the new End Date field also applies to pay dates, but is not relevant to period. start/stop dates to ensure this example). proper credit calculation. If you will be paying employees in a single batch with a pay period that extends between March and April, you may be able to perform the following steps: 1. Separate the payroll into two pay periods: one containing March charge dates and the other containing April charge dates. 2. Adjust the SS Credit Start Date to be sometime later in April. 3. Run the payroll for your March pay period. This will ensure that tax credits calculate correctly on March (pre-ARPA) charge dates. 4. Finally, reset the start and end dates to their appropriate values and run your April batch to begin compliance with the new legislation. This strategy is especially useful if your first April charge dates will fall significantly later than April 1, as it will provide more time for you to make the appropriate calculations and wrap up your pre-ARPA payrolls without worrying about the April 1 deadline.

Finally, we suggest that you use each pay code’s Conditional Rules to create a new custom payroll warning. Associate these warnings with both your old and new COVID-19 pay codes during the changeover period (see the example below). This can help raise the profile of these pay codes for payroll staff and serve as a reminder that the changeover is in progress.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 4 Chapter 1 Introduction

Important Notes About Tax Reporting The COVID-19 legislation defines the ways in which businesses can claim tax credits for wages paid as coronavirus-related sick/medical leave. PrismHR uses several system-defined tax deduction codes to track the accumulation of these “qualified” wages, taxes calculated on based on those wages, and associated benefit plan costs.

2021: Updates to Tax Credit Caps The new COVID-19 legislation resets the accumulation of tax credits for coronavirus-related paid leave; in PrismHR, this means the caps will reset for the following system-defined tax deduction codes: • 00-81 (COVID-19 Paid Sick Leave — Wage credit) • 00-82 (Credit for Medicare tax on qualified wages) • 00-84 (Benefit plan costs associated with COVID-19 Paid Sick and Family Leave) PrismHR will begin accumulating the tax credits against this reset cap for all charge dates from April 1, 2021 onward. The new 00-80 tax credit cap will also be increased to $12,000 from $10,000 as specified by the legislation. Please note that, unlike the credits listed above, the accumulation of this credit will not reset to $0 on April 1.

Updating Medicare and Social Security Tax Credit Settings When the new regulations take effect on April 1, our understanding is that there will be a new credit for Social Security tax, which can be associated with employee qualifying wages. Because of variations in interpretation, PrismHR also allows you to specify a pay date upon which 00-82 (Medicare tax) credits will stop accruing. To set this date, use the new Medicare Credit End Date field on the COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters form.

PrismHR also implemented a new tax deduction code: 00-87. This code will track the accumulation of the new Social Security tax credit on payroll vouchers. You can set up a SS Credit Start Date and a SS Credit Billing Event on the COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters form. The start and end dates are based on pay dates, not

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 Introduction

charge dates; this will allow service providers to organize their payroll batches and pay them in such a way that pre- and post-ARPA credit accumulations are handled separately.

Note: Previously, the instructions below specified that the new pay codes should have a tax exemption set up for Medicare tax. This has now changed. Do not apply any tax exemptions to these pay codes.

Finally, service providers will need to set up new pay codes from which the tax credits will be calculated. You can add these pay codes to the existing tables on the COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters form. The Emergency Paid Sick Leave (Self-Care) Pay Code table now supports multiple values to accommodate this. The new pay codes you create should be exact replicas of the old ones, except with no tax exemptions. As with the previous pieces of COVID-19 legislation, some of these features and descriptions are subject to change as further guidance becomes available.

New Tax Codes The system uses the following new tax deduction codes to track the various COVID-19 rebate credits. Note that benefit cost credits are distributed between two tax deduction codes corresponding to the Families First Act and the CARES Act.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Introduction

Tax Code Description 00-86 Social Security Tax Deferral 00-87 Social Security Tax Credit (replaces 00-82 under the newer American Rescue Plan Act).

These tax deduction codes populate on the MasterTax PTS download. You can also apply tax adjustments to them in the system. As with all other federal tax deduction codes, the system tracks these at the employer level. This is a purposeful decision to align the tax credits with their Form 941 tax liability. However, Families First tax credits will apply to — and will ultimately be reported at — the client level. According to IRS Form 7200, all PEOs with clients claiming tax credit must complete Schedule R (client-by-client breakdown) with their Form 941 return. Additionally, the CARES Act permits certain distressed businesses to defer their employer-side OASDI (Social Security tax) payments. Statutory language clearly establishes this is a client-level election, despite PEO reporting at the employer level.

About Tax Code 00-86 To comply with the August 8th Executive Order, “Memorandum on Deferring Payroll Tax Obligations in Light of the Ongoing COVID-19 Disaster,” PrismHR introduced tax deduction code 00-86 to track employee Social Security tax deferrals, which are permitted under the order between September 1 and December 31, 2020. For all employees who defer this tax on payrolls between these dates, the system generates a 00-86 entry. The entry is equal to the negative of the employee’s 00-12 tax value. Values stored under 00-86 accrue on either the client federal entity or employer tax register, whichever is used to store other federal tax data. The system also reports this data on the MasterTax PTS file under an E or F code, as appropriate.

Passing Tax Credits Into MasterTax Note: Under our traditional PEO configuration, credits accrue in MasterTax on the employer level. This means that aggregate client credits will reduce the PEO employer’s 941 liability and deposits. This could result in billing and deposit inconsistencies on a payroll-to-payroll basis. You will also be unable to track these credits appropriately in MasterTax.

MasterTax created three new core tax deduction codes to support the Families First and CARES Acts: • FE0000-116 Federal - Employer Sick Leave Wages Credit • FE0000-117 Federal - Employer Family Leave Wages Credit • FE0000-118 Federal - Employer Employee Retention Credit MasterTax users must map the three PrismHR tax deduction codes to the MasterTax deduction codes as follows:

Within MasterTax, users can toggle whether individual clients defer employer Social Security payments under the CARES act. However, under a traditional PEO configuration, the applicable federal tax data will not exist at the client level. As a result, users will be unable to leverage this setting. We recommend the following two solutions to this issue:

PrismHR Solution Options

Use SBEA Certified PEO Setup In PrismHR, you can enable our CPEO functionality, which was developed to support Schedule R reporting under the Small Business Efficiency Act (SBEA). This configuration enables you to: • Break out federal taxes by client, by employer. • Pass this federal tax data to MasterTax on that level. • Accrue and track credits on the client level and deposit accordingly. • Flag clients in MasterTax for employer-side OASDI deferral. This is the preferred approach if you want the most accurate, consistent, and automated tax management and reporting.

Note: Before you start, please note that it will take time to set up these features. You can consult the PrismHR Customer Support Team and the SBEA User Guide for details about enabling SBEA-compliant functionality. You can find a COVID-specific SBEA setup guide by searching for “SBEA User Guide” in the PrismHR Customer Resource Center.

If you decide to use this solution and you are a non-certified PEO, or if you want to start leveraging this configuration mid-year, we strongly recommend setting the Limit testing on Employer Register flag immediately after flagging the employer as a CPEO.

Self-Manage Tax Settings Users who opt not to leverage CPEO Schedule R functionality can elect to preserve the employer-level configuration within MasterTax and pass these tax credits on that level. Alternatively, users opting not to leverage CPEO Schedule R functionality, who nonetheless want to preserve a client-centric approach in MasterTax, must then self-manage this process. To prevent certain tax deduction codes from flowing into MasterTax, you can enable the Suppress Reporting to MasterTax setting as shown in the images below. Neither of these options will organically generate a Schedule R through MasterTax. However, to better support all users, including MasterTax users, PrismHR also developed the 941 Quarterly Return Worksheet Report to provide some insight into the COVID-19/Form 941 reporting process.

Recording Education Loan Payments Under the CARES Act Use the following guidance to provide support for qualifying education loan payments made to (or on the behalf of) employees, as defined under the CARES Act and as extended under the 2021 Consolidated Appropriations Act.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Introduction

Background The CARES Act (2020) expanded the IRS definition of “educational assistance” to include qualifying payments made by employers toward employee educational loans, specifically between March 27, 2020 and January 1, 2021. In early 2021, the Consolidated Appropriations Act extended this time period through January 1, 2025. The maximum qualifying contribution, per employee per year, is $5250. These payments do not increase the gross taxable income of the employee. This article provides a helpful history and summary of these provisions.

Solution To provide support for this legislative requirement in PrismHR, create a new pay code exempt from all federal taxes and with an annual maximum of $5250.00.

To track these education loan payments in PrismHR: 1. Click the Back Office menu and select System|Change > Pay Codes. 2. Fill out the required form fields, as appropriate for the type of education payment you need to track. 3. Set the pay code maximum: click Actions menu > Maximums. 4. In the table, set the Basis to Annual. 5. Set the Maximum Earnings amount to 5250.00. 6. Click Save to return to the Pay Codes form. 7. Finally, exempt the pay code from all federal taxes: click Actions menu > Tax Exemptions. 8. Specify the following tax exemption settings in the table. When you finish, click Save to return to the Pay Codes form.

Chapter 2 Setting Up Core Features This chapter demonstrates how to configure the primary COVID-19 processing utilities in PrismHR. Please carefully read the introductory sections to ensure proper system preparation.

Before You Begin Before configuring any COVID-19-specific settings, ensure that you have set up all the appropriate pay codes, billing codes, and billing events.

Note: You do not need to set up any new PTO plans for these features. But if you want to do so, you can.

Background In order to claim and properly account for the tax credits specified under the Families First/CARES Acts and the ARPA, you need to create spaces in the system to track each component of the payments and their credits: • Billing Event Codes: for tracking client-level credit rebates on invoices. • Billing Events: to trigger the recording of qualified wage and tax credits, for invoicing purposes. • Pay Codes: for paying any COVID-related wages that qualify for tax credits. • Accounting Settings (not addressed in this document). After creating pay codes for the different types of COVID-19 qualified wages, you should also mark them as exempt from employer-side Social Security taxes (tax deduction code 00-16).

Setting Up Billing Codes for COVID-19-Related Leave You must set up billing codes to track coronavirus-related credits. We recommend using the same setup as the standard tax billing code.

To set up a COVID-19 billing code: 1. Open the Back Office menu. 2. Select Billing Codes under System|Change. 3. Enter a unique Bill Code ID, such as COVID19. 4. If you want, enter a Bill Description. 5. Save the record.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 2 Setting Up Core Features

  1. Repeat for the second bill code.

Setting Up Billing Events for COVID-19-Related Leave You must also set up billing events and associate them with the new billing codes. These events are assigned on the system-level COVID-19 parameters, described later.

To set up a COVID-19 billing event: 1. Open the Back Office menu. 2. Select Billing Events under System|Change. 3. Enter a unique Bill Event Code, such as COVID19. 4. If you want, enter a Description. 5. Select the appropriate Bill Code to associate with this event. 6. Save the record. 7. Repeat for the second billing event.

Setting Up Pay Codes for COVID-19-Related Leave You must set up pay codes to track COVID-19 “qualified” wages. If you have pay codes for state-mandated sick leave in your system, we recommend using those as a model. The procedure below provides general setup information for an example pay code.

To create pay codes specific to COVID-19 leave: 1. Open the Back Office menu. Select Pay Codes under System|Change. 2. On the Pay Codes form, enter a new Pay Code ID, such as COVIDSELF. 3. Enter a Pay Description. 4. Set the Pay Type to Regular. 5. Set the Pay Class to Earnings. 6. For Cash/Non-Cash, select Cash. 7. Set the Calculation Method to Standard. 8. Set the Pay Reason to Hours. 9. For Subject to Work Comp, select Yes, This Pay Code is Subject to W/C. 10. Enter the appropriate Factor. We recommend 0.67. 11. For the Bill Code, enter 000 (Gross Wages). 12. Save the record. Repeat this procedure for all the other pay codes.

You do not need to apply any tax exemptions to ARPA-related pay codes. Important: This exemption still applies after you go over the wage limits. This can be highly problematic. Use extreme caution to avoid exceeding the mandated wage caps.

Important Notes Please note the following about this feature: • You can use this form to assign CARES Act-specific pay codes to the client. • Tax credits will accrue on employees who are paid with the specified pay codes. • They stop accruing once they reach the $5,000 employee limit. • Medicare tax is not credited. • These tax deduction codes populate on both the employer registers and (if SBEA functionality is enabled) the client federal entity registers. • Wage and credit limits are not applied. • If you select the 941 Liability rebate option on the system-level COVID-19 settings, CARES Act credits will be rebated along with Families First Act credits. All these credits are compared with the client’s 941 liability during rebate calculation. • If you assign pay codes with a non-Standard Calculation Method, the system uses Hours Paid (instead of Hours Worked) to calculate CARES Act credits for that employee. • Credit limits were adjusted to conform with new legislation. • Use the ERC Exclusion Dates to disable credit accrual for one or more date ranges. • The COVID-19 Credit Recalculation Utility also respects ERC Exclusion Dates. It zeros out any CARES credits on vouchers found within those date ranges. • The system no longer calculates employer retention credits on employees flagged as business owners. If you still want to perform these calculations, you can enable the Calculate ERC for Owners setting.

Procedure To configure the system for CARES Act compliance: 1. On the system-level COVID-19 settings, assign a billing event to the new Emergency Employee Retention Credit Billing Event field. 2. Click Client and select Client Details under Client|Change. 3. Click the Actions menu and select COVID-19 Client Parameters. 4. In the Emergency Retention Credit Pay Codes list, select all pay codes you set up to track CARES Act compliance. 5. If you need to disable 00-83 and 00-85 credit accrual for certain date ranges (for example, your organization took out a PPP loan), enter the appropriate date ranges in the ERC Exclusion Start and End Date fields. Set the Category for each date range to Cares. 6. Save the record.

Using the COVID-19 Leave Estimate Report This report retrieves employee hours and payment information to help you set up emergency paid leave that complies with the Families First Coronavirus Response Act.

To run this report: 1. If you want to filter by Employee Type or Pay Method, select the appropriate option(s). 2. If you want to filter by employee, select the appropriate Employee(s). 3. Click Run. The report generates.

Analyzing the Report For each employee, the report returns: • General employee information (employee number, name, type, pay method, and hire date). • Hours Worked (total and two-week average). Does not include sick time hours. • Standard Hours (2 weeks). Uses the Standard Hours value on Employee Details > Pay, adjusted based on the employee’s pay method. For example, the value for employees on a monthly pay cycle is:

•    Sick Leave Hours (Suggested, Actual, Taken, and Remaining). Suggested hours default to 80 for full-
     time employees. For part-time employees, the value is their two-week average unless the employee was
     hired within the last 6 months. In that case, the value is just the employee's Standard Hours on
     Employee Details > Pay. You can override the Actual Sick Leave Hours value using a new field on
     Employee Details > Other, called COVID-19 Paid Sick Max Hours.
•    Rates of Pay and 2/3 these values, in compliance with the legislation. The Standard value pulls from
     Employee Details. The Average (Last Pay Period) value is calculated using data from the last pay period.
     The system divides wages by hours, adjusted according to any FLSA settings on the employee's pay
     codes. If no FLSA settings exist, the system simply divides all gross payments to the employee by the
     number of hours.

Establishing Tax Credit Caps and Other Settings (Updated for 2021) You can configure credit cap settings according to your organizational needs. Refer to the following table for descriptions of the fields and their settings. See the sections below for an outline of the FFCRA’s tax credit limits.

CARES Act Employer Retention Credit Rules Please note the following important details about the Employer Retention Credit under the CARES Act: • In 2020, the CARES Act allowed businesses to claim tax credit on 50% of employee wages and healthcare benefit costs paid between March 13 and December 31, 2020. The cap per employee was $5,000 (equivalent to $10,000 in wages paid between these dates). • In 2021, new legislation updated these values to 70% of employee wages and $7000 total. The system performs these calculations automatically for 2021 pay dates, while 2020 pay dates retain the calculation logic described above. The system also tracks credits related to health care benefit payments and employer-side Social Security tax deferrals. For more information, see the field-level descriptions below, as well as the sections below called Deferring Employer-Side Social Security Taxes and Note About Health Care Credits.

2021 FFCRA Credit Rules In March 2021, the legislation governing FFCRA credits was extended. Beginning on April 1, 2021, the system will respect the following qualified wage caps: • FMLA: $12,000 (credit accumulation does not reset) • Sick (Dependent-Care): $2000 or $5110 minus credits from Sick (Self-Care), whichever is less • Sick (Self-Care): $5110 minus credits from Sick (Dependent-Care)

2020 FFCRA Credit Rules

Aggregate • FMLA: $10,000 • Sick (Dependent-Care): $2000, or $5110 minus credits from Sick (Self-Care), whichever is less • Sick (Self-Care): $5110, minus tax credits associated with Sick (Dependent-Care) • If an employee works 8 hours or fewer in a day, there is a cap of $200 per day

Daily (2020) • FMLA: $200 per time sheet line item • Sick (Dependent-Care): $200 per time sheet line item

Default Wage Cap Logic COVID-19 legislation specifies the legal extent to which employers must compensate workers for coronavirus- related leave. Employers can pay employees more than the specified amounts, but they will only receive credit up to the defined limits. Select whether to Cap Aggregate Limits Only or to Cap Daily and Aggregate Limits, both of which are specified in the legislation (see the summaries above). These settings reduce employee pay to the appropriate limits if it exceeds those limits. While we strongly recommend against using this setting in general, you can also select No Limits if you don’t want employee pay reduced in this way.

Default Tax Credit Cap Logic Select whether to enforce the federally defined tax credit caps. You can limit based on either the daily and aggregate or daily cap. You should use the same setting as Default Wage Cap Logic.

Default Suppress Client Rebate The client’s tax credit rebate is reflected as a separate Client Bill Pending entry in an invoice line item. The line item shows the total credits accumulated this pay period, along with the client rebate associated with this invoice. If the entire rebate is not owed at once, the system tracks rebates that are owed and that can presently be taken, based on the limit logic you defined in the above fields. If you don’t want the system to automate the rebate process as described above, select this option. Otherwise, leave this field alone and select an option for Default Client Tax Credit Rebate Cap Logic below.

Default Client Tax Credit Rebate Cap Logic Use this setting to determine the logic the system employs when calculating client credit rebates rebates. There are three options: No Limits, Cap at Client QTD 941 Liability, and Cap at Payroll Batch 941 Liability. The first option simply applies the full rebate to the client. However, we recommend using one of the other two settings. These settings only rebate clients up to their 941 liability (either quarter-to-date or for the current payroll batch). In other words, the amount available to rebate for a payroll = 941 Liability minus system-generated rebates, for the quarter or batch. Medicare tax calculation is included in the total client 941 liability, but is rebated separately. If the rebate for a payroll batch is higher than the 941 limit, the system creates a client bill pending entry with a date of 10/14/2241 for the amount left over after reaching the limit. The choice of date is meant to completely prevent the entry from being pulled into the next payroll run. • No Limits: Rebate the client for the full claimable credit amount for this payroll. The rebate is not reduced according to any rules or restrictions. • Cap at Client QTD 941 Liability: The system will only rebate the client up to the amount calculated for their 941 liability (quarter-to-date).

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 19 Chapter 2 Setting Up Core Features

•    Cap at Payroll Batch 941 Liability: The system only rebates the client up to the amount calculated as
     941 liability for that payroll batch.

For example, if you select the third option and you have $1,000 in creditable wages/ $50 in Medicare tax for a payroll and, in this payroll, you have $2,000 in un-rebated 941 liability, you can rebate the full $1,000 for the payroll because there is enough liability to rebate against. The $50 Medicare rebate is deducted separately.

Default Calculate Health Care Credit Select this option if you want the system to calculate healthcare credits for all clients as defined by the CARES Act.

Medicare Credit Limited to Tax Amount This option is enabled by default. Select this option if you want the system to calculate Medicare tax credits (00-82) as either 1.45% of the accrued Families First credits OR the actual employer Medicare tax amount on the associated voucher (whichever is less). This is the default system logic.

If you do not select this option, the system calculates this credit only using the first strategy, taking the credits accrued under 00-80 and 00-81 and multiplying them by 1.45%. This is the logic implied by the draft Form 941.

Exclude EE S125 Contributions If enabled, the system does not include employee-side contributions to Section 125 plans when determining the healthcare credit.

Note: If you select this option, the system also excludes employee-side FSA plan contributions from the healthcare credit calculation. If you want to include these contributions (the standard system logic), leave this option unselected.

COVID-19 Scheduled Wage Allocation

Note: This logic also applies when you run the COVID-19 Recalculation tool (see Recalculating COVID-19 Credits Retroactively).

In the system, 00-80 and 00-81 credits accrue on sheltered wages. This can affect the values in boxes 5a(i) and 5a(ii) of Form 941, potentially implying that the employee went over the tax limit when they did not. You can use this option to determine how the system handles sheltered wages related to COVID-19 payments. Select None if you want to preserve previously described system behavior and continue including sheltered wages in these calculations. Otherwise, select one of the other options below. • Cap Wage Credits if Sheltered: This option caps COVID-19 wage credits at qualified wages by limiting the credit to 00-12 taxable wages. Generally, this may result in a reduction for Sheltered Earnings. More specifically, the system first takes employee COVID wages and compares them to taxable earnings on the employee voucher. The lesser of these two values becomes the new 00-81 credit amount. The system then subtracts the employee’s 00-81 credits from their taxable earnings and compares this value to their 00-80 credits. The lesser of these two values becomes the new value for 00-80. For 00-83

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 2 Setting Up Core Features

     credits, the system subtracts the employee's 00-80 and 00-81 credits from their taxable earnings and
     multiplies this value by 0.5. If this value is less than the employee's current 00-83 credits, it replaces that
     value as the 00-83 credit.
•    Cap and Allocate to Health Care: The same calculation as described above, but the system also takes
     the amount reduced from the qualified wages above and adds that amount to the newly calculated 00-
     84 and 00-85 values, as appropriate (e.g. the Families First credit adjustment is added to 00-84 and the
     CARES credit adjustment is added to 00-85).

Use Bill Amount for Taxes Select this option if you want to use the value in the Bill Amount column (under the Billing Voucher Payroll Tax tab) when displaying taxes on the Payroll Cost Report. Otherwise, the system uses the tax liability as displayed on the employee voucher.

Bill to Highest COVID Wages Select this option if you want the system to assign COVID-related bill pending items to the worksite location/division/department that has the most COVID-related wages, instead of the location with the most wages in general.

COVID19 Wages on W2 Select this option if you want to display labeled 00-80 and 00-81 qualified wages in Box 14 of employee Forms W-2. The values for 00-81 are further broken down and labeled depending on whether they are associated with dependent care or self care. If you create employee Forms W-2 with this option enabled, the system first checks the pay code parameters above to determine which pay codes correspond to self care leave and dependent care leave. The system then checks the employee’s pay history for the year. If the employee was paid under both pay codes, the system allocates the employee’s pay proportionally on the W-2. If the employee was only paid under one of the pay codes, all 00-81 wages are allocated to the appropriate 00-81 category.

COVID-19 Processing Stop Date Enter the date when you want to the system to stop calculating COVID-19-related credits. The system default is December 31, 2021. Additionally, when FFCRA pay codes are used on charge dates following 09/30/21, the system will generate payments and credits of $0, by default. Payroll warning will also reflect this.
