Tracking Healthcare Payment Credits Logic PrismHR uses two tax deduction codes to track healthcare credits:

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 24 Chapter 2 Setting Up Core Features

•    00-84: Families First Act healthcare credits
•    00-85: CARES Act healthcare credits

Because these credits accrue under two different pieces of legislation, the system uses special logic to calculate and allocate them: 1. Calculates standardized healthcare costs and hours across a given payroll. 2. Adds FSA plan costs for that payroll to the standardized value. 3. Determines the percentage of hours worked under each act (vs. Standard Hours) and allocates credits to the appropriate tax deduction codes, according to these percentages.

The table below includes descriptions of each calculation step, along with the credit cap logic for each act. Note that aspects of this calculation may be impacted by the settings you configured on the system-level COVID-19 parameters form (see above).

Calculation Description Element (Step 1) The system compiles all monthly billing-side costs of any employee plans with an insurance Standardized class of Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, and Short/Long-Term Disability. Healthcare If the plan is flagged as a Section 125 plan, the system includes the full billing amount Cost (employee-side and employer-side). Otherwise, the system only uses the employer Calculation contribution. It then multiplies this sum by 12 to get an annual standardized cost, and then, to get a per- batch cost, divides this value by the number of pay cycles per year for that employee (for example, 52 for a weekly employee or 26 for a biweekly employee). (Step 2) This value is not standardized. Instead, it is handled on a batch-by-batch basis. FSA Plans For a given payroll batch, if the employee has an FSA plan flagged as a healthcare plan, the system takes the standardized healthcare cost (calculated above) and adds the FSA plan’s cost for that payroll (both employer and employee contributions). (Step 3) The system calculates the percent to allocate to each tax deduction code, based on the hours Allocating worked under Families First pay codes and CARES Act pay codes. Costs to the Appropriate Tax Codes For each act, the system divides the hours worked under that act’s pay codes by the employee’s Standard Hours (found on Employee Details). The resulting fraction is multiplied by the total healthcare costs for the payroll, and that amount is allocated to the appropriate act’s tax deduction code.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 25 Chapter 2 Setting Up Core Features

Calculation Description Element Cap Logic For tax deduction code 00-84 (Families First healthcare credit), there is no cap on the amount (Families First of healthcare credits you can accrue. However, healthcare credits stop accruing once you Act) reach the employee’s wage cap as defined under the act.

Cap Logic Healthcare credits stop accruing once the combined amounts in tax deduction codes 00-83 (CARES Act) and 00-85 reach the $5000 limit ($7000 in 2021). Note that this limit includes accrued healthcare credits.

Assign the other billing event to the CARES Act Health Care Credit Billing Event field. 5. Select the Default Calculate Health Care Credit option. If you want to set this up client-by-client, you can set the corresponding setting on the COVID-19 client override form. 6. Click Save.

Chapter 4 Processing Form 941 Certain changes were made to IRS Form 941 in 2020 and 2021, to aid in COVID-19 reporting. PrismHR includes several features that can assist you with completing these forms.

Introduction and Background The changes implemented under the Families First and CARES Acts significantly altered the tax reporting structure of the 2020 Form 941. In the weeks and months following these acts, PrismHR began planning features to track the associated wage and tax credits so they can populate on employers’ quarterly Forms 941. The draft version of Form 941 also evolved over this same period as its instructions became clearer and more precise. New features in PrismHR, developed according to these guidelines, can help service providers pass this new tax information into MasterTax and ensure that their 941 calculations comply with the new legislation. These features include: • Master Tax RTS File v. 39, which introduced file updates directly related to COVID-19 data transfer between PrismHR and MasterTax. • A Form 941 Worksheet report, designed to help employers fill out their tax forms in accordance with IRS calculations. • A Schedule R report, designed to help employers detail their client by client tax data. You can find documentation for these features in the following sections.

About MasterTax RTS 39 through 42 To provide support for COVID-19-related changes to the 2020 Form 941, PrismHR developed support for versions 39 and 40 of the MasterTax RTS file. Version 39 of the file includes updates designed to streamline the passage of COVID-19-related data from PrismHR into MasterTax. Support for MasterTax RTS version 40 was released in October 2020. Support for version 41 was initially released in March 2021 and expanded in May 2021. Support for version 42 was released in July 2021.

To enable version 42 of the RTS file: 1. Click the Work Centers menu and select MasterTax Processing under Work Centers|Tax. Then, under Setup Forms, select MasterTax Interface Parameters. 2. Set MasterTax RTS Import File Version to 42.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 36 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

  1. If you are a Certified PEO or you leverage the PrismHR SBEA features, select Schedule R Breakout.
  2. Click Save.

Important Changes in Version 42 • The file no longer includes 00-87 data. • The file now includes 00-19 data as a positive value, instead of a negative value. • For each 00-19 value in a 500 record, the system creates a corresponding 501 record. Statistic 4 of this record reflects the number of employees who contributed to the 00-19 value in the 500 record. • The file now splits 00-80 and 00-81 data into “Accrual Before April 1” and “Accrual After March 31” categories. Accrual Before April 1 reports under Statistic 2 of the 501 record while Accrual After March 31 reports under Statistic 1. • The file splits 00-84 data similarly. It now reflects pre-April 1 values in statistic 5 of the 501 record . The 501 record displays under code FE0000-116H for sick leave health care expenses, and under FE0000- 117H for family leave health care expenses. The file reports these values employee by employee.

Important Changes in Version 41 • The gross taxable over limit value for New Jersey unemployment tax (31-24) is now reported in statistic 4. • The system creates 600 and 601 records for any employee who paid Eugene, Oregon local tax for the quarter. • The system creates records for any employee who paid taxes to support Connecticut Paid Family Leave.

Important Changes in Version 40 This version of the RTS file includes several minor updates. The most important change is the addition of a new Statistic, which adds support for year-to-date values in the 501 records for 00-80 and 00-81 credits.

Important Changes in Version 39 Version 39 includes the following updates: • Data stored under tax deduction codes 00-80, 00-81, 00-83, 00-84, and 0-85 are passed as positive values, even if they are negative in PrismHR. • Data under 00-82 is not passed and does not appear on the file. MasterTax uses the data from 00-80 and 00- 81 to calculate the Medicare tax credit, so passing this data would result in double accounting. • Tax deduction code 00-84 (Families First healthcare credits) does not appear on the file because this tax deduction code reflects a secondary credit which is dependent on the values in 00-80 and 00-81. Instead, it is divided into two separate tax deduction codes, according to the proportion of sick leave vs. FMLA wages: • FE0000-117H - FMLA component of 00-84 credits. • FE0000-116H - Sick Leave component of 00-84 credits.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 37 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

• On 500 records, CARES Act/Retention credits are recorded under both Quarter-to-Date (positions 95-108) and Year-to-Date (109-122) metrics. The taxable values for these credits are equal to twice the tax amount stored under the credit. For example, if the tax amount under 00-83 was $100.00, the taxable amount in the 500 record is $200.00. This is because MasterTax performs its own calculation on CARES Act creditable wages. • For Q2 only, the RTS file also accounts for Q1 retention credits and passes them into the new tax deduction codes listed below. Quarter-to-Date taxable values (positions 109-122) are double the credit values, for the same reason as described above. • FE0000-178 - Q1 values for 00-83. • FE0000-178H - Q1 values for 00-85. • The system creates 501 records for tax deduction codes 00-80 and 00-81. The format resembles that of 501 records for tax deduction code 00-10. MasterTax uses the values in this record to populate boxes 5a(i) and 5a(ii) on Form 941 (capped by the difference between employee and employer Social Security tax). This means that these boxes should reflect only employee-side taxable wages for COVID-19 sick and medical leave, without generating additional tax on over-limit wages. • Offshoot federal codes are also added to these tax deduction codes, when applicable. For example GU is added for Guam.

MasterTax RTS 42: Calculations and Workarounds Background The American Rescue Plan Act took effect on April 1, 2021 and made multiple changes to earlier coronavirus- related legislation. One major change was the end of the employee-side Social Security tax credit for COVID-19 qualified leave wages, which PrismHR calculated and accrued under tax code 00-87. The elimination of this tax credit entails major differences in tax reporting for the later quarters of 2021. Please note that, in accordance with the federal guidance provided under the ARPA, the new version of the MasterTax RTS file supports: • Its own internal calculation logic for the value that PrismHR associates with tax code 00-87. • Pre-April 1 and post-March 31 credit divisions in the statistics of the 501 records for the following tax codes: 00-80, 00-81, and the health care credit codes FE0000-116H and FE0000-117H. PrismHR uses its own logic to determine the value of 00-87 and to break up the credit reporting under the 501 statistics. In addition, we recognize that clients adopted varying approaches to ARPA compliance. This document provides some basic workaround recommendations, assuming certain system settings were configured in accordance with previous PrismHR guidance. In September 2021, PrismHR released new RTS build settings to automate some of this calculation logic. See PrismHR Solutions for more information.

Guide to Acronyms and Tax Codes Acronym or Tax Code Meaning

FFCRA Families First Coronavirus Response Act (2020) ARPA American Rescue Plan Act (2021, often called “The ARP” in official documents)

00-12 Employee-side Social Security tax 00-16 Employer-side Social Security tax 00-80 Qualifying wage credits for COVID-19 FMLA leave under the FFCRA 00-81 Qualifying wage credits for COVID-19 Sick Leave under the FFCRA 00-84 Qualifying healthcare-related expenses associated with FFCRA payments 00-87 Social Security Tax Credits on qualified wages under the FFCRA FE0000-116H MasterTax code for the portion of 00-84 associated with 00-80 wages FE0000-117H MasterTax code for the portion of 00-84 associated with 00-81 wages

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 39 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

PrismHR Logic and Workarounds To accommodate the split between pre-April and post-March COVID-19 credits, PrismHR implemented logic that divides entire vouchers (not their individual credits) into those two categories, based on whether the voucher Pay Period End Date falls before or after April 1. However, we recognize that many customers are using their own configurations to comply with this credit reporting split, so this logic will not be a perfect fit for every use case. We have identified two major alternative or workaround approaches: • Treat all COVID-19 credits on these vouchers as “post-March” credits. This simpler approach is popular with some customers. • Opt for a more granular COVID-19 credit breakdown. This requires additional manual calculation.

About the RTS Statistics On version 42 of the MasterTax RTS file, in the 501 record for tax codes 00-80 and 00-81, there are three important statistic definitions.

Statistic Description Calculation Logic 1 Social Security taxable amount for All 00-80 and 00-81 credits associated with payroll vouchers the period after 3/31/21 that have Pay Period End Dates on or after 4/1/21. 2 Social Security taxable amount for The difference between the values stored under 00-12 and the period before 4/1/21 00-16, up to the total amount of the applicable FFCRA credits.

5 All creditable wages under the tax All 00-80 and 00-81 credits associated with payroll vouchers code, for the period before 4/1/21 that have Pay Period End Dates on or before 3/31/21.

Note: The FE0000-116H and -117H codes use their own “Statistic 5” value, discussed below.

The values you submit in these statistics will vary depending on your approach toward ARPA compliance, as described below.

Statistic 5 Under FE0000-116H and -117H These credits break down the value stored in tax code 00-84. In the RTS file, their 501 records have a unique Statistic 5 value representing pre-April 1 health care tax credits. In other words, Statistic 5 displays a subset of the total value stored under 116H or 117H. The “excluded” amounts correspond to any 00-84 credits accrued on vouchers with pay period end dates that fall on or after April 1. PrismHR calculates this value voucher-by-voucher, pulling healthcare credits from any vouchers that meet these criteria. It then divides this amount into sub-values for Sick Leave and FMLA. If you want to treat all credits as accruing after April 1, you can set Statistic 5 to 0 for these credit records.

Note: There are extra considerations for customers who want a more granular data breakdown. Because healthcare credit calculations are period-based, it is difficult to obtain a precise day-by-day analysis of credit

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 40 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

accruals. Instead, we recommend apportioning employee 00-84 credits based on percentages of the whole wages paid under FMLA vs. Sick Leave pay codes, even if this is an approximation.

Understanding Previous System Setup Guidance If you followed previous PrismHR setup guidance as specified in our Support Office Hours and the corresponding documentation, the statistic values on your RTS file should be accurate. If not, you may need to perform some manual calculations and adjustments to the file. When this document refers to “previous guidance”, this means: • Removing the Social Security tax exemption from any COVID-19 sick leave/FMLA pay codes after April 1, or creating new pay codes without this tax exemption for the “post-March” payments. • Creating separate payrolls for COVID-19 sick leave/FMLA payments associated with pay periods before March 31. • (In some cases) Ensuring that no employee received COVID-19 sick or FMLA wages that exceeded their Social Security taxable wage limit prior to taking this COVID-19 leave. The workaround sections below will specify when this requirement must be satisfied.

How does this affect Form 941? PrismHR is implementing the same logic across both the RTS file generation features and our Form 941 reports. Therefore, if you need to make adjustments to the Form 941 report output, you can use the exact same workarounds described here.

On the MasterTax RTS File Build form, you can select the following two options: • Use tax code 00-87 to determine SS credit within MasterTax? • Use COVID Credits as post March 31?

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 42 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

Use tax code 00-87 to determine SS credit within MasterTax? If you select this option, the system performs the following calculation during the RTS build: (00-87 tax amount associated with line item) / (0.062). After computing this value, the system uses this value to fill in Statistic 1 of the 501 record for tax code 00-81, up to the value reported under 00-81 on the 500 record. If any amount remains after reaching the 00-81 reporting value, the system enters the remainder into Statistic 1 of the 501 record for tax code 00-80.

Use COVID Credits as post March 31? Select this option to consider any COVID-19 credits accrued in Q2 2021 as “post-March 31” credits, which means they were accrued subject to the American Rescue Plan Act. These credits will be reported accordingly on the RTS file. On the file itself, this means: • On 501 records for 00-80 and 00-81, the full value under these tax codes populates under statistic 1. • On FE0000-116H and FE0000-117H records, statistic 1 is set to 0.

Alternative Approaches This section documents workarounds for this issue that we recommended before we released the solutions outlined above. They are included here for your reference.

  1. Associating all Q2 Leave with Dates After March 31

Note: If you calculated COVID-19-related healthcare credits and decide to use this approach, you must zero out Statistic 5 on the MasterTax records for those credits (FE0000-116H and FE0000-117H).

If no employee who took COVID-19 leave exceeded their Social Security taxable wage limit prior to, or while taking, that leave: 1. In the RTS file, set Statistic 1 equal to the full value of 00-80 or 00-81 as appropriate. 2. Set Statistic 2 equal to 0. 3. Set Statistic 5 equal to 0. 4. Repeat for all applicable clients or employers.

The example below illustrates the 500 and 501 records associated with tax code 00-81. The statistics on the right are separated by plus signs. Note that Statistic 1 is the same for both records, while every other statistic in the 501 record is zeroed out.

If you think some employees exceeded their Social Security wage limit, but you still used our recommended setup for calculating 00-87 accurately: 1. See the section below on using 00-87 to calculate Statistic 1. 2. Set Statistic 2 equal to 0. 3. Set Statistic 5 equal to 0. 4. Repeat for all applicable clients or employers.

  1. Using 00-87 Credits to Calculate Statistic 1

Note: Beginning in PrismHR 1.24.0, the system features an option to perform this process automatically. You will receive a prompt during RTS file generation: select Yes to automatically allocate values to Statistic 1 of the 501 records using the procedure below.

MasterTax performs its own calculation to determine the value of “00-87”, based on data from tax codes 00-80 and 00-81. Therefore, in RTS version 42, PrismHR no longer passes 00-87 data into MasterTax. Instead, you have the option to run this process automatically or perform the manual calculations and adjust the file as needed. You can use this approach even if you have employees who exceeded their Social Security taxable wage limit for the quarter.

To calculate Statistic 1: 1. Take the 00-87 tax amount for the quarter and divide it by 0.062. This is the exact inverse of what MasterTax does in their own program. This ensures proper conversion between our calculated values and the calculation logic implemented by MasterTax. 2. Enter the resulting value in Statistic 1 of the 501 record for 00-81 or 00-80, as appropriate. 3. Repeat this process for any other clients or employers, as needed.

To calculate Statistic 2: If none of your employees went over their Social Security tax limit, and your pay codes were configured appropriately to exempt Social Security tax only on pre-ARPA COVID leave, then Statistic 2 most likely calculated correctly. For this calculation, PrismHR uses the difference between employer-side and employee-side Social Security tax for the quarter. It enters that value in Statistic 2, capped by the total amount of FFCRA credits associated with that record.

  1. Handling Issues with Statistic 2 FFCRA qualified wages are only exempt from Social Security tax prior to the start of the ARPA (before April 1, 2021). After that date, this type of payment is no longer exempt. As in previous quarters, PrismHR relies on the presence of employer-level Social Security tax exemptions as an indicator of major tax-related changes in a particular quarter. If you left the tax exemption enabled on your FFCRA pay codes, the RTS file statistics will reflect those wages as accruing before April 1 even if this is not the

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 44 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

case. The system cannot tell that these are post-April 1 credits because they still have the employer-level tax exemption. You must use tax adjustments to correct this data issue. You have the option of using either major workaround strategy here: • Counting all credits as accruing after April 1, or • Taking a more detailed approach to your credit calculations

To resolve this issue using the “post-April 1” workaround strategy: 1. First, ensure that you calculated Statistic 1 correctly and zeroed out statistic 2. 2. Create a tax adjustment to apply the 00-87 credit to the employee record. 3. Set the credit value equal to the difference between the 00-16 and 00-12 accruals for the employee (this should be a negative value). 4. Repeat for all employees who took COVID-19 leave, regardless of whether they exceeded their Social Security tax limit.

To resolve this issue using a more granular approach: • You can try using the COVID-19 Recalculation Utility to recalculate your Social Security tax credits for April 1 and beyond. Please note that this strategy assumes you still used distinct pay codes for FFCRA and ARPA wages, even though you did not remove the tax exemption on the latter. • You can perform manual calculations to adjust this data. This option will be highly case-specific. Please contact customer support if you need to take this approach and have further questions.

Taking a More Granular Approach Toward Statistic 5 of 00-80 and 00-81 If you need an even more granular approach than those outlined above (for example, you want to define your credit split based on charge dates), your system-generated Statistic 5 value may be underestimated. To calculate Statistic 5 (sum of all pre-April creditable COVID-19 wages), PrismHR currently uses the voucher- level pay period end date break described previously. If you want to count all your credits as accrued after March 31, you must set this statistic to 0 as described previously.

About this Report This report displays suggested values for each box of the 2020 Form 941. It also includes FEIN and employee count information. The following table describes the new and updated report line items, along with their system calculation logic.

Mid-2021 Additions: About the Pre-March and Post-April Categories The Q3 2021 additions to Form 941 subdivide COVID-19 credits even more finely than before, requiring updates to the PrismHR reporting logic. For reporting purposes, the system now divides “Sick and Family Leave” credits into two categories: • Credits accrued on charge dates falling before April 1 (pre-April credits) • Credits accrued on charge dates falling after March 31 (post-March credits) The pre-April category is determined using the following calculation: • For any vouchers with pay period start and end dates prior to April 1, include all 00-80, 00-81, 00-82, 00- 84, and 00-87 credits in this category. • For any vouchers with pay period start dates before April 1 and pay period end dates on April 1 or later (but with the pay date in Q1), determine the ratio of COVID pay codes used on pre-April charge dates versus on post-March charge dates. Multiply this ratio by the values of any 00-80, 00-81, 00-82, 00-84, and 00-87 credits on the voucher, and place each portion of each credit in the corresponding category.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 47 Chapter 4 Processing Form 941

     For example, if 80% of the COVID credits are associated with charge dates before April 1, then this
     category receives (0.8 * sum of total COVID credits). The post-March category would then receive the
     remaining 20%.

The post-March category contains the credits remaining after these calculations, plus credits from any vouchers with pay period start/end dates after March 31.

Background Loans received through the Paycheck Protection Program are forgivable up to 100%, but this value can vary based on several factors: • The loan can only be forgiven for payroll costs over a specified period. • If a client’s full-time equivalent (FTE) count decreases over this period, the loan forgiveness percentage also decreases. • The forgiveness amount can also decrease based on employee compensation reductions. The Payroll Cost Report provides insight into the first bullet point above. The FTE Analysis Report provides insight into the second.

Before You Begin These reports use a new field on the CARES Act Parameters form, called Paycheck Protection Program Loan Start Date.

Before you run any of the reports, navigate to Client Details > Actions menu > CARES Act Parameters and enter the appropriate date in this field. If you do not enter a date in this field, you can enter it in the field that displays on the report setup form.

Full-Time Equivalent Analysis Report Note: You can now exclude specific pay codes from the FTE report logic. On the COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters form, enter these pay codes in the new Exclude FTE Pay Code table.

This report includes all employees with hours that fall within the appropriate PPP window. It also calculates the number of full-time equivalents employed during the given time frame and provides insight into whether, and to what extent, a FTE reduction occurred (see the Reduction Quotient description below). Employee hours are based on charge dates within the associated time frame. The system then divides these hours by the number of days in that period to return a daily hours amount, and multiplies this value by 7 to return a weekly hours amount. Finally, the report divides this value by 40 to return a Full-Time Equivalency value, capped at 1.0 and rounded to the nearest tenth.

Report Background This report displays a breakdown of employees who have hours in the system within two lookback periods and a Covered Period (specified during report setup). The two lookback periods are: • February 15, 2019 – June 30, 2019 • January 1, 2020 – February 29, 2020 Additionally, please note the following:

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 58 Chapter 5 Reports

•    For all employees, the system calculates hours using the total Hours Paid under Standard-type hourly
     pay codes and the total Hours Worked for any other pay codes.
•    The report does not include employees with 0 hours.
•    The report does not include 1099 contractors or business owners.
•    The report does not include pay codes with the Exclude from ACA Reporting option enabled.

Finally, this report calculates several total values: Total FTE and a calculated Reduction Quotient, which indicates whether an FTE reduction occurred during any of the time frames. The Reduction Quotient equals the Covered Period total FTEs divided by the total FTEs for the appropriate Lookback Period. See Analyzing the Report for a description of these calculations.

Running the Report

Note: While the report now runs for very large clients, the Simplified FTE method does not always finish calculating for clients of this size. The standard (non-Simplified) report does run completely for large clients.

To run the COVID-19 PPP Forgiveness Report: 1. Select Reports menu and then select COVID-19 PPP Forgiveness Report under HR|Report. 2. In the Report field, choose Full Time Equivalent Analysis. 3. Enter a Covered Period Start Date if one does not populate. 4. Select whether you want to run the report for 8 weeks, 24 weeks, or until a Custom End Date. 5. If you want to filter the report results by location, select a Worksite Location. 6. If the option displays, select whether you want to use the Simplified Method for FTE calculation. See the description of the system-level parameter in the Cap and Credit settings table of Configuring System-Level Parameters 7. If the option displays, enter your custom start and end dates for Lookback Periods 1 and 2. 8. Click Run. The report generates.

Salary Reduction Report The PPP Salary Reduction Report provides information about COVID-19-related employee pay reductions during the specified PPP covered period. It includes comparison calculations between pre-pandemic pay rates and covered period pay rates, along with indications about whether the employee’s pay was restored according to PPP guidelines.

Report Background The SBA’s Paycheck Protection Program Loan Forgiveness Application describes the calculations you need to complete in order to determine your PPP loan forgiveness eligibility. Forgiveness eligibility is based on several factors, including the use of the loan funds and maintaining PPP staffing requirements. This report is designed to help you quantify your compliance with those staffing requirements. In Table 1 of the Schedule A worksheet, you must specify each employee’s “Salary/Hourly Wage Reduction” if their pay during the loan’s Covered Period was at least 25% lower than their pay during the reference Lookback Period. You must also take into account whether the employee’s pay reductions qualified for any PPP safe harbor provisions before determining the final salary reduction. This report provides: • Calculated employee pay rates for both the Covered Period and the Lookback Period. • A fractional comparison between the two rates. • A determination of whether the employee’s pay rate was restored by the date of submission of the loan forgiveness application. • An estimated final total for the employee’s pay reduction.

Running the Report

Note: Depending on how your organization keys in payroll data, you may need to adjust the report setup dates so that you can capture data from full pay periods. In other words, report calculations may be “off” if you enter the correct covered period start and end dates, because they may not capture the entirety of the pay period data from the beginning or end of the covered period.

To run the report: 1. Select Reports menu and then select COVID-19 PPP Forgiveness under HR|Report. 2. In the report setup field, choose Salary Reduction Report. 3. Enter Covered Period start and end date information as you would for the other PPP reports. 4. Enter the SBA Loan Forgiveness Application Submission Date. The report uses this date in its calculations (see below). If you leave this field blank, the system uses today’s date OR December 31, 2020 (whichever is earlier).

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 63 Chapter 5 Reports

  1. The report breaks out employees as either “Salaried” or “Hourly” based on certain factors. If you want the system to group “Commission” employees as Salaried, select the Treat Commissioned as Salaried? field. (“Commission employees” = employees whose Pay Method on Employee Details is set to Commission).
  2. If you need to use a custom lookback period, enter the Lookback 1 Start Date and End Date.
  3. Click Run. The report generates.

Analyzing the Report

Employee Information The report sorts employees based on two criteria: • Estimated Table Type (1 or 2) • Salaried/ Hourly The second category is based on the employee’s Pay Method on the Employee Details form. “Hourly” and “Driver” employees are considered Hourly (H). “Salary” employees are considered Salaried (S). “Commission” employees are grouped based on whether or not you selected the Treat Commissioned as Salaried? field on the report setup form.

Covered Period Average Annualized Salary/Hourly Rate The Covered Period begins and ends on the dates specified in the report setup parameters.

The calculation involves the following steps: 1. Calculate employee compensation using charge dates within the Covered Period (paid under pay codes flagged as Earnings or Tips). 2. Divide compensation by other figures, depending on Pay Method: • Salaried: Compensation / Active Days * 365 • Hourly: Compensation / Hours, where Hours = hours paid if the pay code is set to Standard and Hourly. Otherwise, hours worked is used. Hours worked are also used if the Pay Reason is set to Units. • The system excludes any pay codes flagged for exclusion for ACA or PPP purposes.

Lookback Period Average Annualized Salary/Hourly Rate This is calculated using the same logic as in the section above, but in this case the Covered Period is replaced by the period from Jan 1 through Mar 31, 2020, unless an override period is entered in the report setup parameters.

Lookback Period Average Hours Worked This column value = (hours worked in the lookback period/ number of days in the lookback period) * 7

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 64 Chapter 5 Reports

Reduction Comparison This column value = Covered Period Average Annualized Rate/ Lookback Period Average Annualized Rate

Feb 15 Rate Restored by: [DATE] [DATE] = Application Submission Date entered during report setup. If you left this field blank, the report defaults to either today’s date or December 31, 2020 (whichever is earlier). The value in this column can be Y, N, or NA. The system prints NA if: • The Reduction Comparison calculation ≥ 0.75. • There is no employee compensation data for February 15, 2020. • The employee is not active on the Application Submission Date. The system prints Y if: • The Reduction Comparison calculation is less than 0.75 • AND • The employee’s annualized pay on the Application Submission Date ≥ their annualized pay on 2/15/20. Otherwise, the system prints N.

Estimated Step 3 Reduction Amount This is the final system estimation of the employee’s Schedule A, Table 1 pay reduction amount. The report prints 0 if the Reduction Comparison calculation ≥ 0.75 The report also prints 0 if the value in the Feb 15 Rate Restored by: [DATE] column is Y. Otherwise, the report uses the following formula: ((Lookback Average * 0.75) - Covered Period Average), and then adjusts that value based on whether the employee is hourly or salaried: • For Hourly (H) employees, multiply by Lookback Period Average Hours Worked, then multiply by 8 (weeks) OR 24 (weeks), depending on the length of the covered period. Any covered period longer than 8 weeks is treated as 24 weeks. • For Salaried (S) employees, divide by 52 (weeks), then multiply by either 8 or 24 weeks, according to the same logic described above.

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 65 Chapter 5 Reports

COVID-19 941 Over-Limit Error Report Use this report to identify employees affected by the employee vs. employer-side Social Security tax over-limit issue.

Background Because COVID-19 credits (00-80 and 00-81) are exempt from employer-side Social Security tax, an employee who was paid COVID-19-related wages in 2020 may have a higher 00-12 (Employee SS Tax) value compared to their 00-16 (Employer SS Tax) value, for that quarter. If this employee later reached the $137,700 Social Security tax threshold under 00-12, the system continued to accrue Social Security tax on the employer side, since the 00-16 value had not yet reached the limit. This behavior is incorrect and can have significant downstream effects. This issue was corrected in the October release and 00-16 now stops accruing as soon as 00-12 reaches the Social Security tax limit. That release also introduced this report, which can help you identify any employees affected by this issue and provide data to help you fix the issue for them.

Running the Report To run the COVID-19 941 Over-Limit Error Report: 1. Click the Back Office menu. 2. Under Operations|Report, select COVID-19 OverLimit Report. The setup form displays. 3. Enter a Year and, if necessary, a Quarter. 4. Select an Employer if you want to run the report for that employer. To run the report for all employers, leave this field blank. 5. Click Run. The report generates.

Analyzing the Report Note: This over-limit issue was corrected in the October release. If none of your employees reached the Social Security tax limit before this release, this report may not pull any data as the issue will not exist for them.

This report returns information about the differences between employer-side and employee-side Social Security tax. It displays the Net Taxable amount, the actual tax amount, and the “over limit” amount for both the employer and employee components of the tax, along with calculated differences between these two components. You can then use this information to correct the records of the affected employees. (Note that employee information was cropped out of the left-hand side of this screenshot). The report provides client-level and employer-level totals for these values (in bold).

COVID-19 Features Guide © 2026 PrismHR 66 Chapter 5 Reports

Employee Retention Credit Recalc Report Note: When applying Employee Retention Credit (ERC) “caps” or limits, both this report and the COVID-19 Recalculation Utility will take into account the fact that the 2020 credit limit was raised for 2021 (from $5000 per employee to $7000 per employee).

In December 2020, the CARES Act legislation was updated, introducing the possibility for businesses to have periods wherein they do not qualify for 00-83 or 00-85 credit accumulation (remember: 00-83 tracks the wage component of the Employer Retention Credit and 00-85 tracks the benefit cost component). Other scenarios are also possible: businesses might retroactively discover that their ERC credit dates overlap with their PPP forgiveness period. In this case, they would need to make adjustments to their reporting periods in order to claim both benefits to the fullest extent possible. To support these changes, there are new exclusion date setup fields on the COVID-19 Client Parameters form (see Setting Up CARES Act Compliance). This new ERC exclusion date feature significantly impacts three parts of the system: • Payroll - ERC credits will not calculate on any pay dates within the specified period. • COVID-19 Recalculation Utility - As noted elsewhere, running this utility after setting up the ERC exclusion dates will cause the utility to zero out ERC credits if those credits are associated with pay dates falling within the exclusion range. • ERC Recalc Report - This report was created to provide more insight into the behavior of this feature. The Employee Retention Credit Recalc Report can help you independently determine any retroactive calculations related to ERC credits. If you need to test several date ranges to maximize your PPP loan forgiveness and ERC credit claims, you can run this report multiple times while adjusting the date range. Compare the outputs of these test reports and use your observations to inform any decisions about your reporting period dates. Alternatively, you can use the report to preview the effects of the COVID-19 Recalculation Utility. PrismHR highly recommends doing this if you plan to run the utility after setting up your exclusion dates.

Running the Report To run the Employee Retention Recalc Credit Report: 1. Click Reports menu and select ERC Recalc Report under HR|Report. A setup form displays containing the name and ID of the selected client. 2. Click Run. The report generates.

Report Output The report data is displayed by employee. It lists the employee’s name, ID, associated Employer ID, and associated Client entity ID. After this general information, the report displays quarterly before and after calculations for both 00-83 and 00-85 credits, extending from Q1 2020 to the current quarter.

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 4 System-Level Setup

System-Level Setup To use the SBEA features in the system, you must first configure a range of settings. Please note that many of these setup procedures are best performed on days where there is no active payroll, because they impact the behavior of payroll processing.

SBEA/COVID-19 Setup Even if you are not a Certified PEO, these settings can help you comply with the 2020 coronavirus legislation by breaking out your MasterTax data on the client level. While the procedures in this guide are very similar to those in the standard SBEA User Guide, some COVID-19-specific changes were added:

•   In Step 2: important notes about CPEO Start Date and Limit Testing on Employer Register
•   In Step 4: important note about SBEA Wage Codes for non-CPEO providers
•   In Step 6: COVID-19-specific instructions regarding MasterTax interface parameters
•   In the MasterTax Files section, added new information about the PTS, RTS, and SBEA Certified
    Relationship files.

This guide also includes documentation provided by MasterTax so you can ensure that both applications are set up to properly handle these new legislative requirements.

Enabling the SBEA Feature Set To begin setting up SBEA features in PrismHR, you must enable SBEA functionality on the global level. After enabling these settings, the system adds new fields to the Employer Details form. Use these fields to designate an employer as certified and set up basic SBEA reporting information.

To enable the SBEA features in PrismHR:

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 1 System-Level Setup

  1. Click Back Office.
  2. Under System|Change, select Global Configuration.
  3. Select the Enable SBEA Feature Set option. This turns on the features that support SBEA compliance.
  4. Click Save.

Flagging Employers as Certified PEOs After you enable SBEA features, you can designate employers as certified PEOs and specify a range of dates for collecting SBEA-related tax information. After you indicate that an employer is SBEA-certified, you must complete the setup process to run any payrolls that include a client or employee assigned to this employer — either as primary or alternate.

To designate an employer as a CPEO: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Under Employer|Change, select the Employer Details form. 3. Enter the Employer ID. Employer information populates the form. 4. Select Certified PEO. This indicates that the employer is certified as a PEO by the IRS. 5. Enter the Certified Start Date. This is the date the certification went into effect. SBEA tracking begins with payrolls where the pay date is on or after this date. 6. If the certification expires, you can also enter the Certified End Date. 7. Click Save.

Limit Testing on Employer Register After you enable the SBEA feature set, the system automatically performs limit testing using data from the client federal entity tax registers. However, if an employee works for multiple clients under the same employer, the limit testing does not take this into account. Use the Limit Testing on Employer Register field to adjust this behavior so that the system checks the employer register, rather than the client federal entity register, during this testing. Consider the following example:

 •   John Doe works for both Client A and Client B, both under Employer 1.
 •   John's federal tax cutoff is $7000.
 •   John earns $5000 at Client A and $5000 at Client B.

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 2 System-Level Setup

The portion of John’s taxed income will depend on which register the system checks. This depends on how you have set up the system: Employer is Not Marked as a CPEO If Certified PEO is not selected, the system calculates taxes for all $5000 of John’s Client A wages and only $2000 of John’s Client B wages, or $7000 total. This is the correct tax limit. Employer is a CPEO, Limit Testing on Employer Register is Disabled If Certified PEO is selected and Limit Testing on Employer Register is not selected, John pays taxes on all $5000 from both clients. The system does not consider Client B’s wages along with Client A’s wages because they are stored in different client federal entity tax registers. Therefore, the system does not take into account that John has reached his tax limit. Employer is a CPEO and Limit Testing on Employer Register is Enabled If Certified PEO and Limit Testing on Employer Register are both selected, the system calculates taxes for all $5000 of John’s Client A wages and $2000 of John’s Client B wages, or $7000 total, the same as if Certified PEO were not selected.

Creating Client Federal Entities After you flag the employers that are SBEA certified, you can use the Create Client Federal Entities feature to create the client federal entity records for all clients of your certified employers.

Note: To accrue taxes properly and report SBEA information, you must create client federal entity IDs and assign them to the clients. You must also have the client federal entity information set up before running payrolls so that the system includes the client federal entity ID on the payroll vouchers.

Federal Entity IDs After an employer is flagged as a Certified PEO on the Employer Details form, a new Federal Entity ID field displays on the Client Details form for each client serviced by that employer. You must assign a Federal Entity ID to each client. If you do not assign this ID to each client federal entity (CFE), your payroll will fail with a “hard” error because this causes severe issues later in the SBEA reporting process. The Create Client Federal Entities utility performs this task for each client automatically.

Using the Create Client Federal Entities Utility To create client federal entities:

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 3 System-Level Setup

  1. Click Work Centers, then go to Tax > SBEA Processing > Setup > SBEA Auto Create Client Federal Entities.
  2. Select an Employer ID (the employer must be a Certified PEO).
  3. Enter a Certified Relationship Start Date, which is the date the contract was signed. This controls the SBEA wage code. Wage code A will be on any voucher after this start date. If the date is left blank, Wage code C is used.
  4. Click Run. A report displays with the processing steps, number of records created, and the date and time the process ran.

Checking Client Federal Entity Information Client Details

You can confirm that a client federal entity ID was assigned to a client on the Client Details form: 1. Open Client Details (found under Client|Change). 2. In the Contract panel, locate the Federal Entity ID field. 3. If this field contains a value, the system assigned a CFE ID successfully.

Client Federal Entities

You can view other details about client federal entities on the Client Federal Entities form: 1. Click Back Office. 2. Under Employer|Change, open Client Federal Entities. 3. Enter or select an Entity ID. All information about the CFE populates on the form. 4. Review this information and click Save if you made any changes.

Special Considerations In some special cases, manual adjustments to the client federal entity records are required:

 •   If any of the clients of the employer(s) share an FEIN, you need to manually edit the client
     records. This is because the system creates separate federal entity records for each of those
     clients and assigns those different federal entity IDs to the clients. You must edit the clients and
     set them all to the same client federal entity ID in the Client Details Detail tab.

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 4 System-Level Setup

•   If any of the clients’ worksite locations operate under different FEINs than the client, you need to
    assign a unique client federal entity ID to those locations in the Worksite Locations Other
    Parameters panel. If the entity does not exist, you must first create it in Client Federal Entities.

Updating Vouchers with SBEA Information The SBEA Voucher Update Utility takes the federal taxes that were previously tracked and accrued at the employer level and associates them with client federal entities. It adjusts previously processed payroll vouchers by flagging them with the client federal entity ID that the employees worked for. It also marks each voucher with the appropriate SBEA wage code.

Note: Run the SBEA Voucher Update Utility during off hours. Do not rebuild tax registers while processing payroll. This process can take a while. Federal taxes must be associated with the client federal entity to ensure correct client tax Schedule R reporting for SBEA purposes.

Your organization needs to use this utility if:

•   You did not complete SBEA setup before your certification start date. The most common
    example is to accommodate a retroactive certification.
•   You are making adjustments mid-year or backdating start dates.

SBEA Wage Codes Note: If you are not a CPEO, you do not need to worry about SBEA Wage Codes.

The voucher update utility adds two pieces of information to each voucher: client federal entity ID and SBEA wage code. You created and assigned CFE IDs in the previous step. The system determines which wage code to post. There are three options:

•   A - The client is in a certified relationship with the employer.
•   B - The client opts to use the 95% rule for a particular worksite exclusion.
•   C - The client is not in a certified relationship with the employer.

Checking Voucher Information You can confirm that the utility posted the CFE ID and SBEA wage code to each voucher on the Payroll Voucher form.

To check the SBEA information on a specific payroll voucher: 1. Open the Payroll Voucher form, found under Payroll|View.

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 5 System-Level Setup

  1. Enter or select a Voucher Number. The form populates with information.
  2. Check the values in the Client Fed. Entity and SBEA Wage Code fields.
  3. Repeat for any other vouchers you want to check.

About Client Federal Entity Tax Registers Client federal entity tax registers track tax information for a specific federal entity, for SBEA reporting purposes. PrismHR supports SBEA requirements for updating the client federal entity tax registers. These features are not covered in this document, as they are not necessarily part of the SBEA workflow. You can learn more about these features in the dedicated payroll documentation.

• The Transfer Tax Basis and Transfer Tax Basis Import utilities support the SBEA feature set. These tools adjust employee tax bases and amounts, and they account for successor wages and the adjustment data flows to the client federal entity. • Transfer Tax Basis Entry is in the Payroll menu under Payroll|Change. • Transfer Tax Basis Import (From Successor) is in the Back Office menu under Operations|Import Processing. • Tax Adjustment Entry also adjusts client federal entity registers, correctly apportioning the changes. This form is in the Payroll menu under Payroll|Change.

SBEA Guide to COVID-19 Legislation © 2026 PrismHR 6 System-Level Setup

Rebuilding Client Federal Tax Registers If one or more employers in your organization are SBEA-certified and you use MasterTax, you need to have payroll vouchers stamped with the A, B, or C designation. The system has a utility for updating existing vouchers from 2017 and later. When you enable the SBEA feature set, the system stamps all new vouchers appropriately.

Note: Rebuild tax registers during off hours. Do not rebuild tax registers while processing payroll. This process can take a while.

To perform a rebuild: 1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > SBEA Processing > Setup > SBEA Rebuild Client Federal Entity Tax Register. 2. Enter a tax Year. 3. Optional: Select an Entity ID to limit rebuilds to one or more clients. If left blank, the rebuild is performed for all clients. 4. Click Run. The system deletes the register, sorts vouchers, and takes each voucher and runs them through a payroll posting routine that rewrites the tax registers. PrismHR recommends performing the 941 tax register rebuild.

Note: You receive an email notification when the Rebuild Client Federal Entity Tax Register process has completed or failed.

FUTA Credit Displays the year in which a FUTA credit reduction was taken and the Reduction state where it was taken. Maintenance FUTA credit reductions occur when a state borrows money from the Federal Unemployment Trust Fund to pay unemployment insurance benefits for its residents. If a state has outstanding loan balances, this lowers the credit rate by 0.3% for each year in arrears until these loans are repaid.

SBEA Tax Code If you use Schedule R reporting (the client-by-client report Reporting Override breakdown), you can use this setting to override client-level tax reporting. In this table, specify any tax codes that you want to report on the employer level of the MasterTax RTS and PTS files.

MasterTax Files Customers who enabled the SBEA feature set can also use the MasterTax PTS and RTS files to report their tax data in accordance with the act. When properly configured, the system will create F codes on the MasterTax reporting files, identifying the federal tax data based on the associated client federal entity.

Note: Before submitting your files with MasterTax, you must alert MasterTax Support that you are a PrismHR customer and that you are planning to submit SBEA files. If you do not, you could be charged additional fees by MasterTax.

PTS File The PTS file breaks out federal tax data by client. If the client is associated with multiple CPEO employers, the client will be associated with multiple F codes on the reporting files. This helps to link voucher data based on the common pay agent (the employer).

Important MasterTax Interface Settings • Provide SBEA Payroll Breakout: If this field is enabled, the PTS file will break out the federal tax basis and liability amounts by client federal entity.

•   Include Certified Relationship Setups: If this field is enabled, the PTS file output will include
    the 210 (company setup) records that link the client federal entity to the employer. The system
    creates the 210 record specifically for employers. On the 210 record for each employer, position
    45 indicates the EIN Type. When this value is P (as shown below) it indicates that the employer is
    a common pay parent.
•   The 9-digit number after the P is the employer FEIN.
•   Likewise, on the 210 record for the client federal entity (F code), position 45 will be a C, which
    denotes the client as a common pay child. The next 9 digits are the EIN for the associated
    employer.

Note: In order for the system to associate the 210 records with the F codes, you must enable Send Company Tax Record in PTS File on the MasterTax Interface Parameters. Activating this setting can cause issues in MasterTax if the FEIN and Unemployment ID numbers in PrismHR do not match the FEIN and unemployment IDs in Mastertax. If this describes your situation, PrismHR recommends using the SBEA Relationship file instead of performing company setup on your daily PTS file (see below).

RTS File The MasterTax RTS (reconciliation tax summary) file accommodates client federal entities for 941 R reporting.

Note: PrismHR is working with MasterTax to support the 940 R; MasterTax does not support the 943 R.

To support the RTS file, you must set your MasterTax RTS version to 36 or higher. see Setting MasterTax Interface Parameters for more information.

About the File Effective January 2020, SBEA employers can enable the Build W-2 Records? parameter to break out Form W-2 reporting records on the RTS download. The Build FUTA Exempt records? field can only be used with MasterTax versions 37 and above.

To file as a CPEO in MasterTax, you must contact MasterTax Support to verify that you have a MasterTax PEO license. The PTS import file creates the requisite client structure within MasterTax. The import assigns new client payroll codes (which begin with the letter F) to existing clients that were previously set up within MasterTax, and creates new companies for clients that have not been set up. A client company record would typically already be set up in MasterTax for any client in a client reporting state. The file will also create the Common Pay Agent link to link the Employer to the Client for Federal tax codes so that when MasterTax creates the 941 Schedule R for the Employer, it will have the appropriate client information. Before importing this file into MasterTax, we strongly recommend reviewing your current configuration within MasterTax by navigating to Company View, selecting a Company, and clicking the FEIN link under the Company tab

Note the following implications of the import: • All new client payroll codes on the file with the same FEIN will link together under a single company record within MasterTax; • This company record will have a Common Pay Agent link to 1 employer; • If a client company with the same FEIN already exists in MasterTax, any new client payroll code(s) with that FEIN will link under this existing client company record; • If a client company with the same FEIN does not already exist in MasterTax, any new client payroll code(s) with that FEIN will create and link under a new client company record.
