Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction Report Center is a centralized and consolidated reporting tool. It comes with many predefined reports that you can use as is or that you can quickly customize to meet the specific requirements of your organization. You can also easily define the presentation of the output and change it at any time as your requirements change.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 1 Chapter 1 Introduction

Accessing Report Center Service Providers and Worksite Managers can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard or from Employee Portal. See your administrator if you do not have the access you require.

Accessing from the PrismHR Dashboard A service provider or worksite manager can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard.

To access Report Center from the Work Centers panel: 1. Open the PrismHR Dashboard. 2. On the Work Centers panel, click Report Center in the Reporting section.

To access Report Center by searching: 1. Open the PrismHR Dashboard. 2. In the Search box, type Interactive Reports. 3. Click Report Center in the list of results.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 2 Chapter 1 Introduction

Workbooks In Report Center, reports are defined with three key terms: workbooks, pages, and datasets. A workbook refers to the entire report, such as the ACH History report or the Employee General Info report. A page on a report refers to a specific view for the report, including the columns that will display and any additional visualizations. A dataset refers to the category of information collected in the system. Each report pulls information from one or more data sets and displays them as pages based on selected settings. These terms are analogous to a spreadsheet program, with the workbook referring to the spreadsheet file, the page being a tab in that file, and the dataset as hidden information that was used to generate that spreadsheet. These terms are important when viewing Sigma help documentation and guides, but are not used extensively throughout this documentation.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 3 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page On the Reports page, the list of reports shows only the reports to which your administrator has given you access. There are two basic types of reports. l System reports come with Report Center and are predefined. You can temporarily configure a system report based on your requirements. l An administrator can modify a copy of a system report and save it as a new custom report. An administrator can also modify a custom report and save it as a new report. If the administrator shares a custom report with your role, that report is shown in your list of reports. The list of reports on your Reports page depend on your security settings.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 4 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Searching for reports You can search for reports by entering text in the Search box on the home page. Searches are case insensitive for partial or full matches in the report name or description. For example, searching for tax presents a list of reports where the word tax appears anywhere in the report name or description. In the following example, the search results contain reports whose names or descriptions include the word “tax.”

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 5 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Accessing Views On the Reports page, you can access a list of views available for a report. The views that are available on a report depend upon your security settings.

To access the views for a report from the Home page: 1. Launch Report Center. 2. Scroll through the list (or search) and click the report panel. The Report Details panel displays. Alternatively, select the Views link below the report name to display a list of views. Select a view to open the report to that Page View.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 6 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Opening a report The list of reports shows only the reports to which you have been given access. See your system administrator if you have questions or need access to additional reports. You can open a report from the Report Center Home page or from within another report that you have open.

To open a report from the Home page: 1. Launch Report Center. 2. Scroll through the list (or search) and click the report name.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 7 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Chapter 3 Viewing Reports Reports are displayed in tables which are similar to spreadsheets, with individual pages that display data and visualizations. Report Editors can customize the columns that display on a report, as well as create visualizations and tables to help analyze data more efficiently.

Selecting Pages on the Report Each report contains one or more pages. The page properties determine which columns and visualizations display to the viewer. Pages are displayed near the top of the screen. Select a page to view the report using that page’s specific configuration. The pages you can access for each report depend on your security settings.

Resetting a Report As you specify parameters, sort columns, or adjust visualizations, you may want to restore the report to its default state. After making any changes to your current view on a report, you can select Reset in the upper-right corner to restore the report to the default view.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 8 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Controlling Parameters on a Report Parameters can be used to control what data displays on the report. The available parameters display near the top of the page, underneath the Page selection. When you select parameters to include on the report, the report results are immediately filtered according to your selection.

Using parameters, you can quickly filter results, clear selections, or search for specific values to instantly update the displayed report data.

To filter results by a parameter: 1. Select an available parameter from the available fields. 2. Select the check mark to include one or more individual parameters. When you select one or more options, only records with those options display on the report. If the parameter is a date field, you can select specific dates to include on the report, select a range of dates, or select time frames. For example, you could include the 2nd and 9th of January, all dates from the 1st of May to the 1st of June, or the last ninety days.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 9 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

To clear selections from a parameter: 1. Select the x icon to clear the parameter selection. Once cleared, the parameter is set to include all results.

To search for values in a parameter: 1. Select an available parameter from the available fields. 2. Enter search criteria in the search bar that displays at the top of the selection menu. The selection menu is immediately updated with search results, which can be selected to filter the report data. In addition, you can sort the values for the parameter to expedite your search. Select the Sort icon to sort by ascending or descending order.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 10 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Controlling Columns on the Report Each report page comes with a set of columns that display data. Much like a spreadsheet, columns display individual entries as cells. Each column represents either a set of data or a calculation performed on data sets. These columns can be organized by sorting the report based on an individual column’s data.

To sort the data in a column: 1. Select the Dropdown icon on a column. 2. Select the Ascending icon to sort the data in ascending order, or select the Descending icon to sort the data in descending order. The report can also be sorted according to multiple columns in sequence by defining a custom sort. For example, a report could be sorted by Column A in descending order, followed by Column C in ascending order.

To create a custom sort: 1. Select the Dropdown icon on a column. 2. Select the Custom Sort icon. The Sort form displays. On the Sort form, you can define sort orders for multiple columns. The Sort form is applied in descending order. 3. In the first row, select the Column name to pick a column to sort. 4. Select an ascending or descending order in the Sort order field. 5. In the Nulls field, select whether null values should be considered first or last in a list, or leave the field on default settings. The default selection places null values last. 6. To add an additional row to the Sort form, click + Add new. 7. Repeat the selection process for each row you add. 8. Once all options are selected, click Apply. The Custom Sort will sort the report according to all rows included on the Sort form in sequential order. For example, you could create three rows and select Entity ID, Pay Date, and Journal ID. The

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 11 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

entire report would be sorted by Entity ID, then data for each entity ID would be sorted by Pay Date,
and the rows for each pay date would be arranged by Journal ID.

Some columns can be expanded to display additional rows of data for individual items contained within the column. For instance, the year column in a summary report could be expanded to show a row for each month.

To expand a column: 1. Select the Plus icon next to the column name. Additional data displays. 2. Select the Minus icon to minimize the column. Columns can be summarized to display an overview of the data for that specific column. This overview includes statistics such as the most frequently occurring values, the row count, the average, the median, and the variance.

To display a summary of a column: 1. Click the Dropdown icon on a column. 2. Select Column details. The Column Details form displays. The name and equation for the column appear in the About section. The Top Values section displays the most frequently-occurring values in that column. The Summary section shows the number of rows, number of null items, and number of distinct values. The Statistics section shows the average, median, maximum, minimum, and other statistics.

Note: The Column Details section also displays the Unidata attributes for the report, which allows users to learn exactly which Prism fields correspond to the data.

  1. When you are finished reviewing the details, click the X icon to close the Column Details form.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 12 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Controlling Visualizations Visualizations are graphical representations of data, such as charts and graphs. Visualizations can be used to see patterns, trends, correlations, and outliers for data sets in a focused and easily understandable format. In addition, visualizations can be examined for further information on a report to see the underlying data.

To view a visualization’s data: 1. Right click on the visualization. 2. Select Show underlying data. A table of data displays, which includes all the data for the selected visualization.

To drill down to a visualization’s data: 1. Double click on a visualization to drill down to its data.

To expand a visualization: 1. Hover the cursor over a visualization. A small menu displays in the upper-right corner. 2. Click the Expand icon to expand the visualization. The visualization is maximized to encompass the entire page.

To minimize an expanded visualization: 1. Hover the cursor over a visualization. A small menu displays in the upper-right corner. 2. Click the Minimize icon to minimize the visualization. The visualization is reverted to its default size.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 13 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Exporting Reports Reports can be exported for presentations, further calculations, or archiving. Reports can be exported into several formats, including CSV, XLS, and PDF.

Note: The export function is linked to security settings for individual user accounts. Editors and Explorers can typically export all files, while some Viewers can be granted export access on a case-by- case basis.

To export the current page of a report: 1. Select the (Additional Options) icon on a column. 2. Select Export. 3. Select a file format. Selecting PDF provides the option for Portrait layout or Landscape layout. Once a format is selected, the report will be downloaded as the selected file type.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 14 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Chapter 4 Explore Mode Explore mode provides an isolated environment that allows you to perform unrestricted ad-hoc analysis without affecting saved workbook versions. You can use Explore mode when you need quick answers to specific business questions, but you don’t need to retain the analysis for future use or sharing.

Note: Changes made to a report using Explore Mode can be saved as Views. Unsaved explorations are available in the Recents page for 30 days. Making permanent changes to a report or creating new reports requires the Editor role.

Accessing Explore Mode The Explorer user type grants access to Explore mode, which can be enabled directly from a report. You can freely toggle between View mode and Explore mode on each individual report.

To enable Explore mode: 1. Open a report. 2. Scroll through the list (or search) and click the report icon or the information icon. The Report Details panel displays.

Using Explore Mode You can perform ad hoc analysis in Explore mode. Like Edit mode, this includes the following functionality: l Create, modify, and delete content such as pages and elements

l Edit the workbook layout

l View, filter, and sort underlying data

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 15 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

l View and change the data source of a workbook

l View the workbook lineage

l View custom SQL logic

l Export workbook pages or element data

Worksheets Dataset worksheets allow you to structure and manipulate its data. You can create calculations, group data, apply filters and formats, add parameters, etc. A dataset’s worksheet must contain at least one data source. Examples of data sources include tables from your organization’s data warehouse, uploaded CSVs, and even other datasets.

Worksheet Tab

Each worksheet page is divided into several parts. Worksheet pages are designed with a similar appearance and functionality to spreadsheets to make it easier to review, analyze, and manipulate your data.

Creating Data Elements Each workbook can contain multiple elements sourced from a variety of data sources. You can pull in new data sources at any time and are not restricted to a single source per workbook or workbook page. An element’s data can be sourced from cloud data warehouse (CDW) tables, Sigma datasets, uploaded CSVs, written SQL, or other workbook data elements.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 16 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Note: Creating data elements is a feature only available to Editors. Uploading CSVs and writing custom SQL are features only available to organization Administrators.

Creating a Data Element from a New Source While in Edit mode, you can create a data element from a source that is not currently in use in the current workbook.

To create a data element from a new source: 1. Select Add New. The Add New panel displays. 2. In the Data Elements section, select the desired element type. These include Table, VIZ, or Pivot Table. 3. In the Select source for Table section, select the New tab. 4. Select the source type. For most users, this will be Tables and Datasets. The Select source form displays. 5. In the Select source section, select a table or dataset from the available options. 6. Click Done. The new element displays on the editor panel and is available to customize.

Creating a Data Element from a Current Source While in Edit mode, you can create a data element from a source currently in use in the current workbook to save time and set up new elements more efficiently.

To create a data element from an in-use source: 1. Select Add New. The Add New panel displays. 2. In the Data Elements section, select the desired element type. These include Table, VIZ, or Pivot Table. 3. In the Select source for Table section, select the In Use tab. A list of sources currently in use on the page displays. 4. On the In Use tab, select a workbook element or dataset from the available options. 5. Click Done. The new element displays on the editor panel and is available to customize.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 17 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Creating a Data Element from an Existing Element via the Editor Panel Using this option, you can create a new element from an existing element on the workbook using the editor panel. For example, you could create a table for additional calculations that pulls information from an existing data table.

To create a data element from an existing element: 1. Select Add New. The Add New panel displays. 2. In the Data Elements section, select the desired element type. These include Table, VIZ, or Pivot Table. 3. In the Select source for Table section, select the Page Elements tab. A list of elements on the page displays. 4. On the Page Elements tab, select an element from the available options. 5. Click Done. The new element displays on the editor panel and is available to customize.

Creating a Data Element from an Existing Element via the Canvas Using this option, you can create a new element from an existing element on the workbook using the page’s canvas. Using this method, you can select the source immediately at the start to quickly get results, which can be helpful for reports with a long list of elements.

To create a data element from an existing element via the canvas: 1. Hover the mouse over the element you would like to use as a source. The Context menu displays in the upper-right corner. 2. In the Context menu, select the (Create child element) icon. 3. Select the desired element type. These include Table, VIZ, or Pivot Table. The new element displays on the editor panel and is available to customize.

Data Elements Workbooks typically contain a collection of elements on a single page and/or distributed across multiple pages. There are three element types: data elements, UI elements, and control elements. Each has a unique function, and they collectively allow you to display, interact with, and provide additional context to your data. Workbook editors define elements and can individually configure them for viewer interaction.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 18 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Data elements include tables, pivot tables, and visualizations built directly from a data source. A workbook can contain a variety of data elements derived from multiple data sources.

Note: An Editor license is required to create data elements and tables. Explorers can still create visualizations.

This section describes the data elements available on a report page in more detail. l Tables. Tables are a data element with a spreadsheet-like interface for structuring and manipulation of data in a familiar environment. Tables support much of a traditional spreadsheet’s functionality, like creating calculations and applying filters and formats. They also support a variety of other features such as data grouping and summaries. Unlike a spreadsheet, data in tables is managed on a column level rather than individual cells. Calculations and formatting changes are applied to every cell in a column. l Visualizations. Visualizations are graphical data elements that add visual context to your analysis. They allow you to create, explore, and view your data in a more focused and digestible format. By adding visualizations to a workbook, you can reveal patterns, trends, outliers, and correlations crucial to creating a compelling data narrative. Visualizations include bar charts, line charts, KPI charts, Area charts, scatter plots, combo charts, box charts, pie charts, sankey diagrams, funnel charts, gauge charts, region maps, point maps, and geography maps. l Pivot Tables. Pivot tables are specialized data tables which can be used to calculate, summarize, and analyze data to find trends and patterns. Select a Pivot Row or Pivot Column, then add additional columns to the Value field. Columns added to the Value field are aggregated automatically according to the type of column. l Input Tables. Input tables are dynamic workbook elements that support structured data entry. They allow you to integrate new data points into your analysis and augment existing data to facilitate rapid prototyping, advanced modeling, forecasting, what-if analysis, and more— without overwriting source data. l Linked Input Tables. Linked input tables support data entry alongside existing datasets, or data elements in the same workbook. As a child element, a linked input table includes one or more columns that reference source columns in the parent element. This includes a primary key column, which provides row identifiers that define the input table’s granularity and link manually entered data to existing data in the parent element. Maintaining the data relationship between the input table and parent element requires the primary key column to reference static data in the parent element. All other linked columns can reference variable data, which is continually updated in the input table to reflect live data from the root source.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 19 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

UI Elements Workbooks typically contain a collection of elements on a single page and/or distributed across multiple pages. There are three element types: data elements, UI elements, and control elements. UI elements include buttons, dividers, images, spacers, embeds, and text used to add context and/or workbook styling. This section describes the UI elements available on a report page in more detail. l Text. Text UI elements allow you to add titles and captions to your workbook pages. You can choose the size, style, and font. The text can include dynamic content from formulas. For more information see Text Elements. l Images. You can add an image to your workbook page by uploading or referencing a URL. You can use images settings to change how images fit within the dashboard container, and reference control variables within the image embed URL to customize images on a per-dashboard basis. l Buttons. A button directs users to an external website URL or a different Sigma page. You can choose whether the link opens in a new browser tab, and you can optionally add control values. There are also customization options for button title and style. l Embedded Element. An embed element adds a webpage, video, or other Sigma workbook to a page. Any iFrame-enabled URL can be embedded. Use control variables within your embed URL to customize what content is displayed according to different inputs. l Dividers. A Horizontal divider visually partitions elements or groups of elements on a page. A spacer creates empty visual space on the page canvas, pushing elements up, down, to the left, or to the right. l Plugins. You can add plugin elements to workbooks, to support custom functionality. You only have access to plugins registered with your organization. Plugins are third-party applications built to add additional functionality into an existing product. For example, a software developer in your organization may create a plugin that lets you display your data in a chart type not otherwise supported in the report builder. l PDF Export Elements. The Page Break element can manually set a page break for PDF exports onto the report.

Control Elements Control elements (controls) and data elements combine together on reports. Data elements display the data, and controls manipulate the displayed data by filtering and/or using parameters. Controls are basically filters, and sometimes the terminology is interchangeable. Any field can be turned into a

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 20 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

control element, and editors add controls to a workbook to manipulate the workbook’s data based on user input.

Note: Control elements fulfill the same role as the parameters in the legacy report system.

When a user views an existing workbook and does not have permissions or the need to edit the report, control elements can provide a way to customize the data that displays. The user can change the value of a control element to update the displayed data in any elements targeted by that control. For example, a List control shows the filter values from which you can select:

The targeted data element updates to show the filtered results:

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 21 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To create a control: 1. If you are not in Edit mode, select Edit mode. 2. In the editor panel, click + Add Element. 3. Select a control type. The new control element displays on the page. 4. In the Settings panel, select configuration settings for the control. 5. In the Targets panel, select the element to be controlled.

Types of Controls You define a control by setting its type, settings, and target data. The following control types are provided: l List. A list presets a set of options, and the user can select which values on the list are included. All other values are excluded. Lists can be used to control Text, Numbers, or Dates columns. A maximum of 200 values can be displayed on a single list. l Text. The text control allows the user to search for full or partial matches for an input text string. The input can be set to Contains, Starts with, Ends with, or Like. This option can be used to control Text columns.

l Number or Number Range. A Number control uses a single value, while a Number Range provides a range between two numbers. This option can be used to control Numbers columns.

l Date. The Date control uses a single date as a parameter value. Only values with the matching date are included in the data. This control supports both fixed and relative dates. This option can be used to control Dates columns.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 22 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

l Date Range. The Date Range control can be used to specify two dates, and only values within the specified range are included in the data. This control supports both fixed and relative dates. This option can be used to control Dates columns.

l Top N. The Top N filter can be used to only display the top # of columns on a report, such as the highest three values or the top five earners. This control can be customized to display the Top N, Bottom N, Top Percentile, or Bottom Percentile. This option can be used to control Text, Numbers, and Dates columns.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 23 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

l Drill Down. The Drill Down control allows users to view pre-defined layers of data. The editor defines a drill path by selecting a value source. When the user views the item, they can select the values from the drill path to drill down to that data. This option can control Text, Numbers, Dates, and Boolean columns.

l Switch. The Switch control is a binary toggle which can be used to switch between True and False values.

Convert an Existing Filter to a Control When performing an ad-hoc filter on a report, you can convert the filter you have created directly into a control. The original data element is automatically added as a target for the control. The control can then be customized with additional targets or settings using the editor panel.

Note: When you create a control from an element filter, the existing filter remain accessible. Changing the input value of the filter updates the input value in the control and vice versa.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 24 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To convert an existing filter to a control: 1. If you are not in Edit mode, select Edit mode. 2. Click the (Filter) icon for the corresponding element. The Filters menu displays. 3. Click the (Additional Options) icon. The Additional Options menu displays. 4. Select Convert to page control. The filter is converted into a control, and the editor panel displays with the control’s configurable settings.

Synchronizing Controls Synced controls are workbook control elements that have identical, synchronized copies. Both filter controls and parameters support synced copies. For example, a report could show the entire organization’s sales data on one page, and focus on individual regions on a second page. The Date controls for the pages could be synchronized so that you can quickly compare overall and regional sales data without reentering the date range.

To synchronize controls: 1. Select the control to copy and synchronize. 2. Hover the cursor over the element and select (Additional Options). 3. Select Create a synced copy. A copy of the control is added to the page. 4. Hover the cursor over the copy and select (Additional Options). 5. Select Move to to move the copied element to a new page. The synchronized copy is moved to the new page. 6. In the Targets panel, select the element on the new page to be controlled by the synchronized copy.

Identifying and Editing Data Sources While in Edit mode, you can select an element to quickly identify and edit its data source. You can use this feature to inspect data sources, make changes to existing elements without recreating them, and help construct new elements.

To identify an element’s data source: 1. While in Edit mode, select the element. An element’s data source is listed at the bottom of the editor panel when the element is selected.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 25 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To edit an element’s data source: 1. While in Edit mode, select the element. 2. Click the (Dropdown) icon. 3. Select Change source. The Edit source panel appears. 4. Make selections on the Edit source panel to choose a different source. These options include a new source not in use on the workbook, a source currently in use, or a page element.

The Formula Bar Each worksheet has a formula bar positioned near the top of the page.

Custom calculations can be created using the Formula bar. You can create custom columns by entering a mathematical formula that can employ data elements from one or more data sets. Formulas are applied to columns, not cells. When a formula is applied to a column, it is applied to all rows in that column. Every column has a formula, including those that directly reference data from your data source. To view a column’s formula, select the column and its formula will automatically appear in the formula bar.

To create a custom calculation: 1. While in Explore or Edit mode, select New Column. 2. With the new column selected, select the Formula bar at the top of the edit panel. 3. Enter the formula in the Formula bar. The system automatically generates suggestions to complete function names and column names. 4. Once the formula is complete, press Enter. The formula calculation is applied to the new column, and the calculated data displays.

The Function Index The formula bar includes the (Function Index) icon located to the left of the calculation section. Selecting this icon opens the Function Index in a new window. The Function Index is a comprehensive list of functions that are usable in Sigma. You can browse the index to brainstorm ideas of how you can calculate your data, or investigate specific functions to get further information about a calculation. The Function Index is an essential tool for expanding your knowledge of functions to perform complex analysis of your data.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 26 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Configuration Panel The Configuration Panel is used to add, review, and modify elements on a worksheet page.

The Configuration Panel options depend on which element is selected on a page. These options include: Add Element: Select this panel to add a new element to a page, including tables, visualizations, and pivot tables. For more information, refer to the corresponding element type. The Editor license is required to create certain elements. Page Overview: Select this panel to display an overview of all elements on the page in a list format. Using this list, you can select and edit elements quickly and efficiently, without having to locate them on the page itself.

Element Properties: Select this panel to customize the properties of an element, such as the groupings and columns of a data table or the layout of a visualization.

Note: The icon for the Element Properties panel changes depending on the type of element currently selected.

Element Format: Select this panel to customize the appearance of an element, such as fonts, text size and color, background color, stylistic details of charts and graphs, and other features. The options available in this panel depend on the type of element selected.

Actions: This feature is currently in beta. This panel can be used to define custom actions on reports. For example, you can define an action so that clicking an icon at the end of the report immediately scrolls the page back to the top.

Creating Tables Tables support much of a traditional spreadsheet’s functionality, like creating calculations and applying filters and formats. They also support a variety of other features such as data grouping and summaries.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 29 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To create a table: 1. If you are not in Edit mode, select Edit mode. 2. In the Editor panel, click + Add Element. 3. In the Data Elements section, select Table. 4. In the Select source for Table section, select the a data source. The table is created using the columns available in the data source.

Columns and Cells While tables are similar to spreadsheets, data is managed at the column level rather than on individual cells. This means actions such as calculations and formatting changes are applied to every cell in a column. Managing data at the column level ensures consistency and accuracy, and prevents common errors, across large and ever-growing sets of data.

To add a new column to a table: 1. If you are not in Edit mode, select Edit mode. 2. In the Editor panel, click Add Column. Additional options display.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 30 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

  1. Select Add new column. The new column is created, and the cursor moves to the Formula Bar.
  2. Enter a formula in the Formula Bar to create a new column.

To search for a column to add to a table: 1. In the Editor panel, click Add Column. Additional options display. 2. Select Add column via. 3. Select Lookup. The Add Lookup panel displays, where you can search for a column. 4. In the Select element field, select a data source. 5. In the Column to add field, select which column should be included. 6. To create an aggregate of this field, select an aggregate type in the Aggregate field. 7. In the Map two elements section, select two columns with matching values to use as keys for comparison. For instance, if you are pulling a column from payroll data to add to a table using sales data, and both data sets have a Client ID field, the Client ID could be used as a key to match the new column to the current data set. 8. Click Done. The new column is added to the table.

To search for a column to add to a table: 1. In the Editor panel, click Add Column. Additional options display. 2. Select Add column via. 3. Select elect Period over period comparison. The Add Comparison panel displays, where you can search for a column. 4. Select the main value to use in the Compare field field. 5. To create an aggregate of this field, select an aggregate type in the Aggregate field. 6. In the Using date column field, select a date period for the comparison. 7. In the Comparison time frame field, select a time frame. 8. Make selections in the Output fields to customize the final column. 9. Click Done. The new comparison column is added to the table.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 31 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To add a column from current sources: 1. In the Editor panel, click Add Column. Additional options display. 2. Select Add source columns. A list of all columns on data sources currently in use on the page displays. 3. Select one or more columns using the check boxes to add to the table.

Groups and Groupings Groups and groupings, which are unique to tables, are an excellent tool for comparative analysis. They allow you to analyze rows of data based on shared values within a single column. Any column in a table can be used to define a grouping. When used to define a grouping, the column becomes a grouping key. Its individual rows merge into single cells based on their distinct values. Subsequently, the rows of data to the right of the key column in the table are bundled into groups based on each unique value in the key column. Group aggregates can then be calculated based on the cell values within each row in the group.

To add a group to a table: 1. While in Edit mode, select the table. 2. In the Element Properties panel, select the column to use as the grouping key and drag the column to the Groupings section. The column is added as a grouping key for the table.

Subtotals Subtotals are aggregate values of a single column. Subtotals can be defined on a column-by-column basis to total up specific sections of data.

To create a summary of a data table: 1. In Edit mode, select the menu icon of a column. 2. On the Editor panel, select Show totals.

Summaries Summaries are single-value column aggregates that are calculated at a table’s highest aggregation level. Summaries can be created in Edit mode.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 32 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To create a summary of a data table: 1. In Edit mode, select the data table. The editor panel displays. 2. Select Summary in the table footer. 3. Click the (Add Summary) button. The Summary menu displays. 4. Select one of the following summary options: l New Summary: Select this option to create a blank summary column and display the formula bar. Type in a custom formula to create the summary. l Row Count: Select this option to create a summary of the total number of rows in the table. If the table includes groupings, this calculation will match the total number of rows in the highest grouping. l Aggregate Column: Select a column or search for a column in the Aggregate Column section to create a summary aggregate, such as Sum or Count. The new summary displays at the bottom of the table. To customize the summary, select the summary field and click the (Menu Dropdown) icon. Using this menu, you can customize the summary just like an ordinary column.

Applying Conditional Formatting Tables can be formatted with conditions to highlight certain values. These conditions are created as rules in the Table formatting.

To apply conditional formatting: 1. Select the Table. 2. Select the (Element Format) icon. 3. Select Conditional Formatting. 4. Select + Add rule. A new rule is created, which can then be defined with additional options. 5. In the Apply to field, select a variable for the rule, or select All columns to apply the rule to all columns in the table. 6. Select a format for the rule to apply. These options include: l Single Color: If the rule in the Formatting rule field is true, the color is applied to the cell.

l Color Scale: The selected color scale is applied to the variable based on its relative value. This color can be applied to the cell or characters based on the selection in the Apply field.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 33 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

l Data Bars: Each cell displays a bar of the selected color with a width depending on its relative value. A customized number range can be defined using the Customize Domain field.

Creating Pivot Tables Pivot tables are specialized data tables which can be used to calculate, summarize, and analyze data to find trends and patterns.

To create a pivot table: 1. If you are not in Edit mode, select Edit mode. 2. In the editor panel, click + Add Element. 3. In the Data Elements section, select Pivot Table. 4. In the Select source for Table section, select the a data source. 5. In the Pivot Rows section, select one or more variables to be added as rows of the pivot table. If multiple variables are defined, each variable is grouped in sequential order. In the example above, Store Region is the first variable and forms the primary group, with Store State as the second variable. 6. In the Pivot Columns section, select one or more variables to be added as rows of the pivot table. If multiple variables are defined, each variable is grouped in sequential order.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 34 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

  1. In the Values section, select the values to be shown in the Pivot Table cells. If multiple variables are added, the order of the variables can be defined by changing their position in the Values section.

Note: Pivot tables can be expanded and collapsed by both rows and columns if multiple variables are added to the Pivot Rows or Pivot Columns sections.

Defining Aggregates Variables added to the Value section are aggregated by default. Aggregation type (e.g. Sum vs Count) is dependent on the original column’s value type (e.g. text, number, date, etc). Aggregations can be changed to customize the Pivot Table.

To change the aggregation of a value on a pivot table: 1. In the Editor panel, hover over the variable in the Values section and click the menu icon. 2. Select Set aggregate. 3. Select the type of aggregate to use for the variable.

Applying Conditional Formatting Pivot tables can be formatted with conditions to highlight certain values. These conditions are created as rules in the Pivot Table formatting.

To apply conditional formatting: 1. Select the Pivot Table. 2. Select the (Element Format) icon. 3. Select Conditional Formatting. 4. Select + Add rule. A new rule is created, which can then be defined with additional options. 5. In the Apply to field, select a variable for the rule. The options available include the variables in the Pivot Rows, Pivot Columns, and Values. 6. Select a format for the rule to apply. These options include: l Single Color: If the rule in the Formatting rule field is true, the color is applied to the cell.

l Color Scale: The selected color scale is applied to the variable based on its relative value. This color can be applied to the cell or characters based on the selection in the Apply field. l Data Bars: Each cell displays a bar of the selected color with a width depending on its relative value. A customized number range can be defined using the Customize Domain field.

Joining Tables Editors can join data between warehouse tables or datasets to expand the scope of their custom reports and analyze data in unique ways. Joining data takes multiple data sets and combines them together using a join key, or a key piece of data shared by both sets. For example, you might join a set of employee insurance records and a set of employee retirement records. Each data set contains the Employee ID field. By using the Employee ID as the join key, the two tables can be combined together, with each employee’s insurance and retirement records being organized by their Employee ID.

To create a table join from scratch: 1. Click the + Add Element button. 2. Select Table. 3. On the Element Properties panel, select Join in the New column.

The Select source panel displays. The Select source panel includes the New, In Use, and Page

Types of Joins

Lookup: Lookup returns all of the rows in the current data and data from the matching rows in the joined data while maintaining the number of rows in the current data. If Sigma finds more than one match for the current data in the joined data, it returns a * in the corresponding row. Lookup functions like a VLOOKUP function in spreadsheets.

Inner Join: The inner join returns the rows that exist in both the current data and the joined data. Removes all rows that do not have data in both the current data and joined data.

Left Outer Join: The left outer join returns all of the rows in the current data, and all the data from the matching rows in the joined data. It adds rows when there is more than one match. This can result in an expanded row count.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 40 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Right Outer Join: The right outer join returns all of the rows from the joined data, and the data from the matching rows in the current data. It adds rows when there is more than one match. When the current data has more than one row that matches to joined data, all of the matches rows are retained.

Outer Join: A full outer join returns all of the rows from the current data and all of the rows in the joined data, making matches where possible.

3rd Party Import Process Editors can use the new 3rd Party Import process to import a CSV file from outside sources to be used in reports. After importing the file, the data is implemented as a grid implement within the report, which can be manipulated like other data sources, including sorting, filtering, grouping, pivoting, and creating visualizations.

Note: This feature is only available for editors. Once the data has been imported by an editor, the workbook can be shared with other users.

Note: For security purposes, access to the 3rd Party Import process requires specific permission for each individual. Administrators can grant access to this feature.

To import 3rd Party Data: 1. In the report workbook, enter Edit mode by selecting Edit. 2. Click the (Add Element) icon to add a new element.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 41 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

  1. In the Data Elements section, select CSV. The Upload CSV form displays.
  2. Drag a file into the Upload CSV section or click Browse to locate the file.
  3. Use the Parsing Options section to configure the headers, delimiters, and other separators if necessary. A preview of the table displays on the Results tab. The system automatically attempts to match headers to column names and values to each attribute type, but the editor can override the values to make corrections to the import.
  4. Once the table has been verified, click Save. The data is saved as a new data table element and displayed on the workbook. The data can then be manipulated and used for visualizations just like any other table.
  5. Rename the table. By default, the table is named New Input Table, but the editor can immediately rename the table to any appropriate name.

Note: CSV files are limited to 200 MBs for this feature. To import larger data sources, editors should split the file into several CSVs and merge the tables together.

Joining 3rd Party Import Data While data from the 3rd Party Import process can be manipulated directly, some editors may wish to join the table with information that already exists in the system. The import process does not create a dataset, and therefore the data can’t be combined with a table join. However, the data can be merged into a single element using the lookup feature.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 42 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To merge 3rd party data with an existing source: 1. In Edit mode, click the Down Arrow icon on the column name. An options menu displays. 2. Select Add New Column > Via Lookup. The Add lookup window displays. 3. In the Select element field, select the data tables to merge into the current element. 4. In the Column(s) to add field, select the columns to merge into the existing data. 5. In the Map two elements section, select two columns with matching values to use to join the two tables together, much like selecting join keys to join tables. 6. Verify that the match will work properly using the KEYS WITH MATCHES section, then click Done. The selected columns are merged into the selected data table.

Customizing Visualizations Visualizations feature various properties and formatting options that determine how your data is represented. With a wide range of customizable configurations, you can enhance your visualizations and ensure they present meaningful and actionable information.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 44 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To customize the properties of a visualization: 1. Access a report in Explore Mode. 2. Select the visualization on the report.

  1. Select the (Element Properties) icon to customize the functionality of the visualization. The Element Properties panel displays.
  2. Make changes on the Element Properties panel to customize the visualization. The changes are applied automatically.
  3. Select the (Element Format) icon to customize the appearance of the visualization. The Element Format panel displays.
  4. Make changes on the Element Format panel to customize the visualization. The changes are applied automatically.

The Element Properties Panel The Element Properties panel requires you to select a visualization type and configure source columns to define chart properties, including axis categories, metrics, colors, and tooltips. You can convert data value types, change the data aggregation or truncation, and customize chart markers and tooltips. Depending on the visualization type selected, you may also have options to change the chart orientation, modify data stacking, and add trellis rows and columns.

The Element Format Panel The Element format panel allows you to customize the appearance of various components, including the visualization title’s content, size, and alignment. Depending on the visualization type selected, you may also be able to format the background, axes, legend, data labels, reference marks, trend lines, and more.

Formatting Visualizations The Element format panel allows you to customize the appearance of various components, including the visualization title’s content, size, and alignment. Depending on the visualization type selected, you may also be able to format the background, axes, legend, data labels, reference marks, trend lines, and more.

Bar Charts Bar charts are typically used to compare values across categories or groups of data. Create basic single- series bar charts, or build advanced charts to compare multiple variables, measure values against reference marks, evaluate parts of a whole, and more. Bar charts contain the following variables: l X-Axis: This variable controls the horizontal axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. l Y-Axis: This variable controls the vertical axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. You can define multiple variables on a bar chart by adding multiple columns on the Y axis. You can customize the orientation of the bar chart using the Element Properties panel. The following options display directly below the Visualization selection menu:

   Orientation
   Vertical: Categorize data on the x-axis and measure
   values on the y-axis to create vertical bar marks.

   Horizontal: Categorize data on the y-axis and measure
   values on the x-axis to create horizontal bar marks.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 46 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Line Charts Line charts are typically used to assess how values change over time. Create basic single-line charts to spot trends and identify anomalies in your dataset. You can also build advanced multi-line charts to analyze and compare multiple variables over the same period of time. Line charts contain the following variables: l X-Axis: controls the horizontal axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. l Y-Axis: controls the vertical axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. You can define multiple variables on a line chart by adding multiple columns on the Y axis. On the Element Format panel, you can define different line styles for your line chart.

Straight Create straight lines between data points.

Smooth Create a curved line that runs through data points.

Step Create a step up or down between data points, with the vertical line occurring at the midpoint.

Step Create a step up or down between data points, with the (Before) vertical change occurring before the horizontal line.

Step Create a step up or down between data points, with the (After) vertical change occurring after the horizontal line.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 48 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

In addition, you can customize how null data points are displayed on the line chart.

Zero Plot null values as zero-value data points.

Interpolate Disregard null values and continue the line path between non-null data points.

Hide Omit line paths through null data points.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 49 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

KPI Charts Key performance indicator (KPI) charts highlight single metric values typically used to measure performance or progress toward goals. Create a KPI chart to summarize the total value of a metric for a specific period, or include additional data to compare the metric’s value over time and measure it against a benchmark or target value. KPI charts include the following variables: l Value: This variable determines that value that will be used to gauge performance.

l Timeline: If a timeline is enabled, the Value will be displayed over a reporting period.

l Comparison: If a comparison is enabled, the Value is compared to either a static metric or a sequential metric. KPI charts include several variations, which can be configured by including and defining properties for the Timeline and Comparison elements.

Name Summary Image

Summary Summarize the metric’s global value to Value understand overall performance or magnitude. Requires a defined Value.

Benchmark Summarize a metric’s global value against a Summary benchmark or target value. Assess relative Comparison performance and gain insight into patterns, relationships, and correlations. Requires a defined Value and a Comparison with Column selected.

Period Value Measure a metric’s period value to analyze performance during a specific time interval (like week, month, or year). Requires a defined Value and a Timeline.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 50 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Period Measure a metric’s value in one period (a week, Comparison month, or year) against another to perform a sequential or period-over-period comparison. Requires a defined Value, a Timeline, and a Comparison with Period selected.

Benchmark Compare a metric’s period value against a Period benchmark or target to assess relative Comparison performance and gain insight into patterns, relationships, and correlations. Requires a defined Value, a Timeline, and a Comparison with Column selected.

Area charts contain the following variables: l X-Axis: This variable controls the horizontal axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. l Y-Axis: This variable controls the vertical axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. You can define multiple variables on an area chart by adding multiple columns on the Y axis. On the Element Format panel, you can define different area styles for your area chart.

No Stacking Areas start from the X axis and might overlap. Stacked Areas stack on top of each other. Stacked 100% All areas add up to 100% of the area.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 52 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Scatter Plot Scatter plots are typically used to demonstrate a correlation (or lack thereof) between two different variables. Create basic scatter plots to assess patterns, trends, and outliers in your dataset. You can also build advanced charts to include additional variables, plot trend lines, and display data points across quadrants. Scatter plots contain the following variables: l X-Axis: This variable controls the horizontal axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. l Y-Axis: This variable controls the vertical axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. You can define multiple variables on a scatter plot by adding multiple columns on the Y axis. On the Element Format panel, you can define different styles for your scatter plot.

Single For each data series, enter a hex code or select an option Color from the color palette or color picker.

By Select a source column to define color categories, then Category select or customize a color palette for the resulting multiple series.

By Scale Select a source column to define a color scale, then select a color range to apply to the marks.

You can use the Size tab to define the size of each point on the scatter plot. You can use the Point Style section to define the shape of the points, including circles, squares, crosses, diamonds, and triangles.

Conditional Formatting When you select Single Color for the scatter plot, you can configure formatting rules that determine colors according to value-based conditions. This creates exceptions to the single-color selection, allowing you to highlight values that meet specific conditions. For example:

Rule Formatting Result

Reference Marks On the Element Format panel, you can define reference marks for your scatter plot.

Combo Charts Combo charts are a type of visualization that uses a mixture of chart types. Sigma combo charts support bars, lines, areas and scatter plots. Combo charts contain the following variables: l X-Axis: This variable controls the horizontal axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. l Y-Axis: This variable controls the vertical axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. You can define multiple variables on a bar chart by adding multiple columns on the Y axis. On the Element Format panel, you can define different styles for your combo plot.

Bar The variable uses the Bar Chart configuration options. Line The variable uses the Line Chart configuration options. Area The variable uses the Area Chart configuration options. Scatter The variable uses the Scatter Chart configuration options.

Box and Whisker Charts Box and whisker charts display the distribution of a set of values along an axis. They are also commonly known as box plots. Box and Whisker charts contain the following variables: l X-Axis: This variable controls the horizontal axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. l Y-Axis: This variable controls the vertical axis of the graph. To add a variable, click (Add column). Then, select Add new column. You can define multiple variables on a bar chart by adding multiple columns on the Y axis. l Split By: If this optional variable is defined, it creates a second grouping under the first grouping defined on the X-axis. On the Element Format panel, you can customize the Box and Whisker chart to display vertically or horizontally.

Pie and Donut Charts Pie and Donuts Charts are used to visualize data as a percentage of a total, displayed as a circular area. Pie and donut charts contain the following variables: l Color: This variable defines the color scheme used by the pie or donut chart.

l Value: This variable defines the column that is aggregated to create the plot. The aggregation is automatically set to Sum or Count depending on the source column’s value type. On the Element Format panel, you can define different certain elements for your pie and donut charts. Tooltip: Choose columns to show when hovering over points in the chart. Trellis: select columns to serve as trellis rows or columns to split the chart.
