Sankey Diagrams Sankey diagrams are typically used to assess the flow and change of data between stages in a process or system. Create simple Sankey diagrams to demonstrate data distribution, workflows, networks, and more, or build advanced multi-level diagrams to analyze complex data relationships and identify changes in variables across stages, categories, or periods. Sankey diagrams contain the following variables: Stage: This variable configures the stage categories using distinct values in a source column or custom formula. This source data can be optionally categorized in the following ways: l Truncate Date: Categorize date values by an interval or unit of measure, such as week or month.

l Transform: Convert the column to another data value type.

l Format: Display data labels in the selected format.

Variable: This configures the source column to use as the data path. The column data is automatically aggregated. This source data can be optionally categorized in the following ways: l Set Aggregate: Calculate values based on the selected aggregation method.

l Transform: Convert the column to another data value type.

l Format: Display data labels in the selected format.

On the Element Format panel, you can define different styles for your Sankey diagram. l To rename a source column, double-click the column name in the Stage or Value property, then enter a new name. l To edit the chart title, double-click the title in the visualization, then enter a new title.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 58 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Funnel Charts Funnel charts are typically used to measure values across sequential stages in a linear process. Create funnel charts to evaluate inputs across each stage and discover potential issues and bottlenecks in a workflow.

Note: When your data source includes a single column with stage names as values, use the Stage property. Alternatively, if the data source breaks down each stage as a distinct column of data, aggregate the individual stage columns in the Value property.

Funnel charts contain the following variables: Stage: This variable generates stages for the levels of the funnel chart. Value: This variable configures the source column to use as the data path. The column data is automatically aggregated. This source data can be optionally categorized in the following ways: l Set Aggregate: Calculate values based on the selected aggregation method.

l Transform: Convert the column to another data value type.

l Format: Display data labels in the selected format.

On the Element Format panel, you can define different line styles for your funnel chart.

By If only one source column is configured in the Value Category property, the chart defaults to categorical colors that represent stages.

By If multiple source columns are configured in the Value Category property, the chart defaults to stacked series with (Multiple) categorical colors that represent each of those columns.

By Scale Select a source column to define a scaled color variable, then select a color range to apply to the marks.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 59 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Gauge Charts Gauge charts are typically used to display a measurable value against a radial scale. Create gauge charts to evaluate growth, assess performance, or track progress toward a goal. Gauge charts contain the following variables: Value: This variable determines the column or calculation used for the values on the gauge chart. Minimum: This variable determines the minimum value on the gauge. Maximum: This variable determines the maximum value on the gauge. Target: This optional variable adds a target value to the gauge. On the Element Format panel, you can define different line styles for your gauge chart.

Single Enter a hex code or select a color for the gauge fill (the area that color extends from the minimum value to the measurable value).

By Select a color scale to apply to the gauge. Scale

Conditional Formatting When you select Single Color for the gauge chart, you can configure formatting rules that determine colors according to value-based conditions. This creates exceptions to the single-color selection, allowing you to highlight values that meet specific conditions. For example, you can define the variable colors at different percentages so that anything less than 25% shows in red, 25-75% shows in yellow, and 75% and higher shows in green. You can also define conditions based on the Value field. For example, if the value field has met a threshold, the gauge could show in green, but if the value is beneath the threshold, the gauge displays in red.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 60 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Maps Maps are visualizations and can be created via the PAGE ELEMENTS section of your workbook’s editor panel or directly from an existing data element. Workbooks support three distinct map types: Region, Point and Geography. You should choose your map type based on your available data and the results you wish to see. For example, if you want to map a text column [State] with cell values like “Colorado” and “California”, you should choose a Region map type. Region maps contain the following variables: Region: This variable requires a text column indicating the region. The following region types are supported: l Countries (defined by name, formal name, acronym, or ISO 3166-1 indication)

l US States (defined by name or shortcode)

l US Counties (defined in “Name, State” format, or by FIPS code)

l US Zip Codes

l Canada Provinces (defined by name or shortcode)

Point maps contain the following variables: Latitude: This variable requires a number column containing the latitude coordinates. Longitude: This variable requires a number column containing the longitude coordinates.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 61 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Geography Maps Geography maps (Map - Geography visualization type) support datasets with geography data (WKT format) or variant data (GeoJSON format) and are typically used to illustrate geospatial objects on a map. You can create a connection map to display spatial networks, correlations, and relationships, or build a choropleth map to identify variability and patterns across distinct geographic areas.

Views The Views feature allows users to save the changes made to a workbook for later viewing. Views are only visible to their creator. In addition, the Views feature saves snapshots of recent explorations on a report, so even if a user forgets to create a view, they can go back to the report later and see their previous changes. For example, if you set the date and location controls on a workbook to display results for the last three month in a specific region, you could save a view to quickly view the workbook with those exact conditions again. The Views menu can be accessed by clicking the Views button or the (Views) icon.

To create a View: 1. On a workbook page, make changes using controls or the Explore mode. 2. Click the (Views) icon. The Views menu displays. 3. Select Save as new view. A new view is created for the current view.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 62 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

To load a View on a workbook: 1. Click the (Views) icon. The Views menu displays. 2. Select Saved views. A list of all your views displays. 3. Click the name of the view. The workbook updates with the view configuration.

To delete a View: 1. Load a view on the current workbook using the procedure above. 2. Click the (Views) icon. The Views menu displays. 3. On the view to clear, select the (Options) menu. 4. Select Delete. The view is deleted.

To manage Views: 1. Click the (Views) icon. The Views menu displays.

  1. Select Manage saved views. The Views panel displays with a list of all your saved views and custom views. On the Views panel, you can set a view as your default, edit the name of a view, or delete the view.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 63 Chapter 4 Explore Mode

Revisiting Recent Configurations The Views feature saves snapshots of recent explorations on a report for up to thirty days. These display on the Explorations tab of the Views panel, with timestamps indicating when the change took place. You can load a recent exploration by selecting a timestamp from this panel. In addition, you can click the arrow icon next to the timestamp to view details about what changes were made.

To view recent changes on a report: 1. Click the (Views) icon. The Views menu displays. 2. Select Manage saved views. The Views panel displays. 3. Select the Custom views tab. A list of recent views displays. These are snapshots of recent changes made on the report, arranged according to their timestamps. 4. Select a timestamp to load the recent view.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 64 Chapter 5 Creating and Publishing Workbooks

Chapter 5 Creating and Publishing Workbooks Workbooks have three states: explore, draft, and publish. When you create a workbook, it is in an explore state until you actively save the first version. You can keep a workbook in the explore state and never save it. For example, you may need conduct ad hoc data exploration and analysis that is only needed in the current moment, and you don’t want to clutter folders with one-off documents. Unsaved workbooks are called explorations and are available in the Recents page for 30 days. You can save a workbook for continuing your analysis and setting up reporting. If you decide to share your exploration with your colleagues, you can publish the workbook.

Ad hoc Data Exploration New, unsaved workbooks are also referred to as explorations. Explorations are ideal for ad hoc analysis, when you want to explore your data and move on without saving your work for future use. To save an exploration as a published workbook, click Save as in the exploration’s header.

Drafts and Publishing Edits made to a workbook are automatically saved as a shared, live draft. Multiple editors can collaborate on a single draft in real time. All active editors see a list of other users currently in Edit mode and the element they each have selected. Clicking Publish publishes all drafted changes to the workbook. This includes changes drafted by all editors on the live draft.

Note: After publishing, the creator and administrators have permission to access the new workbook. Permissions must be granted to other individuals or user roles.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 65 Creating a Report From Scratch Editors can create brand-new reports from scratch in Report Center to present and analyze data in new ways. Using the report builder, you can create a new workbook in the system, select one or more datasets for the report, and customize which elements appear on screen. This feature gives you complete control over reports on any dataset you can access, as well as the ability to share these customized reports with other users.

To begin creating a new report: 1. Access the Report Center home screen. 2. Click New. The New Workbook form displays. 3. In the Workbook Name field, enter a name for the new report. 4. Click Create. The new report is saved into the system, and the report builder opens.

Report Builder Overview The Report Builder is a comprehensive tool that allows an editor to compose the elements that display on each workbook page. Each workbook page provides a canvas and standard element manipulation tools that make it easier for you to design and compose the visualizations you need, especially when a page is to be used as a dashboard.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 66 The Report Builder is divided into the following sections.

  1. The (Folder Options) icon is used to access the main menu for the report. This menu can be used to rename, move, delete, send, save, schedule exports, or browse documents for the report.

  2. The (Add New Element) icon is used to add a new element to the page. Elements include data tables, visualizations, pivot tables, input tables, linked input tables, text, images, buttons, embedded elements, dividers, plugins, and control elements.

  3. The (Page Overview) icon is used to access the Page Overview, which displays a list of all elements on the page. You can use the Page Overview to duplicate, copy, move, rename, and delete elements, as well as change the source data for an element.

  4. When an element on the grid has been selected, the (Element Properties) icon can be used to display the Select source for table menu, which can be used to change the data set used by the selected element.

  5. The Undo and Redo buttons can be used to quickly undo actions or redo actions that have been undone.

  6. The Add/Delete Grid Rows slider can be used to resize a selected element.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 67 7. The Design Grid is the canvas on which all elements for the page display. The grid uses a simple snap-to-position feature to allow elements to be easily positioned on the page. When composing a report, you arrange the elements on the grid to determine the visual composition of your report. 8. The Editing menu can be used to customize how you are currently viewing the report. Using this menu, you can choose to see the desktop or mobile version of the report. In addition, you can preview the report as an explorer or viewer, view the currently published version of a report, and discard the draft. 9. When the report is complete, you can use the Publish button to publish the report and make it available for viewing.

Elements Workbooks typically contain a collection of elements on a single page and/or distributed across multiple pages. There are three element types: data elements, UI elements, and control elements. For more information about data elements, refer to Data Elements. For more information about UI elements, refer to UI Elements. For more information about control elements, refer to Control Elements.

Adding Elements to a Page You can add elements to the report using an easy drag-and-drop interface. Elements snap to the grid for simple positioning, and can be resized and adjusted to achieve the desired layout.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 68 To add an element to a page: 1. Click the (Add New Element) icon. The Add New Element menu displays. 2. On the Add New Element menu, select the desired element and drag it onto the page. Drag it above or below an existing element to position it above or below the content, or drag it to the side of an existing element to arrange the two elements side-by-side. The element is added to the page, and the Properties panel for that element displays. 3. If the element displays data, select data sources for the element from the available options. l The New tab can be used to select from new data sources, including tables and datasets for the organization, creating a new join table from existing data, or creating a union of multiple data sources. l The In Use tab displays data sets already in use on this workbook for convenient selection.

l The Page Elements tab allows you to select existing tables and visualizations from this workbook to use as data sources for additional elements. For example, you could create a new join table from existing data sets that displays in table format, then create a visualization that uses that table as its source data. Once a data source has been selected, the Element Properties menu displays. 4. Make selections in the Element Properties menu to determine the content of the element. For example, you can select the columns which display in a table, or determine the background color and alignment of a text box. Once you have added the element to the page and selected its properties, you can make adjustments to the element directly on the canvas or from its Element Properties menu.

To customize the element on the page: l To reposition the element, you can drag the element across the canvas and snap it into place.

l To resize the element, you can use the corner icons of the element to change its height and width. l To create a new element directly from an existing element, click the (Create Child Element) icon. Select Visualization, Table, Pivot table, or Linked input table to generate an element of the selected type with the data source already set to the parent element. l To revise the data source for an element, scroll to the bottom of the Element Properties menu and select the element name. Select Change source to display the data source selection menu again, where a new data source can be configured.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 69 l Click the (Additional Options) icon next to the element to display a menu allowing you to duplicate, copy and paste, move, or delete the element.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 70 Desktop and Mobile Layouts Workbook pages have two different modes: desktop layout and mobile layout. In addition, these modes can be synched or unsynched. By default, the synced mobile layout automatically rearranges the elements to stack on top of each other to better fit the narrow dimensions, based on the ordering in the desktop layout from top left element going to the right and down. You can choose to edit the mobile layout and create a custom mobile layout that is not synced with the desktop layout’s order of elements. The unsynched mobile layout will have its own design, which can be customized independently of the desktop layout. You can change the size of your browser to see the design in desktop or mobile sizes. The breakpoint for mobile is 600 pixels canvas width (note the browser size is larger than the canvas size when you are designing, due to the elements panel).

Creating a Report From Existing Report Editors can create a new report from an existing report to set up a modified version more quickly. Creating an existing report will save a new version with a new name, and you can edit the new report with the same tool set used to create a report from scratch.

To create a report from an existing report: 1. Open an existing report. 2. Select Save As. The Save a Copy form displays. 3. In the Name field, enter a name for the new report. 4. In the Destination section, select a destination where the report will be saved. 5. Click Save. The new report is saved to the destination and opens in edit mode. The existing elements of the report are populated into the editor, where you can make changes just like creating a report from scratch.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 71 Scheduling Reports How to Schedule a Report Clients can schedule reports using the dedicated Scheduling button on each workbook.

To schedule a report: 1. Select a report to schedule for export. 2. Click Schedule. The Schedule Exports form displays. 3. Click New. The New Scheduled Export form displays. 4. In the Name field, enter a name for the scheduled report. 5. In the Destination field, select a server destination for the report. If the destination has not be added to the system, see the Adding a Server Destination section. 6. In the Remote Directory field, enter the file directory destination for the export. 7. In the View field, select which view to use for the export. 8. In the Page Element to Export field, select which element will be exported. Only one element can be included in each export, but multiple exports can be created for the same workbook. 9. In the Export File Name field, enter a file name for the exported CSV file. 10. In the Schedule section, select a schedule for the export. The Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Custom options each include separate selections to support different schedules. In addition, you can select which time zone to use for displayed times in this section. 11. Click Save.

Schedule Section Details When scheduling a new export, the selection in the Repeat Every field determines the fields that display to provide customization for different schedules. The options are as follows: l Repeat Every Day: Select the interval for how frequently the report is scheduled. Options include Daily, Week, Month, and Custom. l Daily: Select Once in the Frequency field to schedule the report once per day at a specific time of day. Select Multiple times to display fields allowing the schedule to repeat by hours or minutes. To have the report only run multiple times during a certain interval, select Between in the Interval field, then select the time period for the report to run. For example, a report can be run every hour at the 30 minute mark between 8 AM and 5 PM.

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 72 l Week: Select the days of the week on which the report will run. Select Once in the Frequency field to schedule the report once per day at a specific time of day. Select Multiple times to display fields allowing the schedule to repeat by hours or minutes. To have the report only run multiple times during a certain interval, select Between in the Interval field, then select the time period for the report to run. l Month: Select the day of the month on which the report will run. In the Frequency field, select the time of day when the report will be run. l Custom: Enter a custom schedule code to determine the report’s schedule. For more information about custom codes, select the link directly below the field.

Adding a Server Destination On the New Scheduled Export form, clients can add a server destination, set up a user name, and enter either a password or private key to provide access to this server.

Note: To send a report to your SFTP server, you will need to configure your server to whitelist the following IP addresses: 18.189.25.215 , 18.189.24.76 , 18.216.45.20, 18.116.126.247, 18.216.89.32, 3.21.84.175.

To add a server destination: 1. On the New Scheduled Export form, select the Destination field. 2. Scroll down in this menu and select +. The New Destination panel displays. 3. In the Destination Name field, enter the server name. 4. In the Host field, enter the host name or IP address that supports the sftp:// protocol. 5. In the Port field, enter the port number. 6. If the server uses a password, select Password in the Authentication field. Enter your User Name and Password in the corresponding fields. - or - If the server uses a private key, select Private Key in the Authentication field. Enter your User Name and Private Key in the corresponding fields. Please note that the private key must follow the legacy PEM format. Select the ? tooltip for more information. 7. To verify the connection to the server, click Test Connection. 8. Click Create.

How to Edit, Send, Pause, Duplicate, or Delete a Scheduled Export Clients can make changes to a scheduled report using the Schedule Exports form. By selecting the action menu for the report, the client can access the following options:

Report Center Editor Guide © 2025 PrismHR 73 l Edit: Select this option to display the Edit Scheduled Export form and edit the export.

l Send Now: Select this option to run the scheduled export immediately.

l Pause: Select this option to pause the export and prevent it from being run in the future.

l Resume: Select this option on a paused export to resume the normal schedule.

l Duplicate: Select this option to duplicate the scheduled export and edit the copy. This is recommended for exporting multiple elements from a workbook using multiple exports. l Delete: Select this option to delete the scheduled export.

Chapter 1 Report Center Sigma Implementation Guide

Chapter 1 Report Center Sigma Implementation Guide Welcome to the next generation Report Center. This implementation task sheet will outline the four steps that needed to be taken to setup this platform for your beta testers. This process will require five different steps to activate your environment: l Providing access to the Next Generation platform in Prism.

l Accessing Next Generation System.

l Syncing your user roles.

l Distributing access to Reports.

l Selecting your license types.

© 2025 PrismHR 1 Chapter 1 Providing Access to Next Generation Report Center

Chapter 1 Providing Access to Next Generation Report Center We recommend for beta the users are set up as Report Center User Administrators under the user role. Based upon client request, the security model has been updated so that any user that is configured as a Report Center User Administrator is automatically granted access to all workbooks. Client Access Group security will remain in place for individuals that are set up as administrators.

To assign user roles: 1. Select Change > User Roles. 2. Enter the Role ID or click the field title and select the role from a list. The form populates with specific information on that role..

© 2025 PrismHR 2 Chapter 1 Providing Access to Next Generation Report Center 3. In the Forms section, locate Report Center (New), which is found in the Work Centers Type and Reporting Category. 4. In the Access field, set the access for Report Center (New) to Full. 5. Click Save.

© 2025 PrismHR 3 Chapter 1 Accessing Next Gen System

Chapter 1 Accessing Next Gen System When the access is provided, the user will now see the new menu available under the work centers. Selecting this item on the menu signs the user in to the next generation Report Center platform and links to the home screen.

Note: The previous version of Report Center has been renamed Report Center (Legacy).

To access the new Report Center: 1. Navigate to the Enhanced Dashboard. 2. Under Work Centers, select Report Center (New). Users that are set up as Report Center Administrators in Prism will automatically see all reports and an administration icon in the upper right hand corner. For users that are not administrators, the screen will

© 2025 PrismHR 4 Chapter 1 Accessing Next Gen System appear blank unless the administrator has provided access to reports for their assigned user role. If you do see a blank screen, please contact your administrator and request access to reports.

Note: Beta version does not have column level security (Restricted Fields) in place. This will be available prior to our go live.

© 2025 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 Syncing Your User Roles

Chapter 1 Syncing Your User Roles When you first access Report Center, you will need to sync your user roles from Prism to Report Center. This will need to be accomplished by a report center user administrator. To complete this task, click on the Administration button in the upper right hand corner. The Administration form displays. Then, click the Sync Roles button.

© 2025 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Distributing Reports

Chapter 1 Distributing Reports If some users performing beta testing are not report center administrators, these users must be granted permission to access the reports by an administrator. To distribute access, simply click on the Edit Multiple Reports button.

To distribute access to reports: 1. Navigate to the Report Center home screen. 2. Click Edit Multiple Reports. Check marks display next to the report names.

© 2025 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 Distributing Reports 3. Select the reports to be distributed. The Edit Multiple Reports side bar displays.

© 2025 PrismHR 8 Chapter 1 Distributing Reports 4. Click Add Roles. The Add Role Access form displays.

  1. Select one or more roles to grant access to the selected reports.
  2. Click Add Access. The selected roles are granted access to the reports and the form closes.

© 2025 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Selecting License Types

Chapter 1 Selecting License Types For next gen platform, there will be three different user types (Viewer, Explorer, Editor). During beta testing, all users will be assigned the Viewer license type. This can be updated by any report center administrator. Viewer - User is allowed to generate reports they have been assigned access to, but lack the ability to customize the report. Explorer – User has ability to completely customize the report to their specifications. This includes adding removing columns, grouping, creating visualizations and pivot tables, creation of dashboards, ability to edit the joins within the report. This will also allow them to save the customizations as bookmarks (Formally Report Views). The user also has all capabilities of the Viewer type. Editor – User has complete access to create or manipulate reports for all users to see, as well as all capabilities of the Viewer and Explorer types.

Note: During the beta, clients are limited to three editor licenses.

To adjust the license type, the user must log into the system to create their User ID. After this is completed, the administrator can access the administration center and change the user’s license type. Do note the User ID must be sent to the data warehouse for it to appear on the user tab, so it may take several minutes for the user to appear to the administrator.

To assign user roles: 1. On the Report Center home screen, click Administration.

© 2025 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 Selecting License Types 2. Select the Users tab.

  1. Select the User ID that requires a license change. The User Detail form displays.

  2. In the License Type section, click Edit.

  3. Select the new license type for the user.

  4. If the user requires additional permissions for sharing reports or exporting data, select them under Additional Permissions. Editors have access to these features automatically.

  5. Click Save. The license for the User ID is changed to the selected type.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 3 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction Report Center is a centralized and consolidated reporting tool. It comes with many predefined reports that you can use as is or that you can quickly customize to meet the specific requirements of your organization. You can also easily define the presentation of the output and change it at any time as your requirements change.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 1 Chapter 1 Introduction

Accessing Report Center Service Providers and Worksite Managers can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard or from Employee Portal. See your administrator if you do not have the access you require.

Accessing from the PrismHR Dashboard A service provider or worksite manager can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard.

To access Report Center from the Work Centers panel: 1. Open the PrismHR Dashboard. 2. On the Work Centers panel, click Report Center in the Reporting section.

To access Report Center by searching: 1. Open the PrismHR Dashboard. 2. In the Search box, type Interactive Reports. 3. Click Report Center in the list of results.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 2 Chapter 1 Introduction

Workbooks In Report Center, reports are defined with three key terms: workbooks, pages, and datasets. A workbook refers to the entire report, such as the ACH History report or the Employee General Info report. A page on a report refers to a specific view for the report, including the columns that will display and any additional visualizations. A dataset refers to the category of information collected in the system. Each report pulls information from one or more data sets and displays them as pages based on selected settings. These terms are analogous to a spreadsheet program, with the workbook referring to the spreadsheet file, the page being a tab in that file, and the dataset as hidden information that was used to generate that spreadsheet. These terms are important when viewing Sigma help documentation and guides, but are not used extensively throughout this documentation.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 3 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page On the Reports page, the list of reports shows only the reports to which your administrator has given you access. There are two basic types of reports. l System reports come with Report Center and are predefined. You can temporarily configure a system report based on your requirements. l An administrator can modify a copy of a system report and save it as a new custom report. An administrator can also modify a custom report and save it as a new report. If the administrator shares a custom report with your role, that report is shown in your list of reports. The list of reports on your Reports page depend on your security settings.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 4 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Searching for reports You can search for reports by entering text in the Search box on the home page. Searches are case insensitive for partial or full matches in the report name or description. For example, searching for tax presents a list of reports where the word tax appears anywhere in the report name or description. In the following example, the search results contain reports whose names or descriptions include the word “tax.”

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 5 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Accessing Views On the Reports page, you can access a list of views available for a report. The views that are available on a report depend upon your security settings.

To access the views for a report from the Home page: 1. Launch Report Center. 2. Scroll through the list (or search) and click the report panel. The Report Details panel displays. Alternatively, select the Views link below the report name to display a list of views. Select a view to open the report to that Page View.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 6 Chapter 2 Navigating the Reports Page

Opening a report The list of reports shows only the reports to which you have been given access. See your system administrator if you have questions or need access to additional reports. You can open a report from the Report Center Home page or from within another report that you have open.

To open a report from the Home page: 1. Launch Report Center. 2. Scroll through the list (or search) and click the report name.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 7 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Chapter 3 Viewing Reports Reports are displayed in tables which are similar to spreadsheets, with individual pages that display data and visualizations. Report Editors can customize the columns that display on a report, as well as create visualizations and tables to help analyze data more efficiently.

Selecting Pages on the Report Each report contains one or more pages. The page properties determine which columns and visualizations display to the viewer. Pages are displayed near the top of the screen. Select a page to view the report using that page’s specific configuration. The pages you can access for each report depend on your security settings.

Resetting a Report As you specify parameters, sort columns, or adjust visualizations, you may want to restore the report to its default state. After making any changes to your current view on a report, you can select Reset in the upper-right corner to restore the report to the default view.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 8 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Controlling Parameters on a Report Parameters can be used to control what data displays on the report. The available parameters display near the top of the page, underneath the Page selection. When you select parameters to include on the report, the report results are immediately filtered according to your selection.

Using parameters, you can quickly filter results, clear selections, or search for specific values to instantly update the displayed report data.

To filter results by a parameter: 1. Select an available parameter from the available fields. 2. Select the check mark to include one or more individual parameters. When you select one or more options, only records with those options display on the report. If the parameter is a date field, you can select specific dates to include on the report, select a range of dates, or select time frames. For example, you could include the 2nd and 9th of January, all dates from the 1st of May to the 1st of June, or the last ninety days.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 9 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

To clear selections from a parameter: 1. Select the x icon to clear the parameter selection. Once cleared, the parameter is set to include all results.

To search for values in a parameter: 1. Select an available parameter from the available fields. 2. Enter search criteria in the search bar that displays at the top of the selection menu. The selection menu is immediately updated with search results, which can be selected to filter the report data. In addition, you can sort the values for the parameter to expedite your search. Select the Sort icon to sort by ascending or descending order.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 10 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Controlling Columns on the Report Each report page comes with a set of columns that display data. Much like a spreadsheet, columns display individual entries as cells. Each column represents either a set of data or a calculation performed on data sets. These columns can be organized by sorting the report based on an individual column’s data.

To sort the data in a column: 1. Select the Dropdown icon on a column. 2. Select the Ascending icon to sort the data in ascending order, or select the Descending icon to sort the data in descending order. The report can also be sorted according to multiple columns in sequence by defining a custom sort. For example, a report could be sorted by Column A in descending order, followed by Column C in ascending order.

To create a custom sort: 1. Select the Dropdown icon on a column. 2. Select the Custom Sort icon. The Sort form displays. On the Sort form, you can define sort orders for multiple columns. The Sort form is applied in descending order. 3. In the first row, select the Column name to pick a column to sort. 4. Select an ascending or descending order in the Sort order field. 5. In the Nulls field, select whether null values should be considered first or last in a list, or leave the field on default settings. The default selection places null values last. 6. To add an additional row to the Sort form, click + Add new. 7. Repeat the selection process for each row you add. 8. Once all options are selected, click Apply. The Custom Sort will sort the report according to all rows included on the Sort form in sequential order. For example, you could create three rows and select Entity ID, Pay Date, and Journal ID. The

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 11 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

entire report would be sorted by Entity ID, then data for each entity ID would be sorted by Pay Date,
and the rows for each pay date would be arranged by Journal ID.

Some columns can be expanded to display additional rows of data for individual items contained within the column. For instance, the year column in a summary report could be expanded to show a row for each month.

To expand a column: 1. Select the Plus icon next to the column name. Additional data displays. 2. Select the Minus icon to minimize the column. Columns can be summarized to display an overview of the data for that specific column. This overview includes statistics such as the most frequently occurring values, the row count, the average, the median, and the variance.

To display a summary of a column: 1. Click the Dropdown icon on a column. 2. Select Column details. The Column Details form displays. The name and equation for the column appear in the About section. The Top Values section displays the most frequently-occurring values in that column. The Summary section shows the number of rows, number of null items, and number of distinct values. The Statistics section shows the average, median, maximum, minimum, and other statistics.

Note: The Column Details section also displays the Unidata attributes for the report, which allows users to learn exactly which Prism fields correspond to the data.

  1. When you are finished reviewing the details, click the X icon to close the Column Details form.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 12 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Controlling Visualizations Visualizations are graphical representations of data, such as charts and graphs. Visualizations can be used to see patterns, trends, correlations, and outliers for data sets in a focused and easily understandable format. In addition, visualizations can be examined for further information on a report to see the underlying data.

To view a visualization’s data: 1. Right click on the visualization. 2. Select Show underlying data. A table of data displays, which includes all the data for the selected visualization.

To drill down to a visualization’s data: 1. Double click on a visualization to drill down to its data.

To expand a visualization: 1. Hover the cursor over a visualization. A small menu displays in the upper-right corner. 2. Click the Expand icon to expand the visualization. The visualization is maximized to encompass the entire page.

To minimize an expanded visualization: 1. Hover the cursor over a visualization. A small menu displays in the upper-right corner. 2. Click the Minimize icon to minimize the visualization. The visualization is reverted to its default size.

Report Center Viewer Guide © 2025 PrismHR 13 Chapter 3 Viewing Reports

Exporting Reports Reports can be exported for presentations, further calculations, or archiving. Reports can be exported into several formats, including CSV, XLS, and PDF.

Note: The export function is linked to security settings for individual user accounts. Editors and Explorers can typically export all files, while some Viewers can be granted export access on a case-by- case basis.

To export the current page of a report: 1. Select the (Additional Options) icon on a column. 2. Select Export. 3. Select a file format. Selecting PDF provides the option for Portrait layout or Landscape layout. Once a format is selected, the report will be downloaded as the selected file type.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 10 Getting started This guide provides the information you need to administer Report Center reports. The reports provide capabilities that let your users easily report on data that is relevant for your organization. It is intended for the user responsible for the administration and support of Report Center. To get started, you need to perform a few simple setup tasks to grant users the appropriate access to Report Center and individual reports.

Configuring access to Report Center Providers and Worksite Managers can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard or directly from Employee Portal. As the administrator you need to configure the appropriate type of access for each user role. • For both types of access, the logged on user must have HRPY.WORK*INFRC added to the user’s role. • An additional requirement for access from Employee Portal is to add Report Center to the template.

Adding the Process ID In order for Service providers and Worksite Managers to access Report Center from the Work Centers panel on the PrismHR Dashboard, you need to grant their roles access to the HRPY.WORK*INFRC Process ID.

To add the HRPY.WORK*INFRC Process ID: 1. From the PrismHR dashboard, click (Back Office). The list of Back Office items opens. 2. From System|Change, select User Roles. The User Role Search page opens. 3. Click Role ID. The User Role Search page opens. 4. In Show Type, select Service Provider or Worksite Manager.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 1 5. Select a role. The User Roles page shows the role name and description. 6. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance page opens. 7. Scroll through the list and select The Work Centers type, the Reporting category, and the HRPY.WORK*INFRC Process ID.

  1. Click Save. The selected type and category are added to the User Roles page. Report Center is now available from the Work Centers panel on the PrismHR Dashboard.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 2 9. Click Save.

Adding Report Center to the Employer Portal Template Employee Portal managers can see the Report Center menu only if BOTH of the following conditions exist: • The logged on manager must have the HRPY.WORKINFRC Process ID added to the manager’s user role. See the preceding section for instructions about how to add HRPY.WORKINFRC to the manager’s user role. • Report Center must be added to the template. If either condition is missing, the manager does not see the Report Center menu.

To add Report Center to the Employee Portal menu: 1. Click the WORK CENTERS menu. 2. From the Employee Experience Work Center, click Employee Experience Configuration. The Employee Experience Configuration form opens. 3. Click Configuration Templates. The Configuration Template form opens. 4. Click the Name of the template to edit. 5. Click the Menu tab. 6. To enter a top-level menu item, click . The new item is shown in the menu.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 3 7. Complete the following steps:

 For this option                                Do this
 Title                                          Enter Report Center.
 Hover Text                                     Enter Report Center.
 Navigation Actions                             Enable Component and select Report Center from the
                                                list.
 Icon                                           Select an icon to display for the menu item. This option is

  1. To apply the change to all clients using the template, click Save. To apply the changes to specific clients, click Apply to Client(s). In the Client Search, select the clients to use the template and click Apply. After saving, the Report Center menu is shown on the Employee Portal Dashboard.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 4 Configuring access to administration functions Each user who will administer Report Center needs to have the Report Center User Administrator role.

To designate the service provider user administrator: 1. Log on to PrismHR as SUPERUSER or the equivalent role. 2. In the menu bar, click (Back Office). 3. In System|Change, select Users. 4. In User ID, enter the user name or click the link to find the user. 5. In Account Management Roles, select Report Center User Administrator.

  1. Click Save. When a Report Center User Administrator opens Report Center, the Administration icon is shown in the header area of the Report Center home page.

Administration home page The Administration page is your starting point for performing the following administrative functions: • Provide access to individual reports. • Grant access to restricted fields within the reports. • Create categories and tags for each report so that users can filter the list of reports based on them. • Filter the list of reports based on their datasets. • Manage custom reports.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 5 • Edit metadata for any report, including the Name and Description (for custom reports only), tags, categories, and roles. • Delete reports. To open the Administration home page, click the Administration icon on the Report Center home page. Administrators can see all reports (including custom and private reports) in the Administration area. This enables them to have an end user experience without cluttering the home page with private reports. However, on the Report Center home page, users and administrators see only reports that were explicitly shared with them (where they are a member of at least one role that the report is shared with) and private reports that they created.

The Administration page provides a Reports tab and a Roles tab. The following sections provide detailed information about how to use each tab.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 6 Chapter 2 Managing report security

Chapter 2 Managing report security As a Report Center Administrator, you are responsible for ensuring that users can access only the information they need. This includes access to reports and access to restricted fields in those reports.

Note: Some reports are predefined as Service Provider Only. If you try to assign or share these reports, a warning is shown. If non-SP users previously had access to a report that is now predefined as Service Provider Only, they no longer see that report on their home page. Any custom reports that are based on a Service Provider Only system report are also designated as Service Provider Only reports.

Viewing the Roles tab The Administration > Roles tab provides a list of roles that shows the role name, ID, role type, and the number of reports and restricted fields accessible for each role. You can filter the list by searching for a role or by selecting a role type. You can see a list of reports or restricted fields by clicking the number in the Report Access or Restricted Field Access column.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 7 Chapter 2 Managing report security

Granting access to reports By default, users cannot access reports until you grant one role to which they belong access to each report that they need. To get started, select the Roles tab on the Administration page. You can grant access to Service Provider Only reports only to service providers.

For each role, the following information is displayed: • The Role Name column lists all roles by default. To filter the list, enter text in the Search box. To sort the list of roles, click the arrow in the column header. Sorting toggles between ascending and descending alphabetical order. • The ID column displays the internal role ID. • The Role Type column displays the type of each role. Roles of all types are displayed by default. To filter, expand the Role Type list, select one or more types, and then click Done. You can select or clear all roles by clicking Select All or Clear All. Combine search text and role type filters to further narrow the list. • The Report Access column displays the number of reports to which the role has access. • The Restricted Fields column displays the number of restricted fields to which the role has access. You can add or delete access to reports for a selected role.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 8 Chapter 2 Managing report security

To add access to one or more reports: 1. On the Roles tab, select a role. The system opens the selected role and displays Reports and Fields tabs. 2. Select the Reports tab, if it is not already selected. • If the role does not have access to any reports, you are prompted to add a report. Click Add or the Add Report link. • If the role already has access to some reports, the reports are listed. Click Add. The Select Reports window opens. It shows the name of each report to which the role does not have access and the tags associated with it. Reports to which the role already has access are not shown.

  1. Select the reports to make accessible to the role. You can filter the list of reports by entering text in the Search box. Messaging helps prevent you from accidentally granting WSM users access to reports that contain sensitive information (such as internal cost information). Do not select any report that contains Service Provide confidential information (such as internal cost data) .
  2. Click Add. The report is added to the list of reports that the role can access.

To delete access to one or more reports: 1. On the Administration > Roles tab, select the role. The Reports tab displays the reports to which the selected role has access. 2. Click (Remove) for the report. 3. Click Save. A message informs you that the role was successfully updated.

Granting access to restricted fields In Report Center, fields that contain sensitive information are predefined as restricted. By default, restricted fields are not visible to users, even when they have access to reports that contain those fields. To grant users access to a restricted field you must add to each role the restricted fields that users in that role should be able to access. You also need to add and update access for roles when required. Each restricted field may appear on multiple reports. Field security and report access work together to provide two layers of data security. To see a restricted field on a report, the user needs access to both the report AND the restricted field. If a user does not have access to a restricted field, the field does not appear in the columns list or the Add filter list on any report. To that user, it looks as if the field does not exist. You cannot edit role details such as role name, description, or the users who belong to each role in Report Center. You need to do that in PrismHR. To get started, select the Roles tab on the Administration page.

The information in restricted fields falls into the following categories:

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 10 Chapter 2 Managing report security

• Personal Identification Information (PII) • Banking • Employee Pay

Note: If a user exports a report that contains sensitive information, other users may be able to see and access exported data that they don’t have access to in Report Center. Be sure that your users understand this and be prepared to help them regarding the proper safeguarding of sensitive information.

To provide access to restricted fields: 1. On the Administration page, click the Roles tab and select a role. 2. Select the Fields tab. • If the role does not have access to any fields, you are prompted to add a field. Click Add or the Add Fields link. • If the role already has access to some fields, the fields are listed. Click Add. The Select Fields page opens. The Column Type column shows the type of data that the field contains.

  1. Select the fields to make accessible to the role. You can filter the list of fields by entering text in the Search box or by making a selection in the Category box.
  2. Click Add.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 11 Chapter 2 Managing report security

  1. Click Save. A message informs you that the role was successfully updated and the fields the role can access are shown on the Fields tab.

To delete access to restricted fields: 1. On the Roles tab, select the role. 2. Click (Remove) for the fields. 3. Click Save. A message notifies you that the role was successfully updated.

Managing categories Categories are analogous to file folders in which related reports are organized. By assigning reports to categories, you enable your users to view the list of reports based on some commonality that makes sense for your organization. For example, you might create a category called Tax and assign various tax reports to it. You can assign a report to only one category.

Maintaining custom reports The predefined reports that come with Report Center are called system reports. Chapter 4 Managing views Report Center grid reports include a collection of data that is usually presented in a large number of columns. Typically, you use the same report for many different tasks and share it with many different clients. Using views, you can save frequently used report configurations for a specific purpose or client so that you can quickly switch between variations of the same report based on your current requirements. For example, you can save a view that filters a different set of data than the default, or that hides columns that are not needed for a particular situation. Views can also help to prevent cluttering your Report Center home page with multiple copies of the same report with only slight variations. As an administrator, you can create views for each report and share them with other users. You can also create private views that are not shared. Your starting point for working with views is the Views menu that is available on each report. Both administrators and other users can create views, but administrators have additional options that are not available to other users. Notes: • Views apply only to grid reports. Templated, Chart, and Map reports do not support views. • You cannot include pivots in views. • You cannot copy or migrate views from one report to another. • You cannot change the default view from the Administration area. See Changing Your Default View for details.

Reports vs. views The following table describes some differences between reports and views.

Report View Appears as a separate entity on the Report Center home page with its own Belongs to a specific name and description. report.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 23 Chapter 4 Managing views

Report View Sharing is by PrismHR user role. Sharing is by user type or client. Easy to share with groups that have separate PrismHR roles (for example, Easy to share with specific internal departments). specific types of users and clients (for example, worksite managers at a single client).

Report sharing and view sharing work together. A user must have access to the report to see its views. Views honor client access groups and restricted fields security. For instance, if you share a view that has the Employee SSN column visible with all Service Provider users, users who do not have access to the SSN field do not see it.

When to use views Views can be especially helpful in the following circumstances: • You frequently use the same report for several different tasks, and you want to be able to quickly switch between formats optimized for each task. • You want your own personal preferred view for a report, and you don’t want to or don’t have permission to change the report’s default view. • Different clients want their own version of the same report with different columns, grouping, and other parameters. • You need to export similar data in different formats for different providers. For example, assume that you want to share 401k or benefits data with different carriers, where the underlying data is basically the same, but every carrier wants it formatted differently. You can create a single “401k export” report, set up a different view for each carrier, and then toggle between them to export). It may make more sense to create a new report in the following circumstances: • You need to be able to share based on different PrismHR roles. For example, you may need to share one report with your Payroll department, and a different report with your Benefits department. • The purpose of a report is different enough from other reports to require its own title and description on the home page. • A report needs to have different tags and categories on the home page.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 24 Chapter 4 Managing views

Types of views When you expand the Views menu, you can set up different types of views that are based on your organization’s requirements. A description of each numbered option is provided following the screenshot.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 25 Chapter 4 Managing views

The maximum number of views shown in the Switch views area is 4. The following sections describe the information shown in the Views menu.

1 - View heading The View heading shows the currently selected view area.

2 - Currently selected view A check mark identifies the currently selected view (shown if not the client or your view).

3 - Client view Client views (sometimes called “client default views”) associate views with clients. They are intended to fill many of the same needs as Client Parameters in PrismHR payroll reports. Client views are helpful when many clients need basically the same report, but they want it formatted differently. Without views, you would need to create a different copy of the report for each client, which could make your report list very crowded. With client views, you can share the same report with all of your clients, and then create a client view for each client who wants different special formatting. The client view is shown as follows: • When a single client is selected in the global client selector, and the client has a designated client view, it is shown as Client view (Name). If the name is too long to fit in the menu, it is truncated. If the selected client does not have a designated client view, nothing is shown. • When a client view is selected, the selected view area shows “View: Client view (name)” with a check mark next to the name. If the view settings were changed, the selected view area appends (edited) to the client view name. Selecting the view from the menu reapplies it and shows it as selected. • When multiple clients are selected, the following message is shown at the top of the menu “Client view (select a single client to enable).” • When switching clients, the selected view does not change, but the client view for the new client becomes available in the Views menu. The previously selected view still shows as selected in the selected view area and its name view moves to the top of the Views menu. You can select the new client view but it is not automatically applied. • Worksite managers see their client view applied by default when they visit a report for the first time. If you have a single client selected and that client has a client view assigned, the client view is shown in the Views menu for quick selection. When you have more than one client selected, no client views are shown.

4 - Your view “Your View” enables users to have their own preferred view for each report. Setting a view as “Your View” adds it as a shortcut in the Switch Views area of the Views menu so that it is easy to apply. This is useful when you frequently use the same view, especially when you don’t have permission to or don’t

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 26 Chapter 4 Managing views

want to change the Report Default view. Both administrators and other users can have their own “Your View” for each report.

5 - Report default Each report has a Report Default view. For system reports, the Report Default is built in and cannot be changed. However, you can create additional views and configure them however you like. For custom reports, the Report Default view is set by the report creator. The settings applied to the source report at the time of report creation become the Report Default view. The report creator or an administrator can change the Report Default view by making changes and then re-saving the report.

Administering views As an administrator, you can create views for each report and share them with other users. You can also create your own private views that are not shared. Your starting point for working with views is the Views menu that is available on each report. Views administration is not available in the Administration area. Both administrators and other users can create views but administrators have additional options that are not available to other users. For example, users can create private views but they cannot share them.

Best practices for naming views Developing a consistent naming convention for views will help users find and work with them effectively and efficiently. Some suggestions follow. • For optimal usability, name views based on either their purpose (such as Reconciliation or Monthly summary) or their display characteristics (such as Grouped by Department). • Do not include specific client names in views for the following reasons: • The same view may be associated with multiple clients. • Users may be confused about whether they’re looking at a view name or a client name. • Names longer than about 50 characters are truncated in some areas of the user interface.

Saving a view You can save the current report settings as a new view using the Save as a new view option on the Views menu. When saving views, be conscious of the filters you have applied, as they will be saved with the view. For instance, it is better to save a view with a relative date of “Pay Date in past 90 days” than with an absolute date such as “Pay Date: After 1/1/2021” because the relative date continues to work whenever it is applied.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 27 Chapter 4 Managing views

You can save a new view by opening the report, configuring the report parameters, and then selecting Save as new view from the Views menu or Save as view from the Save toolbar. You can change an existing view by applying the existing view, making changes, and then selecting Save changes from the Views menu. This opens the Save As View dialog box, which contains the Basic Info, Sharing, and Limit Sharing for Client tabs.

Note: Only Report Center administrators can see the Sharing and Limit Sharing by Client tabs. All other users see only the contents of the Basic Info tab.

Each client can have only one client view, so if a client view is already selected for client A, and then you save a new view and select Default view for client for client A, the new one becomes the client view.

To save a new view: 1. Open the report. 2. Select one of the following options: • On the Views menu, select Save as a new view. • On the toolbar, click (Save) and then select Save as view. The Save As View dialog box opens. The following sections explain how to use each tab.

Entering basic information The Basic Info tab displays the report parameters that will be saved as part of the view, including filters, columns, groups, aggregates, and sorting. It also provides a text box where you enter a name for the view. If you select Make this your view, the view is designated as your preferred view for this report. You can have multiple saved views for a report, but you can designate only one at a time as Your View . Saving a second view as Your View replaces the previous designation . This option is available for all types of users and views. If you accidentally replace your view, select All Views, edit the previous view, and select Make this your view.

Configuring sharing The Sharing tab specifies who can access this view. The sharing settings enable you to easily share views with specific kinds of users at specific clients. Sharing is based on the User Type of the logged in user. This is set in the Users page in PrismHR. A user must have access to a report to see its views. If you select Private, only you and other administrators can see the view. If you select Shared, the view is shared with specific kinds of users at specific clients. Sharing is based on the User Type of the logged in user, which is configured in the Users page in PrismHR. The following options are available. You must select at least one option to share the view. Leaving all options cleared is the same as selecting Private. • Service Providers • Worksite Managers • Trusted Advisors

The settings on the Sharing and Limit Sharing by Client tabs work together. tabs work together. The Limit Sharing by Client tab is used to set up both client sharing and client views. If Default view for client is selected, this is the (default) client view for users at this client.

Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports As an administrator, you can schedule reports to run at specified times or certain intervals. By creating a scheduled job, you can specify when a report will run, what parameters to use, and which configuration to display. Multiple scheduled jobs can be assigned to a report, each with its own frequency and configuration. In addition, files can be uploaded to a Secure FTP site. Scheduled jobs are available for parameter-driven reports throughout Report Center.

Note: In order to schedule reports, it may be necessary to whitelist the following public IP addresses on your secure FTP server:

l 18.189.25.215

l 18.189.24.76

l 18.189.34.145

l 18.216.45.20

Viewing Scheduled Jobs Administrators can access the Scheduled Jobs form by selecting the Schedule button on the toolbar of a parameter-driven report.

The Scheduled Jobs form displays a list of all jobs scheduled for the specific report. Each job can be assigned an individual name and description to assist organizing your jobs. Jobs can be assigned to one or more clients to meet customer needs. In addition, this form displays the jobs current status, including jobs that are scheduled to run later, jobs currently queued to run, jobs that are running at this moment in the background, and jobs that have been disabled.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 36 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

Scheduled jobs can be edited from this screen by selecting the Edit ( ) icon. Using this option, you can change the job’s parameters, configuration, schedule, or other details. The next time the job is run, it will use the edited specifications. You can run a job directly by pressing the Run ( ) icon. The job will run in the background, and you can display the report once it is finished.

Adding a Scheduled Job On the Scheduled Jobs form, you can add a new scheduled job for the specified report.

To add a Scheduled Job: 1. In Report Center, select a parameter-driven report. 2. Click Schedule. The Scheduled Job form displays. 3. Click Add Job. The Add Scheduled Job form displays.
