 Description                                    Enter a description for the job. This can be any description,
                                                and should be used to help organize your scheduled jobs.
  1. Click Save. The job is saved in the system, and the job details form displays.

Using the job details form, you can edit a job’s parameters, configure how the report displays, specify file transfer actions, and set up the job schedule.

Note: To change information on the job details form for an existing job, simply click the Edit button for the job on the Scheduled Jobs form.

Selecting Parameters and Configuring the Report The Parameters for Job Runs tab displays parameters to use on the report. You can select the same parameters that are available when running the report directly in Report Center. When entering information in date fields, you can use keywords to add relative dates. For example, enter Today-1M to have the report run data from one month before the job is scheduled to run. By using relative dates, you can maintain timely data sets for reports that will run in the future.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 38 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

The Configure Report tab can be used to select columns and aggregates for the report. You can customize how the scheduled job displays the report, allowing you to set up different scheduled jobs for different information.

Note: You can add groups to the report to change how your report displays on the Configure Report tab, but the groups are not saved when the report is exported. This follows the same export functionality as when running the report manually.

Setting up Secure FTP Transfers for a Scheduled Job When you schedule a report to run, you must add a secure file transfer to the job. When the report finishes running, a document will be securely transferred to a specified destination. You must set up your own Secure FTP protocol for this function to work. For more information about Secure FTPs, see Setting Up a Secure FTP Using the Raw Key Text Protocol.

To add a secure file transfer protocol: 1. Click the Edit icon on the scheduled job you would like to modify, or create a new scheduled job. The job details form displays. 2. Click the Plus icon on the Actions tab and select SFTP - Secure File Transfer. The SFTP - Secure File Transfer form displays.

  1. Enter the host URL in the Host field.
  2. Enter the port number in the Port field.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 39 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

  1. To place the file in a specific folder, enter a file path in the Remote Directory.
  2. Select an Authentication Mode.
  3. Enter a Username. In addition, enter a Password or Raw Key text based on the selected authentication mode. Note: Path to Key is not currently available, and is scheduled for a future release.
  4. Click Test Connection to test the connection to the host URL.
  5. Make selections in the Files to Upload section to modify the file. Click the format selection to select a CSV format, Excel format, or PDF format. Select Configure to display the Attachment form, where the file name and formatting can be modified. To add a new file, click the Add button. To delete a file, click the Delete icon.
  6. To add a condition to sending the file, select Run on a condition and select a report and number of records in the options that display. Conditions allow you to specify that the file should only be transferred if there are a minimum number of records on the report.
  7. Click Done to save the SFTP information.

Selecting the Schedule for a Scheduled Job You can schedule a job to run the report once in the future, or on a recurring basis.

To add a schedule to a job: 1. Click the Edit icon on the scheduled job you would like to modify, or create a new scheduled job. The job details form displays. 2. Click the selection in the Schedule tab. The Schedule form displays.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 40 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

  1. Select the Enabled option to enable the scheduled job.
  2. Using the Interval option, select an interval for the scheduled job.
  3. Make selections in the date fields based on the selected interval. For example, select days of the week on a Weekly interval, or specify a date or day of the month on a Monthly interval.
  4. Select a day to start the schedule in the Start Date field.
  5. Select a day to end the schedule in the End Date field, or leave the option blank to make the schedule continuous. The dates of the next scheduled runs for the report display in the Next runs section.
  6. When the schedule is finalized, click Done to save the schedule.

Setting Up a Secure FTP Using the Raw Key Text Protocol When setting up a Scheduled Report with the Send to FTP Job Action, two SFTP protocol options are available. l Password

l Raw Key text

For Raw Key text options, Report Center requires an unencrypted RSA Private Key.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 41 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

These keys are often generated in Public Private Key (PPK) format by the SFTP vendor and need to be converted to a usable format. Keys can also be created from scratch and provided to the SFTP vendor.

PPK to an Unencrypted RSA Private Key The following guide provides instructions for creating a PPK and converting it to the PEM format (RSA Private Key). If a PPK is already on hand, skip to the “Load” step below. This guide uses a free tool called PuTTYgen, which is available here: https://www.puttygen.com/

To create and convert a PPK: 1. In PuTTYgen, select Key.

  1. Select SSH-2 RSA key.

  2. Click Generate.

  3. Follow the instructions to move your mouse cursor and generate random numerical data.

  4. Select File and Save private key.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 42 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

  A warning will display, indicating that the key does not have a passphrase. Select Yes.

  1. Select a target location and name for the resulting .ppk file.

  2. Load the recently created PPK file.

  3. Select Conversions and Export OpenSSH key.

    A warning will display, indicating that the key does not have a passphrase. Select Yes.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 43 Chapter 5 Scheduling Reports

  1. Choose a target location and name the file, adding an extension .pem.

  2. Open the .pem file with a text editor. The key header and body should be in base 64, using numbers and letters.

  3. Paste the Raw Key text into the Report Center SFTP Job Action or point Report Center to the path of the .pem file.

    The Public key within PuTTYgen may then be shared with the SFTP Vendor if they have requested a corresponding public key.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 44 Chapter 6 The New Data Warehouse

Chapter 6 The New Data Warehouse The Report Center Data Warehouse is a data platform designed specifically for cloud computing, with modular architecture that hybridizes traditional database storage with virtual computation for query processing. The resulting Data Warehouse offers the simplicity and security for storing data in traditional shared-disk architectures, while retaining the speed and flexibility of cloud computing. This guide provides information about the integration between Report Center and the Data Warehouse structure. It covers the advantages of the Data Warehouse, the transition process from Elastic to the Data Warehouse, and common questions users might have about their own customizations to Report Center. Report Center will be migrating its data storage and processing from the Elastic database to the Data Warehouse in a series of phases. This migration will improve the core Report Center experience in a number of ways. The Data Warehouse structure provides improved performance, especially for customers running reports on significantly large data sets. In addition, the migration to the Data Warehouse will allow Report Center to incorporate data from the entire Prism family of applications in the future, including Client Space and Time and Labor Management.

Report Migration Reports will be migrated to the Data Warehouse architecture as smoothly and seamlessly as possible. This rollout will occur during our standard release cycle which is biweekly on Wednesdays and Thursdays. The report center teams are prioritizing the reports for migration that are both commonly run and resource-intensive to maximize the benefits of using the Data Warehouse’s architecture and provide the greatest performance improvements as soon as possible.

Each report that is migrated to the Data Warehouse will be tagged, and Prism Default reports that pull from the Data Warehouse will be denoted by a specific icon (as seen above).

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 45 Chapter 6 The New Data Warehouse

The Elastic version of a report will still be available after the report has been transitioned to the Data Warehouse. Users can run either version of the report to compare differences, verify that the transition proceeded smoothly, and provide feedback. In addition, the report that is generated out of elastic will also now have a tag that will show the date when the elastic report will be removed from the system. One month after a report has been migrated to the Data Warehouse, the HRP version of the report will be disabled. In addition, one month after the migration to the Data Warehouse, the Elastic version of the report will also be removed.

User-Created Reports and Customization Just like the Prism default reports, each user-created report that is derived from a report generated out of the Data Warehouse will automatically have the Data Warehouse tag added to the report for tracking.

Migration of User-Defined Reports and Views The most powerful feature in Report Center is the ability to create reports and views. We are currently working to build a script that will migrate these user defined reports and views to generate using the data stored in this new data warehouse. l When the migration script is run, any user defined reports & views built off the query will automatically be created in the Data Warehouse. l In order to ease the change management process, any users that had access to these reports and views in Elastic will now have access to them in the Data Warehouse. l Important Note: Given the schema differences between the new and old data warehouses, it is possible that some columns may not be visible on the report after the migration script is generated. PrismHR will be providing a list of data attributes that will not be included on these custom reports and views.

Security The following steps will be taken during the Data Warehouse migration process: l The Report Center administrator must distribute access to the PHR Default reports that have been migrated to the new data warehouse.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 46 Chapter 6 Release Notes

l Field security cannot be transferred from the Elastic reports to the Data Warehouse reports. If a user was given access to restricted fields on a report, an admin will need to give them access to those fields on the Data Warehouse version. l If an Elastic version of a report was tagged as a favorite, the Data Warehouse version will also be tagged as a favorite. l All user-defined reports and views will be copied from the Elastic version of a report over to the Data Warehouse version. Users will receive a prompt indicating that the view will be recreated in the Data Warehouse version of the report when the original version is set to be removed. l Scheduled Jobs will be copied from the Elastic version of a report approximately one month after the report has been migrated to the Data Warehouse.

July Enhancements This section describes the enhancements included in the Report Center release for July 2024.

Additional Editor Roles

During the initial beta for the Next Gen Report Center, clients were limited to a total of three Editor roles in their organization. That limitation has now been removed, and additional Editor roles can now be allocated to users on the system. Please note that allocating more than three Editor roles does change the license subscription plans. If another Editor role is assigned, a notification displays, instructing the administrator that this change will require an additional Editor license. JIRA # RC-5892

Delete User-Created Reports

User-created reports can now be deleted by their owners. The Report Details on the Report Center home screen now includes a Delete button, which can be used to permanently delete the user-created report. This button only displays when editing a single workbook, and only for the user who is designated as the owner of the report.

Note: Core reports cannot be deleted.

JIRA # RC-5675

Display Owner on Shared Reports

Shared reports now display the owner of the report on the Report Details panel. When any user with access to the report displays the report details, they can now determine who owns the selected report. JIRA # RC-5692

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 75 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Favorites Tab for Reports

Users can now designate reports as favorites be selecting the (Star) icon on a report. Once added as a favorite, these reports can be easily accessed using the new Favorites tab on the Report Center home screen.

Using this new tab, users can quickly navigate to their most commonly used reports to access information more efficiently. JIRA # RC-5519, RC-5520

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 76 Chapter 6 Release Notes

View Role Details

Administrators can now review more detailed information for user roles in the system using the new Role Details form. From the Roles tab on the Administration form, select a role in the Role Description column to access the Role Details form.

On this form, administrators can review details about a role’s access, permissions, and license type. In addition, the license type can be switched from this form by selecting the Edit button. JIRA # RC-5921, RC-5925

June Enhancements This section describes the enhancements included in the Report Center release for June 2024.

Activate and Deactivate Users

Administrators can now activate and deactivate users from the Users tab on the Administration form. To deactivate a current user, select Deactivate in the Actions column. To reactivate a user, select Activate in the Actions column. In addition, users can be activated and deactivated on the User Details form. Click a user name to display this page, and then select Activate or Deactivate in the Status field.

Note: When a user is deactivated, details cannot be changed on the User Details form, except to reactive the user.

Note: When a deactivated user attempts to log in to the Next Gen Report Center, they are notified that their user ID is deactivated in the system.

JIRA # RC-5695, RC-5696, RC-5823, RC-5837, RC-5838, RC-5873

Bulk Edit Roles

Administrators can now edit roles in bulk on the Roles tab of the Administration form. Select multiple roles to display the Edit Multiple Roles sidebar, where workbooks can be added to all selected roles simultaneously.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 83 Chapter 6 Release Notes

With multiple roles selected, select Add Workbooks to display the Add Workbooks form, where you can search for and select workbooks and permission levels. Once selected, click Add to add the workbooks with the selected permissions to all the selected roles. JIRA # RC-5705

Control Restricted Fields

Administrators can now control access to restricted fields for user roles. By controlling access to these fields, administrators can determine which users can view sensitive information on reports. To allocated restricted fields for a user role, select the Roles tab on the Administration form. Select a user role to display the User Role sidebar. The Fields tab on this sidebar displays a list of the restricted fields that users assigned this role can view. Click Add to display the Add Fields form, where fields can be added to the list. Click the (trashcan) icon to remove a field from this list. A message displays to confirm that the field should be removed. Changes to this sidebar are saved automatically. JIRA # RC-5472, RC-5517

Display Last Login on Users Tab

The Users tab on the Administration form now displays the last time each user logged in to the system. In addition, the tab can be sorted by Last Login. Using this field, administrators can determine if any users have not logged in to the system in a significant period of time, which can help determine which user accounts may require deactivation. JIRA # RC-5824

Display Ownership of a User’s Workbooks

The a user creates a custom workbook, that user now displays as the Owner of the workbook in their Edit Workbook Access form. Administrators can display this form by selecting the Users tab in Administration, select a user, and selecting Edit on the user sidebar. On this form, any custom workbook created by the user displays Owner in the Permissions field and Ownership in the Has Access Via field. JIRA # RC-5847

Review Usage Breakdown

Administrators can now review a breakdown of usage statistics on the Administrator form. These charts display counts of how many users logged into the system by License Type and for total Prism users.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 84 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Using these statistics, administrators can determine the utilization rate of the Next Gen Report Center by their organization to help allocate license types and role access. JIRA # RC-5877, RC-5878, RC-5880

Session Timeout Increased

The time it takes for a session in the new Report Center to timeout has been increased to three hours. In addition, the timeout logs the user out of the system, rather than simply displaying a notification that the session has expired. JIRA # RC-5865

Share Workbooks for Managers and Advisers

Users with sharing permissions can now share workbooks with Worksite Managers and Trusted Advisers, and managers can share reports with other users. When a user with access to sharing selects the Share button on a workbook, managers are now included in the user search results for sharing. When a manager selects the Share button, they can share the workbook with certain restrictions. Managers can always share a workbook with Service Provider users, but can only share with other Worksite Managers if they have at least one Client ID in common with that manager. When the report is shared, managers can only see data for their assigned Client IDs, and other managers who do not have any Client IDs in common do not show up in their search results. JIRA # RC-5525

Dashboards Added

The following dashboards are now available in the next generation Report Center: Client Profitability Analysis Overview - Summary Tab: Provides key performance indicators for clients, including employees, average profit per employee, and profit categories. Client Profitability Analysis Overview - By Industry Tab: Provides key performance indicators organized by types of industries. Client Profitability Analysis Overview - Client SummaryTab: Provides key performance indicators organized by specific clients. Client Profitability Analysis Overview - By Geography Tab: Provides key performance indicators organized by state. JIRA # RDC-2464, RDC-2465, RDC-2466, RDC-2467

Dashboards Now Available

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 98 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Enhancements to Audits for Next Gen Report Center

Additional events have been added as audits in the new report center to improve security and accountability for clients. When an administrator changes a user’s license type on the User Detail form, an audit log is now created. This audit records the PEO, User ID, time stamp, previous license type, new license type, and the ID of the administrator making the change. When a user accesses a report from the home page, a record is saved of the event. JIRA # RC-5728, RC-5729

This report is used to answer the following questions, as guided by NAPEO (for non- Prism customers): A. Select all businesses that were clients of your PEO on 1/1/2023 AND were still clients on 1/1/2024. 1. For all those businesses combined, how many total employees were employed on 1/1/2023? 2. For all those businesses combined, how many total employees were employed on 1/1/2024? 3. How many different client businesses were used for those calculations?

B. Select all businesses that were clients of your PEO for all of January 2024 (or for any other recent month of your choosing). 1. For all those businesses combined, how many total employees were employed on the 1st day of the month? 2. For all those businesses combined, how many employees from the 1st day of the month were no longer employed on the last day of the month (or you can use the 1st day of the next month if that is easier to calculate)? 3. What month/year data are provided?

Sync User Roles With New Button

Administrators can use the new Sync Roles button to manually synchronize user roles. When the administrator creates a new user role, they can synchronize to make them available to be assigned to their users. Previously, this process was performed automatically when the users logged in individually to Report Center, which could create performance issues. To synchronize a newly created role with all users, simply click the Sync Roles button on the Administration form. A message displays indicating that the roles were synchronized successfully. Enhancements This section describes the enhancements included in the first Report Center release for February 2023.

The New Data Warehouse

The Report Center Data Warehouse is a data platform designed specifically for cloud computing, with modular architecture that hybridizes traditional database storage with virtual computation for query processing. The resulting Data Warehouse offers the simplicity and security for storing data in traditional shared-disk architectures, while retaining the speed and flexibility of cloud computing. Report Center will be migrating its data storage and processing from the Elastic database to the Data Warehouse in a series of phases. This migration will improve the core Report Center experience in a number of ways. The Data Warehouse structure provides improved performance, especially for customers running reports on significantly large data sets. In addition, the migration to the Data Warehouse will allow Report Center to incorporate data from the entire Prism family of applications in the future, including Client Space and Time and Labor Management.

Report Migration Reports will be migrated to the Data Warehouse architecture as smoothly and seamlessly as possible. This rollout will occur during our standard release cycle which is biweekly on Wednesdays and Thursdays. The report center teams are prioritizing the reports for migration that are both commonly run and resource-intensive to maximize the benefits of using the Data Warehouse’s architecture and provide the greatest performance improvements as soon as possible.

Each report that is migrated to the Data Warehouse will be tagged, and Prism Default reports that pull from the Data Warehouse will be denoted by a specific icon (as seen above).

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 124 Chapter 6 Release Notes

The Elastic version of a report will still be available after the report has been transitioned to the Data Warehouse. Users can run either version of the report to compare differences, verify that the transition proceeded smoothly, and provide feedback. In addition, the report that is generated out of elastic will also now have a tag that will show the date when the elastic report will be removed from the system. One month after a report has been migrated to the Data Warehouse, the HRP version of the report will be disabled. In addition, one month after the migration to the Data Warehouse, the Elastic version of the report will also be removed.

User-Created Reports and Customization Just like the Prism default reports, each user-created report that is derived from a report generated out of the Data Warehouse will automatically have the Data Warehouse tag added to the report for tracking.

Migration of User-Defined Reports and Views The most powerful feature in Report Center is the ability to create reports and views. We are currently working to build a script that will migrate these user defined reports and views to generate using the data stored in this new data warehouse. l When the migration script is run, any user defined reports & views built off the query will automatically be created in the Data Warehouse. l In order to ease the change management process, any users that had access to these reports and views in Elastic will now have access to them in the Data Warehouse. l Important Note: Given the schema differences between the new and old data warehouses, it is possible that some columns may not be visible on the report after the migration script is generated. PrismHR will be providing a list of data attributes that will not be included on these custom reports and views.

Security The following steps will be taken during the Data Warehouse migration process: l The Report Center administrator must distribute access to the PHR Default reports that have been migrated to the new data warehouse. l Field security cannot be transferred from the Elastic reports to the Data Warehouse reports. If a user was given access to restricted fields on a report, an admin will need to give them access to those fields on the Data Warehouse version. l If an Elastic version of a report was tagged as a favorite, the Data Warehouse version will also be tagged as a favorite.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 125 Chapter 6 Release Notes

l All user-defined reports and views will be copied from the Elastic version of a report over to the Data Warehouse version. Users will receive a prompt indicating that the view will be recreated in the Data Warehouse version of the report when the original version is set to be removed. l Scheduled Jobs will be copied from the Elastic version of a report approximately one month after the report has been migrated to the Data Warehouse.

Known Issues The following sections describe the known issues in this release.

Pivot View is Limited to 500 Rows

Clients have reports issues where the Pivot View on their reports only displays 500 rows of information. This is due to a performance setting which can be changed on individual reports. To change this setting, click Pivot View, and select the Settings icon ( ). Select Performance, and enter a specified number of rows in the Limit Rows field. Click Apply, and the new limit is applied to the report. JIRA # RCRT-3437

Snowflake Reports Display Dates One Day Off

When viewing a report that uses the Snowflake database, dates displayed on screen are off by one day. For example, a date that should display as 3/14/22 displays as 3/13/22. This does not impact reports that are exported, and exported files display dates properly. This issue will be resolved in a future release. JIRA # RC-5028

Enhancements This section describes the enhancements included in the Report Center release for June 2022.

Note: As enhanced versions of HRPyramid and PrismHR reports become available in Report Center, the corresponding HRPyramid reports are retired. In some cases, a single Report Center report replaces multiple HRPyramid reports. See Retired Reports for a complete list.

Scheduled Reports

Report Center administrators can now schedule reports to run at set times and intervals in Report Center. A scheduled job processes the report using the parameters you set at a future time, either as a one-time report or a recurring event. Scheduling is available for parameter-driven reports. Using the scheduling feature, administrators can create job schedules, specify report parameters, configure how the report displays, and set a one-time or recurring schedule for their report. You can set common reports to run on regular intervals, schedule reports to be uploaded to a Secure FTP site, plan reports to run well in advance of when they’re needed, and edit your scheduled details at any time. To schedule a report, open the report and select the Schedule button on the report toolbar. The Scheduled Jobs form displays.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 161 Chapter 6 Release Notes

The Scheduled Jobs form displays a list of jobs for the report, including status, client, and schedule. If the job contains a recurring schedule, the time of the next run and the status of the previous run display.

Select the Edit icon to edit an existing job. Parameters can be changed to apply to the next time the job is run. Select the Run icon to run the job immediately. Select the Delete icon to delete the scheduled job. To create a new scheduled job, click the Add Job button. The Add Scheduled Job form displays.

Click Save to create a new scheduled job, including a name and description. Save the job to open the job details form, where you can select parameters, configure the report, select a schedule, and enable secure file transfers.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 162 Chapter 6 Release Notes

From the job details form, select the report name to display the Parameters for Job Runs tab. You can enter parameters for the report the same way you would run the report in Report Center. Select the Configure Report tab to customize how the report displays, including columns, groups, and aggregates. The report will use the specified parameters each time it is scheduled to run. Select Schedule to set up a one-time or recurring schedule for the report.

Schedules can be configured different time intervals, ranging from hourly to yearly. Reports can be schedule for individual days of the month, calendar intervals, and date ranges.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 163 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Secure file transfers can be added to a regularly scheduled report, allowing you to send a spreadsheet or pdf of the report to a specified secure location. Select Actions to add a secure file transfer action to the report and display the SFTP - Secure File Transfer form. Using this form, you can specify a destination, add authentication such as a username and password or path to key, and choose the format of the file to send. JIRA # RC-179

Improved Performance for Admin and Home Screens

To reduce loading times, the Columns selection is now restricted to individual report forms, and no longer appears on the admin screen or the home screen. The Columns selection only loads the list of available columns on its specified screen, reducing loading time and improving performance. JIRA # RC-4616

Improved Error Messages for Reports

When an employee encounters an error in Report Center which prevents the report from being processed, the system displays a clearer message about the event. The new error message informs the employee that an error prevented the report from processing, and directs the employee to contact support. JIRA # RDC-640

Deduction Code Setup Report Parameters

The default parameters on the Deduction Code Setup report have been changed to work similarly to the Pay Code Setup report in Report Center. The new report parameters show all deduction codes in the system, including obsolete codes. These parameters can be changed to hide obsolete codes or codes from a certain date range. JIRA # RDC-640

Enhancement The Maintenance Release (MR) of Report Center for January 2021 includes the following enhancement.

Messaging when adding reports to a WSM role

Messaging was added to help prevent administrators from granting reports that contain sensitive information (such as internal cost information) to WSM users. In the Report Center Administrator Role detail page, a warning message is shown at the top of the Select Reports dialog box if the role to which you are assigning reports is not a Service Provider. Since you are likely to use tags to identify reports that contain sensitive information, a column was added to display the tags on each report. A tags filter was also added. The look and feel and behavior of tags is identical to other pages (such as the Administrator Reports List).

Known Issues The Maintenance Release (MR) of Report Center for January 2021 includes the following known issues. We are working to resolve these issues in future releases: • Access is available on Prod and Corp sites. Demo sites will be activated at a later date. • Data is from 1/1/19 to current. It is recommended to select Summary Only before exporting or use the Pivot View to apply groups for export. • User Roles who have Report Center processes assigned, but who have NEVER logged on to Report Center, will need to assign reports to the role again in Report Center Administration.

Release Features The Report Center Quarterly Release (QR) for March 2021 includes the following release features.

Report Views

Views enable you to save different sets of report parameters that contain selected information for a specific purpose or client. For example, you can save a view that filters a different set of data than the default, or that hides columns that are not needed for a particular situation. A view can contain anything that changes the display of the report, including: • Currently applied filters • Currently applied sorts (including multiple sorts) • Columns hidden/shown • Column order • Applied groups + group order/hierarchy

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 215 Chapter 6 Release Notes

• Aggregates • Column formats • Column Number, Date, or Time formats Views do not include Pivots. They also do not include clients. That is, you can use any view with any combination of clients. See the Report Center User’s Guide for detailed information about working with views.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 216 Chapter 6 Release Notes

When to use views Views can be especially helpful in the following situations: • You frequently use the same report for several different tasks and you want to be able to quickly switch between formats optimized for each task. • You want your own personal preferred view for a report and you don’t want to or don’t have permission to change the report’s default view. • Different clients want their own version of the same report with different columns, grouping, and other parameters. Many clients want a report with basically the same data but they want slightly different formatting. • You need to export similar data in different formats for different providers. For example, you can share 401k or benefits data with different carriers, where the underlying data is basically the same, but every carrier wants it formatted differently. JIRA # RC-3534

Using the Views menu Each report provides a Views menu. Expand the menu to see various options for working with views. In the following example, a check mark identifies the selected view.

Saving a view You can save a new view of a report by opening the report, configuring the report parameters, and selecting Save as new view from the Save toolbar or from the Views menu. This opens the Save As

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 217 Chapter 6 Release Notes

View dialog box, where you can define the following information. Some of these functions are available only to administrators. • Display the report parameters and assign a name to the view. You can also specify whether to make the view your preferred view (called Your View). • Specify who can access the view. If the view is Private, only you or a Report Center Administrator can see it. If the view is Shared, you can share it with selected roles. • Share the view only with users who have access to selected clients and specify whether it should be the default view for each client. • Change a view and save it with the existing name or a new name.

Listing views The Views menu provides a quick way to see a list of suggested views. You can see a complete list of all the views to which you have access by clicking All views on the Views menu. This opens the All views for this Report dialog box, which shows the following information for each view that you have permission to see. • The name that the user who created the view assigned to it. • Whether the view is selected as your preferred view (Your view). • Sharing options for the view. • The clients whose users can access the view. • The clients for whom the view is the default view. You can also display the report using these view settings or delete it.

Online Help

Report Center now provides online help for both users and administrators. Your role determines which topics you can access.

To open the help system click (Help) next to the Global Client Selector.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 218 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Using the toolbar Use the toolbar to perform these actions. A tooltip is available for each icon.

• Browse to the previous or next topic. • Print the current topic. • Expand or collapse the table of contents in the left panel. • Remove highlighting from topics that you opened from search results.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 219 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Searching for topics To find specific topics, type text in the Search box and click .

The list of results contains all topics that include the specified text in their titles or content. For example, if you type Summary, the results list includes a link to each topic whose title or content contains the word Summary. It shows the total number of matches and displays the text in bold if it is in the topic title. You can also find topics by navigating through the Table of Contents. Just expand and collapse sections until you find what you are looking for.

Submitting documentation feedback Each topic in the help system provides an option for you to send feedback about that topic. Your input goes directly to the PrismHR documentation team and will be promptly answered.

Note: The Send us feedback option is intended for comments about the documentation.

• To send product/release feature requests, submit a PrismHR Idea. Alternately, you can click the following icon at the lower right hand corner of the Report Center home page and use the Feedback option to send feedback directly to our product team.

• For bug reports, submit a support case. JIRA # RC-2578

Known Issues The following sections describe the known issues in this release.

Reports built off of client invoices and employee payroll vouchers do not support data prior to 1/1/2019. Information for 2018 and prior years is not available for these reports. These reports run normally for data after 1/1/2019. JIRA # RC-3587

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 232 Chapter 6 Release Notes

We are actively working on resolving this issue as quickly as possible. JIRA # RCRT-2841

Enhancements This section describes the enhancements included in the Report Center Quarterly Release (QR) for December 2024.

Parameter-Driven Reports

Parameter-driven reports are now available in Report Center, which can be run using parameters selected on the report screen. These reports have been designed based on user feedback to show point-in-time information. Parameter-driven reports are identified by the ( ) icon.

Enter criteria for the report parameters and click Run Report to generate the report using the selected settings. After the report is complete, the other report icons become available. Once generated, these reports populate the traditional grid format and can be managed just like a normal report. Data from the last report is saved and available when the report is reopened. To update the report with the most recent data, refresh the report or re-run it.

Note: Select Run in background to minimize the report and continue working in Report Center. A progress wheel indicates the progress of the report running in the background, and a notification appears when the report is complete.

JIRA # RC-4011

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 233 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Review Available Columns in Administration

The Administration screen has been enhanced with a list of how many columns are available on a report and an option to review each column. The Available Columns field shows a hyperlink indicating how many columns are available on each report. Clicking this link opens the Available Columns screen, which displays the types of data which can be included on the report. JIRA # RC-3865

Indicator Added When Client Selector Not Available

When viewing a report shows results from all clients, the Client(s) field is not available. A tooltip has been added to indicate the field is not available for the current report.

JIRA # RC-3862

Tooltips Added to Category and Tag Management

In Administration, the Manage Category and Manage Tags tabs have been enhanced with tooltips for the edit and delete icons, indicating that these options affect the whole system. In addition, a confirmation message displays when selecting the delete icon to verify the action. JIRA # RC-3197

Version 1.19.0 June 2020

Enhancements The Report Center Quarterly Release (QR) for June 2020 includes the following enhancements.

Restricted Fields In Report Center, certain fields are pre-defined as restricted. Currently, the information those fields contain falls into the following categories: • Personal Identification Information (PII)

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 241 Chapter 6 Release Notes

• Banking By default, restricted fields are not visible to users, even when they have access to the reports that contain those fields. They are not available in the Columns list or displayed in reports. To grant users access, a Service Provider User Administrator must select the fields that should be accessible to role members. This is a two-step process: 1. In PrismHR, a user with the SUPERUSER or equivalent role designates each user who will administer access to restricted fields as a Service Provider User Administrator. This is an initial step that is typically performed only once. 2. In Report Center, the Service Provider User Administrator adds the restricted fields to each role that needs to access them. This step may need to be repeated for regular maintenance. For example, roles may be added or additional restricted fields may become available. See the Report Center Administration Guide for complete details for performing each task.

Note: If a user exports a report that contains sensitive information, other users may be able to see and access exported data that they don’t have access to in Report Center. Contact your system administrator with any questions regarding the proper safeguarding of sensitive information.

Version 1.6.0 .0 March 2020

Enhancements The Report Center Quarterly Release (QR) for March 2020 includes the following enhancements.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 253 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Pivot Functionality Pivot View functionality is now incorporated into Report Center grid reports. Unlike a static report, a pivot table provides an interactive view of data that lets you look at the same data from many different perspectives. You can group data into categories, break it down into years and months, and filter it to include or exclude categories. You can transform rows into columns and columns into rows. And, best of all, you don’t need to write formulas or start over every time you want to organize or summarize the data in a different way.

The toolbar for grid reports provides a Pivot View ( ) icon that you can click to go into Pivot mode, where you have the following options: • Select rows, columns, and values. • Start over by clearing the current settings. • Configure pivot settings and specify whether to display or hide a preview of your selections. • Return to grid view. In Pivot View, the toolbar changes to one appropriate for pivots with two options:

• If you click (Grid View), you return you to the standard grid/columnar view. If you click (Pivot View) again, you return to the previously configured pivot.

• If you click (Export), you can export the report to a CSV file. JIRA # IRP-156 JIRA # IRP-2019

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 254 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Grid Changes This section describes enhancements to grid reports.

Column

The following enhancements were made to the expanding menu on the column header: • A Hide option was added to immediately hide the column. This is equivalent to clicking the Columns icon in the menu bar and clearing the column. • The column name is displayed in a header area at the top of the menu. JIRA # IRP-2265

Group and Aggregate Exports

You can export grid reports that include groups and aggregates to CSV, PDF, or Excel. • If the report contains no groups, the system exports detail data. • If the report contains groups and aggregates, the system exports it with all groups expanded and shows the aggregate type stacked under each group. • If the report is in Summary only view and it contains groups and aggregates, the system exports summary data only and shows each aggregate in its own column. JIRA # IRP-1837

When exporting to PDF. the system automatically expands all groups and shows the aggregate type (Count, Distinct Count, Average. Maximum, Minimum, or Total). JIRA # IRP-1809

Grouped Grid Aggregates • A persistent footer is always visible. • Different settings are used when all columns have totals or nothing or at least one column has more aggregates than just totals. When even one column breaks the aggregates out into sub-cells, all columns follow the same behavior to avoid confusion. • In the “split into sub-cells” case, you can move the column names for columns that don’t have aggregates to the top row so that the main column headers are on the same row across the grid. • All numeric columns, including counts. use comma separators. JIRA # IRP-1807

Group Changes • Adding a new group retains sort specifications for the grid. • A notification message displays when a session times out.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 255 Chapter 6 Release Notes

• Positioning the pointing device over a truncated column heading displays a tooltip that shows the full name. JIRA # IRP-1806

Footer Display

The footer was modified as follows: l The Show All option and the As of date/time stamp were removed from the footer. l The Page size option was moved to the footer. l Large numbers are now shown with comma separators in the footer. JIRA # IRP-1803

Row and Font Size

l   The font size was changed to 13px Open Sans.
l   The row height was increased to its previous setting.

JIRA # IRP-1800

Summary View Toggle

A summary view of columns with aggregates is available. This feature provides a more concise view of the data by hiding any columns that do not contain aggregates. The setting toggles between viewing and hiding columns with aggregates. When you export a grid report that is in “Summary only” view and that contains groups and aggregates, the system exports summary data only and shows each aggregate in its own column. JIRA # IRP-1811

Version 1.21.0 November 2020

Enhancements The Report Center Quarterly Release (QR) for November 2020 includes the enhancements described in the following sections.

Templated Reports This release includes a new report type called Templated. Unlike other types of reports, you configure templated reports by entering parameters that produce a standard output. To generate the report, you define the following parameters: • The client. Terminated clients are shown in italics and followed by a T. The client selected in the global client selector is shown by default. If multiple clients are selected, the first one selected in shown. To search for a different client, expand the Client list. • A payroll date or payroll date range • The field to use as the employee unique identifier: • The employee ID that is defined in PrismHR • The employee number that the worksite manager assigns • The employee clock number defined by the time clock After you generate the report, you can group the results. You can also export the results to PDF format.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 271 Chapter 6 Release Notes

This release includes a Gross-to-Net Register templated report. The following example shows a partial report.

Administration In this release, the Administration functions were enhanced so that administrators can make copies of the system reports that come with Report Center, edit them, and save them as custom reports. Administrators can also edit copies of custom reports and save them as new custom reports.

Creating a Custom Report

As an administrator, you can create a new custom report based on three report types (grid, chart, and map). The current settings of the source system report are used as the new report’s default view settings, including columns, column order, sorting, grouping, aggregates, summary/details, and filters. When you open a report from the Home page, the toolbar contains a Save icon. • When you click Save from a system report, a Save as new report option is available. When this option is selected, the Save Report dialog box appears. • When you click Save from a custom report, both Save and Save as new report options are available. Depending on the selected option, either the Save Report dialog box or the Save As New Report dialog box opens.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 272 Chapter 6 Release Notes

In both dialog boxes, you provide the following information about the new report: • Report Name • Description • Category • Tags • Sharing - specifies whether the new report will be private to the administrator or shared with other users in selected roles. After saving, the dialog box closes and a success message that contains a link to the report is displayed. If errors occur during saving, an error message is displayed. JIRA # RC-3078, RC-3079

Administration Area for Save As

The report list page provides the following enhancements: • A Dataset column displays the name of the dataset on which the report is based. • A Filter was added for the dataset name. When you open a report from the list, the report details page provides the following enhancements: • A Name field was added for custom reports ONLY (not system reports). The name is saved when the page is submitted. • A Created By field was added for all reports (both system and custom). It shows the name of the report owner and the creation date. • A Dataset field was added for all reports (both system and custom). JIRA # RC-3092

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 273 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Deleting a Custom Report

When you open a custom report from the Administration page, the title area provides a Delete icon. Clicking Delete triggers a confirmation popup. • Selecting Yes, delete permanently removes the report from the system and the list page displays a message that the report was deleted. • Selecting Cancel displays the list page and no changes are made. System reports cannot be deleted. JIRA # RC-3109

Icons for Custom Reports If your administrator shared any custom reports with your role, those reports are shown in your report list along with the system reports. The custom report icons are hollow versions of the system report icons that visually distinguish custom reports from system reports.

Version 1.20.0 September 2020

Enhancements The Report Center Quarterly Release (QR) for September 2020 includes the enhancements described in the following sections.

Integration with Work Centers Panel The Report Center menu is accessible to Service Providers from the Work Centers panel on the PrismHR dashboard. See the Report Center Administration Guide for details about how to configure Report Center service provider access from the Work Centers panel.

Integration with Employee Portal The Report Center menu is accessible to managers in Employee Portal. The menu is not shown for users or employees. See the Report Center Administration Guide for details about how to configure Report Center manager access from Employee Portal. JIRA # RC-3110

Administration Previously, the Report Center Administration role was tied to Prism User / Account Management Role / Service Provider User Administrator. Since it may not be appropriate for the Service Provider User Administrator to also be the Report Center User Administrator, the two roles are now separate. When a user with the Report Center User Administrator role opens Report Center, the Administration icon is available on the home page to access administrative functions.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 277 Chapter 6 Release Notes

See the Report Center Administration Guide for details about how to assign the Report Center User Administrator role. JIRA # RC-2816

Security This following sections describe the security enhancements included in this release. See the Report Center Administration Guide for details about how to configure field level and report level security.

Field Level Security

When a Report Center administrator selects restricted fields, the following field names are shown instead of the field alias. • Bank Account Number - Unmasked • SSN - Unmasked • Birth Date JIRA # RC-2869

Report Level Security

Report-level security is now available in Report Center and was removed from PrismHR to avoid confusion. Report Center reports are no longer searchable in PrismHR. JIRA # RC-3038

Categories Administrators can define categories that provide a way to organize reports and access them as a group. See the Report Center Administration Guide for details about maintaining categories. See the Report Center User Guide for details about how to use categories.

Creating a Report Category

An administrator can create categories on the Report Details page in Report Center Administration or directly from the list of existing categories. Entering a new category opens the Add Category dialog box where you enter a category name. Adding a new category automatically applies it to the selected report and the new category appears in all relevant category lists. JIRA # RC-3056

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 278 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Managing Categories

An administrator can add, edit, and delete categories using the new Manage Categories dialog box. To open this dialog box, click the Manage Categories link on the Report Details page. • To add a category click Add. • To edit a category click (Edit). • To delete a category click (Delete). Changes are saved immediately. JIRA # RC-3057

Tags Administrators can define tags that provide a way to access reports based on the tags that are assigned to them. See the Report Center Administration Guide for complete details about maintaining tags. See the Report Center User Guide for details about how to use tags.

Creating Tags

An administrator can add, edit, and delete tags using the new Manage Tags dialog box. To open this dialog box, click the Manage Tags link on the Report Details page. You enter a name and choose a color for the tag. Adding a new tag automatically applies it to the report. Tag changes are saved when you click Save on the main Report edit page. JIRA # RC-2702

Managing Tags

An administrator can add, edit, and delete tags using the new Manage Tags dialog box. To open this dialog box, click the Manage Tags link on the Report Details page. • To add a tag click Add. • To edit a tag click (Edit). • To delete a tag click (Delete). Changes are saved immediately. JIRA # RC-2912

Home Page The following sections describe the home page enhancements included in this release.

Report Center Administration Guide © 2024 PrismHR 279 Chapter 6 Release Notes

Compact View

Grid View was renamed to Compact View and enhanced as follows: • Preview capability was added. • View toggle controls were moved next to Sort. The selected view is encircled in gray. • The icons for view toggle controls were changed. • Sort was removed in compact view (sort is handled by table column headers). • Table and columns resize automatically when the window is resized. JIRA # RC-1718

Viewing and Filtering by Categories

Categories are displayed as follows: • In card view, reports are displayed under their associated categories. That is, categories are used as headers. • In compact view, a column was added to display the category. You can filter by one or more selected categories. By default, Categories: All is selected in the filter list and no filters are applied. Standard Search, Select all | Clear all, and Done options are available. When you search for a report, results are displayed under their category names. JIRA # JIRA # RC-2712

Viewing and Filtering by Tags

Tags are displayed as follows: • In card view, each card displays the tags associated with the report. • In compact view, a column was added to display the tag. You can filter by one or more selected tags in both card and compact view. Standard Search, Select all | Clear all, and Done options are available. JIRA # IRA # RC-622

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction Report Center is a centralized and consolidated reporting tool. It comes with many predefined reports that you can use as is or that you can quickly customize to meet the specific requirements of your organization. You can also easily define the presentation of the output and change it at any time as your requirements change. Report access is role-based. Only the reports for which your role has access privileges are available in Report Center. Before you can begin using Report Center, an administrator must grant you access to Report Center and to any report to which members of your role require access. Report Center applies PrismHR user role security. See your administrator if you need to change your access privileges.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Introduction

Accessing Report Center Service Providers and Worksite Managers can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard or from Employee Portal. See your administrator if you do not have the access you require.

Accessing from the PrismHR Dashboard A service provider or worksite manager can access Report Center from the PrismHR Dashboard.

To access Report Center from the Work Centers panel: 1. Open the PrismHR Dashboard. 2. On the Work Centers panel, click Report Center in the Reporting section.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 Introduction

To access Report Center by searching: 1. Open the PrismHR Dashboard. 2. In the Search box, type Interactive Reports. 3. Click Report Center in the list of results.

Accessing Report Center Using Employee Portal A manager can access Report Center using Employee Portal.

To access Report Center: 1. Open Employee Portal. 2. In the menu list, select Report Center.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 8 Chapter 1 Introduction

Getting Help Report Center provides online help for both users and administrators. Your role determines which topics you can access.

Click (Help) next to the Global Client Selector to open the help system.

Using the toolbar Use the toolbar to perform these actions. A tooltip is available for each icon.

• Browse to the previous or next topic. • Print the current topic. • Expand or collapse the TOC. • Remove highlighting from topics that you opened from search results.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Introduction

Searching for topics To find specific topics, type text in the Search box and click .

The list of results contains all topics that include the text in their titles or content. For example, if you type Summary, the results list includes a link to each topic whose title or content contains the word Summary. It shows the total number of matches and displays the text in bold if it is in the topic title. You can also find topics by navigating through the Table of Contents (TOC). Just expand and collapse sections until you find what you are looking for.

Submitting documentation feedback Each topic in the help system provides an option for you to send feedback about that topic. Your input goes directly to the PrismHR documentation team and will be promptly answered.

Note: The Send us feedback option is intended for comments about the documentation.

• To send product/release feature requests, submit a PrismHR Idea. Alternately, you can click the following icon at the lower right hand corner of the Report Center home page and use the Feedback option to send feedback directly to our product team.

Chapter 2 Navigating the home page On the Home page, the list of reports shows only the reports to which your administrator has given you access. There are two basic types of reports. l System reports come with Report Center and are pre-defined. You can temporarily configure a system report based on your requirements. l An administrator can modify a copy of a system report and save it as a new custom report. An administrator can also modify a custom report and save it as a new report. If the administrator shares a custom report with your role, that report is shown in your list of reports. For both system and custom reports, any changes that you make to report formatting persist the next time you open the same report. However, the system does not permanently change the report. The list of reports on your Home page may contain some or all of the following types of reports. Each report type is described in detail later in this guide.

In both Card and Compact view, you have the following options: • Use the breadcrumb bar to show where the current page fits into the site hierarchy and navigate between levels. See Searching for reports. • Use the Tags list to filter the list by predefined tags (keywords). See Selecting tags. • Use the Categories list to display only reports in selected categories. Configuring columns You can select the fields that appear as columns on a report from a list of available fields. Each report comes with a set of columns that are shown by default. Open the Columns list to see whether additional columns are available.

To select columns: 1. Open a report.

  1. Click (Columns) in the toolbar.
  2. Use the check boxes to select or clear columns individually or click Select all or Clear all.
  3. To search for particular columns, type all or part of the column name in the Search box. In the search results, you can select or clear individual columns or all columns. Selected columns remain selected even if they are currently not visible in the search results. Searches are case insensitive.

Pinning a column You can pin a column to fix it in place and prevent it from scrolling out of view.

To pin a column: 1. Click the column header menu and then select Pin. 2. Select one of the following options: • Pin Left - Pins the column to the leftmost position. • Pin Right - Pins the column to the rightmost position. • No Pin - Unpins the column. If you move a pinned column, the system automatically unpins it.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 25 Chapter 3 Grid reports

Moving a column You can move a column either by dragging it to a new location or by selecting Move from the column header menu.

To move a column by dragging: 1. Click and drag the column header. The cursor changes to a drag icon.

  1. Drag the column to the position you want.

To move a column using the column header menu: 1. Click the column header menu and then select Move. 2. Select one of the following options: • To the beginning - Moves the column to the beginning of the report. • To the end - Moves the column to the end of the report. • To after column - Displays a list of available columns from which you can select the column after which the column will be inserted.

Resizing columns You can resize one or more columns. For example, you can change the width of columns to accommodate the width of the data they contain.

To resize columns: Open a column header menu and then select one of the following options: • Autosize all columns - Automatically resizes all columns. • Autosize this column - Automatically resizes the selected column. • Lock column width - Locks the current width of the column. You cannot resize a locked column. • Unlock column width - Unlocks the current width of the column. so that it can be resized. You can also double-click a column heading divider and then drag it to resize a column.

Grouping data You can create groups to group rows together based on the value in a specific column, and then provide subtotals and other aggregates. For example, a benefits administrator can see all clients who have a specific carrier grouped together, with subtotals for each carrier. Groups are the first implied sorts. Each group is shown in the group bar for the report. The system displays totals for currency fields and subtotals for those fields if you add a group. Grouping in Interactive Reports is similar to “sort” in the PrismHR standard on demand reports. Both functions group data together by a single field, with headers and totals. After you create at least one group, you can create additional groups from the group bar. You can remove a group by clearing the check box in the Group toolbar menu or by clicking the X to the right of the group name in the group bar. In the following example, data is grouped by Client Name, Employee Name, and Deduction Code.

To create a group using the toolbar:

  1. On the toolbar, click (Group).
  2. Select the columns to include in the group. You can find specific columns by entering text in the Search box. A column does not need to be visible in the report to be available for grouping. You can ungroup a grouped column by clearing the check box or by clicking the X to the right of the group name in the group area.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 28 Chapter 3 Grid reports

To create a group from the group bar: 1. Create at least one group. 2. In the Group bar, click Add Group and select the columns to group. You can find specific columns by entering text in the Search box.

To create a group from an existing column: • Open the column header menu and select Group.

To expand groups: • Click the first level group and continue expanding sub-groups.

Viewing summary data When a group is applied to a report, a Summary only option is available on the group toolbar. It displays groups and aggregates and hides all other fields from the display.

A summary view of columns with aggregates provides a more concise view of the data by hiding any columns that do not contain aggregates. The setting toggles between viewing and hiding columns with aggregates.

Aggregating data Using aggregates, you can combine data in various ways. For example, a report can contain aggregate values such as average, count, distinct count, maximum, minimum, and total for any numeric or currency value. You can create aggregates only for columns that are currently visible on the report.

To aggregate data from the toolbar:

  1. On the toolbar, click (Aggregate) and select a column. Each column is listed with an icon that indicates its data type.
  2. Select a column and then select an aggregation option.

                                      Max              The highest value out of all those in the column.

                                      Distinct         The number of distinct (or unique) values for the
                                                       column. For example, if a report contains 300 rows

                                                       are age 35, and 100 are age 45, the distinct count is 3.

Date Max The highest value out of all those in the column.

Filtering data By creating filters, you can narrow the scope of the information displayed in a report to your specific requirements. Filtering reduces the number of rows displayed. For example, in a report related to Benefits, you may want to narrow down the report to see only rows related to medical plans (and not dental, vision, and other plans). You can fine tune filters to display very specific information. The filter options vary depending on the type of data in the column. Filters are cumulative and applied in order. They act like a funnel where each successive filter further narrows down the results of the previous filters. For instance, if one filter is already applied and you apply a distinct filter as your second filter, the list displays only the distinct values remaining after you apply the first filter, not all of the values in the entire data set. Filters are shown in the filter bar of the report. Some reports have filters applied by default.

You can filter the data on a report in the following ways: • Enter search text • Filter based on the values in one or more columns After you create a filter, you have more advanced options for fine tuning it. See Fine tuning a filter.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 32 Chapter 3 Grid reports

Searching is case-sensitive. As you type, the system filters the result list to contain only the characters that you enter. The system filters the report and adds the filter to the filter bar.

To create a filter by entering search text: 1. In Search fields, type the text you want to find and then make a selection from the search results. The system adds the filter to the filter bar and filters the report to your specification. 2. If you want to specify match criteria, click the filter in the filter bar. The Filter by Query String displays your query text.

  1. Click (Options) > Match behavior and specify the conditions for finding data. This option is available only for text searches. • Match exact words • Starts with value • Contains the value (default)

Selecting columns Another way to create a filter is by selecting a column.

To create a filter by selecting column values: 1. In the filter bar, click the Filter icon.

  1. Select a column from the list. The filtering panel opens automatically.

Fine tuning a filter You can fine tune a filter that is shown in the filter bar.

To fine tune a filter: 1. In the filter bar, click the filter. The filtering panel opens and displays the default values for the selected data type. The filtering panel opens automatically if you are creating a filter by selecting a column. 2. Select the information to display. The options that are available depend on the data type. The following table describes the options for each data type.

Data Type Options

Text • Distinct values - This is the default. The system displays a list of all distinct values in the report with selection check boxes. You can select one or more values to show only rows that contain those values in the selected column. • Like -Use ’*’ to match any character sequence. Use ‘?’ to match a single letter or number. • Enter value - Displays an Enter value box where you can specify the values to find. Click + and - to add and delete rows. • Is Empty - Displays rows where the value is empty. • Is Not Empty - Displays rows where the value is not empty. • Sort - Provides options to sort by count or by distinct values.

Currency • Number range - Displays Range boxes where you can enter the minimum and maximum values to find. This is the default. • Number range slider - Display a slider where you can enter the minimum and maximum values to find. • Enter value - Displays an Enter value box where you can specify the exact values to find. Click + and - to add and delete rows. • Is Empty - Displays rows where the value is empty. • Is Not Empty - Displays rows where the value is not empty.

Data Type Options

Date • Date range - Displays From and To areas where you can either type the beginning and ending dates for the range or select them by clicking the calendar. This is the default. • Distinct values - Displays only exact matches. The system displays a list from which you can select check boxes. • Date relative to now - Displays boxes where you can specify a date relative to the current date. You select Past or Next, enter the number, and select a unit (days, weeks, months, or years). For example, if the current date is January 1 and you specify Next 30 days, the system finds all rows with a date of January 30. • Date keyword - Displays an area where you can specify a date using keywords such as YESTERDAY or MONTH_END. Click (Help) for a complete list of valid keywords, modifiers, date formats, and examples. • Is Empty - Displays rows where the value is empty. • Is Not Empty - Displays rows where the value is not empty.

Sorting columns Report Center provides many ways for you to sort the columns in your reports. Sorting toggles one or more columns between ascending and descending order. An arrow is shown in the column heading to indicate the direction of the sort.

To sort a column: • Open the column header menu and click Sort.

To specify the sort sequence: • Open the column header menu and click Sort > Sort ascending or Sort descending.

To sort by multiple columns: • Shift+click each column header. A number in the column header indicates the sequence for the sort. The system assigns sequence numbers based on the order in which you select columns for sorting. After you assign the first sort sequence, you can sort additional columns by opening the column header menu and clicking Sort > Add sort ascending or Add Sort descending.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 37 Chapter 3 Grid reports

To remove sorting for a column: • Open the column header menu and click Sort > Remove sort. In the following example, the report is first sorted by Client Name, then by Pay Date, and finally by Employee Name. If you remove sorting from the Pay Date column, the Employee Name column sequence changes to 2. The sort sequence for a column does not change if you move it to another location.

Showing the database name Using the Options menu, you can specify whether to show the database name (field alias) under the column heading.

To show or hide the database name: • In the toolbar, click (Options) > Show field alias or Hide field alias. The option toggles between showing and hiding the database column name under the column heading. The default option is to hide the field alias.

Displaying rows The footer area for each grid report shows the number of rows displayed.

To select the number of rows to show: 1. Click the current row option shown in the footer area at the bottom of the grid. The default setting is Show all rows. A list of available options opens. 2. Select one of the following options: • Show all rows (default) - Displays all rows so that you can scroll continuously through the report without waiting for the next page to load. • rows per page - Displays rows in pages of 50, 100, 500, 1,000, or 10,000, based on the selected setting. Pagination controls are provided at the bottom of the page to navigate through the pages.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 38 Chapter 3 Grid reports

Creating a pivot table Unlike a static report, a pivot table provides an interactive view of your data that lets you look at the same data from many different perspectives. You can group data into categories, break down data into years and months, and filter data to include or exclude categories. You can transform rows into columns and columns into rows. And, best of all, you don’t need to write formulas or start over every time you want to organize or summarize the data in a different way.

To enter pivot mode or return to your last pivot:

• On the toolbar, click (Pivot View).

To exit pivot mode:

• Click (Grid View). Pivots are saved when you exit.

In Pivot mode, you have the following options. • Export the pivot to a CSV file. • Select rows, columns, and values. • Start over by clearing the current settings.
