If you click (Settings), you have additional options. You may need to hide the preview to see them. • Select a layout: Tree, Tabular, or Tabular with subtotals. • Choose how columns are ordered: Values descending, Values ascending, Group headers ascending, Group headers ascending. • Enable drill-down to view data. • Select an option for displaying aggregates: Total, Average, Minimum, Maximum, Count. Distinct count. • Change the default column header. • Select options for formatting numbers and setting color ranges. • Limit the number of rows and columns. • Display or hide a preview of your selections.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 40 Chapter 4 Working with views

Chapter 4 Working with views Report Center reports include a collection of data that is usually presented in a large number of columns. Typically, you use the same report for many different tasks. Using views, you can save frequently-used report configurations for a specific purpose so that you can quickly switch between variations of the same report based on your current requirements. For example, you can save a view that filters a different set of data than the default, or that hides columns that are not needed for a particular situation. Views can also help to prevent cluttering your Report Center home page with multiple copies of the same report with only slight variations. Each report provides a menu of views that you can access. You can create a private view that is accessible only to you or your administrator can create views and share them with you. A view can contain anything that changes the display of the report, including the following parameters: • Filters (excluding selected clients and data rows) • Columns hidden/shown • Column order • Sorting • Groups • Summary yes/no • Aggregates • Column formatting (under Text Format, Number Format, Date Format in the column header menu)

Notes: • Views apply only to grid reports. Templated, Chart, and Map reports do not support views. • You cannot include pivots in views. • You cannot copy or migrate views from one report to another.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 41 Chapter 4 Working with views

Using the Views menu Depending on your requirements, you can use the Views menu to configure various types of views. Only administrators can create views that are shared with multiple users. Non-administrators can only create private views, which are visible only to the creator and administrators. You can create as many views as you want, but only a few are shown as shortcuts in the Views menu at any given time. You can access the other views by selecting Views > All views. From there you can apply or edit the other views.

The menu heading (1) shows the currently selected view. Expand it to show the Switch views area, which provides a maximum of 4 views that act as shortcuts. The following table describes each type of view.

Number Option Description 2 Current view Shows the name of the currently selected view with a check mark, if not the Client view or Your view.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 42 Chapter 4 Working with views

Number Option Description Shown if not the client or your view. 3 Client view (name) Client views (sometimes called “client default views”) associate views with clients. They are intended to fill many of the same needs as Client Parameters in PrismHR payroll reports. Your administrator may create client views for the client(s) you work with. Worksite managers see their client view applied by default when they visit a report for the first time. Shown if there is one for the current client. 4 Your view Your View enables you to have your own preferred view for each report. Setting a view as Your View adds it as a shortcut in the Switch Views area of the Views menu so that it is easy to apply. This is useful when you frequently use the same view. Shown if the current user has one. 5 Report default Each report has a Report Default view. Only administrators can change the Report Default view. Always shown.

Only administrators can create views that are shared with multiple users. Non-administrators can only create private views, which are visible only to the creator and administrators. Client views are shown as follows: • When a single client is selected in the global client selector, and the client has a designated client view, the client view is shown in the menu as Client view (Name). If the name is too long to fit in the menu, it is truncated. If the selected client does not have a designated client view, nothing is shown. • When a client view is selected, the view area shows “View: Client view (name)” with a check mark next to the name. • When multiple clients are selected, the following message is shown at the top of the menu “Client view (select a single client to enable).” Although no client views are shown in the Views menu, the views are still available to be applied from the All Views dialog box. • When switching clients, the selected view does not change, but the client view for the new client becomes available in the Views menu .

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 43 Chapter 4 Working with views

Saving a view You can save the current report settings as a new private view using the Save as a new view option on the Views menu. When saving views, be conscious of the filters you have applied, as they will be saved with the view. For instance, it is better to save a view with a relative date of “Pay Date in past 90 days” than with an absolute date such as “Pay Date: After 1/1/2021” because the relative date continues to work whenever it is applied. You can change an existing view by opening the existing view and then selecting Edit view settings from the Views menu. This opens the Edit View Settings dialog box, which displays the report parameters that will be saved as part of the view, including filters, columns, groups, aggregates, and sorting. It also provides a text box where you enter a name for the view. Following are some best practices for naming views: • For optimal usability, name views either based on their purpose (such as Reconciliation or Monthly summary) or their display characteristics (such as Grouped by Department). • Do not name views after specific clients for the following reasons: • The same view may be associated with multiple clients. • Other users may be confused about whether they’re looking at a view name or a client name. Names longer than about 50 characters will be truncated in some areas of the user interface.

Note: Only Report Center administrators can share views.

To save a new view: 1. Open the report. 2. Select one of the following options: • On the Views menu, select Save as a new view. • On the toolbar, click (Save) and then select Save as view. The Save As View dialog box opens.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 55 Chapter 7 Exporting reports

Chapter 7 Exporting reports Report Center provides many options for exporting the data in your reports. • You can export grid reports, including those in Summary only view, to CSV, PDF, or Excel formats. In Pivot view, you can export to CSV only. • You can export chart reports to PNG, HTML, JPEG, or PDF formats. • The export options for custom reports depend on the type of system report on which they are based. • You can export templated reports to PDF format. • When you select View data in charts or maps, you can export that data to CSV, Excel, and PDF formats You also have various options for formatting the exported report. The formatting options that are available depend on the report type: • When exporting to CSV or PDF, the Apply formatting option is available to apply the configured type formatting options from the grid. When this option is selected, certain number options can cause numbers to appear as strings. When cleared, dates are strings in ISO-8601 standard format (for example, 2014-05-17T17:00:00.000Z). • When exporting to Excel, the Format dates for recognition in Excel option is available. When this option is selected, the system ignores grid formatting and attempts to format dates so that Excel recognizes them (values are in UTC format). When the option is cleared, dates are strings formatted as they appear in the grid.

Note: Although the data exported has security restrictions, the file itself does not. Depending on where you choose to store the exported files, exporting data may result in the creation of additional temporary and permanent files on your computer. If the exported files contain sensitive data, people may be able to see and access exported reports and data that they don’t have access to in Report Center. Contact your system administrator with any questions regarding the proper safeguarding of sensitive information.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 56 Chapter 7 Exporting reports

Exporting grid reports You can export grid reports (including those in Summary only view) to CSV, Excel, or PDF format. In Pivot view, you can export to CSV only.

To export a grid report:

  1. Open the report and click (Export) in the toolbar.
  2. Select the output format. • If necessary, change the file name that the system supplies. • If you select CSV or PDF, specify whether to apply formatting. • If you select Excel, specify whether to format dates for recognition in Excel, and enter the worksheet name.
  3. Click EXPORT. The system converts the report and saves it in your Downloads folder (or you may be prompted for the download location). You can click CANCEL to cancel the export.

Exporting grid reports with groups and aggregates You have the following options for exporting grid reports that include groups and aggregates: • If the report contains no groups, the system exports detail data. • If the report contains groups and aggregates, the system exports it with all groups expanded and shows the aggregate type stacked under each group. • If the report is in Summary only view and it contains groups and aggregates, the system exports summary data only and shows each aggregate in its own column. See Viewing summary data.

Exporting chart reports You can export charts to PNG, HTML, JPEG, and SVG formats. When you select View data in charts, you can export that data to CSV, Excel, and PDF formats.

To export a chart report:

  1. Open the report and click (Export) in the toolbar.
  2. Select the output format. The system converts the report and saves it in your Downloads folder (or you may be prompted for the download location).

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 57 Chapter 7 Exporting reports

Exporting data in chart or map reports When you select View data in charts or maps, you can export that data to CSV, Excel, and PDF formats.

To export the data in a chart or map report:

  1. Double-click a bar (or other data point) in the chart and click (Export).
  2. Select the output format. • If necessary, change the file name that the system supplies. • If you select CSV or PDF, specify whether to apply formatting. • If you select Excel, specify whether to format dates for recognition in Excel, and enter the worksheet name.
  3. Click EXPORT. The system converts the report and saves it in your Downloads folder (or you may be prompted for the download location). You can click CANCEL to cancel the export or RUN IN BACKGROUND to run it in background mode.

Exporting custom reports You can export a custom grid, map, or chart report to PDF, XLS, or CSV format. The available formats depend on whether it is based on a grid, chart, or map report.

To export a custom report:

  1. Open the report and click (Export) in the toolbar.
  2. Select the output format. The system converts the report and saves it in your Downloads folder (or you may be prompted for the download location).

Exporting templated reports You can export a templated report to PDF format.

To export a templated report:

  1. Open the report and click (Export) in the toolbar.
  2. Select the output format. The system converts the report and saves it in your Downloads folder (or you may be prompted for the download location).

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 60 Chapter 8 Resetting reports to defaults

Chapter 8 Resetting reports to defaults Administrators, service providers, and managers can reset reports to their default settings. When a report returns an error such as “Access to this page is restricted”, resetting the user settings for the report can restore the default view. Saved views are still preserved when restoring a report to the default settings.

To restore a report to the default settings: • In the Profile dropdown menu, click Reset report to defaults. The Reset Report to Defaults dialogue box displays.

• In the Select Report dropdown menu, select a report to reset. • Click Reset Selected Report to restore the report to default settings.

Report Center User Guide © 2024 PrismHR 61 Chapter 9 Parameter-Driven Reports

Chapter 9 Parameter-Driven Reports You define parameters for parameter-driven reports at the time the report is run. These settings can be changed each time the parameter-driven report is generated to show point-in-time information. Parameter-driven reports are identified by the ( ) icon.

Enter criteria for the report parameters and click Run Report to generate the report using the selected settings. After the report is complete, the other report icons become available. Once generated, these reports populate the traditional grid format and can be managed just like a normal report. Data from the last report is saved and available when the report is reopened. To update the report with the most recent data, refresh the report or re-run it.

Note: Select Run in background to minimize the report and continue working in Report Center. A progress wheel indicates the progress of the report running in the background, and a notification appears when the report is complete.
